home_pitcher_note: A free-agent pickup brought in to provide some leadership, the 33-year-old gets his first big league Opening Day nod, partly because of injuries and largely because of performance.
away_pitcher_note: Santana, more than anyone else, has given the Mets reason to believe that they're better than last year. He's charged them with optimism and erased memories of last September -- and all that without throwing a pitch of any consequence.

home_pitcher_note: A 22-year-old from the Netherlands, VandenHurk got a taste of the big leagues last year when he was called up in early April because of an injury situation. He ended up making 17 starts and appearing in 18 games for Florida in his rookie season. The right-hander endured some predictable growing pains at the big league level. To get him more seasoning, he also pitched in '07 at Double-A and Triple-A. In all, he threw a career-high 147 1/3 innings a year ago.
away_pitcher_note: If Martinez was upset about losing his ace status to Johan Santana, he wasn't about to complain. Instead, he has said all the right things in regard to his new teammate, and now, he'll finally have a chance to back up those words on the mound. Set to start the season's second game against the Marlins, Martinez will also be embarking on what he hopes can be his first full season since 2005. Right rotator cuff surgery cut short the end of his 2006 season, after he missed nearly all of last summer recovering from the same operation. For his career, Martinez is 6-6 with a 2.85 ERA against the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: One of the centerpieces in the trade with the Tigers for Dontrelle Willis and Miguel Cabrera, the 22-year-old Miller threw 64 innings with the Tigers a year ago. A first-round pick in the 2005 Draft, Miller may have the most overall talent in the rotation. The lefty, however, still is refining his skills, but he projects to be a frontline starter for years to come.
away_pitcher_note: Oliver Perez enters this season with a hefty contract -- and some hefty expectations. After winning his arbitration case in February and nearly tripling his salary to $6.5 million, Perez embarked on a spring that was quite typical of his career to date. Half the time, he was unhittable. The other half, he was anything but.

home_pitcher_note: If not for a bout of shoulder tendinitis this spring, Olsen was in line to be the Opening Day starter. Now, he is slotted fourth. The 24-year-old has top-of-the-rotation talent, but he's dealt with inconsistencies. Last year, he struggled with his command, and a high walk count led to a disappointing campaign.
away_pitcher_note: The results haven't been there for Morris this spring, but the right-hander has reiterated that he continues to feel more in sync after each subsequent start. After being acquired from the Giants last July, Morris went 3-4 with a 6.10 ERA in 11 starts for Pittsburgh. Morris, the veteran of the staff, can typically be expected to give the Pirates at least six innings per start, though it remains to be seen how successful he can still be after a few years of sub-par results.

home_pitcher_note: A six-run fourth inning on Opening Day led to a rough afternoon for Hendrickson, who makes his second start of the season on Saturday. The 6-foot-9 left-hander was tagged for those six runs in five innings. He was sailing along until he threw 36 pitches in the fourth and was unable to work out of two-out trouble. For his career, Hendrickson is 1-0 with a 3.27 ERA in two games against the Pirates.
away_pitcher_note: Maholm's back stiffness prompted a swap of starters for the Bucs, with Zach Duke filling in for Maholm on Thursday and Maholm slated to go in this game. Maholm opens the season as arguably the least talked about pitcher in the Pirates' rotation, but looking like he could be poised to make a big step forward in his career. He has shown an ability to rely on all four of his pitches consistently throughout Spring Training and has worked to limit the amount of walks that he issues. The left-hander came into camp in peak condition and will look to improve on his 10-win season from a year ago.

home_pitcher_note: Running up a high pitch count hurt VandenHurk in his season debut. Despite being staked to a 4-0 lead after two innings against the Mets, the 22-year-old was lifted after three-plus innings because his count was up to 76. He yielded three runs and exited without a decision. This will be VandenHurk's first appearance against the Pirates. Minimizing pitches and working deeper into games remains a work in progress for VandenHurk, who three times last year lasted as long as six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Though Snell gave up four runs in six innings of work against the Braves in his Opening Day start on Monday, the right-hander continued to show progress in being able to pitch consistently to both the inner and outer halves of the plate. With a fastball and slider anchoring Snell?s pitch repertoire, look for him to continue increasing the frequency with which he pitches inside. Snell will be looking for his first career victory against the Marlins. He has faced them twice before, allowing a total of 10 runs in 7 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Redding ended up having one of the best games of his career, pitching seven-plus innings and giving up just one hit, as the Nationals blanked the Phillies, 1-0, at Citizens Bank Park on Tuesday. The only hit Redding allowed came in the second, when Pedro Feliz singled to center field. After that, Redding retired 15 of the next 17 batters. Redding managed to pitch so well despite that fact that it was cold. The game-time temperature was 49 degrees.  On Monday, Redding will face the Marlins for the sixth time in his career. He is 3-0 with a 2.00 against them.
away_pitcher_note: Miller's debut for the Marlins was a rough one, as the 22-year-old ran up a high pitch count and issued five runs in 4 1/3 innings in a loss to the Mets at Dolphin Stadium. Working deep into games is a concern for the Marlins, and Miller has the makings of being a top-of-the-rotation sensation. For now, he is still learning, and falling behind in counts was a problem against the Mets. It also gave him trouble for most of Spring Training. Miller used 90 pitches in his first start.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Bergmann was cruising through the first five innings, giving up one run against he Philies. Bergmann had a 6-1 lead, but he couldn't get out of the sixth. After getting the leadoff hitter out, Bergmann allowed four consecutive hits and RBI singles to Pat Burrell and Geoff Jenkins to make it a 6-3 game. The Nationals ended up losing the game, 8-7, in 10 innings. On Wednesday, Bergmann will face the Marlins for the 12 time in his career. He is 1-0 with a 5.28 ERA against them.
away_pitcher_note: Despite some rough spots in his first outing, Olsen battled through six innings in a no-decision against the Pirates. The left-hander threw 97 pitches, and he was able to ease the workload of the bullpen, which was overworked in the opening series of the season. Olsen was 2-2 while taking on the Nationals in 2007, and for his career, he is 3-3 with a 4.36 ERA in eight games.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Perez found himself in trouble from the beginning. In the first, Brian Barton led off with a double and Rick Ankiel followed with a two-run homer. By the time he left the game, Perez gave up five runs in four-plus innings and threw 103 pitches. He had problems throwing his fastball for strikes. It didn't help that Perez was pitching with a blister on the middle finger of his left hand. He had the blister since Opening Night against the Braves. Perez is hoping the fingernail grows so he won't put any more pressure on the blister. Perez didn't use the blister as an excuse for his struggles on the mound. He gave the Cardinals credit for scoring runs.
away_pitcher_note: Effective in his last start, Hendrickson tossed 5 1/3 innings, giving up three runs (one earned) on five hits in a win over the Pirates. He struck out four and exited after 88 pitches. Hendrickson has worked at least five innings in both of his starts, and he has shown composure as he works toward battling deeper into games. In his career, Hendrickson has faced the Nationals five times, and he's 0-1 with a 5.40 ERA against them.

home_pitcher_note: Oswalt struggled again with his breaking pitches on April 5 against the Cubs at Wrigley Field, allowing six runs (five earned) on 10 hits over 6 2/3 innings. He felt a slight twinge in his right arm in the middle of the outing but assured his manager and head athletic trainer that the sensation went away in a short time. Oswalt gave up four hits to Derrek Lee, including a solo home run in the third inning. Oswalt faced the Marlins twice last year and allowed just two runs over 12 1/3 innings for a 1.46 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: In all probability, Nolasco will make this start, although it hasn't been made official. The right-hander projects to rejoin the rotation in this spot because Rick VandenHurk was optioned to Double-A following a loss to Pittsburgh on Sunday. Nolasco has made two long-relief stints, last throwing 2 2/3 scoreless innings in relief of VandenHurk. For the season, he has logged 5 2/3 scoreless innings. Before VandenHurk was optioned, Nolasco was going to phase into the fifth starter spot on Sunday at Houston. Now, he likely will slide up two days.

home_pitcher_note: Backe pitched well in his most recent outing on Sunday against the Cubs but had to settle for a no-decision in an eventual Astros loss. He yielded two runs over six innings, reaching the 100-pitch mark for the first time since 2006. Backe allowed 11 baserunners but worked out of several jams, including a bases-loaded situation with none out in the second. He coaxed a double-play ball from Carlos Zambrano and struck out Alfonso Soriano. Backe has faced the Marlins five times in his career and has a 0-1 record with a 2.70 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: The team is exercising patience with the 22-year-old lefty. While he has a world of talent, Miller is definitely struggling. In two starts, he has logged a total of 7 2/3 innings, including a 3 1/3-inning outing at Washington on Monday. Miller was lifted in the fourth inning after he watched a four-run lead shrink to one. He was not involved in the decision on a night he threw 91 pitches. He's struck out nine and walked three while hitting a batter.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez was in line for his first win of the season during the home opener on April 7, but Jose Valverde blew a three-run lead, forcing Rodriguez to take a no-decision. The outing was one of the strongest of Rodriguez's career, and manager Cecil Cooper said the left-hander "grew up a little bit" during that start. He shut out the Cardinals over 7 1/3 innings, allowing three hits while striking out six. He was efficient also, throwing just 91 pitches into the eighth inning.
away_pitcher_note: One of the six players acquired from the Tigers as part of the Dontrelle Willis-Miguel Cabrera trade, the 25-year-old Badenhop will be making his first MLB start. Impressive in Spring Training, Badenhop opened the season at Double-A Carolina, where he made one start before being promoted to replace Rick VandenHurk (optioned to Double-A) in the rotation. In his lone start for Carolina, he gave up one unearned run in 6 1/3 innings. A sinkerball pitcher, Badenhop logged 408 1/3 Minor League innings before getting his first callup.

home_pitcher_note: For a team that needs starters to go deep into games, Olsen is providing some necessary innings. In his last outing, the 24-year-old left-hander worked 7 2/3 innings, following up a six-inning no-decision while facing the Pirates. The 7 2/3 stint was his most since he lasted 7 1/3 innings against the Astros on Aug. 5, 2007. A year ago, Olsen was 0-2 (7.58) in four starts vs. Atlanta. For his career, he is 1-4 (8.54) in eight meetings with Atlanta.
away_pitcher_note: While allowing four earned runs and nine hits in seven innings on Monday night at Coors Field, Jurrjens never lost his composure. After surrendering Matt Holliday's fifth-inning RBI single, he retired seven of the final eight batters he faced. The 22-year-old right-hander has displayed his usual control, recording eight strikeouts and issuing just one unintentional walk in his first 12 1/3 innings this year.

home_pitcher_note: Coming off an economical outing, Hendrickson cruised through seven innings at Washington, allowing one run on three hits. He struck out two, didn't walk a batter, but hit Nick Johnson with a pitch. Still, the left-hander exited after 80 pitches, and provided a much-needed quality start, which eased the stress on the bullpen. Hendrickson has thrown at least five innings in all three of his starts. Lifetime against Atlanta, he is 0-2 with a 4.15 ERA in two games.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson was simply dominant on Friday night while prolonging his career-long success against the Nationals franchise with eight scoreless innings. Now he gets to face a Marlins organization that has also seen him enjoy plenty of success. In the 10 starts he's made against them since the start of 2005, Hudson has surrendered just one earned runs seven times. The veteran right-hander has a 1.87 ERA in five career starts at Dolphin Stadium. The only time he surrendered more than one earned run there came on April 25 last year -- during a game he carried a shutout into the ninth inning.

home_pitcher_note: It was an up-and-down first start of the season for Nolasco, who gave up six runs (five earned) in five innings at Houston. The right-hander was making his first MLB start since May 17, 2007, and his five-inning stint was his most since that day. There were some encouraging signs for Nolasco, as he logged 82 pitches. But in the fifth inning, he gave up two homers. Before joining the rotation, Nolasco threw 5 2/3 scoreless innings out of the bullpen.
away_pitcher_note: While Smoltz's right shoulder might provide discomfort all season, it hasn't proven to be a hindrance while he's allowed just one earned run and combined for 11 innings in his first two starts of the season. The 40-year-old hurler is 14 strikeouts shy of becoming the 16th pitcher in Major League history to reach the 3,000 mark. He is 2-1 with a 2.08 ERA in his past four starts against the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: In his previous start, there was some good news and bad news for Miller. The positive is he worked five full innings for the first time in three starts. The downside? The 22-year-old left-hander was tagged for five runs on eight hits, walking four while striking out six. He did battle, though, after allowing four runs in the second, by tossing three straight scoreless innings. His slider was an effective pitch, but early on his fastball elevated and was hit hard. The five innings were his longest outing of the year. He faces Washington for the second time in 11 days. On April 7, he lasted 3 1/3 innings at Nationals Park, finishing with a no-decision despite allowing six runs.
away_pitcher_note: The last time Redding faced the Marlins was on April 7 and the Nationals lost the game, 10-7. Redding thought some of the damage could have been avoided if he was able to get Alfredo Amezaga out to end the third inning. With runners on second and third, two outs and the Nationals leading by one, Redding was supposed to pitch around Amezaga and go after pitcher Andrew Miller instead. But Amezaga took a 2-2 pitch and doubled to right field, driving in two runs. Miller ended up reaching on an infield single and scoring on Hanley Ramirez's three-run homer, to make it a 7-3 game. Redding lasted four innings and gave up seven runs, only one being scored as earned because of the two errors.

home_pitcher_note: Now with two big league appearances and one start under his belt, Badenhop will make his first home start. The 25-year-old right-hander will face the Nationals -- the team he debuted against on April 9, when he tossed a scoreless ninth. In his start in Houston, Badenhop worked into the sixth inning, but he didn't record an out. So in five-plus frames, he was credited with four runs on seven hits. Badenhop was victimized by the long ball, giving up two homers. Still, he showed signs that he could be a welcomed addition to the rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Hill, who hasn't pitched in the Majors yet this season because of tightness in his right forearm, is hoping to make his first appearance. He pitched six innings for Triple-A Columbus on Sunday and gave up six runs (five earned) on nine hits against Charlotte. Hill was cruising the first three innings, but he then gave up a combined six runs in the fourth and fifth innings.

home_pitcher_note: With each start, Olsen is blossoming into what many envisioned out of him when he broke in as a rookie in 2006. Olsen comes off an efficient and impressive win over the Braves, tossing seven shutout innings. He didn't walk a batter, and exited with 84 pitches. On April 9 at Washington, Olsen threw 120 pitches in 7 2/3 innings in a victory. The last time Olsen started without issuing a walk, before facing the Braves, was on Aug. 22, 2007, against the Cardinals. He ended up losing that day.
away_pitcher_note: Perez had another strong outing last Tuesday, but it wasn't good enough as the Nationals lost to the Mets. Perez pitched six innings, giving up two runs on six hits. His only blemish occurred in the first inning, when David Wright hit a home run with Ryan Church on first. Perez has given the Nationals three good outings thus far, but he doesn't have any wins to show for it.

home_pitcher_note: To put it bluntly, Morris simply has shown very little command with his fastball in any of his three starts this season. He's rarely fooling hitters (evidenced by the 26 hits and 13 runs he's given up in 16 2/3 innings this season), and he has not been able to avoid the big inning in any of his three starts this season. Morris faced the Marlins earlier this month, allowing four runs (three earned) and eight hits in five innings of work.
away_pitcher_note: Aside from a seven-inning outing at Washington, three of Hendrickson's four starts have been either five- or five-plus-inning appearances. He comes off a 5 1/3-inning performance against the Braves, where he allowed three runs (two earned). Hendrickson is pitching to contact, as he has nine strikeouts in 22 2/3 innings. On April 5, the left-hander beat the Pirates in Miami, giving up three runs (one earned) in 5 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Some bad first-inning bounces and a costly error rattled Maholm from the onset of his previous start and put him in a hole from which he would never climb out. He made it through five innings, but allowed a career-high 11 hits as well as six runs (four earned). Maholm's issues could be summed up in two words: poor command. His first start of the season came against the Marlins, when Florida's Mike Jacobs ruined the outing with a fifth-inning grand slam that would chase Maholm from the game. The lefty did, however, strike out nine Marlins in that game.
away_pitcher_note: The Braves uncorked on Nolasco for four homers in 4 2/3 innings in the right-hander's last start. The 25-year-old actually was one pitch away from getting out of big trouble in that game. Down by three in the fifth inning, he had two outs and an 0-2 count on Chipper Jones, who then connected on a homer to right. It sparked three straight blasts off Nolasco, who didn't last the inning. After opening the season in the bullpen, this will be Nolasco's third start. Lifetime against the Pirates, he is 1-1 with a 1.29 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: The versatile, rubber-armed right-hander may have earned himself another round in the rotation with a strong effort in a surprise start Friday night against the Dodgers. Pitching for the fourth time in six days, Bennett didn't get a decision, but was superb, shutting out the Dodgers on two hits in a season-high 4 2/3 innings. He has struggled in three career appearances against Florida.
away_pitcher_note: What was shaping up as a disastrous last outing became a no-decision for Miller. The 22-year-old gave up three runs in the first inning against the Nationals. He labored, throwing 34 total pitches in the first, with 20 pitches out of the strike zone. By working five innings, he matched his season high. Yet, they remain tough innings as he works deep into counts. He exited with 90 pitches against the Nationals. Miller has had back-to-back five-inning games.

home_pitcher_note: James found success on Saturday in his second emergency start of the young season, throwing five solid innings while allowing only one run -- on an Andruw Jones homer -- and four hits. Although allowing the leadoff man to reach in four of the five innings, he frustrated Dodgers hitters, who were 0-for-4 with runners in scoring position. James hopes to frustrate the Marlins, against whom he is 3-1 lifetime, with a 1.19 ERA. Last year he was 2-0 with a 0.66 ERA (one earned run in 13 innings) against Florida.
away_pitcher_note: Throwing strikes typically isn't a concern with Badenhop. It happened to be a problem, however, in his last outing. The 25-year-old, making his second big league start, walked five while allowing three runs to the Nationals. Because he rolled up 80 pitches, he was out of the game after three innings. He wasn't involved in the decision. In his first start, on April 13 at Houston, he lasted five-plus innings in a loss. This will be his second road start and fourth appearance overall. He threw a scoreless inning of relief at Washington on April 9.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo's return to the rotation was well worth the wait, even if he didn't get a win. The 22-year-old underwent knee surgery in Spring Training, but was sharp in his season debut despite a dreary Cincinnati afternoon, holding the Reds to a run on four hits in seven innings. His return could not have come at a better time for the Brewers, who are holding their breath while ace Ben Sheets rests a sore right arm. Gallardo was especially good at Miller Park last season, going 5-2 with a 2.77 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Olsen remains the team's most effective starter, as he comes off his third straight start that lasted at least seven innings. The 24-year-old beat the Nationals in his latest outing, giving up one run -- a homer to Austin Kearns -- in seven innings. Olsen allowed just three hits, and carried a no-hitter into the fifth before Kearns opened with the homer. For his career, Olsen is 1-1 with a 3.44 ERA in three games against the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: Villanueva faced the Cardinals for the second time in five days, and the second outing was certainly was an improvement over the first, when he needed 45 pitches to escape the first inning (17 of those were spent on Cardinals outfielder Rick Ankiel) and was finished after the fourth. In his most recent start, Villanueva limited the Cards to two runs on three hits in seven innings but did walk four batters, two of them with two outs in the third inning, before Troy Glaus cashed in with a two-run double. Villanueva did not allow a run in three appearances against the Marlins last season, all in relief.
away_pitcher_note: After a poor outing on Opening Day, Hendrickson has been one of the hottest starters in baseball during his past four starts. Hendrickson has won each of them, allowing only seven earned runs and 22 hits in 25 2/3 innings. He worked eight strong innings his previous time out during a 10-4 win against Pittsburgh Monday.

home_pitcher_note: Parra was down on himself after allowing three runs in five innings of a no-decision against the Cardinals on Tuesday, even though he was in line for his second Major League win before second baseman Rickie Weeks botched a double-play relay. Parra hasn't pitched past the sixth inning in any of his four starts and hasn't pitched into the sixth since his season debut. He isn't commanding any of his four pitches and said after his last outing, "I'm off. I'm very inconsistent right now. I'm in a rut. It shouldn't be that difficult."
away_pitcher_note: One out away from escaping trouble and being in line for the win, Nolasco gave up four straight hits in the sixth inning of his last start. The end result was a disappointing loss on a night when he actually pitched his best game. Nolasco allowed three runs -- all with two outs and no one on base to start with -- in a loss at Pittsburgh. Otherwise, he had a pretty strong night. Nolasco logged his first quality start of the season -- three runs in six innings. The Marlins ended up losing 3-2. The right-hander logged a season-high 90 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Nothing is coming easy for Miller, but the 22-year-old is taking some small steps in getting better. In his last start -- his first win as a Marlin -- he labored to get through the first inning and allowed an unearned run at Atlanta. Yet, he regrouped, and despite yielding nine hits, he made it through five innings with his team ahead, 3-2. Miller tossed a season-most 98 pitches, with 55 for strikes. Seven times with Detroit last year, Miller reached the 100-pitch plateau, with his career high being 111 on July 23, at the White Sox in 4 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lowe left Wednesday night's start against the Diamondbacks after five innings and 67 pitches with a tight elbow, but after a preliminary exam was still listed to pitch the opener of this series in Florida. He was 0-2 against the Marlins last year and is 5-4 lifetime.

home_pitcher_note: Steady progress is the best way to define Olsen's first month. While he wasn't involved in the decision in his previous start, he strung together 7 1/3 scoreless innings while facing the Brewers at Miller Park. Without his best stuff, he allowed the leadoff batter to reach in seven of the eight innings he opened. And for the first time in 73 career starts, he failed to strike out a batter. Olsen has worked at least seven innings in four straight games, and he has allowed just one run in his last 21 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: For the second consecutive start, Billingsley showed flashes of brilliance, but that was not enough to win. He was overpowering enough to strike out a career-high 12 in six innings against the Diamondbacks, but he also was charged with five runs. He was particularly hurt by a two-run homer from Jeff Salazar, but also allowed the go-ahead run to score on a wild pitch. He's 2-0 lifetime against the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: The silver lining for the 25-year-old in his last start was he battled through five innings after allowing five runs in the first. Basically, Badenhop was his own long-relief pitcher, tossing three scoreless innings. But the damage was done in the first two, as he gave up six runs in a loss at Atlanta. From the third inning on, however, he gave up two hits and retired eight of his last 10 batters. The Marlins are looking for steady progress from Badenhop, who will be making his third start in the Majors.
away_pitcher_note: Hiroki Kuroda got a no-decision against the Rockies, but it wasn't pretty. He allowed five runs on nine hits over six innings and was so off with his mechanics that he started pitching out of the stretch in mid-game. Since his effortless debut in San Diego, Kuroda has had to work hard in his starts.

home_pitcher_note: Basically, Hendrickson deserved better in his last outing. A couple of errors cost him an unearned run in what turned to being a no-decision at Milwaukee. Still, he had a quality start, giving up two earned runs in six innings. The 6-foot-9 former NBA player also had his first career triple, and he scored a run. In his last two starts, at the plate, Hendrickson had a triple, double and single. He now takes on the Padres, a team that he is 1-2 (1.83) against lifetime in nine games.
away_pitcher_note: Germano allowed six runs on six hits and two walks over five innings in his last start for a no-decision against the Diamondbacks. After allowing just four runs, three earned, in his first three starts this season, Germano has allowed 16 in his last two outings. Germano, who fanned a season-high five batters in his last start, has never faced the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: A number of encouraging signs surfaced in Nolasco's last outing, a no-decision at Milwaukee. After laboring in the first inning -- loading the bases without yielding a hit -- he surrendered one run. That's all he allowed as he battled through five innings, and he was in position to nail down the win, but ended up without a decision. The 25-year-old has now logged 26 1/3 innings on the season. That's significant when you keep in mind he was limited to 21 1/3 innings at the MLB level in 2007 because he was on the DL most of the year with elbow inflammation.
away_pitcher_note: Peavy was not able to win his fourth game of the season, though he didn't pitch poorly against Arizona on April 27. Peavy allowed two runs on a home run by Chris Snyder but little else, allowing just four hits over seven innings with three walks and nine strikeouts. The defending NL Cy Young Award winner was upstaged that day by Brandon Webb, who improved to 6-0. Peavy was 1-1 with a 1.93 ERA in two starts against the Marlins last season and took a no-hitter into the seventh inning of a game in Miami. He allowed one hit with 10 strikeouts in that game.

home_pitcher_note: Early inning struggles have hindered Miller for much of his six starts this season. In his last start, a no-decision with the Dodgers, Miller allowed six runs on nine hits while walking two. In 25 2/3 innings this season, Miller has allowed 26 earned runs. It was his shortest outing of the season. Something the team is monitoring is some tendinitis in Miller's right knee. It bothered him during his days with the Tigers.
away_pitcher_note: Maddux was unsuccessful in his third attempt at career victory No. 350 on April 29 in Philadelphia, though he certainly held his own against the power-packed Phillies lineup. Maddux allowed three runs on eight hits with one walk and two strikeouts. He mixed his pitches well and had good command of his fastball, keeping the ball far away from the Phillies' top sluggers, Chase Utley and Ryan Howard. Maddux allowed two runs on six hits entering the seventh inning, when he got in trouble. Still, it was the fourth time this season he's worked into or past the seventh inning, something he didn't always do in 2007.

home_pitcher_note: After four straight starts of lasting at least seven innings, Olsen had a rough outing on Wednesday. The lefty also suffered his first loss, giving up four runs in a season-low five innings against the Dodgers. It also was the first time in six starts the Marlins lost with Olsen on the mound. Olsen now gets to face the Brewers for the second time in three starts. On April 25 at Miller Park, he gutted out 7 1/3 innings of scoreless ball. He yielded four hits that day, and for the first time in his career he didn't log a strikeout.
away_pitcher_note: The Soup was cold at Wrigley Field. Suppan surrendered 11 runs for the first time in his career, though three were unearned, and he coughed up 11 Cubs hits without escaping the fourth inning. It was a sour end to what had been a good month for Suppan, who entered the game 1-0 with a 3.48 ERA despite a no-decision in New York on April 13 in which he was charged with six runs in four innings. Suppan missed the Marlins when they visited Miller Park last week but he's 4-3 with a 3.50 ERA against them in 11 career matchups.

home_pitcher_note: At a time the Marlins needed a starter to step up, Badenhop came through in his last start. While he wasn't involved in the decision -- so he's still searching for his first big league win -- the 25-year-old turned in his first quality start, allowing three runs in six innings against the Dodgers. His six innings and six strikeouts both were personal highs in his five MLB appearances. A sinkerball pitcher, the right-hander induced eight groundball outs to four in the air. This will be his first outing against Milwaukee.
away_pitcher_note: Bush was recalled to replace injured right-hander Yovani Gallardo, who was lost to a serious knee injury and might need surgery. Bush was demoted to Triple-A Nashville a week earlier when Ben Sheets was deemed clear of a minor arm injury, and took a no-decision in his only start for the Sounds. He allowed three runs, only one of which was earned, on three hits while striking out seven batters over six innings against Colorado Springs. Bush is 1-1 with a 5.73 ERA in two starts against the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: A year ago, the lefty went 4-8 with the Dodgers. In his last start, a seven-inning outing against the Padres, he collected his fifth win of the young season. Hendrickson remains economical with his pitches, tossing just 81 in beating San Diego. The Marlins are 5-2 in his seven starts. And since losing to Johan Santana and the Mets on Opening Day, he hasn't given up more than three earned runs in six straight outings. This will be his second start in three appearances against the Brewers. At Miller Park on April 26, he gave up two earned runs in six innings in a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Villanueva retired 12 of the first 13 Astros hitters he faced on Friday but then surrendered hits to eight of the next 10. Four of those hits were home runs, including three in a row to sluggers Miguel Tejada, Lance Berkman and Carlos Lee as a 4-0 Brewers lead slipped away. None of the those three pitches were any good, said manager Ned Yost, who has been frustrated by Villanueva's propensity for allowing quick strikes by opponents. He allowed two runs in six innings against the Marlins at Miller Park on the Brewers' last homestand and took a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Manager Manny Acta has often said that Redding gives him peace of mind when he is on the mound. The skipper has a reason to relax. Two years removed from shoulder surgery, Redding arguably has been the most consistent starter on the team since the second half of the 2007 season. Last Sunday afternoon was no different as Redding had another quality outing and helped the Nationals defeat the Pirates, 5-2. He lasted 6 1/3 innings and gave up just one run on six hits, striking out five batters and not allowing a walk.
away_pitcher_note: Ricky Nolasco threw five straight balls to start Saturday's game against the San Diego Padres. Nolasco regained his command, but not his best stuff, and allowed six runs in a 7-2 loss. He finished with two walks and two strikeouts, and threw 84 pitches, 55 for strikes. The first three runs all scored with two outs. After allowing three runs in the first two innings, he did battle back to pitch a scoreless third and fourth frame before allowing three more in the fifth.

home_pitcher_note: O'Connor will be making his first start since going 3-8 with a 4.80 ERA in 20 starts with the Nats in the 2006 season. O'Connor has previously pitched against the Marlins twice -- both times in '06 -- going 0-1 with a 14.21 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Maybe it wasn't the defining breakthrough game for Miller, but it certainly was significant. In his last start, the 6-foot-6 left-hander was on the winning end in a matchup against Padres legend Greg Maddux. Miller worked a season-high six innings, and scattered four hits and two runs. He walked two and struck out two. Finding consistency is Miller's biggest struggle right now. In beating Maddux, Miller threw 88 pitches, 55 for strikes. This will be his third meeting against the Nationals. He hasn't factored into a decision in his first two tries. Miller last faced Washington on April 18 at home, where he gave up three runs in five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Hill followed his best outing of the season with an inconsistent performance Tuesday at Houston. Hill pitched 5 1/3 innings, giving up eight hits and three runs, keeping the Nationals in the game. He walked four, including the pitcher, which knocked him out of the game. Hill led 3-2 going into the bottom of the fifth and retired the first two hitters on grounders back to the mound. But he allowed three straight singles by the Astros, the last a bloop by Hunter Pence, to tie the game and take away the chance of collecting his first win of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Olsen is coming off the longest outing of his three-year career after going 8 2/3 scoreless innings while giving up two hits and striking out eight to get the win against the Brewers on Tuesday. The win was a much-needed bounce-back outing for Olsen, who had his worst start of the season when he gave up four runs in five innings in a loss to the Dodgers on April 30. Olsen is 2-0 against the Nationals this season, giving up five runs in 14 total innings while striking out five.

home_pitcher_note: Harang has gotten little run support and has the semi-consolation of being the best 1-5 pitcher in baseball. He threw seven innings and allowed three earned runs in a 3-0 loss to the Cubs Tuesday. In Harang's five losses, the Reds have scored two or fewer runs four times. He's worked seven quality starts in eight games and is among the National League leaders in strikeouts with 47.
away_pitcher_note: It took five starts, but Badenhop now can celebrate his first MLB win. The 25-year-old, one of the pieces in the Dontrelle Willis/Miguel Cabrera trade, was victorious in his last outing, beating the Brewers at home. In 5 2/3 innings, he yielded two runs -- both coming on Rickie Weeks' homer. Badenhop had a career most seven strikeouts, and his control was good, as he walked just one. It marked Badenhop's second straight strong outing. On May 1, in a no-decision, he logged a career most six innings, giving up three runs.

home_pitcher_note: Volquez pitched seven scoreless innings in the Reds' 9-0 win over the Cubs and gave up four hits and six walks while tying a career high with 10 strikeouts. He has yet to allow more than one earned run in any of his seven starts. Meanwhile, it's good bet that the Reds' bats will participate big when Volquez pitches. In his five wins, the team has scored 44 runs, including three games with nine or more runs.
away_pitcher_note: Marlins manager Fredi Gonzalez said Hendrickson has earned the right to try to win games. Unfortunately for Hendrickson, the lefty was a bit uncharacteristic with his pitch count during his last start Thursday against the Brewers. Hendrickson, who usually conserves his pitches pretty well, threw over 60 pitches through three innings and exited with 109 after 4 1/3 innings -- being unable to log the required five innings to be eligible to get a win. Still, Hendrickson goes into his start against the Reds having given up three runs or less in seven straight starts.

home_pitcher_note: Arroyo was 0-3 with a 7.56 ERA after a loss to Houston on April 23, but he has pitched reasonably well in his last three starts and has won two straight to get his ERA to 7.14. On Saturday, in New York, he struck out a season-high nine, yielded just one run on four hits over eight strong innings and retired the last 13 Mets he faced in a 7-1 victory. He said he changed his routine between starts a bit and has added a few miles per hour to his fastball. He's 0-1 with a 4.41 ERA in one career start against the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: There were things to build on for Nolasco is his last start. First off, the right-hander was able to close out innings better than he had in previous starts. The end result was he yielded one run on four hits over six innings in a victory at Washington. This is his second start on the road trip. The six innings at Washington matched his season most, previously done in a loss at Pittsburgh on April 22. Nolasco is 0-1 with a 9.00 ERA lifetime against the Reds.

home_pitcher_note: More polish is starting to come with each outing for Miller. The 6-foot-6 lefty has now won three straight decisions. They've come over a stretch of four starts. He last suffered a defeat on April 12 at Houston. In his last outing, his best of the season, he matched his career high with seven innings. He didn't allow a run, and he scattered two hits in beating the Nationals. Miller also matched his career high for strikeouts, seven, and he logged 103 pitches, another high.
away_pitcher_note: Tomko couldn't repeat the sharpness he showed in seven shutout innings against the hard-hitting Angels in his previous start. Facing the Orioles last Saturday, Tomko gave up six runs on nine hits in 5 1/3 innings and absorbed his fourth loss. After surrendering a three-run homer in the first inning, he occupied himself during a nearly two-hour rain delay by studying videotapes of more successful games and that helped when he returned. A former National Leaguer, Tomko is 7-2 in his career against the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: Olsen struggled with velocity and effectiveness in his last outing, a six-inning no-decision at Washington. The lefty gave up four runs on six hits. He was particularly hurt by two home runs. It was the first time all year he had allowed more than one homer in a game. On a chilly 62-degree day in Washington, his fastball rarely reached as high as 87 mph. Still, he battled through six innings, keeping his team within striking distance. At home, he is 3-1 with a 2.41 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Bannister, a self-proclaimed streaky pitcher, trusts that he's launched a hot one with eight shutout innings against the Orioles on Sunday. He gave up just two hits and two walks and no one reached second base. The victory ended a four-loss skid after Bannister had opened the season 3-0. He made an unspecified adjustment that helped him keep his secondary pitches from getting too high and hittable. He'd have tried for a complete game except he admitted his legs were getting a bit shaky so Joakim Soria finished up.

home_pitcher_note: If for a little bit better luck, Badenhop would have been in line for a win in his last start -- a no-decision in Cincinnati. But a throwing error led to an unearned run, and his own wild pitch allowed another run to score. Still, the right-hander met the requirements for a quality start -- three earned runs (or less) over six (or more) innings. His six-innings matched a career high. And in four straight starts, he worked at least five innings. Advancing deeper into games is his next hurdle.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke pitched well enough to win last Tuesday night against the Tigers but left after six innings with the score tied. He threw 100 pitches and gave up nine hits. With the bases loaded and two outs in the sixth, he really revved up and struck out Ivan Rodriguez to keep the score 2-2 and that's been typical of his season. His ERA remained under 2.00 and was second in the American League. He's been so effective that his six-inning stint marked just the second time that he's failed to go at least seven innings in eight starts.

home_pitcher_note: For the second straight start, Hendrickson found himself throwing a lot of pitches when he lost to the Reds on May 13. During his previous start, Hendrickson ended up throwing 109 pitches through 4 1/3 innings. The only difference was he won that game -- allowing just one run to the Brewers on May 8. Against the Reds, Hendrickson -- who went 2-for-2 with a run scored at the plate -- gave up four runs in five innings and threw 93 pitches. During his outing, Hendrickson got into three-ball counts six different times and tossed 33 pitches in the second inning alone.
away_pitcher_note: Owings will be starting on an extra day's rest and is coming off six scoreless innings against the Rockies that earned him his first victory in four starts. He has gone six innings in six of eight games this year, and has never lasted fewer than five frames this season. Last year's National League Silver Slugger at his position, Owings is batting .357 with five runs and three RBIs in 28 at-bats.

home_pitcher_note: Everything seemed to be working out great for Nolasco during his last start on Wednesday against the Reds. Everything until the fifth inning. As has been his problem for most of the season, Nolasco was unable to close out an inning. After pitching four scoreless frames and retiring the first two hitters in the fifth, the righty surrendered two runs on three hits and exited the game after throwing 97 pitches through five full innings. Nolasco gave up five total hits and struck out four but did not actor in the decision.
away_pitcher_note: Webb won his only start against Florida last year when he tossed seven scoreless innings. In his career against the Marlins, he is 3-3 with a 5.05 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Miller is coming off a loss he probably doesn't deserve. The 6-foot-6 righty gave up four runs in five innings during his last start against the Royals on May 16. But two of those runs were unearned as the Marlins lost, 7-6. Miller -- who also gave up five hits, struck out six and walked three -- seemed to get out of a bases-loaded, two-out jam in the fourth inning. But shortstop Hanley Ramirez threw wide to first base, allowing a run to score, and the inning to prolong -- an inning that later saw Miller walk in a run. But after the game, Miller was most disappointed with the two runs he gave up in the first inning. On the year, Miller sports an 8.00 ERA in the first inning.
away_pitcher_note: Haren has lasted at least six innings in nine of his 10 starts this year. In his last start, he picked up a 4-3 win over the Tigers last Friday night at Chase Field. Haren allowed three runs on six hits over seven innings. The right-hander pitched even better in the start before that, but took the loss when Ted Lilly outpitched him in a 3-1 loss to the Cubs at Wrigley Field.

home_pitcher_note: Scott Olsen allowed three runs and walked five in a no-decision in his last outing against Kansas City on Saturday. The left-hander also allowed seven hits, and his velocity -- a concern in his previous outing -- did not top 88. He walked two batters in each of the first and third innings and struck out three batters total. Manager Fredi Gonzalez was happy with the performance, though, and said he would "take that from Olsen every time." Olsen has one win in his last five starts, but has pitched at least six innings in eight out of nine starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Zito was sloppy yet effective against the White Sox in his last start. Half of the 28 batters he faced reached base safely as he yielded eight hits and walked six in five innings. But somehow Zito allowed only two runs, though it wasn't enough to prevent yet another defeat. Zito will try to avoid enduring the same fate as Rod Beck, the last Giant to compile an 0-9 record -- all in relief -- in 1996. Zito is 1-0 with a 4.91 ERA in two career starts against Florida.

home_pitcher_note: Hendrickson knew going into his start against the D-backs -- the team that boasted the Major League's best ERA going into its series opener against the Marlins on Tuesday -- that runs were not going to come easy for his offense. But Hendrickson ended up giving his Fish just enough by going five innings while giving up one run on four hits and striking out seven. The outing, which saw the 33-year-old retire the first nine hitters he faced, gave Hendrickson his sixth win in his last seven decisions.
away_pitcher_note: Misch remains winless in 24 big league appearances spanning three seasons, including eight starts. The Giants haven't won a single one of his starts, although they're averaging only 2.25 runs per game behind him. Misch performed respectably at Colorado last Monday, yielding three runs and five hits in 5 1/3 innings, as he received no decision. Misch has faced Florida only once, pitching a scoreless one-third of an inning in relief.

Cain experienced a strange afternoon last Sunday against the White Sox. He surrendered four home runs, including three in a span of seven batters, after no-hitting Chicago for 4 1/3 innings. The Giants proceeded to lose, 13-8, as Cain was charged with six runs in seven innings. Cain has recorded only four quality starts in 10 outings, while the Giants have posted a 4-6 record behind him.

home_pitcher_note: After two effective starts, one in which he made folks think a no-hitter was possible, Pelfrey endured a poor outing against the Braves Wednesday night. He faced 24 batters in four innings, 12 of them reached base and six of them -- a season high for him -- scored. Pelfrey now has lost five straight decisions.
away_pitcher_note: Nolasco's last start is probably one he'll remember for a long time to come. Against the Diamondbacks on Wednesday, Nolasco found himself matched up against the hottest pitcher in baseball at that point, Brandon Webb. Webb was 9-0 in nine starts coming into the game, but Nolasco pitched seven innings of one-run ball to give Webb his only blemish of the season. The 6-foot-2 righty allowed just three hits and struck out seven. It was Nolasco's longest outing since Aug. 13, 2006, at Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: The Braves swung at pitches early in the count when they beat Santana in Atlanta Thursday. That kept his pitch count down -- 90 in seven innings -- but Santana allowed a career-high 12 hits in those six innings. His winning streak ended at four games. The Mets had won his previous six starts.
away_pitcher_note: One day after turning 23, Miller turned in the start of his life. En route to the Marlins' fourth sweep of the season, the 6-foot-6 lefty turned in seven full innings of shutout ball while striking out a career-high nine hitters. Miller allowed just one runner to get in scoring position and dropped his ERA .85 points to help the Marlins sweep the Diamondbacks, who came into the series with the National League's best record.

home_pitcher_note: Perez struggled through five innings and two batters Friday night at Coors Field, walking a career-high eight and yielding four runs while giving up six hits, including a two-run homer. He has allowed five home runs in his last four games. Though he kept the Mets in the game and left with the score tied, earning a no-decision in the 13-inning defeat, he is in a rut on the road, going 1-2 with a 5.92 ERA in his last four starts away from Queens. He has not fared much better at home, going 1-1 with a 5.60 ERA at Shea this season.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off his worst outing of the season, Olsen was lifted after 3 1/3 innings and 81 pitches in a loss to the Giants last Friday. The left-hander hadn't gone shorter than five innings in his previous nine starts. Olsen was tagged for two home runs, but his fastball velocity reached 89 on a couple of occasions. That's the hardest he's thrown in a few outings. Lifetime against the Mets, he is 1-2 with a 3.94 ERA in eight games.

home_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Myers lost his fourth straight start as he went six innings and allowed four runs on eight hits in a 4-3 defeat at Houston. Myers threw a season-high four walks and tied his season low with only two strikeouts. Myers has five losses and two no-decisions in his past seven starts and hasn't won since April 17 against the Astros in Philadelphia. For his career, he's 5-7 with a 5.01 ERA in 25 games against Florida.
away_pitcher_note: On Sunday against the Giants, Mark Hendrickson allowed five earned runs, while throwing 97 pitches -- 56 for strikes. He struck out five and walked two, but benefited from four home runs hit by the Marlins to pick up his seventh victory. Hendrickson didn't have his best stuff -- he scattered nine hits -- but did battle out of several jams, including a first-and-third jam with one out in the fifth. Hendrickson struck out Rich Aurilia and Travis Denker to end that threat.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels saw his ERA jump from 2.61, which was fourth in the NL, to 3.18 in his last start as he allowed a season-high six runs on seven hits and a walk. Hamels, who was third in the league in strikeouts with 65 entering the game, also didn't record a strikeout in the four innings, his shortest outing of the season. Against Florida, he has a 2-2 record with a 4.13 ERA in four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Considering his history against the Mets, Nolasco will take the outcome of his last start. It was a battle, but the right-hander gave up three runs in five innings, while scattering nine hits. Entering that game, Nolasco had a 1-3 career mark with the Mets, including a 10.80 ERA. Still, Nolasco was able to scratch out his fourth win. Nolasco has won three straight decisions, over a four-start span. His best performance came on May 21, when he yielded one run on three hits in a win over Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: Moyer lasted seven innings in his most recent start, against Colorado on May 26. The left-hander allowed four runs, striking out seven and walking only one. Moyer allowed a three-run home run to Ryan Spilborghs in the first inning, but was able to bounce back and hold the Rockies to one run through the ensuing six frames. He has enjoyed considerable run support lately -- in his last three starts, the Phillies have pounded opponents for 42 total runs.
away_pitcher_note: Surrendering two-out runs was problematic for Miller in his last start. Three of the four runs he allowed against the Mets at Shea Stadium came with two outs. For Miller, the loss at the Mets marked his shortest outing (4 2/3 innings) in five starts. He also had two strikeouts, which was off the pace of his personal most nine in a May 22 win over Arizona. The 23-year-old lefty still has won four of his last six decisions.

home_pitcher_note: Jo-Jo Reyes pitched the best game of his young career on Wednesday against the Brewers. The 23-year-old left-hander struck out nine and allowed two hits in seven innings, but was dealt the loss. Reyes walked J.J. Hardy on four straight pitches to start the eighth inning, and when reliever Blaine Boyer allowed a two-out RBI triple to Richie Weeks two batters later, Reyes' stellar outing was erased. Reyes had been bothered by a blister on the index finger on his left hand, but it was healed by Wednesday's start.
away_pitcher_note: Reduced velocity continues to make Olsen have to struggle to log innings. In his last outing, a five-inning affair at Shea Stadium against the Mets, the left-hander gutted out five innings, giving up four runs on six hits. He was not involved in the decision. He struck out three, and allowed two home runs -- both on 85 mph fastballs. He's now given up four home runs in his last two starts, which total 8 1/3 innings. Olsen has not thrown more than six innings in his last four starts, or since he went 8 2/3 innings on May 6 in a win over the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: Campillo has allowed just one earned run and nine hits in the 15 innings that he’s totaled since becoming a starter on May 20.  The 29-year-old right-hander has shown precise control and the ability to succeed without overpowering stuff.  The fifth-inning homer he surrendered on Thursday was the first run he allowed in a span of 20 1/3 innings.  Campillo has battled a blister on his right middle finger that has caused him to exit the game early in both of his past two starts.
away_pitcher_note: A couple of off-days meant the team could tinker with its rotation. Each time, Badenhop was the starter pushed back. As things shook out, the right-hander ended up going 11 days between appearances. When he threw 1 1/3 innings of relief on Friday at Philadelphia, it was his first appearance since a May 18 start, where he tossed three innings in a loss to the Royals. The first batter Badenhop faced was Ryan Howard, who homered. He then retired the next four he faced. This will be his eighth MLB start, and 10th appearance. On April 24, the 25-year-old gave up six runs in five innings in a loss to Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: After allowing a season-high six walks and tying a season high with six earned runs in his last start, Tom Glavine gave up two runs and five hits in six innings Friday against the Reds, but earned a no-decision. He struck out five and walked two, and the only runs he gave up came in a two-run sixth inning. Glavine has been inconsistent this season. In one start, he will look out of sorts and miss with his location on the corners. In another start, he has pinpoint precision and gives up nothing more than harmless singles.
away_pitcher_note: His last start was a forgetful one. Hendrickson allowed a career-high 10 runs (all earned), which matched a Marlins franchise record now reached four times. The Phillies jumped on the 6-foot-9 lefty, slapping out seven hits and two homers. He had won two straight decisions and seven of eight decisions before his season-short 3 2/3-inning outing. On April 16, Hendrickson beat the Braves, giving up three runs (two earned) in 5 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Jurrjens struggled with his control posted his shortest outing of the season when he lasted just 4 1/3 innings against the Reds on Saturday. He gave up six runs on nine hits with a season-high six walks and two strikeouts in receiving a no decision. He developed a blister on his throwing hand in his previous start against the Diamondbacks on May 26. Jurrjens also became the 383rd different pitcher to give up a home run to Ken Griffey Jr. when he gave up Griffey's 599th in the first inning. He gave up another to Brandon Phillips in the next at-bat, marking the first time in his career that he's given up back-to-back home runs. Jurrjens lost his only start against the Marlins this season on April 15. He gave up two runs on four hits with three walks and five strikeouts in an 8-5 loss.
away_pitcher_note: At a time the Marlins needed a quality start, the right-hander delivered. Nolasco stepped up in a big in his last start, tossing 6 2/3 solid innings in a win at Philadelphia. The victory snapped a three-game losing streak, and quieted a red-hot Philadelphia offense. Nolasco yielded two runs on four hits, and he struck out five. The right-hander has now won four straight decisions since his last defeat on May 3 to the Padres. On April 17, Nolasco faced the Braves in Florida. He came out on the losing end of a 8-0 shutout. In 4 2/3 innings, he yielded six runs.

home_pitcher_note: Miller was able to get through five innings in his last start, a no-decision at Philadelphia. It was a struggle against one of the most dangerous lineups in the game. The left-hander got into some trouble by walking four, but he allowed three runs (two earned) on three hits. He tossed 88 pitches, and exited with a 5-3 lead. Still he wasn't involved in the decision. Miller has logged at least five innings in five of his last six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Cueto pitched five no-hit innings in his last start, a victory over the Braves on Sunday. He recorded his sixth quality start, allowing two runs on four hits in seven innings with a walk and three strikeouts. It marked his longest outing since April 24, but his 100 pitches were the fewest he's thrown since a May 16 start against the Indians. Cueto has 62 strikeouts on the season compared to just 20 walks and has never faced the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: It may not have been a masterpiece, but there were a number of encouraging signs in Olsen's most recent outing. In a no-decision at Atlanta, he worked six innings (his longest start in three appearances). In terms of velocity, his fastball touched 89 mph on a couple of occasions, up gradually. While he allowed two home runs for the third straight start, he did strike out four and scatter four hits. Overall, the outing was a step in the right direction to regaining the touch the left-hander showed in April. Olsen's last win was on May 6, a span six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Arroyo lasted just 4 1/3 innings and gave up five runs on 10 hits with two walks and four strikeouts in a 5-4 loss to Philadelphia on Monday. He threw 88 pitches and gave up three home runs -- the second most he's given up all season in his shortest start since lasting just 1 1/3 against the Braves on May 4. Arroyo's only start against the Marlins this season came on May 14, when he gave up no runs on five hits through seven innings but received a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Tucker is a hard-throwing 21-year-old righty who was one of the Marlins' five first-round picks in 2005. He is the first of the group to make his MLB debut. He was in the big league spring camp the past two years.
away_pitcher_note: Harang stretched his winless streak to four and continued to get very little in the way of run support in his last start, a 3-2 loss to the Phillies on Tuesday. He pitched six-plus innings and gave up three runs on nine hits with a walk and four strikeouts. He threw 113 pitches, which marks the second-most he's thrown all season. Harang's last victory came in his only appearance against the Marlins this season on May 12. He pitched seven innings and gave up four runs on four hits with two walks and four strikeouts, and despite giving up three early home runs, managed to come away with the win.

home_pitcher_note: Not overwhelming but still solid best describes Hendrickson's last outing. At Atlanta on June 4, the left-hander allowed four runs in six innings. He scattered nine hits, walked two (one intentionally). He wasn't involved in the decision. Three of the four runs came on two-out hits. But the six innings were his most since working seven on May 2 in a win over San Diego. He had gone five straight starts without working more than five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Volquez continued his streak of brilliance with seven scoreless innings against the Phillies on Wednesday. The 24-year-old allowed just two hits and two walks with eight strikeouts, lowering his Major League-best ERA to 1.32. Volquez threw 113 pitches -- the second-most he has thrown this season -- 69 of them strikes. His two hits allowed tied for the second-fewest he's given up and the seven innings tied for his longest start. It's the fourth time Volquez has lasted seven innings in a start. His only start against the Marlins this season came in a May 13 win, when he pitched six innings and gave up one run on seven hits with two walks and five strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Nolasco had his four-game winning streak snapped in his last start, losing 7-5 to the Braves in Atlanta. He worked 5 2/3 innings and allowed 12 hits, three of which were home runs. He pitched against the Phillies on May 31 in Philadelphia, earning the victory. He went 6 2/3 innings, giving up four hits and two runs.  He struck out five and walked two. Nolasco is 2-2 in his career against the Phillies.
away_pitcher_note: Myers kept a no-hitter going into the seventh inning of his last start, on Wednesday against the Reds. However, the right-hander conceded a run that inning and ended up taking the loss. Still, his last two starts have shown that his season is looking up after starting out 2-5 with a 5.76 ERA through his first 10 starts. In 19 career starts against the Marlins, Myers is 6-7 with a 4.89 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: At least in the first inning, Miller's last outing started off pretty promising. He fanned the first two batters he faced, but he labored after that. In a loss to the Reds, the 23-year-old gave up four runs in a 3 1/3 innings, matching his season low for innings pitched. He has now dropped two of his last three decisions. On June 1 at Philadelphia, he worked five innings, but was not involved in the decision. He exited with a two-run lead that wasn't preserved.
away_pitcher_note: Hamels was back to his old self in his most recent start. He threw the second shutout of his career, holding the Reds to three hits while striking out four and walking three. The lefty was happy with his ability to locate fastballs low in the zone against Cincinnati, something he had struggled with in his two previous starts, when he allowed 13 runs over 9 2/3 innings. In five career starts against the Marlins, Hamels is 2-3 with a 5.46 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Olsen pitched perhaps the best six innings he's thrown all year during his last start against the Reds on Saturday. But his defense left him with his third straight no-decision. Olsen registered six full innings without giving up an earned run on four hits, a walk and five strikeouts. But shaky defense on the infield made him leave in a 4-4 game. Olsen -- who retired 13 straight batters at one point -- had two outs in the sixth inning when Brandon Phillips' ground ball went off third baseman Jorge Cantu's glove, allowing a run to score. Then, after first baseman Wes Helms let a grounder go off his glove, Andy Phillips hit a three-run double down the left-field line to tie the score. In the bottom half of that inning, Olsen -- who had an RBI single earlier in the game -- was replaced for a pinch-hitter after throwing 85 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer gave up two runs on five hits in 5 1/3 innings, and was in line for the loss Friday if not for a Braves error with two outs in the ninth. Moyer surrendered a two-run homer and a triple in the sixth, before leaving with one out. In his last five starts, Moyer is 4-0 with a 3.94 ERA (14 ER in 32 innings). He hasn't lost in his last five starts, and has pitched at least six innings in that same span. Against the Braves, Moyer struck out four and walked three, which tied a season high.

home_pitcher_note: Sonnanstine got a no-decision Saturday night in Texas after allowing two runs on six hits in five innings. The right-hander is a master of deception, employing an array of pitches that he can throw from all different angles. But he has learned to primarily use his fastball to set up the other pitches. Sonnanstine is 1-0 with a 2.57 ERA in one career start against the Marlins. His last win came May 16 at St. Louis.
away_pitcher_note: After dominating Double-A Carolina all year, the Marlins finally decided to give Tucker a chance in the Major Leagues. He didn't let them down. Making his big league debut against the Reds on Sunday, Tucker went five innings while giving up just one run on two hits and striking out six in the Marlins' win. Tucker walked five batters (one intentional) and threw 89 pitches -- 45 for strikes. His fastball was in the low- to mid-90s for most of the afternoon, topping out at 95 mph twice. The only run he gave up was a two-out single by his opposing pitcher, Aaron Harang. Coming into the game, Tucker had posted a 4-2 record with the Mudcats and a Southern League-leading 1.41 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Garza will be making his 12th start of the season and his first start against the Marlins. On Sunday at Arlington, the 24-year-old right-hander allowed three runs on six hits in four innings before leaving the game after having an altercation with catcher Dioner Navarro. Garza has a mid-90s fastball that sinks, a curve, a slider and a changeup. He has struggled pitching indoors, evidenced by his 4-11 record with a 4.56 ERA in 19 career appearances indoors. But Garza has found Tropicana Field to his liking, pitching to a 3-0 record with a 2.40 ERA in five starts.
away_pitcher_note: Part of history in his last outing, Hendrickson now hopes to get back on the winning track. On Monday, Hendrickson surrendered career homer No. 600 to Ken Griffey Jr. Unfortunately for the left-hander, that benchmark blast wasn't the only time he was taken deep in that loss. Hendrickson allowed a season-most three home runs in a season-low 2 1/3 innings. Hendrickson gets a chance to regroup at a place he is very familiar with. Hendrickson takes on the Rays, an organization he pitched for in 2004 and 2005. Lifetime, he is 2-2 with a 4.02 ERA against his former team.

home_pitcher_note: Jackson made his 13th start of the season Monday night against the Angels, and the 24-year-old right-hander came away with his fourth win after allowing four runs on 10 hits and one walk while striking out two in seven innings. Jackson has electric stuff, which brings the expectations of future greatness, and just lately has he shown signs of being able to harness that ability on a consistent basis. Jackson is 0-2 with an 11.88 ERA in three career appearances against the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: Nolasco had one of his best outings of the season and registered the win in his last start, Tuesday against the Phillies. But the 25-year-old probably deserved to record a shutout. Nolasco gave up three runs (zero earned) on four hits and one walk while striking out three. But the three runs scored on Nolasco came after two-out errors by his defense. Nolasco finished his night after throwing 95 pitches -- 69 for strikes -- against the high-powered Philadelphia offense.

home_pitcher_note: Despite earning the loss facing Toronto in his last start, Silva still had a "quality" start. He allowed three runs on nine hits over seven innings. The right-hander walked none and struck out three. Silva has not recorded a win since April 17. Since that win, he has gone 0-7 with a 7.36 ERA. In his career against the Marlins, Silva is 2-0 with a 2.90 ERA over 31 innings.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Miller best performance of the season ended up with a no-decision. The 23-year-old left-hander tossed seven sensational innings against the Phillies. He allowed one run on four hits with one walk and seven strikeouts. He came out for the eighth inning, but issued a leadoff walk to Jayson Werth, ending his night. The seven innings matched a career high, and in the seventh inning, he was throwing 96 mph. Formerly with the Tigers, Miller has faced Seattle two times in his career, and he is 0-2 with a 3.86 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez put forth a dominating performance during his last outing against the Blue Jays. Seattle's young hurler allowed just four hits while striking out eight over eight innings of work. The only blemish on his impressive afternoon was an unearned run he allowed to score during the bottom of the fourth inning. The 22-year-old has won his past three starts and has not allowed an earned run over those 21 innings. Hernandez left after eight innings against Toronto because of tightness in his legs, but the cramps were not considered to be a major issue and likely had to do with fatigue and the high temperatures at Rogers Centre. He is expected to make his scheduled start against the Marlins, a team Hernandez has never faced during his four-year career.
away_pitcher_note: Olsen had his second straight solid outing on Thursday, but he once again fell short of earning a win. After falling victim to four unearned runs against the Reds on June 7, Olsen made just one bad pitch against the Phillies, but it was a wild pitch that led to two runs in the sixth. Olsen, who retired 12 straight at one point, finished giving up two runs (one earned) on six hits while striking out seven and left after tossing 104 pitches in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Dickey's return to the starting rotation didn't go nearly as well as the knuckleball specialist had planned. The pitch wasn't moving the way it normally does, coming toward the hitting area, and the Nationals had eight hits and seven runs in the first two innings off the veteran right-hander, who was lifted in the second inning. Dickey has faced the Marlins twice in his career and owns a 1-0 record and a 4.50 ERA in four innings.
away_pitcher_note: Tucker went five innings while giving up just one run on two hits and striking out six on June 8. Unfortunately, the young right-hander saw his ERA balloon after his struggles vs. the Rays on Friday night. Tucker tossed five innings but was tagged for seven hits and five runs in his first Major League loss. Of the 97 pitches he tossed at Tropicana Field, 58 were strikes, as Tucker issued three walks and will look for more command vs. Seattle.

home_pitcher_note: Harden tossed a one-hit gem in his last start against the Giants, but a pitch count of 95 forced him out after the sixth inning. He didn't allow a run while walking two and striking out five for his first win since May 23. Before Sunday's game, he had been dealt three consecutive no-decisions. Harden has never faced the Diamondbacks in his career.
away_pitcher_note: The southpaw is coming off a four-hit performance vs. Tampa Bay, during which his six strikeouts were overshadowed by a trio of crippling walks. Hendrickson is always as good as his command, and the veteran pitcher fell behind in the count often in Saturday night's loss. Of the  103 pitches he threw to the Rays, only 57 were strikes. Hendrickson will look to bounce back in Oakland, where he is 2-3 in six games, with a 7.45 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Eveland got the start he had been looking for since his one-run complete game May 21 in his last outing against the Giants. He pitched a solid 6 2/3 innings, allowing just one run on six hits while walking three and striking out five, marking the eighth time in 14 starts he allowed two runs or fewer. The win came after two consecutive starts in which he had walked six or more. Eveland will be facing Florida for the first time in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Coming off a career-high 12 strikeouts in a win over the Rays, Nolasco is emerging into a dependable starter. As a rookie in 2006, he won 11 games, and he is moving closer to that number. He threw a career-most 132 pitches in his 8 2/3 innings at Tampa Bay. In June, he is 2-1 with a 3.98 ERA in three starts. In May, he was 4-1 with a 3.97 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Duchscherer cruised his way through his last outing, a 15-1 A's rout over Brandon Webb and the Arizona Diamondbacks. The right-hander picked up his seventh win of the season, going eight innings, allowing only one run and five hits. Duchscherer has won four of his last five outings and has lowered his season ERA to 2.08. He will be making his first career start against the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: Positive results are starting to emerge for Miller, who stepped up with his second straight strong seven-inning start. In a win over the Mariners, the 23-year-old gave up one run on six hits. He showed he could cruise along without relying on the strikeout, as he fanned two, but also walked two. In a start before that, he struck out seven in seven innings, while giving up one run in a no-decision against the Phillies. Beating Seattle marked his first win since May 22, when he claimed the decision against the D-backs.

home_pitcher_note: After coming out winless in Seattle in his last start, Olsen remains without a victory since he beat Milwaukee on May 6. Not that the lefty has pitched poorly over that stretch, but he was knocked around a bit by the Mariners. In 4 1/3 innings, he surrendered five runs (four earned) on 11 hits. The outing was his shortest in five starts. Typically, he goes at least five innings. He had a string of three consecutive six-plus innings starts snapped.
away_pitcher_note: Sonnanstine picked up his team-leading eighth win of the season Wednesday night against the Cubs, after allowing three runs on seven hits in five innings plus one batter. The right-hander is a master of deception, employing an array of pitches that he can throw from all different angles. But he is at his best when he uses his fastball to set up the other pitches. Sonnanstine will be facing the Marlins for the second time this season, as the 25-year-old picked up a win against the Fish on June 13. In that contest at Tropicana Field, Sonnanstine tossed five 1/3 innings and allowed three runs on six hits.

home_pitcher_note: Three big league starts, three decisions, with two wins. Not a bad way for the 21-year-old to break into the league. In his last outing, Tucker worked a career-long six innings, giving up two runs as he beat the Mariners. Showcasing a 96 mph fastball that day, he threw 94 pitches, striking out four while walking two. This will be his second meeting against the Rays. On June 13 at Tampa Bay, Tucker worked five innings, giving up five runs on seven hits in a loss.
away_pitcher_note: Shields is still searching for his first win since May 9, but his record doesn't do the right-hander justice. Thursday night is a prime example, as he tossed six shutout innings before hitting a glitch in the seventh inning. Shields was charged with three earned runs off seven hits, but the Rays' bats came alive shortly after to notch the victory. The Rays top right-hander, Shields is at his best when he has command of his fastball as he did in his last outing vs. the Cubs, in which he fanned nine Chicago batters. He will travel to South Florida looking for his fifth win, as Shields takes on the Marlins for the first time this season.

home_pitcher_note: While not a quality start, the lefty pitched well in a no-decision in his last outing against the A's. What hurt him was a two-out swing in the fourth inning. He issued a two-out double to Eric Chavez, followed by a two-run homer to Kurt Suzuki. The next pitch was deposited for a home run by Carlos Gonzalez. Still, Hendrickson's 6 1/3 innings marked his longest outing since May 2, when he worked seven. On June 14, Hendrickson suffered a loss to the Rays.
away_pitcher_note: Garza will be making his 14th start of the season and his second against the Marlins. The 24-year-old right-hander earned his fifth win on June 14, silencing Florida's high octane offense. Garza tossed seven innings, allowing only one run on three hits with a trio of strikeouts. Garza has a mid-90s fastball that sinks, a curve, a slider and a changeup. He is coming off Friday night's loss to the Astros, in which Garza was charged with seven hits and three earned runs, with eight strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: Any worries about a setback after his 132-pitch performance on June 15 at Tampa Bay were erased in his last start. In seven innings at Oakland, Nolasco posted another quality start, yet he wasn't involved in the decision. The right-hander allowed three runs on seven hits. His strikeouts were down to three, after he set a career high of 12 at Tampa Bay. Yet, Nolasco threw 103 pitches, and exited with the game tied. On May 21 at Dolphin Stadium, Nolasco beat the Diamondbacks, giving up one run on three hits over seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Owings pitched well in his last outing, against the Twins, but he had little to show for it, as Minnesota put together a six-run seventh inning to win the game. The right-hander cruised through the first six innings, allowing just two hits. In the seventh, Joe Mauer led off with a bunt single, and the floodgates opened. Owings left with the game tied at 1, but Chad Qualls couldn't stop a Twins rally.

home_pitcher_note: With a little more luck, Miller could have had a better outing in his last start. His line read: five runs (four earned) in four innings. But in a four-run third, a mental mistake led to three extra runs coming home in the inning. In all, he threw 86 pitches. On the road trip, he was 1-1, including an impressive seven-innings, one-run performance at Seattle on June 16. On May 22, Miller beat Arizona, giving up no runs in seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Webb rolled through the first four innings of his last start, against the Twins in the Metrodome. The right-hander allowed just three hits and held a 3-0 lead. But the fifth inning started out poorly when left fielder Conor Jackson lost a ball in the roof and things quickly spiraled out of hand. When all was said and done, the Twins managed five runs in the inning and Webb took the loss. In his previous outing, he was roughed up by the A's at Chase Field. Oakland scored seven runs against him in just 3 1/3 innings. In that game, Webb lacked the command that he typically has, particularly when it came to his sinker.
