home_pitcher_note: With some better luck, Olsen could have ended his winless streak in his last outing. Instead, after exiting with a 3-2 lead after seven innings, the lefty settled for a no-decision against Tampa Bay. Olsen hasn't won since May 6 against Milwaukee, a span of nine starts. The lefty is 0-3 in those games. He gave up two runs on four hits with four strikeouts and two walks in his no-decision to the Rays.
away_pitcher_note: Haren has been outstanding in his last two starts. Last time out, against the Red Sox, he outdueled Josh Beckett by tossing seven shutout innings in a 2-1 Arizona win. The right-hander allowed just two hits and walked one, while fanning five. Prior to that start, he held his former team, the A's, to just one run on four hits over seven innings. Haren threw more cut fastballs than he normally does, in part because he figured the A's were more familiar with his repertoire than other teams. He began using the cut fastball this spring, but he got away from it early in the season. It's an important pitch for him because it gives him something to throw rather than just a straight fastball when he falls behind in the count, 1-0, or 2-0.

home_pitcher_note: Tucker's last start was one he'd probably like to forget. The 21-year-old rookie surrendered a career-high seven runs off eight hits against the Rays on Wednesday and was never able to get out of a brutal fifth inning. That inning saw the Marlins give up a season-high 10 runs, with Tucker giving up three before getting a single out. Despite retiring six of the first seven batters he faced, Tucker left after throwing 83 pitches while walking two and striking out three in four-plus innings. The Burbank, Calif., native will be facing the Nationals on Monday for the first time.
away_pitcher_note: Redding had seven straight no-decisions. In each of those decisions, Redding went at least five innings. The last time he won a game was May 19 against the Phillies. His last start was on Wednesday against the Angels. He lasted six innings and gave up two runs on seven hits.

home_pitcher_note: Hendrickson had a hard time commanding his fastball against the Rays on Thursday, and it ended up costing him his fourth loss in his last four decisions. The 6-foot-9 lefty finished the day allowing five runs on five hits and five walks and left the game after throwing 102 pitches -- 56 for strikes -- in just 4 2/3 innings. It was the sixth time in his last 10 outings Hendrickson has thrown over 90 pitches in less than six innings. The most telling moment in that game was when he intentionally walked the No. 8 hitter with two outs to get to pitcher Matt Garza -- who threw a complete-game, one-hitter -- but ended up walking him to load the bases, leading to a run.
away_pitcher_note: Balester will make his Major League debut for the Nationals in Miami, taking the place of the injured Shawn Hill. Balester is considered one of the Nationals' top prospects, and he follows Tyler Clippard and Garrett Mock in getting a Major League appearance in place of an injured Nationals pitcher. Balester is 9-3 with a 4.00 ERA in 78 2/3 innings pitched. The young right-hander has struck out 64 batters while only walking 23 this season.

home_pitcher_note: Nolasco may not make the All-Star team, but he's pitched like one in June. A winner of three consecutive decisions, Nolasco yielded one run in eight innings, with nine strikeouts and one walk, in his last start -- a 3-1 decision over Arizona. Nolasco is more comfortable with his cut fastball, and his fastball is reaching 94 mph. He threw 120 pitches, marking his third straight outing of at least 100 pitches. For the second time in his career, he has a streak of three straight starts of seven or more innings.
away_pitcher_note: Perez pitched well in his return from the disabled list. Working on an 80-pitch limit, the veteran left-hander tossed four shutout innings, striking out three. He said after the start that he felt no pain, and he's expected to make his next start.

home_pitcher_note: The Rockies placed lefty Jeff Francis on the 15-day disabled list on Wednesday with left shoulder inflammation and gave Redman his second chance this year. None of the candidates for the fifth starter spot distinguished himself this spring, so the Rockies went with Redman because he helped the club late last season. But Redman had uncommon problems throwing strikes. Now, after some success at Triple-A Colorado Springs (5-2, 4.64 ERA in nine starts), Redman returns.
away_pitcher_note: In his last outing on Saturday against the D-backs, Miller was masterful through the first four innings, but a rough fifth and sixth ended his night on a sour note. After throwing four straight shutout innings while tossing just 41 pitches to start the game, Miller gave up six runs -- three earned -- in the next two and threw 49 pitches in the process. The 6-foot-6 lefty finished his night in a 5-1 game with two outs in the sixth inning, giving up five hits while striking out four and walking three on 90 pitches. Miller will be facing the Rockies for the first time in his career.

home_pitcher_note: In his last two games, both losses, Reynolds has experienced growth. Two starts ago, he lost to the Mets but lasted seven innings without his best stuff. In his last start, a 4-3 loss to the Tigers, he adjusted to a tight lineup by backing hitters off the plate with inside fastballs. He was charged with four runs in 5 2/3 innings, but two runs scored after he left the game.
away_pitcher_note: On Sunday afternoon against the Diamondbacks, Olsen had a solid outing but got little help from his offense in his ninth no-decision. The 24-year-old -- who came into the game with a 2.58 ERA in his last four starts, but an 0-2 record -- gave up just three runs on five hits while striking out four and walking two before leaving the game after seven innings and throwing 104 pitches. His opponent, Dan Haren, on the other hand, held the Marlins to just one run in seven innings. Florida eventually won on a walk-off single by Jorge Cantu.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa struggled with the command of his fastball and curveball Monday against the Padres. His inconsistency to find the plate put him behind in too many counts, and San Diego took advantage. De La Rosa gave up a season-high 11 hits and six runs in five innings in the no-decision. This was the second-straight shaky start for De La Rosa, who gave up four runs -- two earned -- in just 4 2/3 innings in a loss to Kansas City. De La Rosa is most effective when he uses his wicked slider to strikeout his opponents, but he has just seven strikeouts combined in his past two starts after striking out 10 batters against Cleveland on June 19 and eight batters at the White Sox on June 14.
away_pitcher_note: Working through the lineup a couple of times remains part of the learning curve for Tucker, the 21-year-old rookie right-hander. In his previous start, a no-decision against the Nationals, the hard-throwing former 2005 first-round pick got into trouble in the fifth inning, when he issued solo homers to Elijah Dukes and Dmitri Young. Tucker threw 101 pitches, and gave up six hits. He struck out six, but exited with his team trailing by a run. In his last two starts, Tucker has given up 11 runs in nine innings.

home_pitcher_note: Cook threw his first career shutout, vanquishing the Padres, 4-0, on Tuesday night. He didn't let a runner past second base and forced 15 outs on ground balls. Cook can dominate a game with his sinker, but against an aggressive Padres lineup he crossed up hitters with a four-seam fastball. He finished with four strikeouts and no walks. Cook will be making his fourth appearance against the Marlins. He is 1-1 with a 4.73 ERA against them.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran left-hander has been victimized by the long ball of late. He gave up two in his last outing, including a grand slam to Ronnie Belliard, in a loss to the Nationals. In his last five starts, Hendrickson has allowed nine home runs in a 24 1/3 inning span. Hendrickson has dropped five straight decisions. For his career, he is 2-1 with a 3.00 ERA in eight games at Coors Field.

home_pitcher_note: Maddux struggled mightily in his last start, allowing eight runs on eight hits over 4 2/3 innings against the Rockies on June 30 at Coors Field. Maddux allowed a three-run double to Chris Iannetta and later a three-run home run to Brad Hawpe. He also walked two batters in the first inning, setting up Iannetta's double. Maddux didn't factor in the decision as the Padres, who trailed 8-3 entering the sixth inning, rallied for a 15-8 victory. Maddux has now allowed 14 earned runs over his last two starts. He makes his next start against an Arizona team that hit him hard on April 18 to the tune of nine runs on 13 hits over seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Nolasco put together another successful outing, pitching seven innings of three-hit ball and allowing two runs while striking out eight Nationals batters. Nolasco has now won four straight and has pitched at least six innings while allowing three earned runs or fewer in each of his last five starts. Over that span, Nolasco has compiled a 1.96 ERA, 35 strikeouts and four walks in 36 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Wolf struggled mightily on Wednesday against the Rockies, losing his fourth consecutive game. The left-hander, who has been mentioned as a possible trading chip and has had several scouts watch him recently, allowed two home runs and four walks in four innings against the Rockies. This coming off a start where Wolf lasted just 3 1/3 innings. "I was horrible tonight, I couldn't throw the ball where I wanted to," said Wolf, who had four walks, the third consecutive start in which he's walked at least four. "... I felt like the worst pitcher in baseball. I'm embarrassed with how I pitched tonight."
away_pitcher_note: The 23-year-old was effective for the most part at Coors Field in his last start. In the first game of the road trip, Miller gave up three runs on five hits in 6 2/3 innings in a hitter-friendly ballpark. Yet, he wasn't involved in the decision against the Rockies. The outing was his longest since working seven innings at Seattle in a win on June 16 (three starts). Miller threw 104 pitches, striking out five. He walked three for the second straight start and allowed a home run to Jeff Baker, the first time Miller has been taken deep since June 1 at Philadelphia.

home_pitcher_note: Baek went into his last start having lost his two previous decisions. He had allowed a combined 10 runs in those two starts before taming the first-place Diamondbacks on the Fourth of July, tossing six shutout innings with only two hits allowed in a victory at Chase Field. Baek tied his career high with seven strikeouts. He got ahead in the count and got a lot of mileage out of his offspeed pitches. He has never faced the Marlins, as Baek has spent most of his career in the American League.
away_pitcher_note: The left-hander had gone 11 straight starts without a win. The Marlins gave Olsen plenty of offense in his previous start -- five runs in the first and a 13-4 lead in the fourth inning. But Olsen experienced that nothing is safe at Coors Field, and the Rockies ended up scoring nine runs off the lefty. The nine runs (eight earned) were the most he's allowed all season. But he worked five innings, and was in line for the win. Olsen had thrown at least even innings in two straight starts. Olsen was in line to win that game, but he ended up with a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: With Brad Penny still sidelined, Chan Ho Park remains in the rotation, and he certainly deserves it based on his four starts, including the most recent in San Francisco, where he allowed one run on three hits with seven strikeouts over six innings. Park's ERA as a starter this year is 1.29.
away_pitcher_note: The 24-year-old had Tommy John ligament replacement surgery on Aug. 3 and, after making five Minor League starts, will make his 2008 debut against the Dodgers -- a team he is 1-1 against with a 9.00 ERA in two starts for his career. Johnson pitched eight scoreless innings in his final rehab start for Double-A Carolina on Friday, allowing five hits while striking out seven and walking two while throwing a season-high 111 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Eric Stults took a three-run lead into the fifth inning against the Giants, but when he let the first two batters reach base, he was yanked, having allowed seven hits and two walks in four innings. Since his shutout of the White Sox, he's allowed 16 base runners in 9 1/3 innings. His preparation was disrupted when he flew home for the birth of his son.
away_pitcher_note: Volstad, the Marlins' first-round pick in 2005, pitched two scoreless innings of relief against the Rockies on Sunday to win his Major League debut. After starter Mark Hendrickson gave up four runs in four innings, Volstad came in for the fifth with the Marlins down, 4-3. But the 21-year-old retired six of the 10 hitters he faced, got of a bases-loaded jam in the sixth and left with the Marlins leading. The 6-foot-7 righty was called up from Double-A Carolina on Sunday. In 15 starts with the Mudcats this season, Volstad went 4-4 with a 3.36 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Needless to say Kuroda is back. He came within one eighth-inning pitch of throwing a perfect game Monday against the Braves, yielding just a single base runner in a one-hit shutout in which he struck out six. Kuroda has not allowed a run in 16 innings since returning from the disabled list (right shoulder) on July 2 and has won consecutive decisions for the first time all season. His last two Dodger Stadium starts have been shutouts.
away_pitcher_note: Nolasco is on a roll, pitching at an All-Star level. The 25-year-old right-hander comes off a brilliant eight-inning, five-hit performance at San Diego. He gave up one run and struck out seven, while not issuing a walk. Nolasco has won his last five decisions, and nine of his last 10.

home_pitcher_note: Billingsley's four-game win streak was snapped by the Braves, who roughed him up for a season-high six runs in 5 1/3 innings. Billingsley had a no-hitter through four innings, but issued a key walk in one inning and started another with a home run by Brian McCann. According to manager Joe Torre, Billingsley still tends to start rushing when things don't go well and that compounds his problems.
away_pitcher_note: In the final game before the break, Miller will look to get back on the winning track. The 23-year-old lefty has dropped three straight decisions, and he seeks his first victory since June 16 at Seattle. Up and down all season, the lefty comes off a five-inning stint at San Diego, where he gave up four runs on six hits with four walks and five strikeouts. He threw 92 pitches, with 55 for strikes. This will be Miller's second appearance against the Dodgers. On April 29 at Dolphin Stadium, he worked three innings, giving up six runs on nine hits in a game he wasn't involved in the decision.

home_pitcher_note: The team's most impressive pitcher in the first half, Nolasco is being rewarded. The right-hander will take the mound in the first game of the second half in an important series with the Phillies. Nolasco has won five straight decisions. Before the break, Nolasco was 4-2 with a 3.35 ERA in eight home games, including two starts. Early in the season, the 25-year-old pitched out of the bullpen. In his final outing before the break, Nolasco was impressive again. In six innings at Dodger Stadium, he gave up two runs on five hits with six strikeouts and one walk in a no decision.
away_pitcher_note: The 45-year-old continues to defy hitters nearly half his age, with his slow, slower and slowest pitches. He's posted a 2.63 ERA in two July starts and is coming off an effort in which he allowed one run in seven innings. He dominated the Marlins on June 12 at Dolphin Stadium, surrendering two hits in and one walk in eight shutout innings.

home_pitcher_note: The 24-year-old closed out his first half with an impressive victory, limiting the Padres to one run on four hits in eight innings. Olsen snapped a string of 11 straight starts without a victory, dating back to May 6, when he went 8 2/3 innings against the Brewers. The lefty logged 119 1/3 innings in the first half, and the long break should be beneficial, considering he has had a lack of velocity in the first half compared to how he's thrown in past years.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander continues to give the Phillies a chance to win, and the team is 14-5 in his starts. He was sailing along in his previous outing, before a troublesome seventh inning cost him a decision. He's 1-0 with a career 2.57 ERA in two starts against Florida, having allowed four earned runs in 14 innings.

home_pitcher_note: As far as returns go, Johnson answered a lot of questions in his season debut. Rebounding from Tommy John surgery, Johnson threw five innings, giving up three runs against Los Angeles at Dodger Stadium on July 10. He threw 87 pitches. It was his first MLB appearance since July 4, 2007. Johnson was not involved in the decision, but he exited with a one-run lead. His fastball was clocked as high as 97 mph, and he struck out six without issuing a walk.
away_pitcher_note: The lefty held the Diamondbacks to two runs in seven innings on July 13, but earned a no-decision in a win over Arizona. It was the third consecutive start that Hamels had allowed two runs or fewer. He is 2-3 with a 4.78 ERA in six career starts vs. the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: It's been a storybook beginning to Volstad's big league career. Promoted from Double-A Carolina on July 6, he collected a win that day, tossing two innings of scoreless relief. Then on July 11, in his first big league start, the 21-year-old was on the verge of a complete game, but on his 100th pitch, he allowed a two-out RBI single to Russell Martin. Volstad ended up beating the Dodgers at Dodger Stadium, giving up one run in 8 2/3 innings. So he's allowed just one run in 10 2/3 innings to start off his MLB career. He struck out six in L.A. and walked just one.
away_pitcher_note: Campillo allowed two runs on five hits in six strong innings Sunday against the Padres, and he finally received some run support in picking up just his second win since May 29. He struck out four and walked two. Campillo would have pitched at least seven innings, but he fouled a ball off his left ankle during his at-bat in the seventh. The 29-year-old right-hander has made three appearances against the Marlins this season, including one start. That start came on June 3, when he gave up four runs on six hits -- including two homers -- in four innings. He did not factor in the decision.

home_pitcher_note: The Marlins are expected to make it official after Monday's game, but unofficially, VandenHurk appears the choice to take the mound in the second of three with the Braves. The right-hander opened the season as Florida's No. 2 starter, but he was 0-1 and threw 5 1/3 innings this season before being optioned to Double-A Carolina. With the Mudcats, the right-hander was 3-3 with a 4.32 ERA. He had been on the Minor League DL for a while with an ulnar nerve issue.
away_pitcher_note: Morton allowed one run on four hits in 5 1/3 innings against the Padres on July 12, earning his first win since his Major League debut on June 14. Since that win against the Angels, Morton was 0-2 with a 7.58 ERA in four starts. Against the Padres, he struck out four and walked three. Prior to that start, he had allowed at least five runs in each of his past two starts. The 24-year-old right-hander has never faced the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: Nolasco hasn't been very accustomed to losing recently, but that's exactly what happened in his last start Friday against the Phillies. The 25-year-old gave up four runs on seven hits in seven innings and took his first loss since June 5 -- a span of eight starts. That June 5 loss to the Braves was also the last time he allowed more than three runs in an outing. Going into the All-Star break, Nolasco sported a five-game winning streak and had allowed just six runs in his previous 29 innings. He exited Friday's game after striking out five, walking one and throwing 100 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson battled some post-All-Star-break rust while allowing the Nationals five earned runs in 6 2/3 innings on Friday night, unable to notch his 16th quality start of the season. Hudson faced the Marlins on April 16, when he lacked velocity and allowed six earned runs in a season-short three innings. He is 4-1 with a 2.95 ERA in seven career starts at Dolphin Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Zambrano wasn't as sharp in his most recent outing, as he walked six in 6 1/3 innings in a 4-1 loss at Houston Saturday night, his first loss to an NL Central Division opponent this season. It was the right-hander's third start since coming off the disabled list. Zambrano has not faced the Marlins this season and is 3-1 with a 2.54 ERA in seven career games against Florida.
away_pitcher_note: After holding the high-powered Phillies offense to four runs (three earned) in five innings on Saturday, Olsen picked up his second straight win. That's a big feat considering the 24-year-old went winless in his previous 11 starts. One problem for Olsen pretty much all year, however, has been his velocity. Against the Phillies, the lefty threw 93 pitches, but most of them barely reached 90 mph on the radar gun -- a big reason why he did not record a strikeout for the first time since April 25.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Dempster turned in one of his better outings of the season, while earning his first road victory since June 2, 2006, against the Cardinals. The right-hander pitched eight scoreless innings against Houston, limiting the Astros to six singles and a walk, while striking out seven. Dempster hasn't faced the Marlins this season and is 1-1 with three saves and a 3.00 ERA in 10 career appearances against his former team.
away_pitcher_note: So far, so good on Johnson's return from Tommy John elbow reconstruction surgery. In his first two starts since rebounding from the ligament replacement surgery to his right elbow, Johnson has made steady progress, although he has yet to receive a decision. In his last start, Johnson gave up two runs in 6 2/3 innings against the Phillies. He logged 92 pitches and struck out four, walking three. With his velocity in the 93-mph range, Johnson had his sinker working, as he induced 11 ground-ball outs.

home_pitcher_note: Harden has posted back to back 10-strikeout games for the Cubs, but has yet to get a "W." In his last start against Arizona, he gave up one hit -- a solo homer to Alex Romero -- and took the loss. Harden threw 112 pitches, more than the Cubs wanted him to, but Lou Piniella kept him in the game in hopes that the offense would come alive.
away_pitcher_note: Volstad's third outing may not have gone as perfectly as his previous two, but he still pitched pretty well. On Monday against the Braves, Volstad gave up three runs off six hits and three walks in six innings after leaving with 87 pitches -- 55 for strikes. Volstad got into trouble in the second inning, throwing 21 pitches and facing seven batters, but gave up one run and worked out of a bases-loaded, no-out jam unscathed. Volstad was pitching about an hour away from where he grew up for the first time and had at least 15 members of his family in attendance.

home_pitcher_note: Marquis took the loss in his last start, but was another victim of a lack of offense. He gave up three runs on five hits over six innings -- a quality start. But the Cubs couldn't muster any runs. He has not won since June 21 against the White Sox. He's 4-5 with a 6.88 ERA against the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: VandenHurk was lights-out in his first start with the Marlins since April 6 on Tuesday against the Braves. He threw five innings of no-hit ball while striking out seven and walking five, but had to leave the game early because he had thrown 94 pitches already. VandenHurk added a little bit more velocity on his fastball and, most importantly, he picked up a slider during his time in the Minor Leagues that he used effectively. The only blemish for VandenHurk was a fourth inning that saw him load the bases with nobody out. But he got out of it with two strikeouts and a pop out to the infield.

home_pitcher_note: Nolasco took his second straight loss against the Braves on Wednesday, giving up five runs -- the most he had given up since June 5 against the Braves -- on eight hits in five innings. Nolasco ended up striking out three and walking three before leaving with 84 pitches under his belt. Nolasco has struggled since going on a five-game winning streak between June 10 and July 7 -- when he posted a 1.83 ERA in five starts. Since the All-Star break, he has given up nine runs in 12 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Maine finally got through the seventh inning Wednesday -- a feat he hadn't attained since May 7 -- allowing three runs, striking out five and walking two against the Phillies. His pitch count reached the century mark once again (104), but he stretched those tosses through seven, and, of the six hits he allowed, most of the damage came on back-to-back home runs in the second inning. He'll now face the Marlins, whom he has yet to face this season.

home_pitcher_note: The 24-year-old lefty was hurt by the big inning in his last start, a loss against the Cubs at Wrigley Field. A four-run fifth inning put him in a bind. He was hurt by two homers, and he's allowed at least one home run in five straight starts. In that span, opponents have collected eight homers. Olsen suffered his first loss since June 17. He had been 2-0 with three no-decisions over that stretch.
away_pitcher_note: Perez held the Phillies to one run through 7 2/3 innings Thursday, further cementing his lore as a big-game pitcher with 12 strikeouts -- six with Ryan Howard and Chase Utley in the batter's box. Even though he finished with a no-decision, Perez wielded an almost unhittable slider and an accurate fastball for most of the afternoon until he plunked Howard in the eighth, loading the bases and prompting a call to the bullpen. The Marlins last saw Perez on May 28 -- prior to his recent successes -- hammering the southpaw for five runs in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: The 24-year-old continues to make steady progress in his comeback from Tommy John elbow ligament replacement surgery. Johnson has made three starts, and in all three games, the right-hander was not involved in the decision. Johnson gave up two homers at Wrigley Field, the first two he has allowed this season. The last time Johnson faced the Mets was on Sept. 12, 2006, at Dolphin Stadium. In that game, he sat through more than 80 minutes of a rain delay, and he left after five innings with forearm stiffness. That was the beginning of his arm problems.
away_pitcher_note: Pelfrey continued his streak of impressive pitching performances with another solid outing Friday night. He threw seven innings of one-run ball and limited the Cardinals to seven hits, striking out five. The right-hander did not walk a single batter and has recorded only one walk in his last four starts. Pelfrey said the command on his breaking ball is still not where he wants it to be, but it's getting better. He has now won seven of his last eight starts. He has not lost since May 26 against Florida when he exited after just four innings. Pelfrey is 0-1 with a 9.00 ERA against the Marlins this season.

home_pitcher_note: For the first time since May 2, 2007, Sanchez will be making a big league start. Last June, the 24-year-old underwent right shoulder surgery, and he has worked his way back ever since. He made five rehab assignment starts, including two for Double-A Carolina. In his last outing, the Venezuelan native worked seven innings. In five Minor League starts, he has thrown 28 innings. The highlight of Sanchez's career was his no-hitter against Arizona on Sept. 6, 2006.
away_pitcher_note: Suddenly able to handle runners on base, and able to spot his fastball for strikes and use his sinker to put hitters away, De La Rosa has held opponents to two runs in 12 2/3 innings while winning his last two starts. He held the Reds to two hits in 6 2/3 innings in his last start, a 5-1 Rockies victory. He still walked five in his last game, so there's room for improvement.

home_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Volstad turned in a quality start at Chicago, even though he wasn't involved in the decision. The 21-year-old now will face the team he made his MLB debut against. On July 6 at Coors Field, Volstad threw two innings of scoreless relief, and he collected his first MLB win. This will be his third big league start. At Chicago, Volstad surrendered his first home run of the season -- either at the Minor League or big league levels. It came 19 1/3 innings into his MLB career. He also threw 91 innings at Double-A.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez has demonstrated tremendous aptitude over the course of his first full season. He started rough, but in July he went 5-1 with a 1.74 ERA. Jimenez throws four pitches effectively, and has learned how to adjust when one or more of them is not at its best on a particular day. At Cincinnati on Sunday, he wasn't able to keep his fastball down in the strike zone, but he still overpowered enough hitters for 12 flyball outs in six scoreless innings.

home_pitcher_note: Nolasco was pretty much done in by one bad inning against the Mets on Monday. In the top of the second, Nolasco threw 18 pitches and gave up two runs on three straight hits to start the inning. Other than that, the 25-year-old righty was pretty much in control in the no-decision, allowing seven hits while striking out eight and walking none in six innings. Nolasco left after throwing 98 pitches -- 69 for strikes.
away_pitcher_note: De Los Santos was called up from Triple-A Colorado Springs to start Monday against the Pirates. He walked six in four-plus innings. Although he didn't get the loss in the 8-4 defeat, his start didn't help. Manager Clint Hurdle originally was lukewarm about starting him against the Marlins, but the Rockies did not obtain an experienced option at Thursday afternoon's non-waiver Trade Deadline

home_pitcher_note: In his last start against the Mets on Tuesday, Olsen kept his team in the game by giving up just two runs in 5 2/3 innings. Olsen started off the game on a bad note by giving up three straight doubles, but he was able to get out of the first inning with just one run and cruised in the next four frames. The 24-year-old went on to retire nine of the next 10 hitters he faced after the first inning, but was pulled in the sixth after scattering another run and throwing 24 pitches to six batters. He finished the night giving up six hits while walking two and striking out five.
away_pitcher_note: Rusch has been steady since joining the Rockies' rotation, and was in the lead on Tuesday against the Pirates when he was removed in an offensive substitution. The bullpen lost the game. Rusch gave up three runs on six hits, but didn't strike out any and walked two. The Rockies aren't looking for complete games from Rusch, but being efficient enough to throw six innings would be big.

home_pitcher_note: So far, Moyer has been a can't-miss starter against the Marlins. In 10 career starts, the 45-year-old is 10-0 with a 3.03 ERA against the Fish. Moyer most recently shut them down on July 18, allowing two runs in six innings. The veteran lefty recorded his fifth consecutive quality start on Wednesday night, allowing three runs in six innings against the Nationals to earn his 10th victory of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson won his first game in four starts since coming back from Tommy John elbow reconstruction surgery when he held the Mets to four runs in 6 2/3 innings on Wednesday. The Marlins are now 4-0 in games he starts this season. Johnson was cruising through the first six innings, giving up one run and throwing just 79 pitches in the process. But in the seventh, he ran his pitch count into the triple digits and, with two outs, the last batter he faced hit a three-run homer. In his other start against the Phillies this season, Johnson gave up two runs in 6 2/3 innings in the no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick notched his second consecutive quality start with a win on Thursday against the Nationals, allowing two runs on seven hits in 6 2/3 innings. The Phillies are now 15-7 in the 23-year-old's starts this season, the best mark among Philadelphia starting pitchers. Kendrick last faced the Marlins on July 19 and endured perhaps the roughest start of his young career. The right-hander allowed seven runs on three home runs -- both career highs -- in 4 1/3 innings in taking the loss. In three career starts against the Marlins, Kendrick is 1-1 with a 5.40 ERA.
away_pitcher_note:
In his first start in almost 15 months, Sanchez picked up the win after giving up just two runs on six hits in 5 2/3 innings. Sanchez retired six of the first seven batters he faced, threw first-pitch strikes to 15 of the 25 hitters and left the game with the bases loaded and two outs after throwing 95 pitches -- 56 for strikes. 
Prior to a rough sixth inning, Sanchez only allowed three runners to reach scoring position. He finished off the night with four strikeouts and two walks.

home_pitcher_note: It's been more than one month since the Phils' ace last recorded a win, July 3 against the Braves. On Friday night, Hamels was hit hard for the second consecutive outing, yielding five runs -- four earned -- in six innings, including two home runs. Afterward, the lefty said he had left too many pitches up in the strike zone. Hamels won his only career start against the Pirates, a 2006 outing in which he surrendered three runs in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Volstad wasn't his usual, sharp self in a loss to the Rockies on Friday. Making his fourth Major League start (fifth appearance), the 21-year-old rookie gave up a career-high five runs in a career-low five innings, giving up eight hits while striking out six and walking three. All of the runs charged to Volstad came with two outs. He left after throwing 93 pitches, and had his pitch count at 53 by the end of a two-run third.

home_pitcher_note: Manager Jerry Manuel would have preferred to use Perez on Saturday on an extra day of rest, but the absence of disabled righty John Maine and the fact that Perez threw merely 77 pitches in his most recent start, on Sunday in Houston, prompted the manager to change his thinking. Perez will start on Friday against the team he has beaten twice in three starts this season. He has a 2-2  record -- but the Mets' record is 5-2 -- in his seven most recent starts. His ERA in that period is 1.97.
away_pitcher_note: Nolasco was pretty close to a complete game in a win against the Rockies on Saturday, but he'll settle for a solid eight-inning effort. Nolasco gave up three runs off four hits while striking out a career-high 13 batters and walking none. The 25-year-old's only flaw was not being able to figure out Matt Holliday, who was responsible for two of the runs and three of the hits. Other than that, and a 22-pitch first inning that saw him give up a run, Nolasco was unhittable. He finished retiring the last seven hitters in order and threw 93 pitches. It was his first win in five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Brian Stokes, who has spent all of his 2008 season with the Triple-A New Orleans Zephyrs, will start in place of the injured John Maine. Stokes, 30 next month and in his ninth season as a professional, has a 3-7 big league record, achieved with the Rays in 2006 and last year. His record with the Zephyrs is 10-8. He has a 4.41 ERA in 23 games -- 22 starts -- and 130 2/3 innings. The Mets limited his pitches in his start Wednesday to make him a viable option.
away_pitcher_note: Olsen pitched a six-inning gem on Sunday against the Rockies, but he had to settle for his 11th no-decision of the season after the Marlins' bullpen allowed three runs in the last three innings. Olsen had a no-hitter going through five and finished the day allowing just one hit -- an infield single by the second hitter he faced in the sixth inning -- while walking two and striking out six. But Olsen's biggest enemy was his pitch count, and it reached 94 by the time he finished the sixth. And with the bases loaded and two outs in the bottom half, the Marlins were looking to add to their two-run lead and were forced to pinch-hit for their starter.

home_pitcher_note: Pelfrey picked up his 10th win in a solid performance against the Padres on Tuesday night, holding San Diego to two runs through 6 2/3 innings. He scattered nine hits and struck out three, with one walk. It took Pelfrey some time to settle back into a groove after he gave up big hits, though. The righty surrendered two home runs and each was followed by two consecutive singles from the Padres. He said he has continued to struggle with his sinker since the All-Star break, but Pelfrey worked his way out of jams with runners in scoring position. He hasn't found success against the Marlins yet this season, going 0-2 in two starts against Florida, but he will get another chance Sunday afternoon.
away_pitcher_note: During his last start on Tuesday against Philadelphia, Johnson not only moved the Marlins to 5-0 in games he starts this season, he beat a pitcher who was a perfect 10-0 in his career against Florida. Johnson pitched six shutout innings, giving up just five hits and walking four while striking out three before exiting with 97 pitches -- 55 for strikes -- to beat Phillies left-hander Jamie Moyer. Johnson is now 2-0 in his last two starts. In his only start against the Mets this season, he got the win after giving up four runs in 6 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: It was a rougher second start for the right-hander, who made his 2008 debut on July 31. In his last outing, on Wednesday in Philadelphia, the 24-year-old gave up four runs (three earned) in five innings. He was taken deep by Ryan Howard, and he didn't have his pinpoint command, which got him in trouble. One of his walks and one hit batter cost him two runs. Sanchez's error also led to a Phillies run. Considering he missed more than a season because of right shoulder surgery, Sanchez understandably will have some rough stretches. His fastball was routinely about 88 mph, and he reached 91 mph once.
away_pitcher_note: Pineiro said he felt like "two different pitchers" during his last start. While he struggled in the first three innings against the Dodgers -- giving up a home run to Manny Ramirez in the process -- Pineiro settled down after catcher Yadier Molina convinced him to use the sinker more often. After that, he dominated and gave up only one run over the next four innings. His inconsistency this year has hurt him, he said, and he hopes to get that straightened out for his next outing.

home_pitcher_note: Volstad had the best start of his short Major League career in a critical win against the Phillies on Thursday. The 21-year-old tossed six shutout innings against a high-powered Philadelphia offense -- stacked with strong left-handed bats -- giving up just three hits and walking four while striking out three. It was a big win for Volstad, not only because it allowed his team to take the three-game series against the Phillies, but it was a bounce-back effort just five days removed from giving up a career-high five runs (four earned) in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lohse is in a little bit of a funk for the first time since May, with a 7.27 ERA and five homers allowed over his past three starts. It's not as though he's been awful, but he set the bar very high earlier in the year. With any kind of a decent finish, he has a chance to be the first Cardinals pitcher to rack up more than 15 wins since three pitchers did so in 2005.

home_pitcher_note: An otherwise impressive outing was marred by two home runs in Nolasco's last start. The end result was the right-hander suffered a loss to the Mets at Shea Stadium. For the most part, Nolasco was pretty good, although he was taken deep on a two-run homer by David Wright, and Carlos Delgado added a solo shot. Nolasco has yielded two home runs in two straight games. He did work 6 2/3 innings, and scattered seven hits.
away_pitcher_note: Looper's been an interesting study lately, throwing lots of strikes and giving up lots of home runs. It hasn't hurt him too badly, because the homers have tended to be solo shots. It's not a bad way to pitch if you can keep it up, and Looper has a 2.42 ERA over his past four starts with 15 strikeouts and five walks.

home_pitcher_note: Coming off a loss to the Mets, Olsen has now dropped three straight decisions. He seeks his first win since July 19 against the Phillies. Olsen gave up four runs in the first inning, including a two-run blast to Carlos Delgado. Olsen rebounded and went into the sixth inning, but he was lifted after Fernando Tatis' leadoff single. Tatis ended up scoring, putting Olsen in line for the loss. For his career, Olsen is 1-2 with a 7.00 ERA in three games against the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Much to the relief of the Cardinals, Wellemeyer is back. The pitcher who was so effective in April and May didn't look like himself for much of June and July following his return from an elbow injury. But in his last three starts, he's had stuff and command, as shown by his 13 strikeouts against three walks. He's even making progress with his changeup, to complement his impressive fastball and slider.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, against the Mets on Sunday, Johnson gave the Marlins a much-needed win by limiting New York to two runs in seven innings while striking out five and walking just two. The young right-hander has been rolling ever since coming off Tommy John elbow reconstruction surgery, and the Marlins are now 6-0 in games he starts this season. In his past two starts -- against the National League East-rival Phillies and Mets -- he is 2-0 and has allowed just two runs in 13 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Zambrano lost his first game in 13 starts at home in his last outing, giving up a career-high nine earned runs on 10 hits over 4 1/3 innings against St. Louis. He also served up four home runs for the first time in his career. Zambrano hit a homer himself, his third of the year, but it wasn't enough. He was coming off a shortened outing prior to his game against the Cardinals, so the problem wasn't that Zambrano was tired. He fell behind and the Cardinals took advantage.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez suffered his second straight loss despite a solid performance against the Cardinals on Monday. Sanchez gave up three runs on six hits while striking out eight -- which tied his career high -- and walking two. He left after throwing a season-high 103 pitches -- 69 for strikes. Sanchez's biggest mistake was a two-run homer he gave up to Yadier Molina in the fourth inning, which gave the Cardinals a 3-2 lead they wouldn't relinquish. But after that, the 24-year-old retired 11 of the next 14 hitters he faced.
away_pitcher_note: Marshall got the call over Jason Marquis on short rest or rookie Jeff Samardzija. It'll be the lefty's fourth start this season. He started on June 24 against Baltimore, on June 29 against the White Sox, and July 6 against St. Louis, and picked up a win against the Cardinals. As a starter, Marshall is 1-2 with a 4.08 ERA, giving up eight runs on 18 hits and three walks over 17 2/3 innings. The Cubs had to tweak their rotation after playing a day-night doubleheader against Atlanta on Wednesday.

home_pitcher_note: Volstad's outing against the Cardinals on Tuesday was cut short right before he began to get into a groove. Still, the 21-year-old picked up his first win at home in giving up three runs in five innings to the Cardinals before a long rain delay kicked in. Volstad's only trouble came in the first inning, when he started off the game by loading the bases with nobody out, then gave up a bases-clearing double to Ryan Ludwick. But after that inning, Volstad gave up just two hits and one walk. He retired the last six batters he faced and finished the night throwing 72 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster is coming off a big win over the Cardinals. He gave up two runs on six hits over 6 2/3 innings in the game, striking out six. The former closer is now two wins shy of his career-high of 15. He did not get a decision against the Marlins on July 25, giving up one run on two hits over six innings while striking out six. But he also walked six in that game.

home_pitcher_note: Correia received a no-decision on Thursday in Houston, allowing four runs (three earned) and seven hits in 6 2/3 innings. He left with a 4-3 lead, but the bullpen squandered it in a 7-4 loss. Correia has worked at least six innings in each of his last three starts, recording a 2.84 ERA during that span. Correia has not faced the Marlins this season but owns an 0-1 record with a 7.65 ERA in nine career appearances against them.
away_pitcher_note: Nolasco may have scattered 10 hits, but he only gave up two runs in a no-decision against the Cardinals on Wednesday. The 25-year-old showed great composure, getting out of constant jams with St. Louis putting at least one runner on base in every inning but the fifth. Most of the balls hit off Nolasco were not hit very hard, and the two runs he gave up came on sacrifice flies. However, the constant trouble he found himself in forced him into a rather short outing, as he reached the 100-pitch mark after six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Cain is 3-2 with a 1.81 ERA in his past seven starts, a surge that continued with his last outing -- a 5-1 victory at Atlanta last Friday. Cain worked seven innings in that one, yielding six hits and Atlanta's lone run. He also issued only one walk, which is always a critical factor for him. Cain has not allowed a homer in his last 13 starts. Cain received a no-decision when he faced the Marlins on May 25, surrendering two runs and five hits in six innings as the Giants lost, 5-4.
away_pitcher_note: Once again, Olsen pitched good enough to win but didn't end up getting the victory. The 24-year-old limited the Cardinals to three runs in seven innings on Thursday while striking out six without walking a batter just five days after hurting his ankle, but his offense was held scoreless. In 10 of his 25 starts this season, Olsen has given up three runs or less but has failed to record a win, registering a loss in three of those games. He left after throwing 105 pitches -- 74 for strikes.

home_pitcher_note: Palmer endured a rough Major League debut on Saturday in Atlanta, allowing six runs and seven hits in 2 1/3 innings as the Giants lost, 11-5. Palmer, pressed into the rotation when Jonathan Sanchez went on the disabled list with a strained left shoulder, hadn't pitched in six days, which might have partly accounted for his ineffectiveness. He walked four and threw only 35 strikes in 66 pitches. Palmer vowed to pound the strike zone early in the count more frequently and throw more breaking pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson picked up the no-decision, and the Marlins dropped their first game in seven Johnson starts this year. The 6-foot-7 right-hander left after throwing 112 pitches through six innings with a two-run lead, but the Cubs hit a three-run homer in the ninth to get the win. Johnson allowed three runs on five hits while walking three and striking out eight -- which ties his career high.

home_pitcher_note: Johnson deserved a better fate in his last start, against the Astros. The Big Unit made one mistake, but it wound up costing him the game. His split-finger fastball to Ty Wigginton drifted back out over the plate and was hit for a three-run homer. That proved to be all the scoring in the game, as Roy Oswalt combined with Jose Valverde on a two-hitter. Johnson has 294 wins and will make eight more starts this year, including this one.
away_pitcher_note:
Sanchez was able to notch a win against the Cubs on Saturday despite not having his best stuff. The 24-year-old said he was having a hard time getting his breaking ball over, and because of that, he ended up issuing a season-high five walks and left after throwing 96 pitches -- 54 for strikes -- in 5 1/3 innings. 
But Sanchez did a good job of getting out of jams and gave up just one run on three hits while striking out six in his fourth start since coming back from shoulder surgery.

home_pitcher_note: Petit has pitched well given his inconsistent schedule. As the team's fifth starter, he pitched on seven days' rest in his last start. He got the win in that one, as the D-backs beat the Astros, 11-5. Petit allowed two runs on four hits over seven innings. In his last three starts, he is 1-2 but has a 3.71 ERA. Petit doesn't overwhelm you with his stuff, but he commands it well and has a good feel for pitching.
away_pitcher_note: Volstad did a nice job of getting out of jams while giving up two runs in six-plus innings against the Cubs on Sunday. Through the first three innings, Volstad tossed 63 pitches and put six runners on base but didn't surrender a run. But, after cruising through the next three without allowing a run, the 21-year-old started off the seventh by giving up two hits and left the game. After that, the Cubs put eight runs on the board -- two charged to Volstad -- and he had to settle for the second no-decision of his rookie year.

home_pitcher_note: Since taking a perfect game into the eighth inning against the Padres on July 29, Davis has struggled. His last outing -- also against the Padres -- showed that he might be turning the corner. The lefty allowed a pair of runs on seven hits over six innings. The biggest key for Davis is throwing strikes early in the count. When he does that, he's able to expand the zone. When he falls behind, he has to come in with his fastball and gets into trouble.
away_pitcher_note: A dubious distinction came to an end the last time Nolasco took the mound. The 25-year-old right-hander recorded his first career complete game, beating San Francisco, 6-0, last Tuesday at AT&T Park. The complete game snapped a string of 301 straight games by Florida pitchers without a complete game, which is a Major League record. Nolasco struck out 11 and walked just one, while allowing just two hits. It was also the Marlins' first complete-game shutout since Dontrelle Willis blanked the Phillies, 3-0, on Sept. 10, 2006. The 12 wins also was a personal high for Nolasco, who won 11 as a rookie in 2006.

home_pitcher_note: Jurrjens couldn't bounce back from first-inning struggles against the Mets on Wednesday. He was tagged for five runs (three earned), and his pitch count inflated to 44 through the opening inning. Jurrjens is 1-4 with a 4.35 ERA in his last five starts, and Wednesday night marked the first time he has not thrown at least six innings since May 31. He have up six hits through five innings, recording three walks and no strikeouts. Jurrjens is 1-1 with a 5.25 ERA in two games against Florida this season.
away_pitcher_note: Olsen's record is a bit deceiving, because he's pitched better than his string of dropping four consecutive decisions. In his last outing, a no-decision at San Francisco, the 24-year-old lefty carried a one-run lead into the sixth inning. But he was tagged for four hits in that inning, and surrendered three runs. Olsen exited after six innings, having allowed four runs on nine hits. The lefty has faced the Braves twice this season. He won on April 15, but wasn't involved in the decision on June 2.

home_pitcher_note: Hampton gave his team a chance to win Thursday night, holding the Mets to three runs in his sixth start of the season. After injuries kept him off the mound for three years, he has grown more comfortable with each start of 2008. Hampton said the velocity on his fastball is returning, and it hit 90 mph several times Thursday. He scattered eight hits, striking out two with one walk to come away with the no-decision. Physically, Hampton said he felt good on the mound, and he is making progress with consistent quality pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson has worked at least six innings in five consecutive starts. But in his last outing, the right-hander was not involved in the decision. Still, he was effective at San Francisco, posting a quality start. Johnson gave up three runs on nine hits with four strikeouts at AT&T Park. Johnson has made eight strong starts since coming off the disabled list and seeing his first action on July 10. He has not yielded more than four runs, and in seven of his starts he didn't give up more than three runs.

home_pitcher_note: Based simply on his stuff, the Braves still have plenty of faith in Morton. But while issuing a career-high five walks and retiring just 10 of the 14 batters he faced against the Cardinals on Friday, the 24-year-old right-hander once again showed his youth. Control has been a constant issue for Morton, who hasn't completed three innings in two of his previous three starts. He started this month by allowing just two earned runs in his first 14 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez was pretty solid in his last outing, even though he didn't factor into the decision or record a quality start. The 24-year-old yielded four runs on eight hits in 6 1/3 innings. He added seven strikeouts while walking one in a no-decision at Arizona. What stood out is how Sanchez handled himself and battled head-to-head against Randy Johnson. This will be Sanchez's sixth start of the season.

home_pitcher_note: The 21-year-old will have a big test in the series opener with New York. Volstad deserved a better fate in his last start, a loss at Arizona. In 5 1/3 innings, he allowed four runs, but with a break from his defense, he probably could have escaped with just two runs allowed. Volstad has logged 50 innings in his rookie career, with just two home runs allowed. In nine MLB appearances, and eight starts, Volstad has struck out 32 and walked 23. He's given up 48 total hits.
away_pitcher_note: John Maine will miss his scheduled start Friday after being placed on the 15-day disabled list Monday with a bone spur in his right shoulder. A day off Thursday gives the Mets options and manager Jerry Manuel said it will allow them to go without a fifth starter until Sept. 2. Perez will likely start in Maine's spot Friday, going on regular rest. Against the Astros on Sunday, Perez allowed four runs in 6 1/3 innings. He flashed his mid-90s fastball with eight strikeouts. Perez held the Marlins scoreless through seven innings in his previous start against Florida on Aug. 8.

home_pitcher_note: On a roll, Nolasco returns home after two dominating performances out West. The 25-year-old followed up his two-hit shutout in San Francisco by limiting the D-backs to three hits and two runs in 7 1/3 innings at Chase Field. In those two games, Nolasco combined to strike out 21 and walk two, while allowing five hits and two runs in 16 1/3 innings. With 13 wins, Nolasco has established a career high in victories, and he's won three of his past four decisions.
away_pitcher_note: Pelfrey continued his recent dominance with his second straight complete-game performance on Monday night. He came within two outs of a shutout before the Astros scored their first run of the night. Pelfrey scattered six hits and struck out six without recording a walk. A few weeks earlier, manager Jerry Manuel had expressed interest in giving Pelfrey some extra rest because of the high number of innings he has piled up, but the young pitcher has been economical with his pitches, holding his pitch count total to just 108 through his nine innings Monday. The Marlins have been Pelfrey's one weak spot this season. He is 0-3 with a 10.66 ERA against the Fish.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, against the Braves on Tuesday, Olsen had a rough first inning but rolled the rest of the way in his 5 1/3-inning outing, which resulted in a no-decision after Atlanta pulled off a four-run ninth inning in a walk-off win. In the first inning, Olsen gave up three quick runs, and that eventually led him to a high pitch count, which resulted in his ninth outing of less than six innings. Olsen finished off having allowed four runs on five hits while walking three and striking out three. He left after throwing 103 pitches and got his 13th no-decision of the year despite leaving with a 6-4 lead.
away_pitcher_note: Martinez gave up one run through the first four innings on Tuesday, holding the Phillies at bay as the Mets surged past them. But the fifth inning ruined the veteran's night, upping his total earned runs allowed to five. He escaped with a no-decision, eight strikeouts and two walks, and, though the Mets led when he left the game, the bullpen was unable to hold the lead. Martinez also pushed his arm with 110 pitches, 69 for strikes. Next are the Marlins, whom he faced April 1, allowing four runs in 3 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Johnson continued his dominant comeback from Tommy John elbow ligament replacement surgery by tossing his first career complete game in a win against the Braves on Wednesday. The 24-year-old gave up just one run on four hits while walking three and striking out eight. In his last two innings, Johnson got into a couple of jams with runners in scoring position and less than two outs, but he was able to get away unscathed. The Marlins are now 7-2 when Johnson toes the rubber.
away_pitcher_note: While allowing three earned runs or less and completing at least six innings in his past three starts, Hampton is starting to quiet many of his doubters. The 35-year-old southpaw completed eight innings and allowed three runs in Wednesday's loss to the Marlins. He has steadily regained confidence and shown durability since returning to the mound on July 26, after spending more than three years battling multiple injuries.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez didn't have his best stuff in a loss to the Braves on Thursday. And it was evident from the get-go. Although he didn't give up a run in the first, the 24-year-old was tossed 29 pitches that inning, which led to a rather short outing. Sanchez pitched just five innings, yielding four runs on five hits while striking out two and walking a season-high five. In his last two starts, the Venezuela native has given up eight runs in 11 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Morton provided the finest start of his young career on Thursday, when he limited the Marlins to one baserunner in the first five innings and two runs over six innings.  After allowing 10 of the 14 batters he faced to reach safely on Aug. 22, the 24-year-old rookie right-hander worked on his alignment and proved much more aggressive in the strike zone.  The Braves have raved about his stuff over the past year and as he continues to make mental and mechanical adjustments, he's providing indication that his future is bright.

home_pitcher_note: After a rough first inning that saw him give up the game's first run, Volstad was masterful against the Mets in a no-decision on Friday -- which saw the Marlins lose after a two-out, ninth-inning grand slam by Carlos Beltran. Volstad pitched 6 1/3 innings, giving up just the one run on five hits and three walks before exiting with a 2-1 lead in hand in the seventh inning. After the first inning, Volstad gave up just three hits and threw 78 pitches through 5 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Since becoming one of the most pleasant surprises the Braves have seen this year, Campillo has struggled. The 29-year-old right-hander has gone 1-3 with a 7.86 ERA in his past five starts. In the six starts that preceded this skid, he was 3-1 with a 1.77 ERA. One of his finest starts of the year came at Dolphin Stadium on July 21, when he limited the Marlins to two hits over seven scoreless innings. His offspeed repertoire could prove maddening to Florida's aggressive lineup.

home_pitcher_note: The Cardinals could still get clever with this spot, but it's unlikely. Looper had been pitching extremely well before his dud in Houston on Saturday, and since becoming a starter he's pitched very well against the Marlins. He'll be aiming for a career-best 13th win, though he'll also be trying to avoid falling back to .500. If Looper keeps the ball down, which he couldn't do against the Astros, he'll be fine.
away_pitcher_note: In a no-decision against the Mets on Saturday, Nolasco wasn't his usual, dominant self, but he was able to do just enough to keep his team in the ballgame, which led to an eventual walk-off win. The 25-year-old gave up two runs in the first inning but only scattered one more in his next five. What's most impressive is Nolasco struck out eight batters while issuing only one walk. Over his last seven starts, he's struck out 59 batters and walked just four.

home_pitcher_note: In Wellemeyer's last outing, he picked up the loss, despite allowing just one run on four hits in seven strong innings against the Astros, as they shut out the Cards, 3-0, at Minute Maid Park. Wellemeyer was hard on himself after the game because he couldn't put a bunt down, which could have led to a run. The right-hander is 2-1 with a 2.38 ERA in his career against the Marlins, spanning four outings, one start.
away_pitcher_note: The long ball plagued Olsen in a loss to the Mets on Sunday. That afternoon saw the 24-year-old give up three solo shots, which tied his season high, and exit after throwing 104 pitches in 6 1/3 innings. In the seventh, Olsen was charged with three more runs and threw 15 pitches to four batters before his outing ended. Over his past five starts, Olsen has given up 22 runs in 27 2/3 innings, posting a 6.67 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Plenty has gone wrong on the pitching side for the Cardinals this year, especially when it comes to injured hurlers. There's this good news, though: Wainwright looks like himself. In three games since he returned from the disabled list, Wainwright has 13 strikeouts, three walks and one homer allowed. He's still building back to full strength and sharpness, but if this is building mode, then clearly there's a lot to like.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson has logged six straight quality starts -- minimum of six innings and no more than three runs. The 24-year-old right-hander did struggle, however, in his last start -- a no-decision against the Braves. It was the second straight time Johnson faced Atlanta. On Aug. 27, he tossed a complete-game, four-hitter, and won, 4-1. He threw a season-high 113 pitches on that day. But in his Sept. 1 contest with Atlanta in Miami, Johnson gave up three runs in six innings. The Braves scratched out nine hits, but Johnson didn't issue a walk. The right-hander struck out eight.

home_pitcher_note: Aside from a rain-shortened outing in July, Wednesday's no-decision against the Nationals was Blanton's shortest outing since he joined the Phillies midseason. The right-hander lasted four innings, giving up four runs on six hits. The right-hander was billed as an innings eater when he came over from Oakland, but he has lasted seven innings only twice in nine starts with the Phillies. Blanton has yet to face the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez was locked up in a wild one in his last start on Tuesday. Despite logging his career shortest start -- three innings -- the 24-year-old was not involved in the decision. Sanchez was tagged for six runs on eight hits in his showdown with the Braves. With his command off, he threw 64 pitches, 43 for strikes. Sanchez has faced the Phillies already this season, tossing five innings in a loss at Citizens Bank Park on Aug. 6. The right-hander gave up four runs that day, three of which were earned.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick has struggled against the Marlins this season with a 6.10 ERA in two outings. Kendrick was skipped in the rotation after posting a 9.14 ERA in his past five starts, and will be looking to redeem himself.
away_pitcher_note: The 21-year-old rookie continues to turn in fine performances. Pitching into September for the first time, Volstad has logged 62 1/3 innings at the big league level thus far. Add in another 91 during his tenure in the Minor Leagues, and Volstad has 153 1/3 innings total this season. Volstad comes off a no-decision against the Braves where he gave up three runs on six hits in six innings. He did walk five, which is a personal high. On Aug. 7 at Philadelphia, Volstad threw six shutout innings in a victory.

home_pitcher_note: Myers continued to dominate on Friday against the Mets, keeping New York scoreless on three hits over eight innings. It was just the latest chapter of what has been a remarkable turnaround for Myers since he was sent down to Triple-A Lehigh Valley in July. Since his return to Major League action on July 23, the right-hander is 6-1 with a 1.55 ERA. He was beaten by the Marlins on June 10, giving up five runs in 5 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Nolasco had a strong outing last Friday against the Cardinals, but a lack of run support forced him to take a no-decision. Nolasco allowed just one run through seven innings while fanning four and not issuing a walk. Opponents are hitting just .240 against Nolasco. Having already recorded 184 2/3 innings, Nolasco is well on his way toward reaching the 200-inning plateau.

home_pitcher_note: The 24-year-old left-hander seeks his first victory since July 19, when he took the decision against the Phillies. Olsen has gone nine straight starts without a win. He is 0-6 in those contests. Olsen comes off a setback at St. Louis, where he gave up four runs on five hits in six innings. Olsen is 1-0 in two starts against the Nationals this season.
away_pitcher_note: Martis had a successful Major League debut on Thursday, against the Braves. He threw five innings and gave up two runs on four hits. Martis managed to get the butterflies out of his system after he struck out Gregor Blanco to start the bottom of the first inning. Martis didn't know the significance of getting the first out of his career until pitching coach Randy St. Claire told him to throw the ball into the dugout.

home_pitcher_note: In his 11th start, Johnson suffered his first loss. The 24-year-old right-hander still pitched pretty effectively, despite being tagged with the loss at St. Louis. In 6 2/3 innings, he gave up three runs, while striking out five and walking two. The Marlins are 8-3 in games that Johnson has started. On the season, Johnson has logged 70 1/3 innings, striking out 61 while walking just 22.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Redding pitched six innings and gave up two earned runs at Turner Field. He will pitch against the Marlins on Saturday. In his last start against them on May 9, Redding lasted 5 1/3 innings and gave up six runs -- five earned -- on four hits. Manager Manny Acta said that Redding wasn't pounding the strike zone. Redding walked five batters and three of them scored.

home_pitcher_note: After two straight rough outings, the Marlins are sticking with Sanchez in his normal rotation spot. He actually gets an extra day of rest with an off-day sandwiched in. Sanchez has produced his two shortest stints as a big leaguer. Last Monday at Philadelphia, he lasted just 1 2/3 innings, giving up five runs on five hits. His start before that lasted three innings in a no-decision against the Braves. Before facing the Phillies on Sept. 8, Sanchez was averaging 5 2/3 innings per start in his career, or over his first 30 MLB starts. Sanchez insists that his right shoulder is fine. The team is urging him to be more aggressive attacking the zone. Sanchez had surgery on that shoulder in June of 2007, and he's thrown 39 innings this season in eight starts.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, he went six innings and gave up four runs against the Braves. It marked the fourth time in five starts that Balester has gone at least six innings. Balester will face the Marlins for the first time since he made his Major League debut against them on July 1. Balester pitched five innings and gave up one run.

home_pitcher_note: Volstad left last Tuesday's start against the Phillies early after being struck by a hard comebacker off the bat of Carlos Ruiz in the third inning. Volstad finished off the frame but was replaced for the top of the fourth, finishing the night giving up one run on two hits with two strikeouts in the no-decision. After the game, the injury was described as a bruised right shin for the 21-year-old rookie, who was icing it but did not get an X-ray. Because of the off-day on Monday, the Marlins could push Volstad back to Wednesday for precautionary reasons.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt was brilliant again in his last outing, throwing his second shutout in a row in a win over the Pirates. Oswalt set a club record for consecutive scoreless innings with 32 1/3, breaking JR Richard's mark of 31, set in 1980. Oswalt last faced the Marlins on April 11 at Minute Maid Park, with disastrous results. He yielded eight runs on nine hits and lasted just four innings.

home_pitcher_note: Chalk it up as yet another solid outing by Nolasco last Wednesday. In a win against the division-rival Phillies, the 25-year-old gave up three runs in 7 2/3 innings. In that game, Nolasco struck out eight batters while only waling one -- a stat indicative of his recent success. Over his last nine starts -- which has seen him go 4-1 with a 2.68 ERA -- Nolasco has struck out 71 batters while only walking five.
away_pitcher_note: Backe was told he was a go for Wednesday in Florida, which will mark his first start since Sept. 2. The right-hander missed one start due to elbow soreness but never thought he'd be sideline for long. Backe is 1-1 with a 1.96 ERA over six career games (three starts) versus the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: At last, Olsen is working off a win. By beating the Nationals in his last outing, the 24-year-old lefty ended a string of nine straight starts without a victory. He had gone from July 19 against the Phillies until now. He did win two straight from July 9-19. Olsen had dropped six consecutive decisions. He won despite walking four and allowing six hits. Admittedly, he didn't have his best stuff. Olsen has logged 183 2/3 innings on the season, a career most. He threw 180 2/3 innings a year ago.
away_pitcher_note: The Astros put Arias in injured starter Wandy Rodriguez's place several days ago because they didn't want to take Chris Sampson out of the bullpen and Arias was the only other long relief option. It was a eureka decision, as Arias pitched a career-high five scoreless innings against Pittsburgh in his first career start Monday night.

home_pitcher_note: It could've been yet another dominant night for Johnson on Saturday against the Nationals. But it was pretty successful either way. The 24-year-old limited Washington to just two runs on six hits while walking just one and striking out a career-high nine to get the win. Through the first five innings, Johnson gave up just three hits and kept the Nationals scoreless, but Washington tacked on two runs with a two-out rally in the sixth to shorten Johnson's night. He has now recorded eight straight quality starts.
away_pitcher_note: Don't be fooled by his record. The Brett Myers that began this season for the Phillies and the Brett Myers that returned after a July stint in the Minor Leagues are two totally different pitchers. Before being optioned to Triple-A Lehigh Valley, Myers was 3-9 with a 5.84 ERA. Since returning, he's  7-2 with a 1.80 ERA in 11 starts. Myers' latest dominant effort came Sunday night, as he took the ball on three days rest to pitch the second game of a doubleheader against the Brewers. Nine innings later, the right-hander had his second complete-game victory of the season, holding the Brewers to one run on two hits. Myers is 1-2 with a 5.23 ERA against the Marlins this season.

home_pitcher_note: Even though he is coming off a no-decision, Sanchez is encouraged by his outing against the Nationals. After two straight starts where he didn't last longer than three innings, the fact Sanchez went seven innings in his no-decision shows progress. The 24-year-old right-hander matched his season high for innings. He also threw seven innings in a loss at St. Louis on Aug. 11. His seven innings and three runs (two earned), marked his first quality start since Aug. 11. Sanchez has been working on his fastball command, and the results were seven strikeouts. On Sept. 8 at Philadelphia, Sanchez was roughed up for five runs in 1 1/3 innings in a loss.
away_pitcher_note: In working seven innings on Sunday, Blanton turned in his longest effort since Aug. 8. The righty allowed three runs on five hits and two walks. He had posted a 5.58 in six outings before that, during which he was battling right bicep tendinitis.

home_pitcher_note: The 21-year-old has two more starts to go. After this one, he is lined up to face the Mets at Shea Stadium on Sept. 26. The rookie is getting a big taste of a pennant race. Thus far, he is up to the task. In his last outing, he shut down the Astros, limiting them to one run on five hits in eight innings. It was his second-blongest outing of the year. On July 11, in his first MLB start, he lasted 8 2/3 innings against the Dodgers. Had he been working on a shutout against the Astros, manager Fredi Gonzalez said Volstad would have come out for the ninth inning in hopes of the complete game.
away_pitcher_note: Though he's given up six runs twice in his previous five outings, Moyer has posted a 3.38 ERA overall in his previous 19 outings and is still going strong at 45. He said he was trying to force things in his previous outing and may have been feeling some effects of working on three days' rest in a Sept. 11 outing.

home_pitcher_note: After rough times most of the season, it's starting to come together for Harang. Over his last six starts, Harang has a 1.93 ERA. In Wednesday's 3-0 win over the Cardinals, he fired a six-hit shutout, with no walks and four strikeouts. The right-hander has made some mechanical tweaks lately to get improvement and no longer shows any signs from the sore right forearm that put him on the disabled list earlier this summer.
away_pitcher_note: Nolasco has strung together 10 straight quality starts, and he has now won four straight decisions. The right-hander has won 15 games, the most by any Marlins starter since Dontrelle Willis' 22 victories in 2005. Nolasco now has 199 1/3 innings on the season. He's never reached 200, but will be primed against the Reds in a game that makes up a May 15 rainout. Nolasco faced the Reds on May 14 at Cincinnati. He worked 4 2/3 innings in a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Prior to last Wednesday's action, Martis looked good in his first two big league starts, but the third time wasn't the charm as the Mets outslugged the Nationals, 9-7, at Nationals Park. Martis had a feeling it would be a tough night based on what he went through during his bullpen session a few hours earlier. Martis had trouble commanding his fastball in the session, and he paid for it during the game. Martis lasted three innings and gave up six runs on five hits.
away_pitcher_note: For the first time since July 9 and July 19, Olsen has experienced back-to-back wins. The 24-year-old lefty goes for three straight for the first time since April 9-20. Olsen has two starts left, and he is coming off one of his better efforts. In rainy conditions, he gave up one run on three hits in seven innings. Olsen walked one and struck out seven, beating the Astros at home. On Sept. 12, Olsen beat the Nationals, giving up one run in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Redding, who was trying to win his 11th game of the season, had a rough outing last Thursday. He lasted three innings and gave up five runs (four earned) on seven hits. Redding didn't have one clean inning. It was the second day in a row a Nationals starter couldn't get past the third inning. Shairon Martis also went three innings and gave up six runs to the Mets on Wednesday. Fortunately for the Nationals, the bullpen hasn't been taxed, thanks to the relievers Washington promoted on Sept. 1.
away_pitcher_note: On Friday, Johnson saw his streak of eight straight quality starts get snapped, but he still picked up a win against the Phillies. On a night when the 24-year-old clearly didn't have his best stuff, Johnson gave up a season-high six runs (five earned) on seven hits, while walking one and striking out six. Going into that start, Johnson had posted a 2.93 ERA in his previous four games. This year, he is 1-0 with a 3.00 ERA in one start against the Nationals.

home_pitcher_note: Last Friday was one of Balester's worst outings. He lasted five innings and gave up five runs on nine hits against the Padres. The game seesawed back and forth in the first eight innings. After two innings, the Nationals had a 2-0 lead off right-hander Dirk Hayhurst, but San Diego would come back and take a 4-2 lead by the top of the fourth inning against Balester. Kevin Kouzmanoff highlighted the scoring with a two-run homer. Washington would tie the score in the bottom of the fourth. With Mike Ekstrom on the mound, Balester hit an RBI single and Emilio Bonifacio walked with the bases loaded. The runs were charged to Hayhurst. Both teams would score a run in the sixth inning. Will Venable would drive in the go-ahead run off Balester, while Clay Hensley gave up a sacrifice fly to Bonifacio.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez pitched pretty well in a loss to the Phillies on Saturday, but he had to leave early after suffering a cramp in his right hamstring with two outs in the top of the sixth. The 24-year-old ended up allowing three runs (two earned) on four hits, while walking three and striking out eight -- which matched his season high -- before leaving with 95 pitches under his belt. The unearned run came on an RBI single by Chase Utley, who drove in a run because of errant throws by third baseman Jorge Cantu and Sanchez himself.

home_pitcher_note: The fact that Mike Pelfrey extended his streak on Sunday to five straight starts without a victory was no fault of his own. Pelfrey allowed only three runs to the Braves over six innings, departing after walking the leadoff man in the seventh. He pitched plenty well enough to win, but another bullpen implosion ensured that Pelfrey would leave with a no-decision. In four starts against the Marlins this season, Pelfrey is 0-3 with a 7.91 ERA -- though his best start against them came earlier this month, when he allowed two runs over 6 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Volstad gave up three runs (two earned) in five innings during a loss against the Phillies on Sunday. The outing saw the 21-year-old reach a professional high in innings pitched with 169 1/3. Volstad gave up six hits while striking out three and walking two. Two of the runs came on a rare home run. This season, Volstad has only given up three dingers, and in 91 innings for Double-A Carolina, he didn't allow a single long ball. In his only start against the Mets this season, Volstad gave up only one run in 6 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: After days of withholding his Saturday starter, manager Jerry Manuel finally admitted that pitcher "A," the option who would be counted on to throw in the event that the Mets were tied or trailed in the Wild Card, was Johan Santana. The Mets' ace will pitch on three days' rest, a time crunch which is multiplied by the fact that Santana threw a career-high 125 pitches in his last start Tuesday.
