It was a successful start, though, as Santana limited the Cubs to two runs over eight innings. The only other time Santana has pitched on three days' rest was in Game 1 of the 2004 ALDS, when he allowed one run in five innings against the Yankees.
away_pitcher_note: Nolasco was in line for his 16th win in his last start, but settled for a no-decision after Florida was unable to hold a 4-1 lead in the seventh inning at Cincinnati on Monday. Nolasco allowed three runs on six hits in six-plus innings. The 25-year-old ace of the staff did surpass the 200-innings-pitched mark that day, as he now has 205 1/3 innings. This will be Nolasco's 32nd start, as it winds down his terrific season. Nolasco has struck out 176 and walked 41.

home_pitcher_note: With Johan Santana pitching Saturday, Oliver Perez will also be asked to pitch on three days' rest as the Mets try to make a push for the playoffs. Perez lasted only 4 1/3 innings in his last start Wednesday, allowing five earned runs to the Cubs on six hits and five walks. Against the Marlins, Perez is 3-0 with a 2.03 ERA in 31 innings this season.
away_pitcher_note: Olsen's hopes of ending the season with a .500 record were shattered when he suffered a loss against the Nationals on Tuesday, giving up four runs (three earned) on eight hits while walking one and striking out two in five innings. Still, 2008 has already seen the 24-year-old reach his career high in innings -- going into his last start with 195 2/3, up from 180 2/3 in 2006 -- and, on Sunday, he'll tie his career high in starts with 33. Over his last five starts, he's 2-3 with a 4.46 ERA (15 earned runs in 30 1/3 innings).

home_pitcher_note:
Last year mattered when determining Florida's Opening Day starter. After establishing himself as one of the top right-handers in the National League in '08, Nolasco was rewarded with his first Opening Day start of his young career.

Nolasco comes off a 15-8 season with a 3.52 ERA. The 26-year-old logged a team high 212 1/3 innings over 34 games with 32 starts. Because he was so valuable and so effective as the season wore on, he entered Spring Training with the inside edge to assume the role of ace.

Also impressive about Nolasco's 2008 season was the fact he struck out 186 while walking just 42. He has a goal of walking fewer than 25 this season. For his career, Nolasco is 5-1 with a 3.53 ERA lifetime vs. Washington, including 2-0 (2.08 ERA) last year.
away_pitcher_note:
Manager Manny Acta says he picked Lannan to start the opener against the Marlins because he had 21 quality starts last year.

An 11th-round pick in the 2005 First-Year Player Draft, Lannan had a rapid rise to the big leagues. Two years after being drafted, Lannan went from Class A Potomac to the Majors in one season and had a respectable 4.15 ERA in six big-league games. By early last season, Lannan was the team's No. 1 starter.

Lannan will face a tough Marlins lineup that includes shortstop Hanley Ramirez and second baseman Dan Uggla. It will be the first time Lannan will face Florida during his career. The Marlins were 14-3 against the Nationals last season. Lannan hopes he pitches like last season and puts his start on Wednesday afternoon against the Blue Jays behind him. He gave up seven runs in 4 2/3 innings in a 7-6 loss. Lannan said it was best to get the bad start out of the way before he faces the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: A year ago, Johnson opened the season on the disabled list, as he was recovering from Tommy John ligament replacement surgery. This year, the 25-year-old is the No. 2 starter. Johnson made a strong showing in the second half of '08, finishing up with seven wins in eight decisions. He logged 87 1/3 innings. Two of his wins a year ago were against Washington.
away_pitcher_note: Olsen will face the Marlins, his former team, for the first time in his career. The southpaw threw a career-high 201 2/3 innings last year. It was his best season since 2006, when he went 12-10 with a 4.04 ERA. It helped that he developed a changeup to go along with his fastball and slider.

home_pitcher_note: The 22-year-old Volstad is the youngest in a youthful rotation. A former first-round pick in 2005, Volstad was called up by the Marlins last July, and he became a fixture in the rotation, making 14 starts. This will be his first time facing the Nationals. In his first MLB start, he nearly went the distance, working 8 2/3 innings against the Dodgers.
away_pitcher_note: It will be interesting to see how Cabrera handles the bat in his Nationals debut. Learning how to swing the bat and bunt the ball are two reasons Cabrera didn't represent the Dominican Republic in the World Baseball Classic this spring. Prior to this season, Cabrera acknowledged that he was scared to swing the bat in fear he would get hit by the baseball. It also didn't help that he played in the American League. When he was with the Orioles, Cabrera only swung the bat when Baltimore played National League teams in Interleague Play. Now, Cabrera is in the NL, and he must learn how to do the little things with the bat.

home_pitcher_note: A starter not yet been named, but Sanchez could be the choice. If not, left-hander Andrew Miller will go in this spot. The 25-year-old right-handed Sanchez made 10 starts last year, all in the second half. He joined the rotation in July, as he was recovering from right shoulder surgery. Sanchez is 2-1 with a 3.63 ERA lifetime against the Mets.
away_pitcher_note: Maine will be making his first appearance in a regular-season game since Aug. 23. He had an uneven exhibition season but improved in his later starts. He allowed 40 baserunners in 23 2/3 innings and produced a 6.65 ERA in six appearances. He is starting the fourth game because he has been successful in Miami -- 2-0 and a 3.22 ERA in four career starts there -- and unsuccessful in Cincinnati, where the team opened it season -- 0-2 with an 11.00 in two starts. Maine has a 3-1 record and 2.75 ERA in six career starts against the Fish.

home_pitcher_note: With the Marlins going with a four-man rotation early, Nolasco will make his second start in the first five games. The right-hander faced the Mets six times last year, and he was 1-2 with a 3.48 ERA. For his career, he has faced New York 11 times, and he's 2-5 with a 6.27 ERA against them. During Opening Day on Monday, Nolasco got the win despite giving up five runs on six hits while striking out six and walking none. The 26-year-old retired nine of his first 10 batters before getting into some trouble in the fourth and sixth innings.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez hasn't pitched against the Marlins since Aug. 16, 2007, when he beat them. He has experience in the ballpark now called Dolphin Stadium, having made his first 70 starts for the Marlins from 1997-99. His career ERA in Miami, 3.86, is significantly lower than his overall ERA, 4.37. Hernandez has a 4-3 record in his 10 most recent starts against the Marlins. He produced a 3.07 ERA in five appearances -- two of them starts -- in 14 2/3 innings in Spring Training.

home_pitcher_note: Johnson picked up right where he left off the previous season during his first start of 2009. The 25-year-old pitched 6 2/3 shutout innings against the Nationals on Tuesday, giving up seven hits while striking out eight and walking none. Johnson left after throwing 106 pitches -- 75 for strikes. On Sunday, he'll face off against a Mets team he went 2-0 with a 3.95 ERA against last season.
away_pitcher_note: Pitching in the uncomfortable chill and rain in Cincinnati on Opening Day, Santana did what a starting pitcher is supposed to do -- afford his team a chance to win even when he isn't at the top of his game. Santana shut down the Reds on one hit and four walks for five innings, striking out seven Monday. The run he allowed came after he had spent an extended period on base in the top of the sixth. But he left the game with a lead, and that's all the Mets could ask for, given the conditions. Now he faces the Fish, a favorite entree. Santana produced a 3-0 record and 1.96 ERA in three starts and 23 innings against the Marlins last season. His career numbers against them are 5-0 and 1.83 in five games.

home_pitcher_note: Javier Vazquez limited the Phillies to three runs in six innings during a successful season debut that was ruined when his bullpen squandered a seven-run, seventh-inning lead on Wednesday.  The veteran right-hander enjoyed a stellar March that was highlighted on March 14, when he limited Team USA to one run in five innings of a World Baseball Classic game. Vazquez, who was obtained in a December trade with the White Sox, has gone 5-4 with a 3.45 ERA in 11 starts at Turner Field.  He hasn't faced the Marlins since 2005.
away_pitcher_note: During the series finale against the Nationals on Wednesday, Volstad's only troubles came in the first inning. That's when the 22-year-old right-hander gave up two runs -- one earned -- while throwing 27 pitches and getting behind five of the seven batters he faced. The rest of the way, however, Volstad looked as dominant as he did in the second half of last season. The Palm Beach Gardens, Fla., native went on to throw four no-hit frames thereafter while striking out seven batters -- a career-high -- and throwing 65 pitches. Volstad grew up a big Braves fan, and last season he went 0-1 with a 4.50 ERA in two starts against Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: Lowe opened the season by limiting the Phillies to two baserunners in eight innings. While not as dominant, he still proved to be impressive when he recorded six strikeouts and allowed the Nationals just one run in a three-inning effort that was halted because of a lengthy rain delay on Friday. He is 4-3 with a 4.59 ERA in eight career starts against the Marlins.  During his only outing against them last year, he allowed six runs -- three earned -- and eight hits in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Coming into his fourth season in the Major Leagues, Miller, the Marlins' No. 5 starter, will be making his first start of the year against the Braves. Last season, the 6-foot-7 23-year-old went 6-10 with a 5.87 ERA in 29 games -- 20 starts. Miller started the season in Florida's rotation, going 5-9 with a 5.63 ERA before landing on the 15-day disabled list with patella tendinitis in his right knee on July 18. After posting a 2.33 ERA in six rehab games, he was reinstated from his DL stint in September and finished off the season in the bullpen, giving up seven runs in 6 2/3 innings. The Gainesville, Fla., native is 2-0 with a miniscule 0.69 ERA in four career games against the Braves.

home_pitcher_note: Kawakami pitched around some early jitters and won his first Major League start while recording eight strikeouts and limiting the Nationals to three runs in six innings on Saturday night. Armed with an average fastball, the 33-year-old right-hander relies heavily on a slow curveball that proved to be effective during his successful 13-year career in Japan's Central League.
away_pitcher_note: Making his first start of the season, Sanchez was solid against the Mets on Friday, pitching five scoreless innings against a team he hadn't faced since 2007. The 25-year-old, who gave up four hits and three walks while striking out five, pitched out of trouble in his last two innings of work. In the fourth, he started with runners on first and second but got three straight outs. Then, in the fifth, Sanchez struck out Carlos Delgado with two men on base to end the inning and preserve a two-run lead. In his previous three years in the big leagues, Sanchez is 1-2 with a 5.09 ERA in four starts against the Braves.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Lannan pitched six innings and gave up four runs on nine hits against the Braves. He was given a 3-0 lead by the middle of the third inning against right-hander Kenshin Kawakami. But Lannan would give up the lead by the bottom of the fourth inning, no thanks to the left-handed-hitting Kelly Johnson and Jordan Schafer. To the surprise of manager Manny Acta, Lannan threw almost nothing but fastballs to Johnson and Schafer, and they ended up going a combined 5-for-7 against him. Acta wanted to see Lannan throw more breaking balls to those two hitters.
away_pitcher_note: Nolasco came into his Saturday outing with a 6.27 career ERA against the Mets, and those struggles continued when he gave up four runs on seven hits through five innings. The 26-year-old right-hander, who went 15-8 with a 3.52 ERA last season, has given up nine runs in 11 innings to start the season. On Saturday, Nolasco threw 87 pitches -- 54 for strikes -- and had his pitch count at 65 after four innings.

home_pitcher_note: On Sunday, Olsen was cruising during the first three innings, but got in trouble in the bottom of the fourth. After the southpaw recorded the first two outs of the inning, Olsen walked Brian McCann, and it went downhill after that. The Braves scored three runs, with Jeff Francoeur collecting the biggest hit, an RBI triple. But the Nationals would tie the score in the top of the fifth off right-hander Jair Jurrjens. Elijah Dukes hit a two-run double, then scored on an error by first baseman Martin Prado. But Atlanta retook the lead in the bottom of the inning off Olsen. Both Chipper Jones and McCann had RBI singles. Olsen ended up pitching five innings, giving up five runs on six hits. The outing was better than his season debut on Tuesday against the Marlins. In that game, he gave up eight runs in three innings.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson was as good as ever during a 2-1 win over the Mets and Johan Santana on Sunday, as he gave up just one run on five hits while striking out seven and walking one in his second career complete game. The 25-year-old right-hander retired 14 of the first 15 batters he faced, had a no-hitter going into the sixth inning and was very efficient. Johnson, who was consistently in the upper 90s with his fastball and had about a 10-mph difference with a changeup he used more often than usual, had just 69 pitches under his belt through his first six innings and finished with 113, including 77 for strikes. He needed just 10 pitches to get through a 1-2-3 fourth inning, only allowed four runners in scoring position and struck out six batters through the first five. Through 15 2/3 innings this season -- including a start against the Nationals -- Johnson has given up just one run on 12 hits.

home_pitcher_note: On Monday, Cabrera gave up one earned run in five innings against the Phillies. It helped lower his ERA to 4.91, which is the best among the Nationals starters. Cabrera will face the Marlins for the second time this season. In that first game, Cabrera became the first Nationals starter to pitch past the third inning. But the bad news was that Washington lost to the Marlins, 6-4, at Dolphin Stadium.
away_pitcher_note: On April 8, Volstad worked five innings and allowed two runs on his way to a win over the Nationals at Dolphin Stadium. Now, the 22-year-old gets to face them in Washington. This will be the 6-foot-8 right-hander's first start at Nationals Park. He struck out a career-high seven on April 8. Volstad enters the contest fresh off one of his finest outings. Opening Florida's three-city, nine-game road trip in Atlanta, he worked seven innings, giving up only three hits and one run, which came on Kelly Johnson's homer.

home_pitcher_note: An inability to establish his fastball command early was the ultimate downfall for Ohlendorf in his last start Wednesday, a five-inning outing in which he allowed eight hits and four runs. When Ohlendorf is sharp, he has his fastball sinking with ease and is able to then take advantage of his off-speed pitches to complement that fastball. He did that quite effectively in his first start of the season. Ohlendorf also fell behind too often in his most recent start, which forced him to endure some long counts early. This will be Ohlendorf's first career appearance against the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: The 23-year-old left-hander will make his first appearance against the Pirates. It comes after his first start, a no-decision against the Braves at Turner Field last Wednesday. Miller got off to a good start in Atlanta, allowing one run through four innings. But he got into trouble in the fifth inning, after being staked to a three-run lead. Miller gave up three runs in the inning, and was lifted before logging the third out. In 4 2/3 innings, he allowed four runs on four hits with two strikeouts. Considering he had been working out of the bullpen until then, pitch count is an issue for him. He threw 79 pitches at Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: If Karstens is going to keep his spot as the team's fifth starter, he's going to have to pitch deeper into games than he was able to in his first start of the season. A 17-day game layoff contributed to some rust in Karstens' first start of the year, but the biggest problem was Karstens' inability to throw strikes as his outing progressed. He walked five in four innings. Karstens isn't one to overpower hitters, making it even more crucial that he establish his fastball command early and stay efficient. Karstens has never faced the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: Working into trouble and then getting out of it has pretty much marked Sanchez's first two starts. Still, he's been able to execute when he's had to. In his last outing, at Atlanta on April 16, repeatedly flirted with danger, he turned in a quality start -- two runs in six innings. Still, he gave up eight hits and walked three, while striking out two. The only inning the Venezuelan native retired the side in order was the sixth. In four of the first five innings, he allowed two runners to reach after logging two outs.

home_pitcher_note: Maholm is 3-for-3 in the quality starts category after tossing seven scoreless innings in a win against the Braves on Friday. The lefty did not have his sharpest command, but he battled admirably and used some good defensive work behind him to his benefit. Maholm has quietly put himself among the best left-handed starters in the game as he continues to show he can find a way to keep teams off balance and guessing regardless of whether he has his best stuff. And you know he's on when the ground balls are coming with ease. Maholm is 2-3 with a 4.40 ERA in five career starts against the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Nolasco had a frustrating outing. The 26-year-old worked just four innings at Washington, giving up two runs on seven hits with a walk. He didn't have his best stuff, and he was lifted after 87 pitches. Physically, the right-hander is fine. He just was laboring and manager Fredi Gonzalez didn't want to put another stressful inning on him. Nolasco's lone win was on Opening Day against the Nationals. He is 1-2 with a 1.99 ERA in five games against the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Considering how dominant Johnson was in his first two starts of the season, he was due for a letdown. It came against the Nationals on Saturday. In the first inning, Austin Kearns belted a grand slam off Johnson, who gave up six runs in six innings. The encouraging part of the outing was that J.J., after allowing six runs in the first two innings, stayed in the game, tossing four straight scoreless frames before turning it over to the bullpen. Johnson ended up with a no-decision. Kearns' slam was the first homer Johnson had allowed since Sept. 19, 2008, against the Phillies. J.J. gave up two homers to the Phils that day -- Greg Dobbs and Ryan Howard.
away_pitcher_note: It may be surprising that Myers has been the team's most effective starter, but he has been. Myers has allowed just 18 hits in those three starts, but seven of them have been home runs. Still, he has pitched at least six innings in each of his starts and opponents have hit just .237 against him. If Myers can minimize his mistakes, he should continue to roll. And right now the Phillies need him because the rest of the rotation is struggling.

home_pitcher_note: His last time out, Volstad experienced the second shortest start in his career. At Washington, he worked 4 1/3 innings, and was not involved in the decision. A high pitch count was a problem, as he threw 98 pitches, and he exited with two runners on base. The only start of his career that has been shorter was on Sept. 9 at the Phillies, when he tossed three innings. Walks, thus far, have been an issue. He issued five walks, while striking out five, at Nationals Park. In 16 1/3 innings this season, Volstad has walked 11 to go along with 16 strikeouts. For his career, Volstad is 1-1 with a 1.93 ERA in three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Given that Park has an 8.68 ERA after two starts and that he barely beat left-hander J.A. Happ for the fifth spot in the Phillies' rotation in Spring Training, it might be natural to ask if the Phillies need to re-examine that fifth job. But manager Charlie Manuel said two starts is not enough to draw any conclusions about Park's performance. He will continue to get a chance to pitch. He actually pitched better than his line indicated in Sunday's 5-4 victory over the Padres (four runs in five innings). A defensive miscue in the third led to two runs.

home_pitcher_note: Called upon to temporarily take the place of injured starter Andrew Miller (oblique strain) in the rotation is expected to be Taylor, who would be making his first career Major League start in the series finale against the Phillies, although no official announcement has yet been made. The 24-year-old Taylor, a 10th-round pick by the Marlins in the 2006 First-Year Player Draft, owns a 3.08 ERA in four seasons in the Minor Leagues. In three starts for Double-A Jacksonville this season, Taylor's ERA is at 3.24, having struck out 10 while walking six in 16 2/3 innings. Last year, the Kentucky native pitched mostly for Class A Jupiter, where he went 11-6 with a 3.46 ERA in 23 games -- 22 starts -- for the Hammerheads. Taylor, who last pitched on Monday, wasn't in big league camp with the Marlins this spring but did start one Spring Training game, pitching three perfect innings. Taylor is known mostly a pitch-to-contact guy who possesses great control but not overpowering stuff. Throughout his Minor League career, he's averaged 1.4 walks per nine innings while striking out 6.6. With Miller not eligible to come off his disabled-list stint until May 6, Taylor could make two or three starts for Florida.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer pitched better in his last start Tuesday against the Milwaukee Brewers, allowing four runs in six-plus innings. That fourth run scored more than an hour after Moyer left the game because of a rain delay. It cost him his first quality start of the season, but there is reason to be optimistic. Moyer went 4-1 with a 2.81 ERA in five starts last season against the Marlins and is 11-1 with a 2.95 ERA in 12 starts against them in his career.

home_pitcher_note: Maine said after Wednesday night's poor start against the Cardinals that he discovered something with his delivery in the last few innings. After trying to make a mechanical change with his arms during his first three starts, Maine reverted to his old delivery for his final three innings of work and was much more successful. Maine has dominated Marlins hitters in his career so he should be poised for a strong start.
away_pitcher_note: This will already be Sanchez's second start against the Mets. The right-hander faced them in Florida on April 10, tossing five shutout innings but getting a no-decision. He's made four starts in his career against New York, going 2-1 with a 2.82 ERA in 22 1/3 innings. In his last start, against the Pirates, Sanchez gave up a run in each of the first three innings to get the loss, but finished strong and ended with a seven-inning, six-strikeout performance with just the three runs allowed.

home_pitcher_note: In three starts, the first of which was against the Marlins, Hernandez has gone from a victory to a no-decision to a loss, and his ERA has jumped from 2.70 to 4.63 to 7.31. He surrendered three home runs, two by Albert Pujols, in his 4 1/3 innings against the Cardinals Thursday. Right-handed hitters are batting .354 against him, compared with the .278 average left-handed hitters have produced. Even with his successful performance against them April 11 in Miami -- two runs in 6 2/3 innings -- he has a 6.37 ERA against the Marlins since the beginning of the 2006 season.
away_pitcher_note: Nolasco was roughed up against the Pirates on Wednesday, giving up six runs -- five earned -- while allowing eight hits, walking three and striking out five. The 26-year-old has struggled since coming off a breakout 2008 -- a year that saw him go 15-8 with a 3.52 ERA and earn the Opening Day start for '09. Through four starts this season, Nolasco has yet to register a quality start and has given up 16 earned runs in 21 innings. Despite his struggles, manager Fredi Gonzalez doesn't seem concerned, saying recently, "I'm sure he and [pitching coach] Mark [Wiley] have made some adjustments, but I've got all the confidence in the world that he'll get it. It's one of those things. ... He'll end up with the numbers he should end up with."

home_pitcher_note: The Mets' stopper is set to make his third start at Citi Field against the team that beat him April 12 in Miami. Santana has a 2-0 record and an 0.69 ERA at the Mets' new home. He hasn't lost at home -- Shea Stadium included -- in 11 starts. He has an 8-0 record and 1.34 ERA in those games. He is averaging 12.97 strikeouts per nine innings in his four 2009 starts and has allowed merely 23 base runners in 25 2/3 innings. The four runs the Mets scored against the Nationals Friday night increased, to eight, the number of runs they have scored for Santana this season. In his five most recent starts against the Marlins -- four with the Mets -- Santana has a 4-1 record and a 1.50 ERA in 36 innings. He has allowed 31 base runners and struck out 45.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start against the Phillies on Friday, Johnson was dominant while pitching seven shutout innings. He gave up just three hits while walking two and striking out eight, leaving the game after throwing 102 pitches -- 68 for strikes. The 25-year-old right-hander allowed just three runners in scoring position and ended his night by getting Greg Dobbs looking with runners on first and second and his team sporting a three-run lead. If not for a seven-run meltdown by closer Matt Lindstrom, the Marlins would've improved to 4-0 in games Johnson starts this season. On Wednesday, he'll face off against a team he gave up just one run against while pitching a complete game and edging out ace Johan Santana on April 12. Johnson is 5-0 with a 1.59 ERA in six career starts against New York.

home_pitcher_note: The lefty posted a quality start in his last outing against the Cardinals, but didn't get any offensive support. Marshall held the Redbirds to three runs on six hits and one walk over six innings, striking out five. He did his part, reaching on an error in the fifth which led to the Cubs' first run. He's 1-3 with a 4.38 ERA in his career against the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: Volstad got the no-decision against the Phillies on Saturday after yielding three runs on four hits through seven innings. The 22-year-old right-hander gave up two solo home runs -- to opposing pitcher Chan Ho Park and Ryan Howard -- and ended up walking one while striking out six. In the sixth, Volstad had the bases loaded with nobody out, but he got out of it with just one run across when he got Ryan Howard to ground into a double play and forced Jayson Werth into a groundout to shortstop. On Thursday, he'll face a Cubs team he gave up four runs to through 12 innings in two no-decisions last year.

home_pitcher_note: Harden picked up the win in his last start, a 10-3 decision against the Cardinals. He struck out nine and gave up four hits, including two solo homers, over six innings. Harden admitted he didn't feel right at the start of the game, but as it progressed, his fastball seemed to pick up a few miles per hour, and it helped his changeup. He was hitting 95 mph on the radar gun pretty regularly.
away_pitcher_note: Not much was known about the 24-year-old Taylor before he made his Major League debut against the Phillies on Sunday. Based on his Minor League numbers, though, it was pretty apparent that he didn't walk many batters. That, however, wasn't the case in his first big-league inning, when he threw 22 of his 38 pitches for balls and ended up giving up two runs. Taylor finished off that game allowing four runs on four hits and six walks in 3 2/3 innings as the Marlins were routed at home. But two of those runs came on a misplay by Jeremy Hermida. The 2006 10th-round Draft pick finished throwing 98 pitches -- 49 for strikes.

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander uncharacteristically invited his own doom in his last start, which he began with the NL's top strikeouts (13) to walks (2) ratio. In five innings against the Diamondbacks, he walked four men, two of whom scored to help defeat him. Lilly has a tough bounce-back assignment: The Marlins are the only MLB team he has never defeated, with a career record of 0-4 and 5.53 ERA in five starts against them.
away_pitcher_note: It wasn't all bad in Sanchez's last start. The right-hander did suffer a disappointing loss to the Mets at Citi Field. He did surrender a grand slam to Omir Santos in a six-run first inning. And he did log 40 pitches. From that point, though, you have to credit Sanchez for rebounding and soaking up five more innings, which took some pressure off the bullpen. In all, Sanchez worked six innings, allowing those six runs. His ERA rose from 2.50 to 4.13, however. Sanchez threw 108 pitches, a season high. Sanchez has faced the Cubs once in his career, and he won that decision. This will be his first start ever at Wrigley Field.

home_pitcher_note: Both Zambranos were back in action in his last start, Tuesday in Arizona. The pitcher entered with a 4.85 ERA and held the D-backs to three runs in seven innings. The hitter had been 0-for-9 before logging a three-hit game that included his 17th career homer. Zambrano goes for career win No. 99 against a Marlins team he has handled well in the past.
away_pitcher_note: April was pretty much a struggle for Nolasco. In his five starts, he didn't have an outing longer than six innings, and he reached that total twice. His lone win came on Opening Day, and he had his troubles with shutdown innings. In his last start, at the Mets on April 28, Nolasco had a no-decision, giving up four runs in five innings. Nolasco kept his team in the game and left with the Marlins trailing by a run. Nolasco came up through the Cubs' system, and he was traded to Florida after the 2005 season as part of the Juan Pierre trade. In his lone appearance at Wrigley Field, Nolasco threw two scoreless innings in 2006. It was during his rookie season and it was his first MLB win.

home_pitcher_note: The Marlins are 8-3 in Johnson's 11 starts. But one of those loses came the last time the 6-foot-7 right-hander faced the Brewers. On May 14 at Milwaukee, Johnson worked a season-low four innings in a no-decision. He felt some fatigue in his right shoulder, but since then has rebounded nicely. Johnson has had nine quality starts. The right-hander comes off a victory against the Mets at Citi Field in which he gave up two runs in seven innings, walking two and striking out five.
away_pitcher_note: In an 8-3 loss his last time vs. the Astros on Tuesday, Harang lasted only five innings and allowed six runs (five earned) on six hits with one walk and two strikeouts. While he wasn't overly sharp, he didn't get much help from his defense, which was charged with three errors that led to runs. In eight career starts vs. the Marlins, the right-hander is 3-2 with a 6.70 ERA. Over 45 2/3 innings, he's allowed 70 hits and 12 homers.

home_pitcher_note: "Efficient" and "extremely effective" are a couple of ways you could describe Volstad's last start. Unfortunately for the 22-year-old, he ended up with a no-decision. In terms of being on the mark, however, Volstad was brilliant during his April 30th start against the Cubs at Wrigley Field. In seven innings, the 6-foot-8 sinkerball pitcher threw just 83 pitches, with 58 for strikes. He limited the Cubs to three hits, didn't walk a batter, and struck out five. His problem was that two of the hits left the ballpark. Volstad issued back-to-back homers to Milton Bradley and Mike Fontenot. Still, he went seven innings for the third time in five starts this year.
away_pitcher_note: In a 3-0 victory over the Astros on Wednesday, Volquez wasn't the overpowering pitcher he usually is but had one dominant performance. He threw eight shutout innings (a career high) and dealt with just three base runners. He had one hit allowed (in the first inning), one hit batter and one walk. He threw only 106 pitches and at one point, retired 17 in a row. It was a total turnaround from the seven walk outing he had on Friday vs. the Braves, which included five in one inning. Volquez had six strikeouts but worked ahead and took a couple of ticks off his usually 95-97 mph fastball to induce balls into play.

home_pitcher_note: The 24-year-old is making his third MLB start, and second at home. In his last outing, the left-hander was in line for the win against the Cubs at Wrigley Field. Taylor gave up two runs in five innings, and he exited with a three-run lead. However, the bullpen surrendered that advantage, and he was not involved in the decision. Taylor battled at Wrigley Field, getting through five innings. But he had to work out of jams, as he gave up five hits and walked three. His defense came up big for him. In his first two starts, Taylor has walked nine in 9 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: While making his second start of the season against the Marlins, Lowe will attempt to be more effective than he was on April 15, when he allowed them four earned runs and issued five walks in just five innings. The veteran sinkerballer hasn't issued more than three walks during any of his other five outings and he enters this contest having won consecutive starts for the first time this year. Lowe is 0-1 with a 6.06 ERA in his past three starts against the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: On April 16 at Atlanta, Sanchez worked six innings and gave up two runs in beating the Braves. The right-hander hasn't won since. Sanchez will look to get back on the winning track at home this time against Atlanta. He has lost three straight decisions, and in his last two starts, he allowed six runs in each. Sanchez had a rough time in his previous outing, a four-inning, six-run performance against the Cubs at Wrigley Field. The four innings were a season low. He also has struggled in the first inning of his last two starts, allowing nine runs, including three homers.
away_pitcher_note: Jurrjens will be looking to win for the first time since April 12. The hard-luck right-hander has gone winless while allowing a total of four earned runs in his past four starts. During his rain-shortened two-inning outing against the Astros on Saturday, Jurrjens allowed his first homer in a span of eight starts, dating back to Sept. 11. In three starts against the Marlins last year, he posted a 7.80 ERA and allowed a .333 batting average.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel, in his second start since moving from the bullpen, held the Giants scoreless and gave up six hits in six innings of Sunday afternoon's 1-0 loss. He showed a lively fastball, and as the game progressed his breaking pitches increased in their sharpness.
away_pitcher_note: Vicitimized by a grand slam and a solo home run in his last start, Nolasco watched his losing streak extend to three straight decisions. The 26-year-old threw a season-high 112 pitches in that loss to the Cubs at Wrigley Field. He yielded a grand slam to Derrek Lee and a solo shot to Mike Fontenot. Normally, Nolasco is good about keeping the ball in the park. He surrendered two in his previous five starts, and hadn't been taken deep in three successive outings. Nolasco is 2-0 against the Rockies, and he's 1-0 at Coors Field.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa left Monday night's game against the Padres at PETCO Park with a reasonable line -- five innings, three hits, three earned runs. But three other runs scored as a result of his throwing error, and the three earned runs came on a Scott Hairston home run that put him in position to lose (he wound up with a no-decision in a game the Rockies came back to win, 9-6). At least, he didn't unravel. He finished with three walks and three strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson was solid once again while making his first career start against the Reds on Monday, giving up two runs on eight hits while striking out six with no walks in 7 1/3 innings. The 25-year-old, who left after throwing 102 pitches -- 74 for strikes -- hasn't issued a walk in two starts this season. After getting out of a first-and-third, one-out jam in the top of the first, Johnson didn't put a runner in scoring position until the seventh inning and needed just 68 pitches to get through six. He then allowed Cincinnati to tie the game at 2 in the seventh after giving up three straight hits to start the inning. He's only pitched two scoreless innings of relief in his career against the Rockies.

home_pitcher_note: In his last three starts, Cook has regained the form that made him an All-Star Game participant in 2008. He demonstrated savvy in his last start, when he held the Padres to one run and five hits in eight innings on Tuesday night. That's a team he has beaten repeatedly because hitters feel compelled to pound his sinker into the turf. This time, they laid off, so Cook threw 20-25 breaking and off-speed pitches. However, Cook gave up seven earned runs in 7 1/3 innings in his only start against the Marlins last season and is 1-2 with a 6.10 ERA in four career games against them.
away_pitcher_note: Volstad wasn't as sharp as usual against the Reds on Tuesday, but he still pitched well enough to earn his fourth quality start. The 22-year-old right-hander gave up four runs -- three earned -- on seven hits while walking three and striking out five. But Volstad was pitching out of trouble all night, and he needed 97 pitches to get through his six frames. He also said he did a bad job of holding on baserunners as the first two runs came in after a stolen base. On Sunday, Volstad will be returning to Coors Field -- the place where he made his Major League debut on July 6, 2008, when he pitched two scoreless innings out of the bullpen.

home_pitcher_note: Despite the ugly record, Parra is coming off his three best performances of the season. Although he took a no-decision on May 1 after allowing three hits and a run in six innings against Arizona, Parra finally earned a victory last Wednesday against the Reds. Though he needed 119 pitches to get his team into the seventh inning, he gave up eight hits and two runs in six innings. It wasn't his strongest line of the season, but he's sure to enter the contest against the Marlins with some much-needed confidence.
away_pitcher_note: The Marlins called up Koronka from Triple-A New Orleans on Sunday, sending down outfielder Cameron Maybin to make room. Koronka, a former Chicago Cub and Texas Ranger, has thrown back-to-back scoreless five-inning starts for New Orleans. The left-hander is taking Anibal Sanchez's spot in the rotation for the time being. On May 7, Sanchez exited after 4 2/3 innings with right shoulder discomfort and will be on the disabled list for two months. Koronka hasn't pitched in the Majors since 2007 and has never faced Milwaukee. The Brewers are hitting .262 as a team against left-handers this season.

home_pitcher_note: Looper looked flummoxed and frustrated in his last outing, a 6-5 defeat at Cincinnati. He was 2-0 with a 2.45 ERA through four starts, but he has struggled in the month of May. Against the Reds, he couldn't locate his pitches and finished the contest allowing eight hits and five runs in 3 1/3 innings. Afterward, he bemoaned the fact he didn't give his team a chance to win.
away_pitcher_note: Nolasco earned his first win since pitching Opening Day for the Marlins, and earned his first quality start of the season. He held the Rockies to three runs on eight hits and a walk while striking out five. Nolasco maintained his dominance over the Rockies' lineup, giving him a 3-0 record against them with 26 strikeouts against just two walks. Nolasco gave up runs on a solo homer in the second and a pair of run-scoring doubles in the third, but he found his rhythm and shut down Colorado the rest of the way.

home_pitcher_note: Bush turned in his fifth quality start in his last six outings, holding the Cubs to two runs on four hits in seven good innings on Friday night, but he exited in a 2-1 hole and was spared a tough-luck loss when Ryan Braun hit a go-ahead homer in the eighth. Bush's record is not indicative of the way he has pitched; the team has won each of his last four starts but he's 1-0 in that span.
away_pitcher_note: Not even Coors Field could tame the fast-rising Marlins ace last time out. The right-hander took a shutout through seven innings in Saturday's 3-1 win against the Rockies, giving up one run in eight frames. He struck out five and walked none, bringing his absurd strikeout-to-walk ratio to 43 to six on the season. But Milwaukee does have hope. Before the trip to Denver, Johnson's previous two road starts were pedestrian. He gave up three runs in six innings to the Mets on April 29 and six runs in six innings to the Nationals on April 18. Johnson has never faced the Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: Volstad tossed his fourth straight quality start on Sunday, but he took the loss for a second successive outing. He hasn't won since April 14, his second start of the season. The 22-year-old made his first Major League start against the Dodgers last July 11, and it was a beauty. He tossed 8 2/3 innings of one-run ball, holding Los Angeles to five hits and one walk while striking out six. It is the closest Volstad has come to a complete game in his young big league career.
away_pitcher_note: Stults turned in the best performance of his career on Saturday against the Giants when he threw a four-hit shutout and had a perfect game through 4 1/3 innings. He retired the first 13 batters he faced before allowing a one-out double to Aaron Rowand. It was just one of three hits he allowed all afternoon and he struck out five without issuing a walk. Stults even added an RBI single in the eighth for good measure. Stults is 0-1 with a 4.00 ERA in two career outings against the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: After two solid rehab outings, Miller will be ready to rejoin the rotation against the Dodgers. Now that he's recovered from his oblique injury, the task will be improving his results -- he has allowed eight walks and 14 hits in 11 2/3 innings with the big league club this year, with just three strikeouts. On the bright side, he has yet to allow a home run, and he remains one of the most promising pitching prospects in baseball.
away_pitcher_note: Milton was recalled from Triple-A Albuquerque after Thursday's win at Philadelphia and was immediately placed into the Dodgers rotation. The 33-year-old left-hander hasn't pitched in the Major Leagues since undergoing elbow ligament replacement surgery in 2007. Milton was 3-2 with a 2.83 ERA in seven starts at Triple-A this season. In 10 Major League seasons, Milton is 87-84. He tossed a no-hitter for the Twins in 1999 against the Angels.

home_pitcher_note: With Anibal Sanchez on the disabled list, Koronka was given his first shot in more than two years away from the Major Leagues, and it went swimmingly until the second time through the Brewers' order Tuesday. He allowed a trio of home runs -- two to Prince Fielder -- and wound up taking defeat and coughing up a 3-0 lead in the second inning. His final line was ugly -- five earned runs in 4 2/3 innings, with seven hits and three walks permitted. Still, manager Fredi Gonzalez indicated that the 28-year-old would get another shot.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw lost for the third time in his last five starts, in a 5-2 setback at Philadelphia on Tuesday. The lefty gave up only four hits through six innings, but he couldn't find the plate. He yielded a season-high five walks as his ERA ballooned from 4.91 to 6.00. If there was one positive, the six innings is the longest Kershaw went since an April 15 start against the Giants.

home_pitcher_note: After taking a step forward with his first victory since Opening Day one start earlier, Nolasco took two steps back last Wednesday against the Brewers, lasting just 3 2/3 innings and allowing eight runs. He gave up single tallies in the first three frames and then endured a nightmarish two-out rally oozing with bad luck -- with virtually no well-struck baseballs but five runs scoring. He did take responsibility, however, for two-out walks to the No. 7 and No. 8 hitter, starting a rampage of nine straight Brewers reaching base. The right-hander has yet to find the groove he had for much of last year.
away_pitcher_note: Haren could give Johan Santana and Cliff Lee a good argument as the Majors' premiere hard-luck pitcher. He's taken one loss essentially for every two runs he has allowed. He's been on the losing end of two of the D-backs' three shutouts and, in his last start, Arizona was again scoreless throughout his seven-inning stint. But the right-hander hasn't let the pressure of tight games affect his pitching.

home_pitcher_note: The Marlins can breathe easy -- at least for now as their ace right-hander is good to go. Johnson came out of the game early in his last start against the Brewers at Miller Park on Thursday, going just four innings, giving up three runs (two earned) on three hits while walking five and striking out three. The 25-year-old hasn't gone less than that since June 23, 2007, when he went three innings against the Twins. The reason: Johnson said he felt a little tired in his trapezoid/shoulder area. But after getting a little ice, he did his regular throwing off flat ground the day after his start, and Marlins manager Fredi Gonzalez said, barring a setback, he should be ready to go when his turn comes again. That next turn will come against the D-Backs, a team he threw seven shutout innings against in his only career start.
away_pitcher_note: Garland was scheduled to start Sunday's game in Atlanta, which got postponed by rain. He got shelled by the Reds on Monday, yielding seven runs on 10 hits in 3 2/3 innings. He constantly left balls up in the zone, and Cincinnati made him pay. The D-backs had won Garland's past four starts, three of which were quality outings, including his seven shutout innings May 5 in San Diego. The durable right-hander has now failed to get into the fourth in either of his two losses while pitching into the seventh in his five other starts.

home_pitcher_note: Volstad was looking sharp early on in his last start against the Dodgers on Friday, throwing five scoreless innings while only giving up one hit. But things started to unravel in the sixth, and the 22-year-old ended up taking the loss while giving up four runs on seven hits in six-plus innings. Volstad gave up three runs in a sixth inning that saw him throw 26 pitches and allow Los Angeles to tie the game. The Palm Beach Gardens, Fla., native still hasn't recorded a win since April 14. In his only other start against the Diamondbacks, Volstad took the loss while giving up four runs in 5 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Davis was scheduled to pitch Wednesday anyway after Sunday's rainout, so he will be going on normal rest. Davis had a rough outing his last time out, in more ways than one. The left-hander made a crucial throwing error that led to a two-run second inning for the Braves, and he also took exception in the seventh when he was lifted for a pinch-hitter after just 80 pitches. The D-backs wound up losing the game, 4-3.

home_pitcher_note: After Tuesday night's 5-3 loss, the Marlins announced Penn will make his first start as a Marlin in Game 2. Penn last made a big league start in 2006, while he was with the Orioles. Because he has been used as a long reliever, Penn will be on a pitch count between 60-70 pitches. The right-hander has made 12 relief appearances, and he's logged 17 2/3 innings. His last outing came on Sunday, when he threw 2 1/3 innings on Sunday against the Dodgers, striking out five.
away_pitcher_note: After Sunday's game at Turner Field was rained out, Augenstein was originally scheduled to pitch on Thursday. Now, he'll be going on six days' rest. Augenstein made his big league debut last week against the Reds at Chase Field, allowing five runs in 6 1/3 innings. One of the reasons he had such tremendous success at Double-A Mobile was his ability to throw strikes, and he displayed that in his debut, walking two -- one of which was intentional. Augenstein is taking the spot of Yusmeiro Petit, who in turn was taking the spot of injured ace Brandon Webb in the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Things didn't really get off on the right foot in Miller's first start since April 20 on Saturday, but the 6-foot-7 southpaw weathered it and ended up with the win against the Dodgers. Miller needed 30 pitches -- only 13 of them strikes -- to get out of a one-run first inning and put the leadoff man on in each of his first four frames. But the 23-year-old kept his team in the game through five innings, which saw him give up two runs on four hits while striking out four, walking four and throwing 98 pitches -- 55 for strikes. Miller is 1-1 with a 2.13 ERA in two career starts against the D-Backs.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer was scheduled to pitch Friday, on five days' rest, after the D-backs' rainout at Turner Field on Sunday. But with a doubleheader scheduled for Wednesday after a second straight postponement on Monday, he was moved up to Thursday. Scherzer finally picked up his first big league win last Saturday night in Atlanta. Because of some poor run support and bullpen issues, it took the right-hander until his 24th appearance and 14th start to accomplish the feat. Scherzer was on top of his game against the Braves, allowing just four hits in six shutout innings. The key play in the game was a fake-to-third-throw-to-first pickoff play in the first that turned a first-and-third with one out situation into an inning-ending double play. Scherzer cruised from that point forward.

home_pitcher_note: Monday's rainout threw the week into disarray for the rotation. After Tuesday's game, the Marlins announced Nolasco will take the ball. There was some question because he threw 3 1/3 innings and logged 76 pitches on Monday in a game that was rained out against the Diamondbacks in the top of the fourth inning. One reason the Marlins opted to use Nolasco on four days' rest is because he did so four times early in Spring Training. On Wednesday, the 26-year-old will throw a shorter between-starts bullpen session, so he will be fresher for Friday.
away_pitcher_note: Sonnanstine pitched more effectively than he has in recent outings when he picked up his second win of the season, allowing five runs in 5 2/3 innings to the Indians Sunday at Tropicana Field. Sonnanstine has struggled with his control for most of the season, which is extra punitive to a pitcher who lives by being able to locate his pitches at strategic positions within the strike zone. When Sonnanstine is going well, he is a master of deception, employing an array of pitches that he can throw from all different angles. Sonnanstine is 2-0 with a 3.13 ERA in three career starts against the Marlins, and he is 1-0 with a 3.00 ERA in two career starts at Dolphins Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Sean West, one of five first-round picks in 2005, will make his big league debut on Saturday against the Rays. The 6-foot-8 left-hander is 4-2 with a 4.85 ERA at Double-A Jacksonville. In 42 2/3 innings, West has 50 strikeouts and 22 walks. In his last outing, West took a no-decision while allowing one run on three hits over six innings, striking out six against the Carolina Mudcats. The lefty will face a potent Rays lineup that flexed its muscles on Friday night. Tampa Bay tagged Florida for 15 runs en route to a series-opening victory.
away_pitcher_note: Niemann had his best performance of the season on Monday against the A's, lasting eight innings while allowing three earned runs on eight hits while walking none and striking out three. It was his second consecutive strong start and a good sign for Tampa Bay, which is expecting a lot from its 6-foot-9 No. 5 starter. Keep in mind, though, that Oakland is near the bottom in almost every offensive statistical category this season.

home_pitcher_note: Johnson took his first loss since September 7, 2008 at St. Louis. The 6-foot-7 flamethrower allowed two earned runs over 6 1/3 innings while striking out six D-backs. Johnson hit 96 mph on the radar gun and felt no shoulder discomfort afterward. His latest appearance showed that his arm feels better since his four-inning, three-run outing on May 14th at Milwaukee. He is 10-2 in decisions since coming off the disabled list in July 2008.
away_pitcher_note: Shields was nearly flawless vs. Oakland on Tuesday, lasting a season-high 8 1/3 innings, allowing only five hits and no runs while striking out five. But his teammates couldn't support him, and he ended up getting a no-decision in a game that went scoreless into extra innings. It was a good sign for Shields, who had allowed 10 hits in back-to-back outings (0-2). But he remains the tough-luck pitcher on the staff: he's 1-3 in his past six starts despite a 2.91 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: The Phillies hope Moyer took a step in the right direction Wednesday against the Reds at Great American Ball Park. Following one of the worst three-start stretches of his career, he allowed three runs in six innings in a loss to the Reds. That might not seem like much, but it was just Moyer's second quality start out of eight starts this season. The Phillies bumped Moyer back a day last week, so he would miss the Yankees on Sunday and could face the Marlins, against whom he is 12-1 with a 2.84 ERA in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Volstad did not pitch as well as he would have liked in his last outing but he still picked up his first win since April 14th. The right-hander allowed the D-backs to score four runs on five hits over six innings. Volstad allowed a home run for the third consecutive start, when Chris Snyder took him deep in the fifth. It was the fourth homer allowed by Volstad in his last three starts. There was one glaring positive in the 22-year-old's stat line: a career-high nine strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: The line score didn't look like much on Thursday in Cincinnati. Blanton allowed seven hits and five runs in five innings, but one pitch truly cost him. He had thrown four scoreless innings against the Reds in a 12-5 victory until a flare and a couple of choppers through the infield got him into trouble in the fifth inning. Brandon Phillips then hit a three-run home run to left field at Great American Ball Park to ruin Blanton's day. But Blanton said he took positives out of the start and is hoping this time the line matches his efforts.
away_pitcher_note: Miller took a no-decision in his last outing, but the left-hander had one of his best pitching performances of the season. With his bullpen taxed, Miller threw seven strong innings against the D-backs. The 24-year-old allowed two runs on four hits over seven innings while tying his career high with nine strikeouts. The only major blemishes were a ground-rule double deep to center by Ryan Roberts and a solo homer on an 0-2 count by Chris Snyder. Miller is looking to pick up his first career victory against the Phillies but has had success against some of their biggest stars. Jimmy Rollins, Ryan Howard and Raul Ibañez are a combined 2-for-27 against Miller.

home_pitcher_note: Myers had arguably his best start of the season on Friday in a victory over the Yankees at Yankee Stadium. He allowed just one run through seven innings before surrendering a couple of solo homers in the eighth. But in eight innings, Myers allowed eight hits and three runs, striking out five to pick up the win. Myers has a 2.57 ERA in his past three starts. That's a good sign for a team that desperately needs quality starting pitching.
away_pitcher_note: The Marlins officially announced Badenhop will make his first start of the season on Wednesday in the series finale with the Phillies. A sinkerball pitcher, the team is hoping the right-hander can get his share of ground-ball outs in hitter-friendly Citizens Bank Park. Badenhop has been pitching in long relief since he was called up from Triple-A. He's made 11 appearances in relief, but he also had two starts at Triple-A New Orleans before being brought up in mid April. Because he isn't stretched out to throw 100 pitchers, long reliever Hayden Penn is an option to pitch in long relief.

home_pitcher_note: Overcoming the balk problem that plagued him in his previous start, Pelfrey pitched seven effective innings on Saturday against the Red Sox, allowing two runs -- though that effort was hardly enough for a win. He could have used the confidence boost of a victory heading into Friday's game at Citi Field -- in five starts against the Marlins last season, Pelfrey was 0-4 with a 7.11 ERA. He has beaten the Marlins just once in eight career tries.
away_pitcher_note: West had a decent showing in his first big league start, holding the Rays to two runs on five hits over five innings. The 22-year-old struck out five but also walked four in a no-decision. The 6-foot-8 lefty showed good velocity, topping out at 95 mph while sitting consistently between 92 and 94 mph with his fastball. West threw 91 pitches, nine fewer than his 100-pitch limit. The lefty is still looking for his first big league win.

home_pitcher_note: Redding makes his third start this season against a team that was his nemesis last season. Pitching for the Nationals, he started six games against the Marlins, won once and lost four times. His ERA against them in only 29 innings was 7.76. He allowed six home runs. Chances are Hanley Ramirez will be back in the starting lineup today -- he wasn't last night because of a tight groin -- because he owns Redding. He has three doubles and three home runs in 13 career at-bats against the Mets starter.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson took a no-decision in his last start after leaving the game in position to win. The big right-hander allowed three runs on six hits over seven innings while striking out seven Rays but the bullpen could not hold the lead to get him his fourth win of the season. The last time Johnson faced the Mets he threw a complete game to beat ace left-hander Johan Santana. Johnson has held the Mets' biggest stars in check over his career. Jose Reyes, David Wright and Carlos Beltran are all hitting .250 or lower against him with no home runs.

home_pitcher_note: John Maine had one of his best outings of the season Monday against the Nationals, allowing one run and four hits in six innings while striking out four. Maine is scheduled to next take the mound Sunday against the Marlins, against whom he is 1-0 in two starts thus far this season. Maine has allowed just two earned runs and three hits in 11 innings against Florida this season and owns a 4-1 mark with a 2.49 ERA versus the Marlins in his career. That includes the best start of his career, when Maine struck out 14 Marlins while yielding a single hit in 7 2/3 innings Sept. 29, 2007.
