Two two-strike curveballs that Duke wanted to bounce in the dirt were left high enough for contact, and both ended up being driven for RBI hits. With only one run of support from his offense, that made the difference. In fact, in Duke's six losses this season, the Pirates have scored just five runs for him. They've averaged eight runs a game when he's won. Duke is winless in four career starts against the Marlins. In a combined 19 innings, the left-hander has allowed 12 earned runs.

home_pitcher_note: Nolasco picked up his fifth win of the season after throwing eight innings in which he held Washington to two runs on four hits while striking out eight and walking none. The Nationals hit several balls hard off Nolasco early, including a Ryan Zimmerman solo homer in the second, but the right-hander settled into a groove shortly after. After a rocky second inning, Nolasco got stronger as the game went on, allowing just one runner to reach base and retiring 10 in a row between the fourth and seventh innings.
away_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf had what he described as his most complete performance of the season his last time out on Tuesday, when he tossed seven scoreless innings against the Cubs and struck out a career-best eight. He was able to rely heavily on his slider, a pitch that Ohlendorf has tended to overthrow at times this season. That slider helped the effectiveness of his fastball, which in turn kept Ohlendorf more efficient than he has been most of the year. One of Ohlendorf's best starts this season came against the Marlins back on April 20 when he pitched seven shutout innings and allowed two hits.

home_pitcher_note: Cain is winless in his last three starts, though he has pitched more than capably over that stretch. He received no decision while allowing one run and three hits in eight innings against Texas on June 20, lost at Milwaukee on June 26 while yielding five runs in seven innings and took another no-decision at St. Louis in his last start despite surrendering just one run in seven innings. In Cain's 16 starts, he has been unable to last at least six innings only once, and that was a rain-shortened complete game at Washington on June 4.
away_pitcher_note: West took a no-decision in his last start despite not having his best stuff as the Nationals tagged him for five runs on eight hits over 4 1/3 innings. The tall left-hander struggled from the start and had trouble with Washington's best hitters as Adam Dunn and Ryan Zimmerman combined to go 4-for-6 with two doubles, a home run and three RBIs. West will try to repeat his success against the Giants in his next start. The 23-year-old picked up his first Major League win against San Francisco when he threw eight shutout innings of two-hit ball on June 8.

home_pitcher_note: Facing Florida has been a happy activity for Zito, who's 3-0 in four career starts against the Marlins. Typically a stronger performer in the season's second half (70-36, 3.47 entering this year, compared to 53-57, 4.14 in the first half), Zito probably wouldn't mind kicking himself into gear a start early. He has worked past the sixth inning in only one of his last six outings. The Giants are 3-3 in those games and 7-9 overall when Zito starts.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson had his shortest outing of the season, allowing one run on five hits over 3 1/3 innings, in which he struck out three and walked four. The Marlins ace struggled from the start and did not appear to have his best command as he fell behind hitters throughout the outing. The big right-hander will look to rebound from his disappointing start against the Nationals when he takes the ball in San Francisco to face the Giants. Johnson has held the current crop of Giants to a .243 career average against him and has allowed just one extra base hit, a double by Randy Winn.

home_pitcher_note: Two starts into his Major League career, Ryan Sadowski has nailed down the No. 5 spot in the Giants starting rotation. All has gone his way thus far. The Giants lineup has supported him with 20 runs of support and the right-hander has been pitching to contact, employing his two-seam, sinking fastball. He's retired just six batters on strikes in his 13 innings, but has also yielded just seven hits.
away_pitcher_note: Volstad continues to get hurt by the home run ball. The 22-year-old gave up two homers over the first two innings in his last start against the Pirates. The right-hander allowed four runs in three innings before being lifted after a 45-minute rain delay. Volstad has allowed 15 home runs on the season and at least one in eight of his last ten starts.

home_pitcher_note: Petit needs to pitch well in order to keep his spot in the rotation. The right-hander was on the DL from May 9 until July 3 with right shoulder problems. He did not pitch well during his injury rehabilitation assignment, but the team had few options for the spot at that time and needed to activate him. This is the spot in the rotation that was Brandon Webb's, but the D-backs' ace has not pitched since Opening Day. Arizona has tried several candidates in this spot, including Billy Buckner and Bryan Augenstein, but they're still looking for someone to stake a claim.
away_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Miller earned a win for the first time since June 6. The left-hander held the Pirates to three runs on eight hits over 6 2/3 innings while striking out four and walking one. However, the Bucs were able to hit the long ball against the 24-year-old. Miller allowed two home runs for the first time all season and had only allowed three on the year prior to the game against Pittsburgh. The four-year veteran is looking to win back-to-back games for the first time the season when he faces the D-backs in his next start. Miller took a loss the last time he faced Arizona despite allowing just two runs over seven innings on May 21.

home_pitcher_note: Haren was named to the National League All-Star team on Sunday by Phillies manager Charlie Manuel. The right-hander has been consistently outstanding all season. Of his 17 starts, 16 have been quality -- six innings or more with three or fewer runs allowed. Last time out, against the Rockies, Haren allowed three runs (only one earned) over seven innings. He has not allowed more than two earned runs in a start since May 23 in Oakland, a span of eight starts. Overall, Haren has allowed more than two earned runs just three times this year.
away_pitcher_note: Nolasco won his fourth straight start his last time out, throwing eight shutout innings against the Pirates. It was the second straight eight-inning performance for Nolasco, as he continues to pitch well since returning to the big leagues. Over his past four starts, the right-hander has posted a 0.96 ERA and struck out 32 batters over 28 innings. In his last start, Nolasco struck out 12, good enough for second most in a game for his career.

home_pitcher_note: Garland was saddled with another no-decision in his last outing against the Padres. The right-hander allowed three runs in six innings and left with the game tied. He has not won since May 19, a span of nine starts. His number do not look great, but they are skewed by a few really poor outings. In four starts he has allowed six or more runs, which pushes his ERA up. Only three times this year has he failed to go at least six innings in a game. The May 19 win was against the Marlins in Florida as he held the Fish to one run over six innings.
away_pitcher_note: West's development as a big league starting pitcher continued Monday night against the San Francisco Giants, and he went through some growing pains. The 23-year-old walked three and yielded five runs in six innings. He is winless in his last two starts (in which he's allowed 10 earned runs in 10 1/3 innings). This will be his first start against the D-backs.

home_pitcher_note: Davis finally got a much-deserved win in his last start. That was his first win since June 5. That win as well as the one in his last start came against the Padres. In the most recent one he allowed just two runs over 6 1/3 innings. Davis has deserved more wins, but has struggled from a lack of run support and some poor outings by the bullpen. In his previous three starts before getting the win against the Padres he had allowed two earned runs in 21 innings yet came away with nothing to show for it. He can be frustrating to watch at times as he walks more than his fair share of batters and there always seem to be runners on base. However, the veteran finds a way to pitch himself out of trouble.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson regained his control on the mound Tuesday against the San Francisco Giants but still lost. One start removed from his wild 3 1/3 inning effort against the Washington Nationals, he allowed three runs on five hits in seven innings but received zero runs of support. The right-hander is winless in his last three outings and lost in his May 19 start against the Arizona Diamondbacks, yielding three runs in 6 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Volstad will start the Marlins post-All-Star break schedule following up on his best Major League start. Wednesday against the San Francisco Giants, he tossed his first career shutout, allowing just five hits and whiffing six. Consistency remains the key for the second-year right-hander, as he lasted just three innings in his July 3 start. In two appearances opposing the Phillies this season, Volstad is 1-0, having allowed five earned runs in 13 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: The Phllies have tabbed Moyer for the first start of the second half, in part to give Cole Hamels an extra day of rest and in part because Moyer is 12-2 with a 3.06 ERA in 14 career starts against the Marlins. The 46-year-old lefty is coming off a rough outing against Cincinnati, though, when he allowed two home runs and six runs in five innings. Philadelphia managed to put a four-spot on the board in the bottom of the fifth, so he still recorded the win. But it was a clear setback for Moyer, who had been pitching better lately after early-season struggles.

home_pitcher_note: Following a rough start to the year, the Marlins' Opening Day starter was optioned to Triple-A to try to figure some things out, and it seems like he did. Since returning from his Minors stint, the 26-year-old is 4-2 with a 2.68 ERA in seven starts. In his last outing, though, Nolasco gave up seven runs in six innings against the Diamondbacks. He's 4-3 with a 4.25 ERA in his career against the division-rival Phillies.
away_pitcher_note: Concerned about the toll on his young left arm, the Phillies decided to give Hamels an extra day of rest out of the All-Star break. Hamels threw 227 1/3 innings last year and 183 1/3 in 2007 versus 132 1/3 in '06. "His workload has been increased tremendously," pitching coach Rich Dubee said. "So we still got to get Cole in the right mindset." Hamels has been inconsistent this year. His seasons of ups and downs reached another trough on Saturday, when he allowed three home runs to the weak-hitting Pirates. He only received a no-decision because the Phillies rallied for five runs in the ninth.

home_pitcher_note: An All-Star for the first time, Johnson represented the Marlins for the NL but he didn't pitch. Now, he makes his first start of the second half. After coming back from Tommy John elbow ligament replacement surgery last year, Johnson started to show the baseball world he has a dominant arm. And the beginning of this year -- when the 25-year-old turned in 16 of 19 quality starts, posted an ERA under 3.00 each month of the season and made his first All-Star team -- has demonstrated just how bright his future can be. In his last start on Sunday, he gave up one run in 6 2/3 innings against the D-backs. For his career against Philadelphia, he's 3-1 with a 3.66 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Manager Charlie Manuel called Blanton a "bulldog" after the right-hander's last outing, and for good reason. Blanton has a team-high 10 quality starts this season, including seven in his past nine outings. Over that span, he is 4-1 with a 2.44 ERA. And he has been especially dominant lately. On July 5, he outdueled Johan Santana with 7 1/3 scoreless innings, and on Friday he allowed just four hits and one run over 7 1/3 innings. It was the first time he threw more than seven innings in consecutive outings since April 2008.

home_pitcher_note: From trying to figure out a new delivery, to losing the battle to be the No. 4 starter in the rotation, to being used out of the bullpen to start the season, to suffering a setback by landing on the disabled list, it was an adventurous start to the season for Miller. But the first half ended on somewhat of a high note. Since returning from a stay on the disabled list -- caused by an oblique strain -- the left-hander has gone 3-3 with a 4.04 ERA in 11 starts, and he's only given up more than three earned runs in two of those outings. But against the Diamondbacks, in his last start before the All-Star Break, he lasted just 2 2/3 innings and gave up six runs (two earned) in a no-decision. He's 0-2 with a 4.05 ERA in his career against Philadelphia.
away_pitcher_note: Happ has become the Phillies' best, and most reliable, starter. He still has not lost since his Major League debut in 2007. He has tossed at least seven innings in four consecutive starts, going 2-0 with a 1.80 ERA over that span. The latest gem came in Philadelphia's final game before the All-Star break; Happ allowed the Pirates just one run on four hits over seven innings. He has never started against the Marlins, although over three relief outings against them, he allowed eight earned runs in 7 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: In his first start for the Padres since 2007, Stauffer provided seven solid innings, allowing just four hits and two runs. But San Diego's offense struggled again, and he was on the hook for a loss, even though he tied his career high with seven strikeouts. Stauffer missed all of 2008 while recovering from labrum surgery. He started the season in Double-A and advanced to Triple-A before taking the spot in the rotation vacated by Walter Silva. Against the Giants on July 11, Stauffer was aggressive in the strike zone, using a low-90s fastball and an effective curveball. "I really appreciate the opportunity being here," Stauffer said. "It's been nice having them support me. I can't say enough about the organization."
away_pitcher_note: VandenHurk has not pitched in the big leagues this season but has experience at the Major League level. VandenHurk has made 21 big league starts since 2007, going 5-7 with a 6.96 ERA over 95 2/3 innings. The 6-foot-5 righty opened the season on the disabled list with right elbow inflammation but has gone 4-1 with a 2.77 ERA in nine starts for Triple-A New Orleans since returning on May 30. This will be his first time facing the Padres.

home_pitcher_note: Gaudin was a hard-luck loser in his last start, Thursday against the Rockies, when he allowed four runs, though only one earned, over five innings on four hits. The Rockies drove his pitch count up by taking four walks, which at times has been a nemesis for Gaudin. Of course, the eight strikeouts in five innings also helped contribute to the high pitch count as Gaudin was gone after five innings and 103 pitches. This will be his first start against the Marlins this season.
away_pitcher_note: Volstad struggled to keep the ball in the park in his last start, giving up three home runs against the Phillies on Thursday. The right-hander allowed four runs on seven hits over six innings while striking out five and walking one. The 22-year-old continues to leave pitches up in the zone and opponents are making him pay as he has now allowed 20 home runs over 19 starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: Geer struggled for the second time in as many starts on July 17 against the Rockies, allowing five earned runs on seven hits with four walks in a loss to Colorado. He's now allowed 11 earned runs in his last 8 2/3 innings. Geer also allowed a home run in the first inning to Clint Barmes, making it 23 home runs he's allowed this season, the most in the National League. The walks were out of character for Geer, who hadn't walked a batter in each of his last three starts and had walked just four in his last six combined starts.
away_pitcher_note: Nolasco took a no-decision in his last start, allowing four runs on seven hits over six innings while striking out five and walking two Phillies on July 17. The right-hander struggled a bit in the first, allowing a Chase Utley two-run homer, but settled in afterwards to retire nine straight before giving up another two runs in the fourth. Nolasco has struggled on the road this season, going 2-4 with a 6.99 ERA over nine starts.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw just keeps getting better. In his last seven starts, all won by the Dodgers, he's 5-0 with a 0.63 ERA. And he's even able to do it when he has less than his best stuff, as he showed against the Astros. Lacking consistency with anything off-speed, he threw enough strikes to walk only one and pitch ahead in counts, allowing only two hits in seven scoreless innings.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson looked like he was going to have another outstanding start his last time out. The right-hander held the Phillies to just one hit, a Chase Utley single in the first, over his two innings in a game that was called after a 90-minute rain delay. Johnson was very effective with his pitches, throwing 21 of 30 for strikes. The Marlins ace has not faced the Dodgers yet this season, but if he throws the way he has all year, he will make Friday a long night for the National League West leaders.

home_pitcher_note: Kuroda had one bad inning out of five against the Astros. He allowed three runs, including a two-run homer by Geoff Blum. But he also allowed seven hits and struck out only one. When at his best, he gets ahead in counts and makes defensive hitters chase splitters in the dirt, but it hasn't been happening a lot lately. Manager Joe Torre believes Kuroda overthrows, causing a mechanical flaw that results in pulling his pitches as they are delivered.
away_pitcher_note: Called up from Triple-A New Orleans on July 20, VandenHurk worked six innings that night at San Diego, tossing 88 pitches. The 24-year-old right-hander kept the Padres off the board for 5 2/3 innings, before surrendering back-to-back homers to Adrian Gonzalez and Kevin Kouzmanoff. VandenHurk was 4-1 with a 2.77 ERA in nine starts for New Orleans. He has never faced the Dodgers. VandenHurk collected his first win since June 22, 2008 against the Braves.

home_pitcher_note: Schmidt nearly didn't make it out of the first inning in his first start in two years. But he found a way, and once his offense created a lead, Schmidt didn't let it get away. He's not a hard-thrower anymore and he knows it. He doesn't have much margin for error with a fastball that doesn't get to 90 mph, but he's only being asked to be a fifth starter, not the All-Star he once was.
away_pitcher_note: In the state of California, Volstad is 3-0 in his young big league career. He puts that streak on the line at Dodger Stadium, the site of his first big league start. On July 11, 2008, then 21-years-old, Volstad made his first MLB start a memorable one. He gave up one run in 8 2/3 innings, collecting the win. In his last outing, the right-hander allowed one run in seven innings at San Diego. And on July 8 at San Francisco, the 6-foot-8 right-hander turned in his first complete game shutout, beating the Giants, 7-0. But on May 15 at Land Shark Stadium in Miami, Volstad came up on the losing end to the Dodgers. He gave up four runs in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: On the mark best describes how Nolasco threw in his last start. The 26-year-old struck out 10 in 6 1/3 innings, marking the seventh time in his career that he's had double-digit strikeout totals. In four July outings, the right-hander has struck out 35 in 26 1/3 innings. He's 2-1 with a no decision in the month. He's won five of his last six decisions. This is his first appearance this year against the Braves.Traditionally, he's struggled with Atlanta, posting a 1-4 record and 5.18 ERA. A year ago, he was 0-3 (10.57).
away_pitcher_note: Jurrjens matched up with Giants ace Tim Lincecum and emerged victorious on Wednesday, as he tossed 7 2/3 innings and allowed just one run on three hits. He struck out a season-high nine batters, and has allowed just five hits in his last 12 2/3 innings pitched. After going winless in June, Jurrjens has won four of five starts in July and has won his last three in a row. Against the Marlins on May 7, Jurrjens went seven innings and allowed just two runs on three hits in a Braves win.

home_pitcher_note: Make it 17 straight starts in which Johnson has not allowed more than three earned runs. That builds on his own record. In 1996, Kevin Brown had 15. In Johnson's 20 starts, the Marlins have won 16 times. Lifetime against Atlanta, Johnson is 3-1 with a 2.45 ERA in nine starts. This is his first meeting with the Braves this season. On he season, Johnson has turned in 17 quality starts. At home, the 25-year-old has been especially tough, posting a 4-1 record and 1.98 ERA in 10 starts.
away_pitcher_note:
Kawakami didn't figure into the decision in his last start -- a 5-1 loss to the Giants. The right-hander battled through five innings -- throwing 97 pitches -- while allowing one run on four hits. He also walked four. Kawakami has only faced the Marlins once in his career - a 6-2 loss on April 16. In that outing, Kawakami gave up four earned runs on five hits, striking out seven in six innings.
In 17 career starts against Florida, Vazquez is 6-6 with a 4.67 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: In his last outing, it wasn't technically a quality start. But it was still an encouraging one, even though he was not involved in the decision. Facing the Dodgers at Dodger Stadium, VandenHurk gave up one run on five hits in five innings. A quality start is three or fewer earned runs in six or more innings. VandenHurk's pitch count reached 92 through five, so he exited. This will be his third start since being called up from Triple-A New Orleans. It also is his first home start.
away_pitcher_note: Vazquez picked up his third consecutive win in his last start against the Brewers, giving up four runs on seven hits in seven innings. He also struck out nine. In his last start against the Marlins on April 14, Vazquez took the loss for his first decision of the season. He gave up three runs on five hits in six innings, and struck out a season-high 12 batters (a number he tied in June against the Pirates). In 17 career starts against Florida, Vazquez is 6-6 with a 4.67 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: During the West Coast road trip, Volstad won both of his starts, claiming decisions at San Diego and Los Angeles. However, control has been an issue for the 22-year-old, who walked four in each of those games. In 5 1/3 innings at Los Angeles, he gave up four runs, all in the sixth inning. Home runs remain an issue, as he's surrendered 21 in 21 starts. Volstad faced the Cubs on April 23 at Wrigley Field, giving up two runs on three hits in seven innings. He wasn't involved in the decision, but Florida won the game.
away_pitcher_note: Harden says all of his first-half day/night, home/road stats are lopsided because of bad mechanics, not because he can't pitch during the afternoon. The right-hander wasn't using his legs enough but has figured out his troubles since the All-Star break. He now is 2-0 with a 0.95 ERA since the break, picking up the win in his last start, against the Reds. In that game, Harden gave up one hit -- a Joey Votto homer in the first inning -- before retiring 16 in a row. Harden struck out eight, and he has 21 strikeouts in three starts since the break. He didn't walk a batter against the Reds -- the second time he's done that this year.

home_pitcher_note: After days of uncertainty over who will start Saturday's game, it was announced that Burke Badenhop will get the ball against the Cubs. The right-hander is making his first appearance since returning from a three-game suspension for hitting Dodgers second baseman Orlando Hudson with a pitch on July 26. Badenhop won his only start this season after holding the Phillies to one run over five innings on May 27. Left-handers Sean West and Andrew Miller were other potential options to get the start on Aug. 1, but will not as both started in the Minors on July 29.
away_pitcher_note: Zambrano did not get a decision in his last start against the Astros, but did pitch well. He gave up one run on three hits over seven innings, and that one run came on Carlos Lee's home run. Zambrano did walk four, and struck out four. It was his 13th quality start. He's now 1-1 with a 2.52 ERA in his last six home games and has recorded a quality start in each of those games. He also has a hit in four of his last six games.

home_pitcher_note: Nolasco took a no decision his last time out after holding the Braves to two runs on seven hits over seven innings while striking out five. The right-hander showed toughness on the mound, pitching himself out of several jams. In his next start, the 26-year-old faces the organization that drafted him. Nolasco is 2-1 with a 3.60 ERA over three starts against the Cubs for his career.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster was rusty in his first outing in 3 1/2 weeks. He had been sidelined with a broken right big toe, suffered July 5, and was going to be limited to 80-85 pitches. He threw 85 exact. But that was over five innings. He gave up six runs on nine hits and struck out three. He just wasn't sharp, and the problem was location. He has one win in his last seven starts.

home_pitcher_note: Martin pitched his best game as a member of the Nationals on Thursday afternoon at Miller Park, but it wasn't enough, as the Brewers won the game, 7-3. Martin pitched better than the box score indicated. He lasted six-plus innings and gave up five runs on seven hits. Martin said he felt more comfortable than he did in his previous two starts. He made only two mistakes in the game, giving up home runs to Craig Counsell and Prince Fielder. But shoddy defense by catcher Wil Nieves and second baseman Anderson Hernandez did Martin in.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson overcame some mistakes in his last start to pick up his tenth win of the season. The right-hander surrendered a home run to Casey Kotchman and another to Garret Anderson over six innings of work. The Braves were able score three runs on eight hits against the usually stingy Johnson. While his last start was not as good as some of his previous ones, Johnson continues to shut down opposing offenses. The right-hander has now allowed three or fewer earned runs in 18 straight starts.

home_pitcher_note: On Friday, Lannan had an outing he would like to forget as the Nationals were edged by the Pirates, 5-4, at PNC Park. Lannan pitched seven innings and gave up five runs on nine hits. In the second inning, Lannan was given a 1-0 lead, thanks to an RBI double by Willie Harris. By the fourth inning, however, the Pirates had a 4-1 lead.
away_pitcher_note: VandenHurk's last outing was filled with positives and negatives. The right-hander held the Braves to two runs on four hits over six innings while striking out a career-high nine. However, he struggled in the second inning after hitting Yunel Escobar on a 1-2 pitch. Casey Kotchman followed with a blast to center for a two-run double.  VandenHurk would recover to shut down the Braves the rest of the way and his team would tie the game late to help him avoid his first loss of the season.

home_pitcher_note: Stammen started for Washington on Saturday, and he had nothing in the tank. He lasted three-plus innings and gave up six runs on eight hits. While Stammen was on the mound, outfielder Lastings Milledge burned his former team in the third inning by hitting a two-run double. Stammen didn't record an out in the fourth inning.
away_pitcher_note: Volstad was perfect through four innings in his last start before surrendering a hit to Aramis Ramirez in the top of the fifth. The right-hander flustered Cubs hitters until the seventh inning, when Jake Fox clubbed a game-tying two-out, two-run homer. Volstad finished his start allowing two runs on six hits over 6 2/3 innings while striking out five. The 23-year-old has allowed a home runs in seven of his last 10 starts and 10 home runs over that span.

home_pitcher_note: Blanton continues to pile up innings for the Phillies, which has been sorely needed for a bullpen that has four pitchers on the disabled list: J.C. Romero, Clay Condrey, Chad Durbin and Brett Myers. Blanton allowed seven hits and two runs and struck out five in seven innings Saturday in a 2-0 loss to the Giants at AT&T Park. He is 3-1 with a 1.47 ERA (six earned runs in 36 2/3 innings) in his past five starts, and 5-2 with a 2.33 ERA (21 earned runs in 81 innings) in 12 starts since May 21.
away_pitcher_note: Thanks to an off-day on Aug. 3, Fredi Gonzalez gets to throw one of his hottest pitchers in the opening game of a three-game set against the first place Phillies. Nolasco is coming off another outstanding performance where he held the Cubs to one run on four hits over seven innings while striking out eight. The former Cubs farmhand was especially tough with two outs, ending four of seven innings with called strike outs, and retired the final 14 batters he faced.

home_pitcher_note: Just when it seemed like Phillies left-hander Cole Hamels had turned a corner, he allowed 10 hits and seven runs in five innings Sunday against the Giants at AT&T Park. Things started to unravel for Hamels in that game with a two-out broken bat single from Giants pitcher Barry Zito. Hamels had pitched well to that point, and he had pitched well in his previous three starts, when he went 2-0 with a 2.25 ERA (five earned runs in 20 innings).
away_pitcher_note: Manager Fredi Gonzalez said that he will not announce Saturday's starting pitcher until Friday, but the smart money is on big lefty Sean West, who has been throwing in Double-A Jacksonville since being sent down from the Marlins on July 11. With the big league club this year, West showed positive flashes, but succumbed to inconsistency. In each of his last three starts with the Marlins, he gave up at least five runs. With Jacksonville, West earned victories in his last three starts, most recently on Monday.

home_pitcher_note: Moyer entered Tuesday's 8-3 loss to the Rockies -- he allowed six runs in five innings -- with a 3.82 ERA in 11 starts since May 25. But his previous starts have followed a pattern: good start, bad start, good start, bad start. He allowed one run in 6 1/3 innings July 4 against the Mets, six runs in five innings July 9 against the Reds, zero runs in seven innings July 16 against the Marlins, five runs in five innings July 22 against the Cubs and zero runs in 6 2/3 innings July 27 against the D-backs before he struggled Tuesday against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Seven marvelous innings can be overshadowed by one lousy frame. That's the lesson Johnson learned on Tuesday against the Nationals. The right-hander was nearly unhittable through the first seven, striking out a career-high nine batters while shutting out the Nationals on two hits. Then in the eighth, the bottom of the Nats order knocked four consecutive base-hits before Johnson could record an out. He was relieved from the game, both inherited runners scored, and Johnson received a no-decision in the Marlins loss.

home_pitcher_note: In his fourth start, VandenHurk had his worst start. He only lasted four innings before being lifted for a pinch-hitter, but he admitted that his performance did not merit a much longer outing. VandenHurk gave up five runs on seven hits. He was plagued by the long ball, surrendering three. Ryan Zimmerman sliced a low and away fastball just over the right-field wall and a pitch later, Adam Dunn crushed a pitch into the upper deck. Ronnie Belliard knocked the third home run for the Nationals.
away_pitcher_note: Moehler, who pitched for the Marlins in 2005 and 2006 before joining the Astros, is coming off one of his worst outings of the year. He gave up nine hits and seven runs (six earned), including a grand slam, in six innings against the Giants on Wednesday in Houston. He's pitched in only two games in his career against Florida, but has extensive experience at the Marlins' stadium, where he's 5-11 with a 4.91 ERA in 35 games.

home_pitcher_note: The 22-year-old continues to strive for consistency. In his last start, Volstad let a big lead slip away in what turned into a disheartening loss at Washington. The Marlins had leads of 6-0 and 8-3, but Volstad struggled, giving up seven runs (four earned) in 4 1/3 innings. Allowing home runs has been an issue all season for Volstad, and it was again at Washington. In 23 starts, Volstad has surrendered 23 home runs. At home, the 6-foot-8 right-hander is 3-6 with a 4.97 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt is returning to action for the first time since straining his left lower back July 28 in Chicago. He lasted only 1 2/3 innings in that game before being removed. He hasn't faced the Marlins this year but is 5-4 with a 3.24 ERA in 11 career starts against Florida. That includes a 2-3 record and 3.46 ERA in six starts at Dolphin Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Nolasco has strung together four straight quality starts, coming off an impressive outing at Philadelphia. The 26-year-old gave up a two-run homer to Ben Francisco in the seventh inning, and that was it. He allowed those two runs and struck out seven. In his last two starts, the right-hander has yielded three runs in 14 innings with 15 strikeouts. Nolasco was 2-0 against the Astros last year.
away_pitcher_note: Norris, making his first appearance before the home crowd in his last start Friday, followed up his strong start Sunday in St. Louis by holding the Brewers to three hits and two runs and overcame five walks. He struck out seven batters to improve to 2-0 in two career starts. He pitched seven scoreless innings against the Cardinals in his first Major League start Aug. 2. Norris, 24, was 4-9 with a 2.63 ERA in 19 starts at Round Rock this year, allowing 104 hits, 53 walks and striking out 112 batters in 120 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Last Saturday at Philadelphia, West made his first start for the Marlins since July 11, the night he was optioned to Double-A Jacksonville. The 23-year-old left-hander ran up a high pitch count and lasted four-plus innings. West gave up three runs, with two earned, and he exited after 93 pitches. West was not involved in the decision of a 6-4 Florida victory. The lefty has made 11 MLB starts, and he seeks his first win since June 25 against the Orioles.
away_pitcher_note: Hampton came out of his last start Saturday against the Brewers after only two innings because of a sprained right knee and was later diagnosed with a torn meniscus in his right knee after undergoing an MRI. Hampton is 10-7 with a 4.48 ERA in 25 career games against the Marlins, including 24 starts. He's 4-3 with a 5.19 ERA all-time at Dolphin Stadium in 11 games (10 starts).

home_pitcher_note: It wasn't vintage Josh Johnson in his last start, but the 6-foot-7 right-hander was effective enough to collect his 11th win and 18th quality start in 23 overall outings this season. At Philadelphia, the 25-year-old ace gave up one run on four hits with six strikeouts and one walk. He was lifted after 85 pitches and 55 strikes, but he had some stressful innings. Three double plays helped Johnson get out of jams. The Marlins are 18-5 with the righty on the mound. On May 9 at Colorado, Johnson beat the Rockies, giving up one run in eight innings. Johnson has pitched 154 innings this year; his career high is 157, which came during his 2006 season as a rookie.
away_pitcher_note: Hammel hasn't been sharp lately, and he knows it. In his last start, on Sunday against the Cubs, Hammel gave up 11 hits and had only one 1-2-3 frame in his five-plus innings. Yet he picked up the victory, yielding just three runs -- all earned. In his his past seven starts, Hammel has a 6.48 ERA, though the Rockies have won four of those starts. Hammel's problem right now is that he can't throw his fastball on a downhill plane, thus the pitch is coming out of his hand flat. Therefore, hitters have been able to square up on him.

home_pitcher_note: VandenHurk had his share of baserunners against the Astros on Monday, but he got out of trouble most of the time and got the win after giving up just two runs. Still, the three walks and five hits put his pitch count at 97 after five innings, ending his start a bit early. VandenHurk, taking the No. 4 spot in the rotation with Anibal Sanchez on the disabled list and youngsters Andrew Miller and Sean West fighting inconsistency, has now given up no more than two runs in four of his five starts for Florida this year. He gave up two runs in 4 1/3 innings during his only career start against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Cook left his last start, a 3-1 loss to the Phillies, after five innings and 73 pitches with a hyperextended right big toe. The injury led to his being removed from a start Monday against the Pirates. He suffered it backing up third on Jimmy Rollins' triple. In that contest, Cook was toe-to-toe with the Phillies' Cliff Lee but threw two bad pitches -- one Paul Bako hit for his first homer of the season, the other the triple by Rollins. Cook is 1-1 with a 3.55 ERA in two starts at Florida.

home_pitcher_note: Volstad simply couldn't get out of the fifth inning in a no-decision against the Astros on Tuesday. In that frame, he gave up five runs, fired 35 pitches to nine batters and left before recording the final out. The 22-year-old finished giving up six runs on eight hits and three walks in 4 2/3 innings. Over his last two starts, he's gone a combined nine frames and given up 13 runs (10 earned). Volstad recorded his first career win against the Rockies and sports a 4.15 ERA in three career games (two starts) against them.

away_pitcher_note: De La Rosa had poor arm-side command of his fastball early, but made pitches when they counted. Then he held the Cubs to one run on seven hits in 7 2/3 innings and struck out 11 during the Rockies' 11-5 victory at Coors Field. The fact De La Rosa could recognize overthrowing early and correct it before letting it ruin his outing is a sign of growth.

home_pitcher_note: Norris became the first Astros pitcher to win his first three starts with the team when he beat the Marlins on Wednesday in Miami, but it wasn't pretty. He was the beneficiary of an offensive explosion and won despite giving up 10 hits and five runs -- four earned -- in five innings to improve to 3-0 in three career starts. Norris, 24, was 4-9 with a 2.63 ERA in 19 starts at Round Rock this year, allowing 104 hits, 53 walks and striking out 112 batters in 120 innings.
away_pitcher_note: After his worst outing ever on Aug. 12 at Land Shark Stadium, Nolasco gets a chance for redemption in the series opener at Houston. Nolasco surrendered a career-high 10 runs, topping the nine he yielded to the Mets at Shea Stadium on July 8, 2006. The 3 1/3 innings marked his shortest stint of the year. Previously, he lasted 3 2/3 at Milwaukee on May 13. Nolasco is now 2-1 in his career against the Astros. The right-hander had gone three straight starts of seven innings, and he didn't throw fewer than six innings since June 24.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Bazardo's first start with the Astros and third of his career after spending most of the season at Triple-A Round Rock. He allowed five runs (three earned) in his Astros debut on Aug. 8 and has thrown 4 1/3 scoreless innings in two outings since. He was 9-6 with a 3.20 ERA in 23 games (20 starts) at Round Rock this year before being called up. Bazardo appeared in one game with the Marlins in 2005 before getting into 14 games with Detroit in 2007 and '08.
away_pitcher_note: Without his best stuff, West was able to rely on his changeup to help keep the Astros in check over six innings at Land Shark Stadium on Aug. 13. Now, West will experience his second straight start against the Astros. This time, in Houston. The 23-year-old left-hander was efficient in six innings, limiting the Astros to one run on five hits. He didn't walk a batter, and he struck out three. This will be his 13th start. The rookie has yet to face the same team twice. When he was down at Double-A Jacksonville recently, he worked on improving his changeup and slider. His changeup was an "out pitch" against the Astros in Miami.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez's run of terrific starts came to a screeching halt on Friday in Milwaukee, where he was rocked in his worst outing of the year. He gave up 10 hits, 10 runs -- including three home runs -- and five walks in four innings to snap his personal six-game winning streak. Rodriguez was 6-0 with a 1.35 ERA in his previous nine starts and was named NL Pitcher of the Month for July. He is 2-1 with a 3.65 ERA in six career games against the Marlins, including four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Simply dominant is how to best describe Johnson's last outing. In fact, he had no-hit stuff, flirting with his first no-no. For 6 2/3 innings, the right-hander held the Rockies hitless before Garrett Atkins homered. Johnson worked 7 1/3 innings, allowing one hit and one run, while striking out a career-high 11. The Marlins are 18-6 when Johnson starts, and he has matched his career high for wins in a season (12). He previously did it during his 2006 rookie season.

home_pitcher_note: A pair of Ryan Howard homers provided all of the damage Vazquez incurred on Sunday night, when the righty lost for the first time in eight starts. The 33-year-old Vazaquez had surrendered just three homers over his previous nine starts combined. Enjoying one of his finest seasons, Vazquez has worked at least seven innings in each of his past seven starts and he has been charged with two earned runs or fewer in seven of his past 10 outings. He has allowed six earned runs and 10 hits in 13 1/3 innings against the Marlins this year.
away_pitcher_note: After Thursday's loss at Houston, the team announced Sanchez will come off the disabled list and start in the opener with Atlanta. Sanchez has been recovering from a right shoulder sprain. He last pitched for Florida on June 2 against the Brewers, exiting after three innings with discomfort. The right-hander has made two rehab assignment starts for Double-A Jacksonville. He has been impressive. On Aug. 12, he gave up one run in seven innings, and he exited on Monday after 3 1/3 innings because he was on a limited pitch count. He threw 45.

home_pitcher_note: Hanson has shown no sign of fatigue while going 3-0 with a 2.41 ERA in his three starts this month. The 22-year-old right-hander has also shown improved control while not issuing a walk in either of his past two starts.  Still, he was able to complete just six innings while allowing two runs and compiling 100 pitches against the D-backs on Monday.  This will be his first career start against the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: Because of an off day on Monday, Volstad will get an extra day of rest. The 22-year-old is in his first full big league season, and he's already logged 146 1/3 innings. He last pitched in the first game of Sunday's double-header with the Rockies. The Palm Beach Gardens, Fla., native collected the win in that game, giving up one run in five innings. But his pitch count reached 100. On April 14 in Atlanta, Volstad gave up one run on three hits in seven innings, collecting the win in his only start vs. the Braves this year.

home_pitcher_note: In a startling departure from his consistency of the past month, Lowe allowed all eight of his runs against the Mets in one inning last Tuesday. It marked the first time Lowe had given up more than three runs in an outing since July 5, and the first time the Mets had scored at least eight runs in an inning all season. They were one of the few teams this season to hit Lowe as hard as the Marlins, who tagged him for six runs in five innings on May 6. But Lowe won that game, and hasn't lost to the Marlins in over two years.
away_pitcher_note: Four batters into his previous start, it looked like it was going to be a rough night. Nolasco gave up a two-out double to Lance Berkman at Houston, and Carlos Lee followed with a two-run homer. From that point, Nolasco settled and dominated. He retired 23 straight until one-out in the ninth inning, and he logged a complete game victory, striking out 10 on 115 pitches. Nolasco has a chance to reach double-digits in wins for the second straight year. He won 15 a year ago, and he also posted 11 wins a rookie in 2006. The 26-year-old on July 28 had a no-decision with Atlanta, giving up two runs in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Since rejoining the rotation on Aug. 8, West has made three starts, and his longest outing of them has been six innings. The 23-year-old rookie comes off a loss at Houston. In four innings, he allowed four runs, with three earned. He threw 62 pitches, struck out two and didn't issue a walk. This will be his 14th big league start of the season, to go along with 11 starts and 12 games at Double-A Jacksonville. On May 29, West faced the Mets at New York, and he wasn't involved in the decision. He gave up one run in seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Nelson Figueroa will make a spot start in place of Johan Santana after it was announced Monday that the Mets ace would see a doctor about his ailing elbow instead of making his scheduled start on Tuesday.

home_pitcher_note: A rarity happened in Johnson's last start. The All-Star was unable to turn in a quality start. Twenty of his 25 starts have been quality caliber -- at least six innings and three or less earned runs. At Houston, however, the 25-year-old gave up four runs in 4 1/3 innings. It was his third-shortest outing of the season. Johnson will look to bounce back against a team he has enjoyed great success against. Johnson is 2-0 with a 2.45 ERA in three starts against the Mets this year, and he's 6-0 (2.05) in his career.
away_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Pelfrey put forth his second straight solid start, limiting the Phillies to two runs on six hits over six innings. The right-hander escaped a bases-loaded, one-out jam in his final inning, inducing popups from pinch-hitter Ben Francisco and Jimmy Rollins. Next, Pelfrey will face his career nemesis in the Marlins, against whom he is 1-5 with a 5.36 ERA in nine career starts. Pelfrey did, however, have one of his best starts of the season against Florida earlier this year, holding the NL East foe to one run on five hits in 7 2/3 innings in a no-decision on May 29 at Citi Field. Pelfrey is 0-1 with a 5.94 ERA in three career starts at Land Shark Stadium. Cody Ross is 5-for-14 against Pelfrey with two extra-base hits, while four of Dan Uggla's seven hits off the righty have been doubles. Hanley Ramirez is the only current Marlins batter with a home run against Pelfrey.

home_pitcher_note: The Marlins couldn't have asked for a better return to the rotation for Sanchez than what he gave them his last time out. Making his first start since June 2, Sanchez flirted with a no-hitter at Atlanta on Friday, holding the Braves hitless through 5 1/3 innings before opposing pitcher Javier Vazquez singled. In six-plus innings, the 25-year-old gave up one run and struck out seven. This will be Sanchez's ninth start of the season. He faced the Mets on April 10 but was not involved in the decision. He has had two stints on the disabled list this year due to a right shoulder sprain.
away_pitcher_note: Redding had his finest outing of the season on Saturday against the Phillies, giving up a single hit in five shutout innings. Unfortunately for him, he was working on two days' rest, and the bullpen quickly coughed up a 1-0 lead. Redding is 4-5 with a 5.70 ERA in 12 career starts against the Marlins, including giving up seven runs in four innings in a loss to Florida on May 30. He is 3-1, however, with a 3.82 ERA in his five starts at Land Shark Stadium. Jeremy Hermida is 10-for-17 in his career off Redding with four doubles, a home run and nine RBIs.

home_pitcher_note: A season-long problem yet again hurt Volstad in his last start. In the first inning at Atlanta on Saturday, the 6-foot-7 right-hander gave up two home runs. He's now been taken deep 26 times in 26 starts. After a rough four-run first inning, he did piece together three straight scoreless innings. Still, the last time Volstad has worked deeper than five innings was on July 31, when he threw 6 2/3 innings against the Cubs. Still, the Palm Beach Gardens, Fla., native had won three straight decisions since July 21.
away_pitcher_note: Correia's 26th start of the season clearly wasn't his best as he allowed five runs on 10 hits over 5 2/3 innings against the Cardinals on Saturday. Correia, who has allowed two home runs in his combined last seven starts, allowed a three-run home run to Matt Holliday in the first inning and later a solo shot to Colby Rasmus. Correia's command wasn't bad -- he had two walks to go with two strikeouts -- but he elevated too many fastballs, which the hot-hitting Cardinals took advantage of.

home_pitcher_note: It was a struggle from the start for Nolasco in his last start. The right-hander yielded a three-run homer to Brian McCann in the first inning at Turner Field. He ended up exiting after 4 1/3 innings with the bases loaded at Atlanta, with his team ahead, 5-4. He threw 95 pitches. Nolasco was coming off a three-hit, complete-game win at Houston on Aug. 18, in a game in which he threw 115 pitches. This will be his second meeting with the Padres. At San Diego on July 22, he threw 6 1/3 scoreless innings, allowing two hits.
away_pitcher_note: The Padres will go with LeBlanc to pitch the second game of a three-game series against the Marlins on Saturday. The 25-year-old hasn't started in the big leagues since June 25, when he gave up four runs on five hits and three walks in 1 1/3 innings against the Mariners. This will be his eighth Major League appearance and seventh start; he went 1-3 with an 8.02 ERA as a September callup last year. LeBlanc has made 24 appearances (20 starts) for Triple-A Portland this season, going 4-9 with a 3.87 ERA. The Louisiana native struck out 95 batters and walked 31. LeBlanc, a second-round pick by the Padres in 2006, will be making his first career appearance against the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: West picked up his fifth win of the season after throwing six strong innings for the Marlins. The left-hander held the Mets to one run on six hits while striking out two and walking three. The 23-year-old showed poise and determination throughout his outing by pitching himself out of jams that he got himself into. While West struggled to find the strike zone at times late in his start, he was able to make pitches when he needed to and avoid any damage.
away_pitcher_note: The Padres have been keeping a close eye on the number of innings Latos has pitched and may shut him down in September. Against the Braves on Tuesday, he showed that his arm might be a little fresher than some would expect. He tossed seven innings of two-hit shutout baseball on his way to a no-decision. He didn't walk a batter and struck out four while throwing just 89 pitches before exiting.

home_pitcher_note: Johnson did not have his best stuff his last time out. While he picked up his 13th win of the season, Johnson struggled to put batters away. The right-hander was able to turn in his 21st quality start of the season by holding the Mets to three runs on nine hits over six innings while striking out seven. The 25-year-old improved to 7-0 against the Mets in nine career starts.
away_pitcher_note: Kawakami seemed to be cruising toward winning a second consecutive start on Wednesday before allowing four hits to the only five Padres batters he ended up facing in the sixth inning. While not allowing a run during the first five innings, he looked like the same pitcher who had posted a 2.39 ERA in his previous four starts. Now, the Japanese right-hander will be looking to bounce back against the Marlins, who have tallied 10 earned runs in the 10 2/3 innings he has completed against them this year.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez struggled his last time out after pitching brilliantly in his first outing since returning from the disabled list on Aug. 21. The right-hander had a hard time shutting down the Mets, allowing four runs (two earned) on eight hits over 3 2/3 innings while striking out two and walking three. Sanchez will get a chance to redeem himself when he faces the Braves his next time out. The 25-year-old held Atlanta to one run on two hits over six innings the last time he faced the Braves.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson will make his first Major League start since exiting Land Shark Stadium's mound on July 23, 2008, with right elbow discomfort that would lead to him undergoing Tommy John surgery one week later.  The right-hander said he'll be unfazed by the fact that this return start will occur at the same location where he was last healthy enough to pitch.  Hudson is 7-2 with a 2.63 ERA in 13 career starts against the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: VandenHurk was announced as Wednesday's starter following Monday's 5-2 loss to the Braves. One of Florida's September callups, he has made six starts this season for the Marlins, with the last one coming on Aug. 16 in a loss to the Rockies. VandenHurk has had more success this season in the Minors, going 5-2 with a 2.87 ERA for Triple-A New Orleans over 11 starts. The 24-year-old has faced the Braves once this season, taking a no-decision after holding them to two runs on four hits while striking out nine over six innings on July 30.
away_pitcher_note: Vazquez bounced back from consecutive losses with an impressive seven scoreless innings against the Padres on Thursday night. The 33-year-old right-hander will be looking to avenge the loss he suffered on Aug. 21, when the Marlins used a pair of homers to tally five earned runs against him in just 6 2/3 innings. He is 0-2 with a 4.95 ERA in three starts against the Marlins this year. They are the only team that has handed him two losses this season.

home_pitcher_note: The 26-year-old had some tough luck in his previous start. After striking out the side in order the first inning on Aug. 29 against the Padres, he waited through a 44-minute rain delay to get back on the mound. Nolasco grinded out 5 1/3 innings, striking out seven. But he yielded three runs, and was lifted after 99 pitches. He wasn't involved in the decision. This will be Nolasco's third start of the season against the Braves. He is looking for his first win. The Marlins split the previous two meetings when Nolasco started vs. Atlanta.
away_pitcher_note: Hanson had won four straight starts before a rain-shortened two-inning stint against the Phillies on Friday night handed him his first loss since July 31. The lone damage he incurred came courtesy of Ryan Howard's opposite-field solo homer. The 23-year-old right-hander is 4-1 with a 2.93 ERA in his past five starts. He allowed three earned runs and four hits in seven innings against the Marlins on Aug. 22.

home_pitcher_note: Mock pitched well against the first-place Cardinals on Sunday afternoon, allowing two runs in six innings and striking out five. But he made one big mistake, serving up an RBI hit by Albert Pujols in the sixth inning with first base open to allow the Cardinals to break a 1-1 tie and slip past Washington, 2-1. Mock has won three of his past five starts and has looked impressive since returning to the starting rotation on July 19. He made 13 relief appearances in April before being sent to Triple-A Syracuse to become a starter. "Whoever decided to put Mock in the rotation, it was a good decision," said Cardinals manager Tony La Russa. "Boy, he was very good."
away_pitcher_note: The 23-year-old West has put together a nice stretch of starts. Four of his past six outings have been quality starts, including his past two, both wins. The left-hander beat the Padres on Aug. 30, giving up three runs (two earned) in six innings. He struck out seven, which matched a season high. West has one previous appearance against the Nationals. On June 30, he worked 4 1/3 innings, giving up five runs in a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez took the loss on Monday in San Diego despite a second solid showing since the Nationals signed him on August 26. He pitched a complete game, but allowed three runs on seven hits as Washington mustered little offense. The defeat moved his record at PETCO Park to 0-5, although he owns 12 career wins against San Diego, second most to the team he'll face next, the Florida Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson pitched brilliantly in his last start, no-hitting the Braves for 5 2/3 innings. But things fell apart with two outs in the seventh inning. The right-hander allowed three runs on five hits over 6 2/3 innings while striking out eight and walking three. Johnson will have a chance to bounce back against the Nationals, who scored all four of their runs against him in the eighth inning the last time he faced them.

home_pitcher_note: In his last outing, Martin posted just the second quality start of his young career, holding the Padres to three runs (two earned) in six innings during a losing effort. Martin has opposed the Marlins just once in his career, on Aug. 4, when the righty allowed three runs on six hits in 4 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez struggled with his command at times in his last start, throwing 93 pitches over five innings. The right-hander allowed three runs on five hits while striking out four and walking two. Sanchez will look to pick up his first win since August 21 when he faces the Nationals in his next start.

home_pitcher_note: Redding turned in his second consecutive quality start Wednesday in Colorado, pitching 6 2/3 innings and holding the Rockies to two runs on seven hits and a walk while striking out six. He might well have matched his season high of seven innings had his pitch count not risen with a lot of long at bats, taking hitters to three balls and full counts throughout the outing. He alternated between pitching through traffic in the odd innings and throwing 1-2-3 innings in the evens. He used a couple different deliveries to effectively keep the Rockies off balance, and he largely spared the bullpen by taking a tie game into the late innings.
away_pitcher_note: While VandenHurk held the Braves to three runs (two earned) on six hits over five innings, the right-hander was hit hard. Atlanta's bats seemed to hit everything hard. The Braves smashed several balls to the warning track, but VandenHurk was able to keep the ball in the park, limit the big inning and pitch out of several jams.

home_pitcher_note: Misch was masterful in his second start of the season, taming Coors Field on Thursday and pitching seven innings of two-run ball to notch his first career win in his 13th career start. His first 6 2/3 innings were scoreless, keeping the Rockies to two hits, but he yielded back-to-back solo shots with two outs in the seventh. He mixed his pitches well and was efficient in his approach, keeping his pitch count to 95. He now has a 1.93 ERA as a starter for the Mets, having made consecutive seven-inning starts with a combined three runs allowed. He posted a 4.09 ERA as a reliever and seems to benefit from the space to use all his tools as a starter. He was particularly effective with his offspeed pitches, using them effectively at any point in the count and reminding manager Jerry Manuel of a Tom Glavine-type pitcher.
away_pitcher_note: Nolasco picked up his 10th win of the season Thursday after holding the Braves to three runs on seven hits over six innings while striking out seven. The right-hander did not allow Atlanta to have a big inning against him as he pitched out of a bases-loaded, one-out jam in the fifth to limit the scoring in the inning to just two runs. In this start, Nolasco will try to beat the Mets for the first time this season.

home_pitcher_note: Parnell was masterful in his seven innings against the Cubs last Friday, limiting Chicago to five hits in seven shutout innings. It snapped a streak of three horrendous starts for Parnell, who is still making the transition to the rotation from the bullpen. Parnell has yet to start versus Florida, but he did struggle in seven relief appearances against the Marlins. He gave up three runs on seven hits in four innings lifetime facing Florida. Hanley Ramirez has done the most damage off Parnell, going 3-for-4 with two RBIs.
away_pitcher_note: West struggled in Friday's 9-6 Marlins victory over the Nationals. Florida gave West a pair of early four-run leads, but he couldn't make it past the third inning. He was frustrated afterward because he gave up all five of his runs with two outs and wasn't able to keep the ball down enough against a potent Nationals lineup. Those are the things that he'll be working on before Thursday's start in New York. The bullpen picked West up in this game, but he doesn't want to worry about that again.

home_pitcher_note: For the second straight start, Johnson will be facing the Nationals, a team that's given him some trouble. Last Sunday at Washington, Johnson collected his 14th win, giving up one run on two hits in five innings. He struck out one. The team is monitoring the 24-year-old's innings. He has 183 1/3 on the season, already a career high. He threw 82 pitches at Washington. Johnson's ERA at home is 2.39.
away_pitcher_note: Martin started on Sept. 6 and gave up two runs in 6 2/3 innings, making few mistakes. The first was a big one, however, when Hanley Ramirez hit an 0-1 pitch in the fourth inning for his 21st home run -- and 100th of his career. In the seventh, Martin was able to get two quick outs, but he walked Cameron Maybin and gave up a single to Ross Gload to put runners on first and third. Reliever Ron Villone entered the game and gave up an RBI single to Chris Coghlan. Interim manager Jim Riggleman acknowledged that he was concerned about Martin at the beginning of the game because the velocity on his fastball was down. But Martin picked it up as the game wore on.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez gets a rematch with the Nationals after a great six-inning effort against Washington last Sunday. He gave up only four hits but lost a chance at the victory when the Nats rallied to win on Ryan Zimmerman's two-run homer in the ninth inning. Sanchez did a good job of harnessing his control, staying ahead in the count, striking out five and walking only two. It was one of his best performances of this season.

He allowed three runs on just four hits, but again was bitten by the long ball, giving up two home runs for a second consecutive start. Harang had good velocity and a decent slider in his 99-pitch outing. He left after seven innings with the score tied at 3. It was an improvement from his Opening Day outing when he gave up four runs (three earned) over five innings, with two walks, three strikeouts and two home runs in an 11-6 loss to St. Louis.

home_pitcher_note: It doesn't get much better than Halladay's performance against Houston, his second start in a Phillies uniform. So far, the former AL Cy Young winner's transition to the National League has been a piece of cake. His complete-game gem against the Astros lasted two hours and 21 minutes, with only seven hits allowed, no walks and eight strikeouts. Sure, his initial two outings have come against the Nationals and Astros. But Doc's just getting his feet wet in a new league. He's faced the Marlins twice in his career, and is 0-1 with a 5.00 ERA against them. It will be his first start at home, though, and that should give Halladay an additional edge.
away_pitcher_note: Aggressively pounding the strike zone is what the Marlins have been looking for out of Sanchez. For the most part, the 26-year-old did that in his first start. In six innings, he struck out five and walked just one against the Dodgers. He did have a rough fourth inning, giving up four runs. Sanchez wasn't involved in the decision. The right-hander will make his first road start. For his career, he is 2-4 with a 5.40 ERA against the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Moyer had an interesting debut Saturday against Houston. He retired the first eight batters he faced. He then allowed the next eight batters to reach base to give the Astros a 5-4 lead. He retired seven of the final nine batters he faced. In six innings, he allowed nine hits, five runs, one walk and two home runs. He at least kept the Phillies in the game. They came back to beat the Astros, 9-6.
away_pitcher_note: The long ball haunted Nolasco in his last start against the Reds, when he gave up three home runs -- two to Scott Rolen and one to Orlando Cabrera -- in a no-decision on Monday. The 27-year-old, pretty much unhittable in Spring Training, finished after giving up five runs on nine hits and a walk while striking out four and firing 92 pitches. The last time Nolasco had given up three home runs was June 5, 2008, against the Braves. For his career against the Phillies, Nolasco is 5-3 with a 4.23 ERA in 11 games (eight starts).

home_pitcher_note: Hamels earned his second win of the season on Monday in Philadelphia's home opener against the Nationals, but it wasn't as uplifting an outing as the Phillies would have liked from their No. 2 starter. Hamels labored through 5 2/3 innings, allowing four runs on six hits and 109 pitches. Still searching for his efficiency, Hamels has struggled hitting his spots and mixing in a new cut fastball. Though his performance was a step up from his first start, Hamels is still not at the level Philadelphia expects from him. He has typically struggled in day games throughout his career, and Sunday's matinee against Florida will represent his second straight. He is just 2-6 in his career against the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: It could have been worse for Robertson in his last start. The lefty gave up six runs (three earned) in five innings against the Reds. He trailed by as many as five runs, but settled for a no-decision. The lefty has worked five innings in each of his first two starts and was taken deep for homers twice by the Reds.

home_pitcher_note: Myers is coming off his best outing of the season, on Wednesday against the Cardinals in St. Louis. He suffered the loss in the game, but he threw seven innings and allowed just two runs (one earned), four hits and two walks while striking out seven batters. Myers is 6-11 with a 5.64 ERA in 32 career games, including 24 starts, against Florida. He's started more games against Florida than any other team in his career after spending the first eight years of his career in the National League East with the Phillies. Myers is 1-1 with a 4.18 ERA in six games (four starts) at Minute Maid Park.
away_pitcher_note: The 23-year-old threw a career high 117 pitches in his last outing, which turned into a win over the Reds. Volstad worked 6 2/3 innings, and he was sailing along. The last pitch he threw was belted for a two-run homer by Paul Janish. Still, overall, Volstad had a quality start -- three runs in 6 2/3 innings. He did walk four, and struck out five. His previous high pitch mark was 115 at Tampa Bay last June 27. In his career, Volstad is 1-0 with a 4.97 ERA in two starts against the Astros.

home_pitcher_note: Norris is coming off his first win of the season, when he struck out nine Cardinals in a 5-1 win on Thursday in St. Louis. He lasted only five innings after allowing four hits and three walks and throwing 106 pitches. In two starts this year, he's given up 10 hits, three earned runs and struck out 12 batters in 7 2/3 innings. Norris faced the Marlins twice last year in consecutive starts on Aug. 12 in Miami and Aug. 18 in Houston. He's 1-1 with a 7.59 ERA in 10 2/3 innings in his career against the Marlins. Norris has allowed 19 hits, nine earned runs and struck out 10 in that span.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson had his best outing of the season while getting his first victory against the Reds on Thursday. That night, he struck out 10 batters while walking only one and finished scattering just one run on five hits in his six innings. The 26-year-old recorded five of his first six outs via the strikeout, but he did not go deeper in the game because he accumulated 45 pitches through just the first two frames. After that, though, Johnson said he started getting his rhythm. And it showed, as he retired nine of the last 11 batters he faced. For his career against the Astros, Johnson has struggled, going 0-3 with a 7.36 ERA in three games (two starts).

home_pitcher_note: Paulino is still searching for his first win of the season after taking a hard-luck loss in Friday's series opener in Chicago. He held the Cubs to one run entering the seventh inning before giving up four runs and taking the loss. Paulino went six innings and allowed six hits, three walks and struck out three. He has walked seven batters and struck out seven in two starts covering 11 innings this year. This will be Paulino's first career appearance against the Marlins. Paulino is 5-1 with a 6.49 ERA in 30 career games, including 22 starts, all with the Astros.
away_pitcher_note: Bottom line is his numbers haven't been pretty. But say this about Sanchez, he's found a way to do his part in preserving the bullpen. Sanchez gutted out six innings in his last start, a loss at Philadelphia. The way the game started, it didn't look like he'd last through the first inning. Yet he turned in six innings, giving up five runs on eight hits with four walks and a strikeout. In the first inning, he threw 35 pitches (15 strikes). The Marlins are 1-1 in games that he's started. In his career, he is 1-0 with a 0.75 ERA vs. the Astros.

home_pitcher_note: While Smith's ERA has steadily decreased in his first three 2010 starts, he's still struggling to find any semblance of consistency. His most recent outing, Sunday at Atlanta, is a perfect example. The five hits he allowed are acceptable, though it means he was pitching out of trouble. The seven walks he issued only exacerbated his problems, finally catching up and forcing the left-hander to exit after 5 1/3 innings. Through 17 1/3 innings on the season, 18 strikeouts aren't sufficient to offset 15 hits and 11 walks allowed. For a command pitcher who relies heavily on a plus changeup to compensate for a high-80s fastball and a middling curve, anything less than pinpoint control puts him at a serious disadvantage.
away_pitcher_note: One first-pitch fastball with two outs in the ninth inning stood in Nolasco's way of a shutout last Saturday at Philadelphia. While Jayson Werth delivered a home run, Nolasco still finished with his fourth career shutout. Nolasco became the first Marlin to go the distance since he did on Aug. 18, 2009 at Houston. Of his 109 pitches, 71 were strikes. Nolasco had previously gone as deep as six innings this year. The right-hander has struck out 13 and walked seven this season in 20 2/3 innings.
