home_pitcher_note: In order for Cook to be successful, the right-hander needs to pound the strike zone with a heavy sinker, get hitters to chase it and induce groundouts. When that doesn't happen -- and it hasn't happened consistently enough in 2010 -- Cook struggles. That's what occurred in his last outing Monday at Washington. Cook was tagged for five runs on seven hits in three innings, walking four and forcing manager Jim Tracy to go to his bullpen earlier than he wanted. Cook has won 27 games in since 2008, so he knows how to go deep into games in a pitch-efficient manner. The Rockies need him to regain his ability to be an innings-eating anchor to their rotation.
away_pitcher_note: After pitching in 50-degree temperatures in Philadelphia last Sunday, Robertson said: "This is my kind of weather." Formerly with the Tigers, Robertson is used to pitching in the cold. He likely will have some more in his start at Colorado. The lefty comes off an efficient outing, working 6 1/3 shutout innings at a tough place to pitch -- Citizens Bank Park. Coors Field will present another challenge. Robertson has shown craftiness, like he did in his last start, working around four walks.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa helped his own cause in a 10-4 victory over the Nationals on Tuesday night. His three-run double proved to be the big hit in an eight-run inning. That gave the Rockies an early 10-0 lead. He helped again later with a double and finished 2-for-3 with those three RBIs. But De La Rosa had a tough time despite the early lead, needing 118 pitches to make his way through five-plus innings. The left-hander battled some control problems, striking out six but walking four to improve his record to 2-1 on the season. He gave up four runs on seven hits to Washington.
away_pitcher_note: Volstad has worked at least six innings in all three of his starts. Completing seven has been a challenge. The 23-year-old's best outing was a 6 2/3-inning effort in a win over the Reds. He tossed a career-most 117 pitches that day. His last time out, he was not involved in the decision against the Astros. He gave up three runs on five hits. Volstad has pitched to contact all year. He has eight strikeouts and seven walks in 19 innings. Volstad made his MLB debut in 2008 at Colorado, picking up the win in relief.

home_pitcher_note: Florida's ace has yet to find his groove. He has one win in four starts, and the Marlins have won two of those outings. In his last start, his pitch count was 96 through six innings, and he was lifted at Houston. The Marlins were leading when Johnson exited, but the Astros rallied to win. In 22 innings, Johnson has 22 strikeouts and 11 walks. The team is urging him to be more aggressive and attack the hitters. Johnson has been dealing with some minor adjustments to his delivery.
away_pitcher_note: Latos won his first game of the season in his last start, against the Giants, as the Padres got all of one hit in a 1-0 victory. Latos tossed seven scoreless innings, combining a fastball and slider to get 14 ground-ball outs as the Giants jumped on pitches early in the count against the 22-year-old. Latos, who was shut down for most of last September as the team didn't want to extend his innings, had lost five straight decisions dating to Aug. 14. Latos continues to mature as a pitcher. Even though he often relies on a mid-90s fastball, he isn't trying to simply overpower hitters. He's pitching more to contact and mixing in his changeup frequently.

home_pitcher_note: Coming off his finest performance of the season, Sanchez now looks to build some consistency. The right-hander was effective over 6 2/3 innings at Houston, allowing one run. While he struck out only one, the key stat was he didn't issue a walk for the first time this year. Sanchez has never faced the Padres. He has made one home start, and was not involved in the decision on April 11 against the Dodgers.
away_pitcher_note: Garland helped the Padres cap a 7-2 homestand with a strong outing on Wednesday against the Giants. Garland tossed seven-plus innings in winning his first game with the Padres. He allowed one run, got 14 ground-ball outs and allowed six hits with two walks and one strikeout. "In this park, in any park, that's what you want," Garland said of the ground balls, a sure sign that he was able to bury his fastball and changeup in the bottom of the strike zone. Garland lowered his ERA to 2.86 after something of a rough start to the season because of command issues. The changeup continues to be a good pitch for Garland to go along with his sinking fastball.

home_pitcher_note: Because of a doubleheader on April 24 in Colorado, the Marlins had to shuffle up their rotation a bit. Robertson was impacted. Even though the left-hander threw Game 2 that day, he will come back on three days' rest to face San Diego. The 32-year-old threw 85 pitches against the Rockies, and he worked four innings, taking the loss. In 20 1/3 innings this season, Robertson has struck out 14 and walked 10. Just one of his four starts has lasted longer than five innings -- 6 1/3 at Philadelphia on April 18.
away_pitcher_note: Correia, who led the Padres with 12 victories a year ago, will go for his fourth win of the season in the final game of a three-game series against the Marlins. He took a no-hitter into the sixth inning of his last start against the Reds but left after getting two outs and allowing two runs. Still, the Padres have scored 29 runs for Correia in 23 innings. A year ago, he was left with 10 no-decisions, including eight quality starts in which he didn't receive a win or loss. "I'm never going to complain -- I'd go five innings every time if we're going to win and score like that," Correia said.

home_pitcher_note: Outstanding in his past two starts, Nolasco will look to keep building on his past success. In road games at Philadelphia and Colorado, the right-hander went 2-0, allowing one run in 19 innings, striking out 13 and walking three. Because of off-days and a rainout, he will be throwing six days after beating the Rockies. In those two games, he threw 68 percent of his 214 pitches for strikes.
away_pitcher_note: Olsen atoned for a tough outing in his previous start on Sunday afternoon, pitching seven shutout innings in the Nationals' 1-0 win over the Dodgers at Nationals Park. On Tuesday, Olsen lasted two-plus innings and gave up six runs on seven hits against Rockies. It looked like the lefty would have a similar outing against Los Angeles, as he was in serious trouble in the first inning. The Dodgers loaded the bases with one out, but Casey Blake struck out and Ronnie Belliard flied out to center field to end the threat. Including Blake and Belliard, Olsen retired 13 out of the next 14 hitters he faced. It helped that his slider was his out pitch.

home_pitcher_note: Through three innings of his last start, Volstad was pretty effective, even though he allowed a solo homer in the second to Colorado's Seth Smith. In the fourth inning, the game slipped away from him. The 23-year-old threw 35 pitches in the fourth, and he was out of the game after a season-low 4 1/3 innings in a loss to the Rockies. Volstad seeks his second win of the season, and first since April 14 against the Reds. He had gone at least six innings in his first three starts prior to the rough outing in Denver.
away_pitcher_note: Stammen had his second straight quality start on Saturday, but didn't figure in the decision against the Dodgers. Stammen lasted seven innings and gave up three runs on six hits, but it was the long ball that did him in. The Nats were ahead, 1-0, when Casey Blake hit a two-run homer to give Los Angeles a 2-1 lead in the top of the second inning. Blake hit his second home run -- a solo shot -- off Stammen in the top of the seventh.

home_pitcher_note: So, how does Johnson improve on his last outing? On Monday, Johnson turned in the start of his life, hurling going the distance and driving in three runs in a 10-1 win over the Padres. He Johnson allowed as many hits -- three -- as he had himself. He struck out a career-high 12 batters, allowed just four baserunners -- the other on his only walk -- and was two innings away from the first shutout of his career, until Matt Stairs hit a sacrifice fly in the eighth inning. Still, Johnson will settle for the fourth complete game of his career. That came to fruition when he struck out Chase Headley to end it on his 117th pitch. Johnson came into the game with an uncharacteristic 4.09 ERA and hadn't pitched past the sixth in any of his previous four starts. For his career against the Nationals, the 26-year-old is 5-0 with a 3.51 ERA in 11 games (10 starts).
away_pitcher_note: Lannan will try to get back to pitching more efficiently when he faces the Marlins in the series finale. Lannan admittedly labored over his last two starts, yielding 22 runners and seven runs over 12 innings against the Rockies and Cubs -- even though he was able to keep his team in both games. He looked more in control in an earlier game against the Brewers, holding them to two runs over seven innings. Despite his travails with the strike zone against the Cubs in his last game, he held them to three runs in an eventual 4-3 loss. Still, Lannan noted that he was "sick" of doing things the hard way. Against the Marlins, he has pitched well on occasion and is a career 2-1 with a 4.43 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Why Sanchez has made progress in his last two starts is pretty basic. The right-hander is throwing strikes more regularly. Even though he suffered a loss on April 27 to the Padres, Sanchez was effective over 6 1/3 innings, allowing three runs (two earned). Of his 101 pitches, 65 were strikes, as he struck out seven and walked two. In his previous outing -- April 22 at Houston -- Sanchez threw 89 pitches with 65 strikes in a win. He has walked two in his last 13 innings.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start, Lincecum was three outs away from becoming the first Giants pitcher to win not only his first five starts of the season, but also five games in April, since John Burkett in 1993. A complete game also appeared within reach for Lincecum, who had surrendered three hits, struck out 11 and thrown 98 pitches entering the ninth. But after walking Shane Victorino on four pitches with one out, Giants manager Bruce Bochy pulled Lincecum in favor of closer Brian Wilson. Wilson blew the save, the Giants lost and Lincecum remained 4-0 with a 1.27 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: After going on short rest in his previous start, Robertson will be well-rested for his sixth start of the season. Due to two scheduled team days off, the left-hander will be taking the mound exactly one week after his last outing. On April 28 against the Padres, Robertson was going on three days' rest. For four innings, it wasn't a factor, as he allowed just one hit in that span. But everything changed in the fifth. Robertson faced six batters in the inning, and all reached. He was charged with five runs, all in the inning. He threw 79 pitches and lost his second straight decision.
away_pitcher_note: Zito is 4-0 for the first time in his career. He was 0-7 over his last two Aprils. He's posted five consecutive quality starts. In his last one, he allowed two runs over eight innings. The four consecutive wins is his longest such streak since winning six straight from May 17, 2006, to June 16, 2006, with the Oakland A's.

home_pitcher_note: Mechanically and physically, Nolasco wasn't himself in his last start. The right-hander admitted it was one of those days where he didn't feel quite right. That happens over the course of a season. Nolasco worked four innings, giving up five runs while striking out seven in a loss to the Nationals. It was Nolasco's shortest stint since working 3 1/3 innings on Aug. 12, 2009 against Houston. Lifetime, he is 1-1 with a 1.13 ERA against San Francisco.
away_pitcher_note: Cain fanned eight and allowed only one hit and three walks in eight shutout innings against the Rockies. It was his first win, and it also lowered his ERA from 3.80 to 2.84. He hadn't struck out eight since Sept. 27 last year, and against Colorado they were mostly on his fastball, which was spot-on. It was the third time in his career he's allowed one hit and no earned runs.

home_pitcher_note: Operating on a week's rest, Stammen had trouble controlling his fastball and soft slider in a forgettable outing Saturday night against the Marlins. He allowed four runs (three earned) on seven hits and two walks in four-plus innings in the loss. The effort broke a string of eight consecutive games where Nationals pitchers had quality starts. Now Stammen gets a rematch, this time on his home field. He expects to be sharper in what shapes up as a chance for redemption. He can recall that one of the hits against him last time is hard to be duplicated -- an outside pitch that John Baker nearly golfed off the ground -- and he's mindful that a crucial run-producing two-strike single by Cody Ross came on the same type of pitch that Ross couldn't handle earlier in the at-bat.
away_pitcher_note: Volstad meets the Nationals again. It may be difficult to repeat his previous showing. On Saturday at Sun Life Stadium, Volstad threw a four-hit complete game in a 7-1 win. It was his second career complete game. He walked one and struck out eight. Volstad also had two hits, marking his first career multihit game. On the road this season, Volstad is 0-1 with an 8.71 ERA in two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Left-hander John Lannan was scheduled to pitch against the Marlins, but he will miss the start because of elbow discomfort. Instead, Chico will make his first big league appearance since May 21, 2008. Not too long after that start, Chico had Tommy John surgery and missed almost two years of action. This season, Chico has pitched in five games for Harrisburg and is 1-2 with a respectable 3.12 ERA. The most impressive stat is that Chico has struck out 17 batters in 26 innings and walked just seven batters. Prior to this season, Chico was known to walked a lot of hitters.
away_pitcher_note: In un-Johnson-like fashion, the Marlins ace rolled to his third straight decision in his last outing. J.J. matched a season high with four walks, and allowed two runs in the second inning. He was at 98 pitches through six, and out of the game. Still, Johnson was effective enough to strike out eight, and allow just two runs in beating the Nationals. Now, he faces Washington for the second straight start, this time on the road. Johnson is 6-0 in his career against the Nationals, including 2-0 with a 3.82 ERA in 2009. He has 42 strikeouts in 37 innings this season.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez won his fourth game of the year on Tuesday, but he wasn't as sharp as he was in his previous four starts. He lasted 5 1/3 innings, gave up two runs (one earned) and walked five batters. Hernandez threw 123 pitches and 41 of them came in the first inning, when Atlanta scored the first run of the game. Nate McLouth scored on a sacrifice fly by Troy Glaus. Hernandez said pitching on seven days' rest had an effect on him.
away_pitcher_note: In a no decision against the Giants, Sanchez turned in his third straight quality start. In six innings, he gave up three runs (two earned) and logged 90 pitches while squaring off against Tim Lincecum. In all five of his starts, the right-hander has thrown six or more innings. His lone victory came on April 22 at Houston.

home_pitcher_note: Lilly did not get a win in his last start against the Pirates. The lefty gave up four runs on nine hits over six innings, including three doubles in a row. Very un-Lilly like, Lou Piniella said. Lilly is still building up arm strength after undergoing surgery last November, so he's still in Spring Training mode. The last start was only his third of the year.
away_pitcher_note: Robertson once again cruised along early, then struggled a bit late in a loss to the Giants on Wednesday. The 32-year-old gave up two earned runs on six hits and one walk in 5 1/3 innings, but he cruised through the first five frames. Robertson allowed one run and needed only 52 pitches to get through the first five innings. In the sixth, however, he let the first five hitters reach base -- one on a dropped fly ball by Brett Carroll -- and gave up two runs to eventually suffer his third consecutive loss. Said Marlins manager Fredi Gonzalez about Robertson's recent late-outing struggles: "We're going to sit down and put our heads together -- all three of us [along with pitching coach Randy St. Claire] -- and see what we can come up with, because that's not a guy that does that."

home_pitcher_note: Wells had his shortest outing as a starter in his last game against the Pirates and was mad at himself after the game about it, saying it was "terrible" and "unacceptable." Lou Piniella told him even Cy Young lost a few games. Wells lasted two innings, giving up seven runs, six earned, on five hits and three walks. He walked the first two batters he faced in the game and they were two of the five runs to score that inning. Wells had posted quality starts in three of his five previous starts, so the abbreviated outing was unexpected.
away_pitcher_note: Battling the rain, Nolasco left some balls out over the middle of the plate against the Giants on Thursday, but he still turned in a quality start, giving up three runs on five hits while striking out three and walking none in six innings. He has now turned in three quality starts in his six outings. But because the Marlins failed to score a run in the first five innings for the third consecutive game, Nolasco came away with the loss. It wasn't a great start, but it was an improvement over the 27-year-old's previous outing -- when he gave up five runs in a season-low four innings to the Nats. "He hasn't really been the Ricky we've seen, but today, three runs against a tough opponent ... and he gave us an opportunity to win the game," Marlins manager Fredi Gonzalez said Thursday.

home_pitcher_note: Silva picked up the win in his last start against the Reds, but it was a battle. The right-hander said he had some soreness in his neck and right shoulder -- nothing major, he said -- but it was uncomfortable. Part of the problem was a long fifth inning in which he faced eight batters and gave up four runs. Silva served up 10 hits over five innings and walked one. The good news is that his right wrist seems to be fine after he tweaked it during an at-bat in New York.
away_pitcher_note: The 23-year-old will be making his seventh start, and for the first time since April 25, it won't be against the Nationals. Perhaps that isn't a good thing for Volstad. In his last two starts, he's faced and beat the Nationals, giving up three runs in 18 innings with 12 strikeouts. Volstad has made four career starts with no decisions against the Cubs. He has a 2.81 ERA vs. them.

home_pitcher_note: The Marlins return home from a six-game road trip with Johnson on the mound. The 26-year-old right-hander lost to New York on Opening Day, as he gave up four runs in five innings, with four walks. But for his career, he is 7-1 with a 2.69 ERA lifetime in 10 starts. In his last start, JJ gave up three runs in six innings at Washington, striking out five. Johnson was in line for the win but settled for a no decision.
away_pitcher_note: Santana bounced back from the worst outing of his career (3 2/3 innings pitched, 10 runs against the Phillies) with a solid performance against the Giants. The lefty allowed four runs over 7 2/3 innings in a no decision. Next up are the Marlins, who Santana faced and earned a win against in his first start of the season, allowing one run over six innings while striking out five batters. Santana is 6-1 with a 1.66 ERA against Florida for his career, his lowest ERA against any team he has registered at least five starts against.

home_pitcher_note: Control was a problem for Sanchez in his last start, a no-decision at Washington. The right-hander matched his season high with four walks, and he threw a wild pitch. Two of the runners scored. The 4 2/3-inning stint was Sanchez's shortest of the season. In each of his first five starts, he tossed at least six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Against the Giants on Sunday, Perez failed to make it out of the fourth inning for the second time in his last three starts. The lefty has really struggled with his control, walking 15 over that span, including seven in his no-decision against San Francisco. He has now walked more hitters (25) than he has struck out (22) in six starts this season. Perez will face the Marlins for the first time since 2008, when he went 3-0 with a 2.23 ERA in six starts against Florida.

home_pitcher_note: The left-hander comes off arguably his finest outing of the season. In six innings against the Cubs, he gave up two runs on seven hits. The win was his first since beating the Phillies on April 18. In his first two May starts, he is 1-1 with a 3.18 ERA, striking out eight in 11 1/3 innings. On April 8 at New York, he threw five innings and beat the Mets.
away_pitcher_note: Maine continues to rebound from his poor start to the season, logging his third consecutive quality start against the Nationals on Monday. The righty went six innings, allowed three runs and struck out five, which earned him a loss in the 3-2 game. Maine faced the Marlins in New York in the first series of the season, lasting five innings and surrendering four runs in a no-decision. Last year, Maine logged more starts against Florida than any other team, going 2-1 with a 3.74 ERA in four games.

home_pitcher_note: Now with 43 career wins, Nolasco has moved ahead of Ryan Dempster (42) into fourth place all-time in Marlins victories. Nolasco comes off a win at Chicago, where he gave up one run in seven innings. For the season, the right-hander has 35 strikeouts in 46 2/3 innings. Nolasco beat the Mets on April 7 at New York, giving up three runs in 6 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Niese's first career start against the Nationals was one to forget. The lefty escaped with a no-decision after surrendering six runs on six hits and five walks in 4 1/3 innings. Niese struggled with his control all game and never fully recovered from a first-inning three-run homer by Adam Dunn. Niese will face the only team to hand him a loss this year when he pitches the final game of the series in Miami. He logged a quality start against the Marlins in his first outing of the season, allowing three runs over six innings, but the Mets' offense only scratched out one run.

home_pitcher_note: Volstad has been impressive of late, even in his latest defeat. The right-hander had won two straight decisions before falling to the Cubs at Wrigley Field. He gave up four runs in six innings. What hurt him were four walks. Other than that, he continues to find a way to work into the later part of the game. He has thrown 22 innings in his last three outings, giving up seven runs.
away_pitcher_note: Jackson has pitched better in his past two starts, with one at-bat seemingly doing him in both times. In his last start, against the Dodgers, it was Manny Ramirez's three-run double off the wall in the seventh inning that was the difference between a win and a loss. It's been a struggle for much of the season for Jackson, and he gets himself into trouble when he is not aggressive early in counts. When he falls behind, hitters are more easily able to gear up for his mid-90s fastball. With that in mind, John Hester will catch Jackson in this start because manager A.J. Hinch thinks Hester helps him be more aggressive with the fastball. Jackson was acquired by Arizona in a three-team trade during the Winter Meetings that sent Max Scherzer and Daniel Schlereth to the Tigers. The D-backs are Jackson's third team in three years; he pitched for Tampa Bay in 2008 before being dealt to the Tigers before last year. Jackson throws a fastball, curve, slider and change.

home_pitcher_note: Johnson is his old ace self lately. The 26-year-old hasn't given up more than three earned runs since Opening Day, sports a 2.25 ERA in his last four starts and hasn't walked a batter in his last two outings -- a span of 13 innings. His last time on the mound, Johnson got the no-decision after matching Mets ace Johan Santana pitch for pitch for seven innings. He gave up just one run, scattered three hits and struck out seven. But in a 1-1 game with runners on first and second and two outs in the bottom of the seventh, Marlins manager Fredi Gonzalez was forced to pinch-hit for Johnson, so his outing finished after 95 pitches (71 strikes). In three career starts against the D-backs, Johnson is 2-1 with a 1.35 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Buckner will be recalled from Triple-A Reno to make this start. This is the spot in the rotation that Cesar Valdez occupied the past two times through it. With the bullpen scuffling, though, the team elected to use Valdez in relief. Buckner lost out to Rodrigo Lopez for the final spot in the rotation during Spring Training. He was the front-runner going into camp but pitched poorly in his last few outings. In seven starts for Reno, Buckner is 3-1 with a 3.53 ERA. He has gone at least six innings and allowed three or fewer runs in his past five starts. Buckner has a very good curveball, and the club told him at the end of the spring that he should throw it more and his cut fastball less.

home_pitcher_note: The Cardinals' young lefty doesn't pitch like a rookie. He's poised and doesn't get rattled, but more strikingly, he has four pitches that he throws with confidence in a wide variety of counts. The difference-maker seems to be his slider, which he used to get a slew of strikeouts his last time out. Garcia came through the Minors known for a sinker-curveball combination, but the addition of the slider (which he also sometimes throws smaller, like a cutter) has taken him a major step forward.
away_pitcher_note: A case can be made that Sanchez is coming off his best outing of the season. The right-hander beat the Mets on May 14, and it was his first win since April 22 at Houston. Sanchez matched his season high with seven strikeouts. The seven innings and 108 pitches also were season highs. Sanchez has made eight starts, and in seven of them he has thrown at least six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright is coming off an uncharacteristically forgettable performance, but he often seems to follow those games with some of his best showings. His last time out, he made far too many mistakes with his curveball. That was very unlike him, since the curve is Wainwright's out pitch and one of the finest breaking balls of any National League pitcher.  He's been especially dominant at home, posting a 2.03 ERA at Busch Stadium since the start of 2009.
away_pitcher_note: It's not always been pretty or crisp when Robertson pitches, but for the most part, the veteran left-hander has been getting the job done. Even though he was struck out 25 and walked 19 in 41 1/3 innings, he has been able to minimize damage. Robertson collected a win over the Mets in his last start, giving up three runs (two earned) in 5 2/3 innings. In an injury-plaged 2009 with the Tigers, Robertson logged 49 2/3 total innings. He is closing in on that number now.

home_pitcher_note: Buehrle was extremely sharp in the early going of his last outing at Kansas City. He retired the first 13 hitters and took a 1-0 lead to the sixth. But Buehrle allowed a solo homer to Yuniesky Betancourt in the sixth before the Royals pecked away with a series of bloopers and seeing-eye grounders to post a five-spot in the seventh and send Buehrle to his fifth consecutive loss. Buehrle is determined to stay away from the big inning going forward, but there's not much he can do about it when softly struck balls find holes. For the most part, Buehrle was happy with the pitches he made in Kansas City and hopes to combine the same skill level with a bit of luck in his next start.
away_pitcher_note: "Terrible," is how Nolasco described his last outing. Still, the right-hander collected a victory on a day the Marlins almost blew an early 7-0 lead. In six innings, he gave up three runs (two earned) while striking out three and walking two. Nolasco's velocity was a hair down -- between 88-91 mph. He says it was a bad outing in which he wasn't particularly sharp. For his career, Nolasco if 44-32, which is the fourth-most wins in franchise history.

home_pitcher_note: Floyd took the loss on Sunday in Kansas City, surrendering 10 hits and five earned runs through six innings. Despite those numbers, Floyd felt good about his effort. Several of the hits were grounders that managed to find holes. Floyd didn't allow an extra base hit and thinks the results will come if he makes the pitches that he did against the Royals. Manager Ozzie Guillen said he'd like to see Floyd command his breaking pitches better to set up the fastball. Floyd has gone six innings or more in seven of his eight starts.
away_pitcher_note: Not at his best in his last outing, Volstad was victimized by a couple of errors that cost him two earned runs in a loss to Arizona. In five innings, he was tagged for four runs, with two earned. The right-hander had gone at least six innings in six of his first seven starts. On the road this year, Volstad is 1-2 with a 6.17 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Garcia continues to be one of the steadier forces among the White Sox starting rotation, even though he was projected as the franchise's fifth starter entering the season. Garcia shut down the Tigers on Wednesday afternoon at Comerica Park, raising his career ledger to 17-6 against Detroit, after giving up just two runs on five hits over six innings. Garcia will need to live up to his reputation as "Big Game Freddy" with Florida throwing Josh Johnson, one of the National League's top pitchers, in this series finale. Garcia has found great career Interleague success, tied with six others, including Mark Buehrle, for the third-most victories at 19. His 19-7 record is second best to Buehrle in winning percentage and his 2.57 ERA ranks No. 1 in Interleague Play. Garcia has no record against Florida.
away_pitcher_note: Since an Opening Day loss at New York, Johnson is 4-0 with a 2.08 ERA. The right-hander comes off an overpowering performance against the D-backs, striking out nine in seven shutout innings. JJ has fanned 63 in 57 innings this season. He threw 104 pitches against Arizona, which matches his second-most of the season.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander was at his best in his last start, tossing seven shutout innings at St. Louis on his way to a victory. Sanchez scattered four hits and threw a season-high 119 pitches. He walked two and struck out a season-best eight. At home, the right-hander has struck out 22 and walked six in 25 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: A bullpen implosion prevented Kawakami from picking up his first win of the season, but even more concerning news was a second blister on his right foot and a strained back. Still, Kawakami believes he will make his next scheduled start and will look to build upon his second-longest outing of the season, in which he completed six shutdown innings against the Reds on May 19. Kawakami was 1-3 with a 5.90 ERA (12 earned runs in 18 1/3 innings) against Florida last season.

home_pitcher_note: Slow start. Stronger finish. That basically sums up Robertson's last start. Unfortunately for the left-hander, he gave up four runs in the first two innings of his previous outing. While he rebounded with four straight scoreless frames, he was on the losing end at St. Louis. Robertson is 2-2 with a 3.91 ERA in four May starts.
away_pitcher_note: Hanson was bailed out by a historic comeback Thursday, when he failed to make it out of the second inning after eight of the 16 batters he faced scored. His ERA ballooned from 2.88 to 4.18 in what turned out to be a 10-9 Atlanta win. In his only career start at Sun Life Stadium last Sept. 3, Hanson tossed five innings of two-hit ball, giving up just one run before the Atlanta bullpen collapsed in an 8-3 loss. That came just 12 days after the 23-year-old's only other career start against the Marlins, when he struck out seven hitters in seven innings and gave up three runs on four hits. Hanson was the winner of that 4-3 contest.

home_pitcher_note: Erase what happened in Chicago and move on. That's what Nolasco said he would do after allowing eight runs in 5 1/3 innings against the White Sox. It was the most runs he's allowed since yielding a career-most 10 runs on Aug. 12, 2009 vs. the Astros. Nolasco chalked the game up as making some mistake pitches that the White Sox didn't miss.
away_pitcher_note: Hudson has been dominant this month, going 4-0 over five starts and 35 2/3 innings with an ERA of 1.26. The right-hander continued his dominance Friday in Pittsburgh, allowing just three hits over eight innings in a 7-0 Atlanta win. Hudson has even been flashing his bat, recording five hits this month and driving in a run during each of his last two outings. The 34-year-old is 6-1 with a 2.67 ERA in nine career starts at Sun Life Stadium, where he last pitched Sept. 1, a 4-3 Braves win that saw him go 5 1/3 innings, giving up two runs off six hits while striking out five.

home_pitcher_note: Riding a three-game losing streak, Volstad looks to get back on the winning track. Although the right-hander last won on May 7 at Washington, he hasn't pitched that poorly. He comes off a quality start at Chicago, where he gave up three runs in six innings to the White Sox. At home, Volstad is 2-2 with a 2.67 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick seemed to have things working in his favor until he allowed four two-out runs in the fifth inning Saturday in a 5-0 loss to the Boston Red Sox at Citizens Bank Park. Kendrick lasted just 4 2/3 innings, allowing eight hits, five runs and two walks and striking out two. It was the first time since April 14, when Kendrick lasted just 1 2/3 innings against the Washington Nationals, that a Phillies starter had not pitched at least five innings. Phillies starters entered that night 20-10 with a 3.34 ERA, which ranked third in the National League. They had pitched six or more innings in 18 of their previous 19 starts to that point. Kendrick hopes to pitch deep against the Marlins in the series opener Friday night.

home_pitcher_note: Wins are common for Johnson. Not recording a strikeout isn't. In his previous start, at the White Sox, Johnson tossed six shutout innings. However, for the first time in his career as a starter, he failed to log a strikeout. As a rookie in 2006, he threw three innings of relief against the Reds without posting a strikeout.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay has pitched brilliantly for much of the season, but he suffered his worst start with the Phillies on Sunday against the Red Sox at Citizens Bank Park. He allowed eight hits, seven runs and two walks and struck out just one in 5 2/3 innings. He struggled following a 132-pitch effort in his previous start, which had many wondering if Halladay is tired of throwing a lot of pitches this season. He said he is fine. After throwing just 99 pitches Sunday, he should be.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez continued what is looking like a resurgent 2010 season with a win against the Braves on Tuesday, when he gave up two runs in 6 1/3 innings and exited with one out in the seventh and 116 pitches under his belt. The 26-year-old has now given up no more than two runs in seven consecutive starts. On Tuesday, he scattered five hits and four walks but was constantly able to pitch out of trouble and rack up six strikeouts -- two against rookie sensation Jason Heyward. Sanchez's worst start of the season came against the Phillies, when he gave up five runs in six innings on April 16.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer had thrown six or more innings in every start this season, until he struggled a bit in an 8-0 loss Tuesday to the Mets at Citi Field. Moyer allowed seven hits, four runs and two walks in five innings, his shortest outing of the season. But Moyer has had great success against the Marlins in his career. He is 13-5 with a 3.18 ERA in 18 starts against Florida. The Phillies could use some of that magic in the series finale against them Sunday.

home_pitcher_note: Robertson logged a season-high 107 pitches in his previous start, a no-decision against the Braves. The veteran left-hander exited with a 2-1 lead after six innings, allowing an unearned run. He struck out five. His previous season-high pitch count was 105, turned in twice before.
away_pitcher_note: Last time out, Narveson simply didn't have good command of his pitches. Not one of them. His counterpart on the night, Astros ace Roy Oswalt, was dominant. Together, those two things gave Narveson his second loss of the season. Narveson allowed four runs over four innings on eight hits while striking out just two batters. In his last three starts, Narveson has a 1-2 record after winning each of his first two. Both losses have come at home, while all of Narveson's wins have been on the road. As the Brewers travel to Florida for a four-game set, Narveson will make his first career start against the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: Rain cut short Nolasco's last outing. The right-hander was taking the mound for the fifth before play was halted against the Braves. So his line was four innings, and he was tagged for three runs on eight hits. He threw 64 pitches, and was tagged with a loss. Nolasco has dropped two straight starts, allowing 11 runs in 9 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: While not great by any means, Bush's last start, against the Astros, was a drastic improvement from his previous outing against the Twins, in which Bush lasted just one-third of an inning and gave up seven runs on six hits at Target Field. After waiting a long six days to pitch again, Bush lasted five innings while giving up two unearned runs on four hits. Bush did not factor in the decision, but kept the Brewers close enough to pull out the come-from-behind win over the Astros for their first home series win since taking two of three from the Rockies to open the season. In five career starts against the Marlins, the Brewers right-hander is 2-3 with a 5.70 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Bottom line is Volstad has dropped four straight decisions. The untold line is the 23-year-old has been deserving of a better fate. Volstad comes off a tough defeat at the hands of the Phillies, giving up three runs in 6 1/3 innings. He entered the seventh inning in a 2-2 game, and exited with two runners on. One of them scored. In his four-game losing streak, he has given up 12 earned runs in 23 1/3 innings. In all four games, he kept his team right in it.
away_pitcher_note: Tossing his first career shutout, Gallardo pitched as well as he has all season and as well as manager Ken Macha has ever seen in his last outing. Gallardo scattered eight hits over his nine innings and did not walk a batter until the second-to-last one he faced. It was the Brewers' first shutout since 2008 and the club's first complete game since April '09. In his career, Gallardo has faced the Marlins just once. He tossed seven scoreless innings, giving up just six hits while walking two and striking out five.

home_pitcher_note: History happened when Johnson last took the mound, but fate wasn't on his side. Johnson was impressive in seven innings against the Phillies. He allowed one unearned run. However, he had the misfortune of pitching the same day Roy Halladay tossed the 20th perfect game in MLB history. Johnson had a string of 20 straight scoreless innings snapped with an unearned run. He hasn't allowed an earned run in 25 straight innings.
away_pitcher_note: Capuano will be making his first Major League appearance since Sept. 28, 2007, after more than two years spent rehabbing a left elbow injury that required Tommy John surgery, the second of his career. Capuano replaces fellow lefty Manny Parra in Milwaukee's rotation and has a chance to put to rest a nasty streak. Since a May 17, 2007 win over the Nationals, in which Capuano worked eight scoreless innings, the Brewers are 0-22 when Capuano has pitched. He is 0-12 with a 6.08 ERA in that span, which includes 18 starts and four relief appearances.

home_pitcher_note: Though Dickey did not have a good feel for his knuckleball early, he found the pitch as the day wore on, holding the Brewers to four runs in seven innings last Sunday in Milwaukee. It marked his second consecutive victory, and the third straight game in which he has given the Mets a strong chance to win. Next up for Dickey is Florida, a team he has not faced since 2008.
away_pitcher_note: In tossing 6 2/3 shutout innings against the Phillies his last time out, Sanchez lowered his ERA to under 3.00. Sanchez has won four straight decisions. In six starts in May, the right-hander was 4-0 with a 1.93 ERA. In those games, he struck out 35 in 37 1/3 innings. On the road, Sanchez is 2-1 with a 3.00 ERA on the season.

home_pitcher_note: After one rehab start in Triple-A, Jon Niese is expected to come off the disabled list to face the Marlins. The rookie left-hander has not pitched since suffering a mild strain of his surgically repaired right hamstring on May 16 in Miami. After a brief period of rehabilitation and one Minor League start, he would be making his ninth start of the season. Niese has faced the Marlins one other time this season, holding them to three runs over six innings in his first start of the year.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran lefty exited his last start after 5 1/3 innings, trailing by four runs and leaving the bases loaded. Yet the Marlins rallied and Robertson settled for a no-decision. Robertson has worked at least five-plus innings in six consecutive starts. On April 8 at Citi Field, he beat the Mets, 3-1. He also collected a second win against New York on May 15 at Sun Life Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: It took Takahashi three outings to allow his first runs as a starting pitcher, but he did so in a big way, serving up a grand slam to Jerry Hairston Jr. on Monday in San Diego. Takahashi allowed six runs in all in that game, lasting merely four innings -- but prior to that he had submitted consecutive scoreless efforts against the two teams that played in the World Series last year, the Yankees and Phillies. He will look to return to that form this Sunday against the Marlins, a team he has faced only in relief.
away_pitcher_note: The strikeout returned to Nolasco's game in his previous start, and so did a victory. The right-hander snapped a two-game slide, and won for first time since beating Mets on May 16. Nolasco makes his third start of season against New York. He is 1-0 with a no-decision. In his last start, a win over the Brewers, he struck out eight in seven innings. Nolasco had gone five straight starts with three strikeouts in each of them.

home_pitcher_note: After Phillies manager Charlie Manuel criticized Kendrick for his pace on the mound May 28 in Florida, Manuel said Kendrick had his best start of the season Wednesday against Atlanta at Turner Field. Kendrick allowed just one run in seven innings in a 2-1 loss to the Braves. Kendrick liked his pace, too. It probably is not as simple as that, but he would like that to continue against the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: The 23-year-old seeks his first victory since May 7 at Washington. Volstad had dropped his last four decisions, but in his last start he was in line for a victory. Against the Brewers, he exited with a one-run lead in the sixth, but he wasn't involved in the decision. Volstad faced the Phillies on May 28, giving up three runs in 6 1/3 innings. He took the loss.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Halladay's reunion against the team he accomplished history against less than two weeks before, and the Marlins will be under a lot of pressure to get a hit -- any hit -- against the Phillies ace who threw a perfect game vs. them on May 29. Halladay wasn't perfect on Friday, but he earned his eighth win by shutting down San Diego for two runs in seven innings. The Padres hit him well, but Halladay worked out of trouble and bared down when he had to. He gave up three hits and one run in the first inning, and another run in the fifth, but overall had another solid outing to snap Philadelphia's losing skid.
away_pitcher_note: When he last faced the Phillies, on May 29, Johnson was on the losing end of Major League history. Roy Halladay tossed the 20th perfect game in MLB history that night at Sun Life Stadium. Johnson gave up one unearned run over seven innings, striking out six in the loss. In his last start, the right-hander beat the Brewers, giving up one run in seven innings with eight strikeouts. Johnson has allowed one earned run in his past 32 innings.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Halladay's reunion against the team he accomplished history against less than two weeks before, and the Marlins will be under a lot of pressure to get a hit -- any hit -- against the Phillies ace who threw a perfect game vs. them on May 29.
