In his last start, the right-hander beat the Brewers, giving up one run in seven innings with eight strikeouts. Johnson has allowed one earned run in his past 32 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Shields had the tough duty of pitching against the Rangers in 100 degree heat on Saturday afternoon in Arlington, and he came away with his fourth loss of the season. Shields received little help as only three of the six runs scored against him were earned. He has built a reputation as a pitcher who will do whatever is necessary to pitch his team into the seventh or eighth inning. He is a master at using his fastball command to setup one of the best changeups in baseball. Shields is 2-1 with a 4.12 ERA in six career starts against the Marlins; he is 26-16 with a 3.44 ERA in 66 career starts at Tropicana Field.
away_pitcher_note: In May, Sanchez was on a roll, going 4-0 in five starts. Now, the 26-year-old looks to get his first win in June. The right-hander suffered a loss at the Mets to open the road trip. Sanchez gave up four runs in 5 2/3 innings, walking four. Prior to that, he had won his previous four starts, and his ERA was 1.33 in that 27-inning span.

home_pitcher_note: Garza wasn't at his best in his last outing, but he battled to put together a decent start. The right-hander went 5 2/3 innings and gave up four runs on six hits and two walks while striking out four batters against the Rangers on Sunday. His ERA climbed from 3.08 to 3.31 after the performance, but he got his sixth win of the season after going winless in his previous five starts. Garza has been outstanding at times this season, particularly at the beginning of the year, and he has consistently given the Rays a chance to win even when he has not had his best stuff. He will be making his 13th start of the season and the third of his career against Florida. In his previous two starts against the Marlins, he recorded a stellar 1.13 ERA and 0.38 WHIP in 16 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Nolasco was in line for a victory in his last start, but ended up with a no-decision. The Marlins watched a four-run lead slip away against the Mets. Nolasco exited after 5 1/3 innings, and he was charged with three runs. The right-hander was coming off a solid seven-inning victory over the Brewers on June. 1. He's only completed six full innings twice in his last five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Niemann had arguably the best outing by any Rays pitcher this season in his last start against Toronto on Tuesday, when he threw a two-hit shutout. He walked only one batter and struck out six while throwing 69 of his 114 pitches for strikes. The quiet, 6-foot-9 right-hander took a no-hitter into the sixth inning and has become the most consistent starter in a rotation of excellent Rays pitchers. He pitched primarily with his fastball but mixed in his offspeed stuff later on. He has recorded 10 quality starts in 12 outings this season. The shutout was the third of his career, and he became the seventh Tampa Bay pitcher in team history to throw two shutouts in a Rays uniform. Niemann will make his 13th start of the season Sunday and the second of his career against the Marlins. He threw six four-hit, one-run innings in his only other start against Florida.
away_pitcher_note: Volstad was given a big lead twice in his last start. Both times he couldn't hold it, and he was lifted after four-plus innings. Volstad had a tough time trying to preserve leads of four runs and three runs at Philadelphia. The right-hander ended up with a no-decision. He hasn't won since May 7, as he's lost four straight decisions.

home_pitcher_note: Beating the guy who has already been perfect this season has risen Johnson to another level. In his last start, Johnson tossed eight shutout innings, retiring the final 17 he faced at Philadelphia, in a victory over Roy Halladay. In his last six starts, the ace is 4-1 with a 0.43 ERA (two earned runs in 42 innings). His lone loss was to Halladay. He gave up an unearned run in seven innings on the night Doc tossed a perfect game. Johnson threw 113 pitches at Philly.
away_pitcher_note: In his last start against the Mariners, Wilson pitched seven innings, giving up only two runs on four hits with four strikeouts. It allowed Wilson to retake the team lead in quality starts with eight. He's only pitched two-thirds of an inning in his career against the Marlins, giving up a hit while registering a strikeout. He only carries a 1-4 record in Interleague Play with a 5.26 ERA in 32 games.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez was effective in his last start, going seven innings and giving up four runs on four hits and three walks while striking out four. He didn't need to be, though, as the Marlins lineup put up a season-high 14 runs against the Rays. Still, the right-hander's solid outing put Florida in good enough position to withstand a Tampa Bay rally that brought the final score to 14-9. He was not as sharp as he could have been, throwing 61 of his 103 pitches for strikes while his ERA climbed to 3.36, but he got his sixth win of the year. This will be Sanchez's 13th start of the year and his second Interleague outing. He has never faced the Rangers in his five-year career.
away_pitcher_note: Hunter is making his third start since being recalled from Triple-A Oklahoma City. He beat the Mariners, 12-3, in his last start, allowing three runs in six innings. Opponents are hitting .185 off him in two games and right-handed hitters are 2-for-20. Opponents are also 1-for-9 with runners in scoring position. He is 11-8 with a 4.83 ERA in 24 Major League starts over the past three seasons. Hunter began this season on the disabled list with a strained muscle in his left rib cage. He was 1-2 with a 4.06 ERA at Oklahoma City before replacing Derek Holland in the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Victimized by three solo home runs in his most recent start, Nolasco comes off his shortest outing of the season. The right-hander worked 2 1/3 innings in a loss at Tampa Bay, giving up five runs on nine hits. In his past two starts, he has struggled, allowing eight runs in 7 2/3 innings with four walks and four strikeouts. Finding consistency has been a struggle for Nolasco, who is 2-3 with a 5.73 ERA in six home starts.
away_pitcher_note: The Rangers decided on Nippert over left-hander Matt Harrison because the Marlins have a predominantly right-handed lineup. Last year, he was 3-3 with a 4.65 ERA in 10 starts and 2-0 with a 1.86 ERA as a reliever. His longest outing this season is three innings and 47 pitches against the Blue Jays on May 14. He threw 37 pitches over two innings against the Rays on June 6 and has pitched just once since then. He threw 22 pitches over 1 1/3 innings against the Mariners last Thursday in Arlington. He has not pitched on the road trip but has a 2.53 ERA on the road this season.

home_pitcher_note: Robertson will make his first start in two weeks Friday, but it will be the second time he's faced the Rays in a week. The left-hander came out of the bullpen in relief of Ricky Nolasco on Saturday in St. Petersburg and held Tampa Bay to just one run on four hits and a walk in 5 2/3 innings of relief. He also struck out five batters in the appearance, throwing 56 of his 83 pitches for strikes. Robertson pitched well enough to keep Florida close enough to make a strong comeback effort, but too much damage had already been done. Robertson has not recorded a win since May 15 against the Mets, but he might earn another victory if he can match his previous performance against the Rays. Robertson may have benefited from the fact that Rays manager Joe Maddon's lineup was set up to hit a right-handed pitcher, which it did well against Nolasco, so he may face more of a challenge the second time around.
away_pitcher_note: Garza struggled Saturday night against the Marlins, allowing four earned runs in 5 2/3 innings, but he still battled to pick up his seventh win of the season. Garza has the best stuff on the staff, which he can put on display in any given start, and he seems to be maturing on the mound, which has led to his no longer allowing his emotions get the best of him. Garza is 1-0 with a 1.00 ERA in one start at Sun Life Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: For the second straight start, Volstad draws the Rays. This time, it will be at Sun Life Stadium. The right-hander beat Tampa Bay last Sunday at Tropicana Field. It was his first victory since May 7. In six innings at Tampa Bay, Volstad gave up one run on four hits. He did walk four, which was a concern, and he struck out three. In 78 1/3 innings this year, the 23-year-old has struck out 49 and walked 33.
away_pitcher_note: Niemann faced the Marlins on Sunday at Tropicana Field and came away with his first loss of the season after allowing five runs on nine hits in six innings of work. Sunday's outing equated to just the third time in 13 starts that Niemann did not give the Rays a quality start. Because Niemann stands 6-foot-9, he creates a difficult downward angle for hitters, who rarely face a pitcher of his height. He is 0-0 with a 1.50 ERA in one start at Sun Life Stadium; he is 12-5 with a 4.17 ERA in 27 career appearances on the road.

home_pitcher_note: One out away from being 8-2, Johnson instead remains at 7-2 heading into a tough contest against the Rays. In his last outing, the 26-year-old gave up one run in seven innings, striking out seven. He was in line for a win, but closer Leo Nunez allowed a two-out, two-run pinch-hit triple to Matt Treanor in the ninth inning, which rallied the Rangers to a 3-2 win. Still, Johnson lowered his ERA to 1.86. In his last seven starts, he has surrendered just three earned runs (four total) in 49 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Price had live stuff Tuesday against the Braves, but he lacked command of his fastball, which elevated his pitch count and led to a shortened outing as the 24-year-old left-hander threw 113 pitches in five innings. Nevertheless, he still managed to pitch his way out of several jams to pick up his 10th win of the season. While Price did not have his fastball command against the Braves, the No. 1 pick of the 2007 Draft has shown a lot of improvement in that area, which has made his slider and curve even more effective. Price is 1-0 with a 1.42 ERA in one career appearance against the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: After a great start to the season, Guthrie has lost his last four starts with a modest 4.78 ERA. He seemed to be on his way to breaking that streak on Wednesday against the Giants, with only two runs allowed in a tie game entering the sixth. But his friend and former Oriole Aubrey Huff took him yard to lead off the inning. Juan Uribe went back-to-back on him with another blast, but the righty regrouped and finished the inning to give him six or more in all but one of his 14 starts this year. Guthrie makes his first career start against the Marlins on Tuesday.
away_pitcher_note: Producing a quality start in his last outing didn't land Sanchez his seventh win. In six innings against the Rangers, Sanchez gave up three runs (one earned), while striking out six and walking one. He gave up eight hits and lost for the second time in three outings. For the season, Sanchez has thrown 81 innings. He logged 86 total last year, spending time on the DL with shoulder problems.

home_pitcher_note: It has been a great month of June for the young southpaw. After throwing six innings of one-run ball against the Padres on on Friday, Matusz now sports a 2.39 ERA in four starts this month. In his previous two outings he threw a career-high 117 pitches against the Red Sox and then went a career-long eight innings against the Mets. He is looking for his first win since April 18 against the Marlins, a team he has never faced.
away_pitcher_note: Nolasco didn't have his best stuff while taking the loss against the Rangers on Thursday, but he did have enough to keep going. Through six innings, Nolasco had given up four runs (two earned) and thrown 80 pitches. But with his team trailing, 4-3, with two outs and nobody on in the bottom of the sixth, manager Fredi Gonzalez opted to pinch-hit for Nolasco. Reliever Tim Wood gave up two runs the next half-inning, but afterward, Nolasco said he was fine with the decision. In four June starts, Nolasco is 1-3 with a 5.66 ERA. In two career starts against the Orioles, the 27-year-old holds a 1.93 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Finally, Millwood got a win. Not only had the Orioles' most veteran starter failed to pick up a "W" in his first 14 outings, but he had gone 0-4 in his previous four starts. After being plagued by poor run support while he started the season with a 3.71 ERA in 10 starts, the 35-year-old righty had struggled to the tune of a 9.53 ERA since then. It took a six-inning, three-run effort against the Padres and a sixth-inning go-ahead homer by Adam Jones to bust the slump. Now he moves on to the Marlins, against whom he's started more games (23) than any other team except the Nationals (25). But he hasn't had much luck in those outings, going 6-9 with a 5.29 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran lefty played the role of stopper in his previous start. By tossing six solid innings against the Rays, he helped the Marlins snap a three-game losing streak by limiting Tampa Bay to three runs (two earned) while striking out six in six innings. It was Robertson's first win since May 15, against the Mets, a span of four starts and one long-relief appearance.

home_pitcher_note: After facing the Rays in back-to-back starts, Volstad gets back to pitching against the NL. Foremost, the 23-year-old will be looking for some consistency. He collected a win and had a no-decision in those two meetings with Tampa Bay. In his last outing, he worked 5 2/3 innings and gave up four runs on seven hits. He was hurt in the sixth inning, yielding three runs. Volstad exited with the Marlins trailing by three, yet he didn't factor into the decision. Volstad has won one of his last five decisions.
away_pitcher_note: Richard, who has a knack for keeping the ball down and getting a lot of ground-ball outs, was hit hard at times in his last start against the Orioles. Richard allowed five runs (four earned) on eight hits in six innings, including a two-run home run to Adam Jones in that sixth inning that broke a tie. Richard walked one and struck out five, but he often was hurt when he couldn't bury his pitches in the strike zone as he typically does when he's throwing well.

home_pitcher_note: With each outing, Johnson continues to established himself as one of the best in the league. JJ comes off a brilliant, nine-strikeout, one-run outing over eight innings against the Rays. Over his past 57 innings, he has given up five runs, just four earned. That's an 0.63 ERA over eight straight starts. Johnson's career record is now 42-18. He has 98 strikeouts in 100 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Garland snapped a three-game losing streak on Sunday against the Orioles, allowing four earned runs -- all in the first inning -- in six frames to earn his seventh victory of the season. He struck out three, walked two and retired the final 14 batters he faced, dating back to the second inning. After admitting he lost his composure in his previous start against the Blue Jays because he was openly upset with the home-plate umpire, Garland said he was mentally able to bounce back much better against the Orioles after the rough first inning. "I took a step off the mound, I caught my breath and pretty much told myself, 'It happens. There's nothing you can do,'" Garland said after Sunday's game. "I started making pitches and keeping the ball down, and I think the big key was throwing my offspeed pitches for strikes." Garland is 3-4 with a 4.39 ERA in seven road starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: It's been an up-and-down June for Sanchez, who was in a lose-one-win-one patter. Sanchez comes off a win at Baltimore and he is 2-2 in the month with one start to go. Sanchez has thrown 88 1/3 innings this season, which is more than he tossed in 2009 (86). He missed considerable time due to shoulder injuries.
away_pitcher_note: Latos, the 22-year-old from nearby Coconut Creek High outside Miami, returns home to face the Marlins. Latos wasn't bad in his last start against a Florida-based team: He tossed seven scoreless innings in his last start against the Rays in St. Petersburg, allowing three hits. Better still, he struck out eight, including the last three hitters he faced. He's 7-1 over his last nine starts for the Padres with a 1.81 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Nolasco had one rough inning in his last start, but the end result worked out pretty well. After yielding two runs in a four-run second, the right-hander settled, threw seven total innings and struck out eight. He beat the Orioles and collected his first win since June 1. Nolasco faces the Mets for the fourth time. He's 1-0 with two no-decisions. On June 6 at New York, he pitched 5 1/3 innings, but the Marlins let a five-run lead slip away in a loss.
away_pitcher_note: Dickey turned in the best outing of his season in his last start, against Detroit, throwing eight shutout innings and allowing just six baserunners. He beat Florida earlier this month in Citi Field and has gone at least six innings in every 2010 start.

home_pitcher_note: The last time Robertson faced the Mets, New York scored six runs in 4 2/3 innings on June 5 at Citi Field. This time, the game will be in San Juan. It also will be Robertson's fourth start against the Mets this season. He is 2-1 against them.
away_pitcher_note: The Tigers hit Takahashi with ease in his last start, as the lefty lasted only four innings before being chased after surrendering six runs. The 35-year-old rookie gave up five runs in 5 1/3 innings against the Marlins in his only start against Florida this season.

home_pitcher_note: One fastball that caught too much of the plate denied Volstad a win in his last start. Will Venable of the Padres homered, and Volstad was tagged with a hard-luck loss. For the first time this year, he didn't walk a batter. He hasn't faced New York this season.
away_pitcher_note: Pelfrey gave up a leadoff home run to Denard Span last time out but settled into a two-run, six-inning performance that earned him a win. He hasn't faced the Marlins yet this season but has struggled for his career against Florida, going 1-6 with 5.63 ERA in 10 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Even with Jair Jurrjens returning to the rotation, manager Bobby Cox has decided to continue with Medlen as a starter. The right-hander has allowed four runs or fewer in all of his starts this year and surrendered just one against the Tigers on Friday.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson lost on Saturday to the Padres, when he was defeated despite giving up just two runs in eight innings for his 14th consecutive quality start. That outing also ended Johnson's run of eight straight starts pitching at least six innings and giving up no more than one run.

home_pitcher_note: Hanson can't remember ever struggling so much in two successive starts. In uncharacteristic fashion, the righty has allowed 15 total runs in his past two outings. In each start he completed 3 2/3 innings, good for a 17.18 ERA. Hanson struck out four batters during that span.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez gave up just two runs (one earned) in six innings to produce his 10th quality start against the Padres on Sunday. But because the offense couldn't get anything going, he left after throwing just 85 pitches and wound up with the loss.

home_pitcher_note: Hudson has been one of the most effective and dominant pitchers in the National League this season, and that hasn't changed recently. The right-hander has completed at least seven innings in his past five starts and hasn't allowed more than four runs in a outing all year.
away_pitcher_note: Home runs have been Nolasco's biggest headache. In his last start, New York's Jason Bay belted two off the right-hander, who has surrendered 19 in 16 outings. However, Nolasco has won two straight, and he struck out nine in his second straight win.

home_pitcher_note: John Ely has battled through a June slump and four-game losing streak to rebound with a pair of quality starts, most recently beating the Giants. He's not overpowering, but he has a full repertoire of pitches and he's not intimidated by Major League competition.
away_pitcher_note: With a little more luck, Robertson would have come out with a victory in his last start. Instead, he finished with a no-decision, but the team ended up beating the Mets. The lefty gave up four runs in six-plus innings. His season innings high is 6 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: In his third start off the disabled list, Vicente Padilla pitched a gem against the Giants, allowing one run in seven innings. The return of the Opening Day starter has been a big boost to a starting rotation that was looking quite ragged without him.
away_pitcher_note: Perhaps it's a sign of maturity. Volstad overcame a 28-pitch first inning in his last start, a frame in which he gave up three runs (two earned) to the Mets. He regrouped and posted five innings in a no-decision. This is his second meeting with L.A., having lost on April 9.

home_pitcher_note: Hiroki Kuroda is coming off his worst start of the year, lasting only 1 2/3 innings while allowing six earned runs. The worst part is that neither he nor the staff could really explain why, other than a lack of command of any pitch other than the fastball.
away_pitcher_note: It's been dominating and frustrating when Johnson has pitched of late. In his last four starts, he has received five runs of support. The result is he's 1-2 in those outings, including a no-decision against the Braves. In six innings at Atlanta, he struck out eight.

home_pitcher_note: Don't judge Lopez's solid 2010 campaign by his most recent start. Saturday against the Los Angeles Dodgers, the veteran allowed nine runs, but just two of them were earned. The D-backs infield committed five errors behind him (and a sixth after he left).
away_pitcher_note: Consistently, Sanchez has been able to give his team at least six innings an outing. He has reached that mark in four straight starts. The team, however, is 2-3 in those outings. That's despite four straight quality starts. The team is 8-8 in his starts.

home_pitcher_note: Sunday against the Dodgers, Haren allowed just one run on six hits over seven innings but didn't factor into the decision. Eighty-two of his 117 pitches were strikes. He has spun three straight quality starts.
away_pitcher_note: Home runs have been problematic. In 17 starts, Nolasco has yielded 20. Consider a year ago, he yielded 23 in 31 starts. In fact, In 103 2/3 innings, Nolasco has surrendered more homers than walks (19). Still, he has won three straight, striking out 11 at Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: On Monday against the Cubs, Kennedy allowed a season-high seven runs on nine hits over 5 2/3 innings; he struck out six. The D-backs' No. 3 starter yielded four-plus runs in back-to-back outings for the first time all year. Throwing quality strikes is his panacea.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran makes his final start before the All-Star Break. With 89 1/3 innings, he's already well surpassed his innings (49 2/3) in an injury-plagued 2009. He's gone exactly six innings in three of his past four starts and is 2-1 in those games (the team is 3-1).

home_pitcher_note: Enright will be making his third big league start after being called up from Double-A Mobile. In his last start against the Cubs, he cruised through five innings before allowing three runs and being knocked out in the sixth. Enright is known for having pinpoint control.
away_pitcher_note: Nothing is official, but the team is leaning toward giving the 21-year-old right-hander his first big league start. He has appeared in three games as a reliever since being promoted from Double-A Jacksonville, where he was 5-1 with a 2.03 ERA in 14 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Riding a four-game winning streak, Nolasco most likely will get the first start of the second half. That could change if Josh Johnson flips to Friday. Nolasco is 2-0 with a 2.57 ERA with 17 strikeouts in 14 innings in July. On April 30, Nolasco lost to the Nationals.
away_pitcher_note: Strasburg continued his stellar rookie season in the Nationals' 8-1 win against the Giants last Friday. He allowed only one run on three hits with eight strikeouts in six innings. Strasburg has never faced the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: After pacing the Major Leagues in ERA in the first half, Johnson will be coming off his second trip to the All-Star Game. Johnson enjoyed one of the best first halves in franchise history, winning nine games. In 122 innings, he has fanned 123 compared to 28 walks.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez will look to bounce back after a rough start against the Giants on Sunday. He gave up five runs on five hits in five innings in a 6-2 loss. Hernandez is 13-8 with a 3.52 ERA in 29 career games against Florida.

home_pitcher_note: For making his first big league start, Sanabia received the scorecard after the Marlins beat the D-backs on July 11. What Sanabia has yet to collect is a big win. Because he hadn't started since June 19, he was on a strict pitch count, and he tossed 3 1/3 scoreless frames.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander has struggled as of late. Stammen gave up a total of 11 runs in his past two starts, against the Giants and Mets. He allowed four runs on six hits in 5 1/3 innings in his last outing, a 10-5 loss to San Francisco on Saturday.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez posted 10 quality starts in 17 starts in the first half, and his seven wins are his most since he was 10-3 as a rookie in 2006. Sanchez has thrown 103 1/3 innings, and he's struck out 71 with 39 walks. This will be Sanchez's 18th start, which will be a career high.
away_pitcher_note: Jimenez appeared to right the ship in his last start, holding the Cardinals to three hits and one run in a 4-2 win on July 8. Working ahead efficiently, he threw 93 pitches in eight innings. He had allowed 17 runs in 17 2/3 innings in three previous starts combined.

home_pitcher_note: The lefty opened the year as the No. 3 starter. He gets the fifth start of the second half, and second this year vs. the Rockies. He lost on April 24 at Coors, giving up five runs in four innings. For the most part, Robertson gives five or six innings per start.
away_pitcher_note: Francis earned a no-decision in the Rockies' 9-7 loss to the Padres on Sunday, but confessed his command to both sides of the plate has not been where he'd like to see it. The lefty has not won since June 13, taking one loss in that span.

home_pitcher_note: It's been a pretty daunting stretch for Nolasco. In his last three starts, he has drawn Tim Hudson, Dan Haren and Stephen Strasburg. He did win two of those before losing to Strasburg and the Nationals, which snapped a string of four straight victories.
away_pitcher_note: Hammel struck out a career-high 10 and went seven strong innings in his last start, but took a 3-2 loss to the Reds. Hammel was bailed out of trouble by a home run-saving catch by center fielder Dexter Fowler in the fifth, but in general handled himself well.

home_pitcher_note: Make the string 12 starts and counting. That is how many consecutive starts Johnson has gone without allowing more than two earned runs. The MLB leader in ERA, JJ has given up one earned run in 20 innings in July. This season, he has 130 strikeouts in 128 innings.
away_pitcher_note: In two starts since returning from a left middle finger injury, De La Rosa has struggled to find his fastball command. In his last outing, a loss to the Reds, he also shied away from breaking pitches. The Rockies need for him to regain form.

home_pitcher_note: The rookie right-hander comes off his first MLB win, beating the Nationals in his first home appearance. Sanabia threw 5 1/3 scoreless innings, striking out five while walking two. Brought up on June 22 from Double-A Jacksonville, he has struck out 17 in 17 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Lowe hasn't been overwhelming in his previous three outings, but he has been effective. In those three starts, the right-hander has completed 17 2/3 innings with a 3.57 ERA. He also continues to refrain from giving free passes, walking just four during that span.

home_pitcher_note: In line for a victory in his last start, Sanchez settled for a no-decision. He exited with the lead after six innings, and the Marlins ended up beating the Rockies. The right-hander has gone four straight starts without a win since beating Baltimore on June 22.
away_pitcher_note: In an effort to rest his arm, the Braves haven't started Medlen since July 7 against the Phillies. Since then he's made three relief appearances -- allowing one run total -- as the Braves hope their conservation efforts pay off with Medlen in the stretch run.

home_pitcher_note: Manager Edwin Rodriguez said there is a "75 percent chance" Volstad will start the series finale. He threw 70 pitches on Wednesday night for Triple-A New Orleans and should be ready if called upon.
away_pitcher_note: Since returning to the starting rotation on June 30, Jurrjens has been nothing less than spectacular. In his four starts since coming back, the righty is 3-0 with a 2.19 ERA while completing 24 2/3 innings. He's struck out 20 batters and walked just 10.

home_pitcher_note: The Giants own a 12-8 record in Zito's starts. They've been particularly fortunate in his six career starts against Florida, winning each game. Typically a strong second-half pitcher, Zito has recorded a 1.17 ERA in his two starts since the All-Star break.
away_pitcher_note: Nolasco reached a milestone in his last start, collecting his 50th career win, making him second all-time in Marlins history. He gave up two runs in eight innings while striking out eight against the Rockies. He suffered a loss to the Giants in Miami on May 6.

home_pitcher_note: Cain's coming off an impressive performance at Arizona, where he allowed three hits in eight shutout innings. His nine strikeouts matched a season high. Cain is 5-3 with a 2.63 ERA at home, compared with 3-5, 3.50 on the road.
away_pitcher_note: Thirteen and counting. JJ is riding a string of 13 straight starts without allowing more than two runs. He has given up one run in 12 1/3 innings since the break, but he comes off a no-decision, in which he allowed one run in 6 1/3 innings to the Rockies, fanning 11.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez experienced a bizarre five-inning outing at Arizona last Friday. He continually pitched from the stretch, resulting from four hits allowed and five walks, but struck out 10 and yielded only one run.
away_pitcher_note: If his first three big league starts are any indictation, Sanabia has the ability to pitch out of trouble. He has an 0.69 ERA in those games. His WHIP is 1.69 as a starter. He's given up 16 hits, walked six and hit a batter in 13 innings.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Bumgarner's first start at home since June 26, when he made his season debut for the Giants in an Interleague affair against Boston. Since then, Bumgarner has recorded a 1.87 ERA in five road starts, winning the past four in a row.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez was in line for his eighth win when he took the mound last Saturday. But after a three-run lead disappeared, he was not involved in the decision. The team is closely watching his innings pitched. He has 115 1/3 right now after throwing 86 a year ago.

home_pitcher_note: LeBlanc is coming off his first victory since June 12. He allowed three runs in six innings against the Pirates and was able to overcome two solo home runs. His fastball command was good as he didn't walk a batter for the first time since April 29.
away_pitcher_note: Back in the rotation after being optioned to Triple-A, Volstad had a solid return to the big leagues in a no-decision against Atlanta. The right-hander threw six innings, giving up three runs to the Braves. It was his 18th start of season and first since July 6.

home_pitcher_note: Correia, after scuffling in June, has won his last two starts. He allowed two runs on six hits in six innings against the Pirates. He walked three and didn't strike out a single batter, partly because he struggled with his breaking ball in the start.
away_pitcher_note: Nolasco threw 6 1/3 innings, striking out seven at San Francisco, to start off the road trip. He came away with his team-high 11th win. He has won six of his past seven decisions. He has won four of five with 40 strikeouts in July.

home_pitcher_note: Garland was a tough-luck loser in his last start against the Dodgers on July 7. He allowed two runs on five hits over 6 2/3 innings.  He walked two and struck out five. He's in pursuit of his 10th victory of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson had gone 13 straight starts since May 8 of pitching at least six innings while allowing no more than two runs. That ended at San Francisco, when he allowed three in seven. In July, JJ gave up five runs in 33 1/3 innings, but had two wins.

home_pitcher_note: After posting a 4-3 record at Triple-A New Orleans, West was promoted to fill Alex Sanabia's rotation spot. At New Orleans, West had a 4.12 ERA. In his last start, July 27, he threw a shutout. West had 20 starts in '09 for Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: Halladay returns to Florida, where he enjoyed his best individual pitching performance -- a perfect game on May 29. He also will try to help the Phillies win the opening game in a road series for the first time since May 28 against Florida.

home_pitcher_note: You have to go back to Sanchez's no-hitter in 2006 to find an outing better by the 26-year-old right-hander. Sanchez comes off a gem at San Francisco, tossing a one-hit shutout. He matched a career high with eight strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Kendrick is 1-0 with a 1.35 ERA since the Phillies demoted him to Triple-A Lehigh Valley on July 21. They called him back up after Jamie Moyer injured his left elbow, and he hasn't missed a beat. He hopes the trend continues Wednesday.

home_pitcher_note: Fresh off a win at San Diego, Volstad looks to stay on track. Before July 30, he hadn't won since June 13 at Tampa Bay. On June 8, he gave up six runs (five earned) in a no-decision against the Phillies. He has walked three in three straight starts.
away_pitcher_note: Oswalt certainly is hoping for improvement in his second career start with the Phillies. His first was shaky at best. He allowed seven hits, five runs, two walks and hit two batters in a loss Friday to the Washington Nationals.

home_pitcher_note: July was kind to Nolasco, who was 5-1 in six starts with 47 strikeouts in 42 innings. The right-hander is 3-1 since the All-Star Break with 30 strikeouts and five walks. He is 0-2 with a 5.92 ERA vs. St. Louis in five appearances.
away_pitcher_note: As expected, Wainwright got back on track in his last start after one shaky one. Now he goes back on the road, but Florida is an excellent place to pitch. In 38 career innings against Florida, Wainwright has 37 strikeouts and 10 walks.

home_pitcher_note: The All-Star had a string of 19 straight quality starts snapped at San Diego on Sunday, when for the first time since April 10 he did not go at least six innings. JJ seeks his first win since July 17. Since the All-Star Break, he is 1-1 (3.24).
away_pitcher_note: In his Cardinals' debut, Jake Westbrook tossed six innings while allowing just two earned runs against the Astros. The right-hander struck out seven, but took a no-decision. Westbrook is 1-0 with a 1.13 ERA in his career against the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: The 24-year-old comes off his first start of the season, a loss to the Phillies and Roy Halladay in Miami. In five innings, he allowed nine hits and five runs (four earned). He faced Washington twice last year, and gave up 10 runs in 7 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Suppan will start in place of the still rehabbing Kyle Lohse in the rubber game against the Marlins. The veteran is coming off his first win of 2010 in his last outing on July 31, when he tossed 5 1/3 shutout innings against the Pirates.

home_pitcher_note: Strasburg is slated to make his return off of the 15-Day D.L. in this spot. Strasburg will throw a simulated game on Thursday and in the bullpen on Saturday before his comeback. On July 16, Strasburg shutout out Florida for six innings.
away_pitcher_note: A 58-minute rain delay hindered Sanchez's warmup routine in his last start, and it showed. The right-hander gave up four runs on seven hits in 4 1/3 innings in a loss to the Phillies. He was coming off a one-hit shutout at San Francisco.

home_pitcher_note: Olsen was hit hard in his last start, a 6-1 Nationals loss to the D-backs last Tuesday.  The lefty gave up five runs on seven hits (including two home runs) in 5 2/3 innings. Olsen is 1-1 with a 4.70 ERA in four career starts vs. the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: Since returning from Triple-A New Orleans, Volstad has made three starts, and he's 1-0 with two no-decisions. He has thrown 16 2/3 innings, and allowed seven runs. In each of those outings, he has walked three while striking out six.

home_pitcher_note: Hernandez has been sharp in his past two starts and looks to continue his recent success. In both outings -- a win and no-decision to the D-backs and Dodgers, respectively - he allowed only one earned run and went more than seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Impressive for so long, Nolasco comes off an outing he'd rather forget. In a loss to the Cardinals, the right-hander gave up seven runs in five innings. His only start worse was eight runs at the White Sox on May 21. Away, he is 8-2 with a 3.86 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Volquez didn't get a win Saturday vs. the Cubs, settling for a no-decision in a 4-3 Reds victory. But he was pleased with his progress following 6 2/3 mostly well-pitched innings. "I finally got everything together now," Volquez said.
away_pitcher_note: Six times Johnson exited with his team leading only to settle for a no-decision. The All-Star leads the Majors with his 1.97 ERA, and he comes off allowing two runs over eight innings against the Cardinals. JJ last won on July 17.

home_pitcher_note: Leake is coming off the worst start of his young career, having given up seven runs (six earned) on nine hits in a career-low 3 2/3 innings against the division-rival Cardinals. This will be the rookie's first appearance against the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: Last Sunday against the Cardinals, the left-hander had his second start washed out due to rain. West's lone start was a loss to the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Bailey, who has been out since May 23 with right shoulder inflammation, will start in place of the suspended Johnny Cueto. Bailey tossed seven shutout innings in his final Triple-A rehab start Aug. 5 and added a scoreless relief inning Tuesday.
away_pitcher_note: With 135 1/3 innings, Sanchez has already logged a career high. He seeks 10 wins for the second time of his career. He won 10 as a rookie in 2006.

home_pitcher_note: Efficiency issues and an inability to put away hitters got McDonald in trouble in his last start. He went to seven three-ball counts, four coming after he got ahead 1-2 or 0-2. McDonald is stretched out now, meaning he has no pitch limitations.
away_pitcher_note: Volstad has won two of his past three starts, with a no-decision. He worked five innings in beating Washington his last time out. He last threw as many as six innings on July 25.

home_pitcher_note: Since coming off the disabled list, Zach Duke has notched four quality starts in six outings. The wins, though, aren't falling as easily. The good news for Duke is that his next start will come at home, where the Bucs have given him good run support.
away_pitcher_note: Nolasco blanked the Nationals for six innings on Thursday, allowing six hits with one walk and eight strikeouts. He's won four of his past five decisions.

home_pitcher_note: Ohlendorf threw 6 2/3 shutout innings in his last start, but he didn't factor in the decision after the bullpen allowed the Astros to pull ahead in a 4-1 loss. Ohlendorf fanned seven batters against two walks and four hits.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson said he feels fine physically after his shortest outing of the season, Friday at Cincinnati. He lasted just 3 2/3 innings in a 7-2 loss to the Reds, allowing a season-high six runs and a career-high 10 hits.

home_pitcher_note: Locke will make his first Major League start in place of Charlie Morton. The Bucs acquired Locke from the Braves back in 2009 in a package for outfielder Nate McLouth. The 23-year-old lefty posted a 2.22 ERA in 28 1/3 innings for Indianapolis.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez received a no-decision in his last start after giving up just two unearned runs in six innings against the Phillies. The right-hander is 1-1 with a 2.77 ERA in his career against the Pirates. He is 4-4 with a 3.83 ERA this season on the road.

home_pitcher_note: McDonald limited the Astros to one run and three hits in 7 1/3 innings to win Monday. McDonald struck out six for the second time in eight starts. He's given up three runs or fewer in 18 of his past 20 starts.
away_pitcher_note: Vazquez earned the win in his last start against the Mets, allowing just one run over seven innings with seven strikeouts. With one more victory, it'll be his 12th straight year of double-digit wins. In 13 starts since June 28, he has a 2.43 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Beachy gave up just two hits and one run in 5 2/3 innings of a 3-2 loss at Philadelphia on Sept. 7. He left the game tied at 1. Philadelphia scored single runs in the eighth and ninth.
away_pitcher_note: Volstad remains winless in his past six outings and has lost his last four decisions. In his last start against the Mets, he received a no-decision after allowing two runs on six hits. He is 0-2 with a 6.35 ERA against the Braves this season.

home_pitcher_note: Minor takes the hill after giving up seven hits and four earned runs in five innings of a 6-5 win over New York on Thursday in the first game of a doubleheader. Minor surrendered a grand slam to Jason Bay.
away_pitcher_note: Hand was a hard-luck loser Wednesday after allowing one run in six innings vs. the Mets. Hand allowed three hits and walked four. Opponents are hitting just .227 off Hand, but he's hurt himself by walking 32 batters in 50 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Delgado allowed just three hits and one run in a five-inning effort against St. Louis on Friday. He left with the lead, but lost a chance at his first  win when Craig Kimbrel blew his first save since June 8.
away_pitcher_note: Ricky Nolasco allowed three runs on nine hits in six innings on Friday, picking up his 10th win as the Marlins routed the Pirates 13-4. Since the All-Star break, he's posted a 5.77 ERA in 64 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Kendrick hasn't pitched since returning from paternity leave. He last pitched on Aug. 24 against the Mets. In a losing effort, Kendrick threw four innings allowing seven hits and six runs (two earned) and gave up two homers.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez comes off his third career one-hitter -- second of 2011. He struck out 11 Pirates. He is making his 30th start of the year. This will be his fifth start of the year against the Phillies. He has yet to factor into a decision.

home_pitcher_note: Lee snapped his scoreless streak at 30 2/3 innings in Saturday's 3-2 victory over Milwaukee. He allowed just one earned run in seven innings. Lee is in the running for the Cy Young, with Roy Halladay and Clayton Kershaw his two closest competitors.
away_pitcher_note: The 23-year-old righty will make his first start and second appearance of the season. A September callup, Sanabia made 12 starts as a rookie in 2010. In his lone outing this year, he struck out two and walked two in a scoreless inning at Pittsburgh.

home_pitcher_note: Lannan had one of his worst outings of the year and it proved costly, as the Nationals were pounded by the Astros at Nationals Park on Saturday night. Lannan ran into trouble in the third, when 11 men came to the plate.
away_pitcher_note: Vazquez is making his 30th start of the season. The veteran, who has hinted that he will retire after the year, has now gone 12 straight seasons with at least 10 wins. He is 2-0 with an 0.69 ERA in September. He is 5-3 (2.65) in the second half.

home_pitcher_note: Making his second start of the season, Strasburg left after pitching three innings in his last outing. In the first inning, Strasburg threw 31 pitches and allowed an RBI single to Carlos Lee.
away_pitcher_note: Volstad last faced the Nationals on Aug. 3 at Washington, and he came out on the winning end of a 6-4 decision. That day, he gave up four runs on seven hits in five innings. He comes off a two-run, seven-hit no-decision in five innings at Atlanta.

home_pitcher_note: Wang has not yielded more than four earned runs in nine starts since his return, though he also has completed six innings just four times. He is looking for his first win since Aug. 16, when he went 6 1/3 against the Reds.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie lefty has shown signs of being a solid big leaguer. What he needs to show more of is consistency. Hand has lost four straight starts. In his last start, he led by a run in the sixth, but gave up a three-run homer to Atlanta's Brian McCann.

home_pitcher_note: A hard-luck seventh inning cost Nolasco in his last outing, a 4-1 loss at Atlanta. He was victimized by a three-run Alex Gonzalez homer after tossing six shutout innings. Nolasco is at 197 1/3 innings on the season.
away_pitcher_note: Minor is 2-0 with a 3.74 ERA in his past four starts and took a no-decision in his last one, which also came against the Marlins. He limited the Fish to one run on four hits in 5 2/3 innings and has a 6.52 ERA in two career starts against them.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez comes off a tough loss to Philadelphia, in which he gave up two runs in six innings with seven strikeouts. That effort came after a one-hit, 11-strikeout win at Pittsburgh. In his past three starts, he's 1-1 with a 0.86 ERA and 23 strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Delgado has allowed just one run in three of his five starts this season. That continued in his latest start against the Marlins on Wednesday, when he allowed one run in five innings of work. He has a 1.80 ERA in his past two starts.

home_pitcher_note: What a turnaround from a terrible start. Vazquez threw his first complete game since 2005 in his last outing, when he blanked the Nationals. In his last four starts, he is 4-0 with an 0.31 ERA (1 runs in 29 innings).
away_pitcher_note: Lowe had his worst start of the year last time out against the Mets, allowing six runs in just 2 1/3 innings of work. The righty is 0-3 with a 10.13 ERA in his last three starts but is 1-0 with a 1.42 in his two outings this season against Florida.

home_pitcher_note: Gallardo is getting hot at a good time. He matched his career high with 12 strikeouts in a Sept. 11 win over the Phillies and set a new mark with 13 strikeouts against the Reds last weekend.
away_pitcher_note: Volstad had one of his finest performances in a while. The right-hander still hasn't won since July 10, but he allowed one run in seven innings in a no-decision in Washington. He lost to the Brewers on June 4, giving up three runs in seven innings.

home_pitcher_note: Greinke has a 1.93 ERA over his last five starts and has been excellent at Miller Park, where he is 10-0 with a 2.89 ERA. The Brewers have won all 13 of his Miller Park starts.
away_pitcher_note: In his first start of the season, the 23-year-old right-hander received a no-decision after allowing one run on six hits in six innings against the Phillies in Game 2 of a doubleheader. Sanabia takes over Brad Hand's spot in the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Narveson has worked on irregular rest all month because of ill-timed off-days, and it showed in his last start against the Cubs. His changeup, usually sharp, was erratic, and Narveson needed 75 pitches for only four innings.
away_pitcher_note: In consecutive starts against Atlanta, Nolasco has cruised until four-run seventh innings. He received a no-decision in his previous outing after going 6 2/3 innings and allowing five runs  (four earned). He has a 6.00 ERA in one start vs. Milwaukee.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez lost his last start against the Braves after allowing a three-run second inning. He went just five frames and threw 83 pitches. He is 8 2/3 innings shy of his first 200-inning season. Sanchez is tied for seventh in the NL with 191 strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: On Tuesday, Milone pitched six scoreless innings, allowing four hits, striking out two and walking none. It marked the third time in four starts Milone didn't walk a batter.

home_pitcher_note: Vazquez has pitched 25 consecutive scoreless innings, setting the franchise record for a starter. Over his past 11 games, he has gone 6-2 with a 1.54 ERA, which ranks third in the Majors. He pitched a complete-game shutout last time against the Nats.
away_pitcher_note: Lannan earned his career-high 10th win on Wednesday. It wasn't his best outing, as he allowed three runs on eight hits in five innings against the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Volstad, a South Florida native, will make the final start of the season and the last game for the team as the Florida Marlins at Sun Life Stadium. At home, he's 3-7 (5.04 ERA). He had a strong seven-inning start vs. Milwaukee in his last start.
away_pitcher_note: In his worst start of the year, Strasburg found himself in trouble in the first inning, throwing 38 pitches and allowing three runs -- two earned. Strasburg settled down, retiring nine out of the last 10 hitters he faced.

summary: 2012-03-11 - Miami Marlins @ New York Mets (Completed Early: Rain)

home_pitcher_note: Set to make his third straight Opening Day start, Johnson will throw the very first pitch at Marlins Park. Regarded as a key to Miami's playoff hopes, Johnson is looking to bounce back from a shoulder injury that limited him to nine starts in 2011.
away_pitcher_note: Chris Carpenter's setback opened the door for Lohse to start the season opener. The Opening Night start will technically be the second of Lohse's career, though the first came only because of a rainout. Lohse led the rotation in wins and ERA in '11.

home_pitcher_note: Cueto had a 2.31 ERA in 24 starts and 156 innings last year after missing five weeks with right biceps/triceps issues. He also missed a couple of late-season starts. Cueto, 26, has looked decent in camp and will be making his first Opening Day start.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran left-hander makes his Miami debut after spending his entire career with the White Sox. Buehrle has a string of 11 straight seasons throwing at least 200 innings. He's 2-0, 0.60 ERA lifetime against the Reds.

home_pitcher_note: The Reds acquired Latos from the Padres to be the No. 2 starter behind Johnny Cueto and gave up a lot to get him. He looked good in Spring Training and showed no ill effects from a strained left calf suffered later in camp.
away_pitcher_note: Nolasco enters the season with 64 wins, four behind Dontrelle Willis for the club record. The right-hander logged 206 innings a year ago, and he's had four straight seasons of 10 or more wins. He's 41-27 on the road lifetime.

home_pitcher_note: Arroyo struggled all last season, in part, because of lower velocity. That didn't seem to be a problem during camp as Arroyo was often in the upper 80s and 90s. He also worked on a new grip for his sinker to keep hitters off-balance.
away_pitcher_note: The unpredictable Zambrano is getting a fresh new start with the Marlins. He's certainly familiar with the Reds, posting a 17-11 (3.28) career mark against them. Zambrano has won at least 10 games in seven of eight years.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels is one of the big three, but he gets the fourth start of the season because the Phillies want him to pitch the home opener against the Miami Marlins. It's a nice honor for Hamels, who can become a free agent following the season.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez missed time with right shoulder soreness early in Spring Training. He made 32 starts in 2011, striking out 202 in 196 1/3 innings. He was 2-5, 3.74 ERA against NL East teams. He was 0-1 in three starts at Philly.

home_pitcher_note: Halladay looked like his typical dominant self in Thursday's 1-0 victory over Pittsburgh at PNC Park. He allowed just two hits and struck out five in eight scoreless innings, silencing some concerns about his rough spring.
away_pitcher_note: Opening Night was a battle for Johnson, who matched his career high by allowing 10 hits to the Cards. While healthy, Johnson admits that the consistent sharpness of his pitches is not quite there. It's a work in progress.

home_pitcher_note: The Phillies didn't need their fifth starter until April 15, but they didn't want Blanton to wait that long to pitch, so he's going to make his debut in the series finale against Miami. He's hoping to rebound from an injury-marred 2011.
away_pitcher_note: Buehrle made his Marlins and NL debut on April 5 at Cincinnati. He labored early, needing 28 pitches to get through the first inning. He lasted six innings, giving up two earned runs on seven hits over 108 pitches. He walked two and struck out five.

home_pitcher_note: An impressive eight-inning performance at Cincinnati moved Nolasco within three wins of matching Dontrelle Willis' franchise mark of 68. Nolasco is 65-51 all-time. He struck out five and didn't issue a walk at the Reds.
away_pitcher_note: Harrell pitched seven scoreless innings against the Rockies in his season debut Saturday, allowing three hits and striking out four. That was the first time in his career he went seven innings, and he's never faced Miami.

home_pitcher_note: Perhaps it was a case of nerves or an adrenaline rush, but Zambrano got off to a slow start in his Marlins debut, giving up three runs in the first at Cincinnati. He settled, fanning six in a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Norris had a quality start in his first outing of the season Sunday against Colorado, giving up four hits and two runs in seven innings while striking out eight. He's 1-1 with a 6.65 ERA in four starts against the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: Splendid in his first start of the season, Sanchez looks to build on his 6 1/3-inning outing in Philadelphia. His command was sharp in his 95-pitch, 64-strike performance. He has responded from spring shoulder soreness.
away_pitcher_note: Happ threw six innings and got the win with a quality starts in his first outing of the season while beating the Braves on Monday. He's 2-2 with a 4.79 ERA in eight career games against the Marlins, including five starts.

home_pitcher_note: Regaining his old form is a work in progress. Knocked around twice in two starts, Johnson has given up 21 hits in nine 2/3 innings. He allowed a career-high 11 in his last start. Johnson seeks his first win since April 19, 2011.
away_pitcher_note: Dempster has given up three earned runs over 14 1/3 innings in his first two starts, but he still doesn't have a win. The Cubs haven't been able to give him any run support. He's 4-1 with a 2.11 ERA in his career against the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: Despite two straight quality starts, Buehrle finds himself with an 0-2 record. Both tough losses came on the road. At Philadelphia, he was perfect for three innings, but yielded three runs in 6 1/3 innings, which was too much.
away_pitcher_note: Garza nearly notched his first shutout with the Cubs in his last start, going 8 2/3 innings vs. the Brewers. But he was pulled because of pitch count and after an errant throw into the stands. For the game, Garza gave up three hits and fanned nine.

home_pitcher_note: Nolasco had a solid last outing, holding the Astros to two runs on four hits over five innings in a no-decision. However, the right-hander threw a lot of pitches, needing 90 to get through five innings. He will try to be more efficient vs. the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Samardzija cruised through the first four innings of his last start but then the Cardinals batted around in the fifth. He threw 103 pitches for his second successive 100-plus game. The Cubs want to keep an eye on him.

home_pitcher_note: The Nationals didn't get a stellar performance from left-hander Ross Detwiler on Sunday afternoon against the Reds. Detwiler ended up throwing five innings and allowing five runs -- one earned -- on six hits in an 8-5 loss.
away_pitcher_note: It hasn't always been pretty, but Zambrano is getting the job done. He's ended up with two no-decisions in games Miami led entering the ninth. He did walk six in his last outing, but allowed one run against Houston.

home_pitcher_note: On Monday, Strasburg was solid vs. Houston in his third start of the season. He lasted six innings, allowed two runs on six hits, struck out five hitters and walked one. Strasburg threw 93 pitches, 61 strikes.
away_pitcher_note: In 17 career starts against the Nationals, Sanchez is 7-0 with a 2.06 ERA. The right-hander has thrown well in two starts this year. He struck out seven in a no-decision vs. the Astros. He has 10 strikeouts in 12 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: After Sunday's rainout, the Mets bumped Santana back a day in the rotation to keep their other four starters in order. That gives Santana an extra day off after one of the worst outings of his career, in which he gave up six runs in 1 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Rained out on Sunday at Washington caused Johnson's schedule to change. Now he gets two days of extra rest and will start the series opener against New York, a team against whom he is 8-1 lifetime. He is 1-1 at Citi Field.

home_pitcher_note: Dickey's previous start was his worst in four years. He'll need to improve if he plans to match last year's performance vs. the Marlins, which included a 3-0 record and zero earned runs.
away_pitcher_note: After two hard-luck losses, Buehrle logged his first win as a Marlin. It was in impressive fashion, as he went eight innings, allowing one run against the Cubs. He even had an RBI single. He's never pitched against the Mets.

home_pitcher_note: Niese has made three consecutive quality starts, making him the team's most dependable starter thus far. He also tossed a quality start in his only game against the Marlins last season, holding them to two runs over seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Fresh off his second win of the season, Nolasco is two shy of matching Dontrelle Willis' franchise record of 68. The right-hander is 66-51 lifetime after he beat the Cubs. Nolasco is 5-7 against the Mets, 1-1 at Citi Field.

home_pitcher_note: Zambrano has strung together three straight quality starts, and yet the right-hander seeks his first win. He suffered a hard-luck loss at Washington in his last outing, giving up one run on two hits in seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Saunders was a hard-luck loser Saturday against the Braves. He threw seven solid innings, allowing just two earned runs on six hits. Through 21 innings this season, Saunders has given up three earned runs total.

home_pitcher_note: Dominating is the best way to describe Sanchez's first three games, yet he has just one win. In 19 1/3 innings, he has 19 strikeouts and just four walks. He's scattered 16 hits, and has two straight no-decisions.
away_pitcher_note: Kennedy snapped the D-backs' five-game losing streak on Sunday, pitching seven innings vs. the Braves and giving up three earned runs on nine hits. He hasn't lost a regular-season decision since Aug. 18 against the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: It was the Josh Johnson of old in his last start, but the ace wasn't rewarded with a win. JJ had a no-decision after allowing one run and striking out nine in 6 2/3 innings. JJ exited with the lead. His last win remains April 19, 2011.
away_pitcher_note: Miley started in place of the injured Daniel Hudson on Monday and tossed six shutout innings against the Phillies. He made the team thanks to a strong Spring Training, and his first three appearances of the year were in relief.

home_pitcher_note: All four of Buehrle's outings have been quality starts, yet the veteran has one win and three losses. Buehrle is coming off a tough setback at New York, giving up two runs in seven innings. He has never faced Arizona.
away_pitcher_note: Corbin will be making his Major League debut. He is taking the place of Josh Collmenter, who was sent to the bullpen. Corbin was impressive in Spring Training, and in his first four starts for Double-A Mobile, he had a 1.67 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Cain will never make excuses for a poor performance, but the lack of slope on Cincinnati's mound may have contributed to his lapses in his previous start. Struggling to adjust to the conditions, he allowed homers to Brandon Phillips and Ryan Ludwick.
away_pitcher_note: Nolasco, a California-native, is 3-0 with a 0.76 ERA at AT&T Park. And he's 4-2 with a 1.61 ERA lifetime against the Giants. He remains two wins shy of the Marlins' wins record, held by Dontrelle Willis, who had 68.

home_pitcher_note: Historically, Zito has experienced mixed success in May during his 11-year career. Though his lifetime record for the month is 18-17, his 3.38 ERA is his second-best, eclipsed only by his 3.19 August ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Zambrano found himself in jams for most of his last start but always managed to limit damage. The right-hander allowed just three runs while surrendering 10 hits over six innings. Zambrano will look to improve in his next outing against the Giants.

home_pitcher_note: Vogelsong began to establish himself during his 2011 renaissance last May. In six starts, he compiled a 1.78 ERA with a WHIP of 1.189. That's also when he proved he could excel at AT&T Park, yielding one earned run in 20 1/3 innings in three outings.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez set a personal high with 14 strikeouts in his last start, a no-decision against Arizona. He tied for the second-most strikeouts ever by a Marlin. A.J. Burnett did it twice, and the team mark is 16 by Ricky Nolasco.

home_pitcher_note: Bass retired the first 17 hitters he faced in his last start against the Giants. He lost, 2-1, to Tim Lincecum but struck out a career-high eight batters in eight innings. Bass got some funny-looking swings on his slider and changeup.
away_pitcher_note: That first victory still eludes Johnson, who last won on April 19, 2011. JJ has had his ups and downs in five starts. He comes off a rough outing, allowing five runs on 10 hits in 5 1/3 innings to Arizona. He struck out eight.

home_pitcher_note: Richard allowed two runs in the first inning of his last start against the Giants, but settled down thereafter, retiring 14 of the next 16 hitters he faced. Richard allowed eight hits in seven innings with two walks and two strikeouts.
away_pitcher_note: Buehrle's last start is one the veteran would like to forget. He gave up two homers among eight hits and seven runs (four earned) allowed over five innings in his fourth loss of the year. Buehrle will try to bounce back at Petco Park.

home_pitcher_note: After four starts, Wieland is still searching for his first big league win. On Monday, he gave up five runs (three earned) in five innings, including two homers to Ryan Braun. Wieland struck out a career-high eight and walked two (one intentional).
away_pitcher_note: Brilliant at San Francisco (one run in 7 1/3 innings) to start the road trip, Nolasco looks to string together two straight wins away from home. If he does, he will match Dontrelle Willis' franchise-record victory total of 68.

home_pitcher_note: Rodriguez is the ace of the Houston staff and has pitched like one of late, going 3-0 in his last three starts. The Astros are maximizing the lefty's use by starting him every fifth day, even when it means skipping another starter.
away_pitcher_note: Zambrano has a string of four straight quality starts, and he has yet to log a win. Big Z has been in a tough-luck situation. In San Francisco in his last outing, he threw seven shutout innings. He faced Houston on April 14, a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Rodriguez's first big league appearance this year. Rodriguez, who went 1-6 with a 5.27 ERA in 43 games (eight starts) for the Astros in '11, was 1-3 with a 4.97 ERA at Triple-A. He's replacing Kyle Weiland.
away_pitcher_note: The last three starts have been impressive, as Sanchez has given up five earned runs in 21 innings. He has 38 strikeouts in 33 1/3 innings on the year and limited San Francisco to one run in seven innings in his last start.

home_pitcher_note: Harrell won for the first time in five starts on Friday, holding the Cardinals to three earned runs in 5 1/3 innings. He hasn't pitched as well as he did on April 7 when he threw seven scoreless innings against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson had a rough time in his last start, giving up six runs in the third inning in San Diego in a no-decision. He struck out one and was unable to hold a five-run lead. JJ still seeks his first win since April 19, 2011.

home_pitcher_note: The veteran prides himself on going deep into games. Buehrle did that in his last start, logging the Marlins' first complete game of the season. The 116-pitch outing was his first nine-inning complete game since July 23, 2010.
away_pitcher_note: Throwing a season-high 108 pitches in his last outing, Santana will go Friday on extra rest for the sixth time in seven starts. The lefty struck out 11 Marlins, also a season high, over 6 2/3 innings of one-run ball earlier this year at Citi Field.

home_pitcher_note: Nolasco tied Dontrelle Willis' Marlins record with his 68th win in his last start, a seven-inning outing in San Diego. Now he gets a chance to set the mark for himself vs. the Mets.
away_pitcher_note: Featuring one of his best knuckleballs of the year, Dickey held the D-backs to a run over eight-plus innings Sunday. He'll make his debut at Marlins Ballpark after stringing together 13 innings without an earned run last year at Sun Life Stadium.

home_pitcher_note: Zambrano earned his first win in a Marlins' uniform Monday, throwing a three-hit shutout in a 4-0 win at Houston. Zambrano's efforts put him at the top of the list among Miami starting pitchers with a 1.98 ERA and a 1.02 WHIP.
away_pitcher_note: Four walks drove up Niese's pitch count Monday in Philly, forcing him to throw 101 pitches over five innings. Efficiency will be the challenge for Niese against the Marlins, who mustered four hits off him in seven innings last month.

home_pitcher_note: Sanchez turned in perhaps his best performance of the season Tuesday in Houston, going seven innings while allowing no earned runs on five hits. He struck out eight and walked two, but got a no-decision when the Marlins blew a 2-0 lead in a 3-2 loss.
away_pitcher_note: Lincoln makes his first start, subbing for Erik Bedard (back spasms), after excelling in scattered relief chores. His ERA is third-best among NL relievers. Lincoln made 17 starts for the Bucs in 2010-11 (5.54 ERA in them), but is more confident now.

home_pitcher_note: Johnson had arguably his best outing of the year his last time out, a seven-inning, two-run effort against Houston in which he fanned six and walked two. He is 2-0 with a 1.64 ERA in his career against Pittsburgh.
away_pitcher_note: Correia hopes to stay away from that one inning that seems to hurt him every start, spoiling good overall efforts. Has lacked a put-away pitch, but competes well. Even he may be buying into that "road killer" rep; he's lost four of 17 road starts.

home_pitcher_note: The lefty is coming off three challenging outings. He gave up six earned runs in 4 2/3 innings of a 9-7 12-inning win in St. Louis on Friday. Before that, he posted back-to-back efforts combining for 15 earned runs in 11 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Buehrle didn't earn a decision against the Mets on Friday, but he did have a quality start, lasting 6 2/3 innings, scattering eight hits and two runs while walking two and striking out three. He threw 64 of 102 pitches for strikes.

home_pitcher_note: Beachy has six successive quality starts after allowing just one run over six innings in a win at St. Louis on Saturday. He also added an RBI single in the win. The righty has given up two earned runs or fewer in all seven starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Going for sole possession of Miami's career wins record, Nolasco struggled. He gave up six runs on nine hits in a loss to the Mets. After walking three total in his previous three starts, he walked three in the first frame and hit two batters late.

home_pitcher_note: Masterson's command woes continued on Sunday in Boston, where the Red Sox tagged the sinkerballer for six runs (four in the first inning) on seven hits over six innings. Masterson walked just one, but he hit three batters.
away_pitcher_note: Luck has not gone Zambrano's way, as he comes off another no-decision in a game in which he was terrific. He gave up one earned run (two total) in seven innings. It was the first earned run Zambrano has allowed in his last three starts.

home_pitcher_note: Gomez pitched a solid seven innings on Monday and allowed just three hits the Tribe's 5-4 win over the Twins. But he received a no-decision because the bullpen gave up three eighth-inning runs.
away_pitcher_note: Sanchez was handed his first loss of the season his last time out, despite notching his seventh quality start in as many outings. Sanchez went seven innings and gave up three runs, including one homer, on six hits while fanning five and walking one.

home_pitcher_note: Derek Lowe's impressive start to the 2012 season stayed in high gear as he posted his first shutout in seven years in a 5-0 Indians victory against the Twins on Tuesday.
away_pitcher_note: Johnson earned his first win in 13 months his last time out, pitching seven innings against the Pirates. He gave up two runs on six hits for his second straight quality start. The righty fanned six and walked one, relying heavily on his curveball.

home_pitcher_note: For a change, Buehrle got plenty of run support in an 8-4 victory at Atlanta on Wednesday. He failed to register a quality start for just the second time in eight outings, allowing four earned runs on six hits. Buehrle struck out four and walked one.
away_pitcher_note: Moyer held the D-backs to just one run through 6 1/3 innings Wednesday on six hits and two walks with five strikeouts. With this start at the new Marlins Park, Moyer, 49, will make an appearance in the 50th ballpark of his Major League career.

home_pitcher_note: Nolasco has lost his past two starts after winning his first four decisions. He allowed four runs in four innings vs. the Braves on Thursday after surrendering six runs to the Mets in 4 2/3 innings in his previous outing.
away_pitcher_note: Nicasio walked five and lasted just 4 2/3 innings in his last start, a no-decision in a 9-7 loss to the D-backs. Nicasio was affected by a bruised right hip suffered on a first-inning line drive, but has recovered after receiving treatment.
