home_pitcher_note: Koehler missed his last outing with a stiff neck, so he'll be extra rested as he tries for a second straight quality start. In his last outing on June 15, he went seven innings and held the Yankees to one run and three hits.
away_pitcher_note: Kershaw made a quality start against the Cubs, but all three runs he allowed scored on two homers. He's allowed 11 this year, already more than the nine allowed last year.

home_pitcher_note: Urena is showing promise and that's one reason he's getting another start. But it will be a tough one, against a strong lineup. The rookie is 1-1 (3.57 ERA) in three home starts. But he's struck out just seven in 17 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Greinke hasn't allowed a run in his last two starts, but he hasn't been credited with a victory since May 5 as the offense seems inclined to shut down when he pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Latos seeks his first win since June 13, when he allowed one run in seven innings vs. Colorado in Miami. That's been his lone home win, as he is 1-3 with a 7.60 ERA at Marlins Park. On May 10 at San Francisco, Latos gave up one run in seven.
away_pitcher_note: Vogelsong looks to build off his recent hot streak as he's tossed 12 2/3 straight scoreless innings in his last two outings. In his last start against Miami on May 10, he gave up one run in seven innings in a 3-2 win.

home_pitcher_note: Haren has dropped three straight decisions, posting a 4.42 ERA in that stretch. The veteran has been a workhorse, logging at least six innings in seven of his last eight starts. He last won on June 3 vs. the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: Heston will face the Marlins for the first time in his career. The right-hander is coming off a 13-8 win against the Padres in which he threw seven innings and gave up two runs.

home_pitcher_note: The anticipated return of Fernandez has arrived. The 22-year-old, who had Tommy John surgery on May 16, 2014, will make his first MLB start since the injury. In five rehab starts, he struck out 33 in 24 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Cain recovered well from his offseason surgeries (he also had a bone spur removed from his right ankle last September) but still needed the first few months of this season to regain arm strength.

home_pitcher_note: Hammel's most dominant start of the year came June 1 against the Marlins, when he struck out 11 over 6 2/3 innings. He looks to rebound after having his last outing interrupted by multiple rain delays.
away_pitcher_note: In a gutsy win over the Dodgers in his last start, Koehler showed he is capable of performing in big games. It's now a matter of performing on the road, where he's 2-3 with a 6.21 ERA. He's 4-1 (1.68) at home.

home_pitcher_note: Acquired Friday from the Bucs for cash considerations, Richard, 31, will be making his Cubs debut. The lefty underwent shoulder surgery in July 2013, and was 4-2 with a 2.09 ERA in nine starts at Triple-A. He's pitched for the White Sox and Padres.
away_pitcher_note: Cosart is making his first start since May 13 against the Dodgers. He went on the 15-day disabled list (vertigo) after that outing, and returned to the Marlins on Sunday in a relief role, allowing two runs in four innings.

home_pitcher_note: Hendricks' next start could go a long way in determining whether or not he's regaining his rookie form. It had been a struggle for Hendricks before he blanked the Mets over seven innings last time out.
away_pitcher_note: Injuries slowed Latos the first two months, but in four June startshe was 2-1 with a 3.86 ERA and he's struck out 24 in 25 2/3 innings. Latos' velocity also bounced back in the month, with him reaching the mid-90s.

home_pitcher_note: Miley has pitched fewer than six innings in three of his past seven starts and will be gunning for a more efficient outing this week. He needed 103 pitches to work five frames on Thursday.
away_pitcher_note: Haren has lost three straight decisions, and he seeks his first win since June 3. Still, he's been steady and solid. In his last six starts, he is 1-3 with a 4.17 ERA, going at least 5 2/3 innings in all of them.

home_pitcher_note: Despite posting an 8.18 ERA over his past eight starts, Porcello will stay on turn in the Boston rotation. He gave up seven runs in a season-low two innings vs. the Jays on Saturday.
away_pitcher_note: Koehler has won three straight one-run decisions in tough places against tough opponents. He edged the Cubs, 2-1, at Wrigley Field, and got the best of Yankees right-hander Masahiro Tanaka and Dodgers lefty Clayton Kershaw.

home_pitcher_note: It was a triumphant return for Fernandez, who beat the Giants on July 2, his first start in 14 months. Fernandez struck out six and homered. A week after his win, this will be his final start before the All-Star break.
away_pitcher_note: Lorenzen will look for results similar to his last outing vs. Miami on June 21. The righty earned the win as he tossed seven innings and allowed two earned runs. In two starts since, he's 0-1 (four earned runs in 9 2/3 innings).

home_pitcher_note: Phelps makes his first start since June 21 after spending another stint in the bullpen, where he tossed 4 1/3 scoreless innings in two appearances. He posted a 3.84 ERA in 13 starts this year.
away_pitcher_note: Leake is coming off of back-to-back poor starts. On Sunday, the Brewers had him laboring with a 28-pitch first inning and had several hard-hit balls.

home_pitcher_note: Conley got the callup from Triple-A to make his first MLB start in place of Mat Latos, who was scratched with a right foot contusion. Conley, 8-2 (2.33) at New Orleans, threw one inning of relief in his MLB debut earlier this season.
away_pitcher_note: Iglesias has been on the disabled list since June 5 with a left oblique strain but has recently made two rehab starts at Triple-A Louisville. Prior to his injury, the rookie made four starts with the Reds and allowed 11 runs in 21 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Haren continues to give the Marlins a reliable presence in their rotation. In 17 outings, he has recorded 12 quality starts and pitched at least six innings on 13 occasions.
away_pitcher_note: Due to Wednesday's rainout, Cueto will sneak in one more start before the All-Star break. He's coming off two straight stellar outings, as he's 2-0 while allowing one run and six hits in 17 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Morgan looks to regroup from his loss to the Dodgers on July 8, in which he surrendered five runs on six hits in just four innings. The rookie allowed just three earned runs in 12 1/3 innings in his first two career starts.
away_pitcher_note: Fernandez has made two starts since his return, and so far, so good. He's earned two wins while allowing just three earned runs in 13 innings and striking out 15. In his career vs. Philly, Fernandez is 1-1 with a 2.86 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Billingsley is coming off a start against the Giants in which he allowed four runs in five innings. The right-hander picked up his first win since April 10, 2013, against the Dodgers on July 7, but has not looked like his former self this season.
away_pitcher_note: Koehler has won three of his last four decisions, but in his last start on July 8, he lost 6-3 in Boston. He faced the Phillies once this year and received a no-decision. He is 2-1 with a 4.30 ERA in 8 career appearances vs the Phils.

home_pitcher_note: Hamels gave up nine runs, the most he’s ever allowed in his 10-year career, in a 15-2 loss to the Giants on July 10. The left-hander’s ERA rose from 3.02 to 3.63 in the defeat, in which he lasted just 3 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Miami's most dependable starter in the first half, Haren has a team-high 111 innings. Haren has 149 career victories, and he's 40 strikeouts away from 2,000. But he's 2-6 with a 4.24 ERA against the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: De La Rosa lost his last two starts of the first half, giving up 10 runs in 8 2/3 innings. His longest outing of the season came on May 18 against the Marlins, when he gave up two runs in nine innings and took a no-decision.
away_pitcher_note: Phelps is making his 19th appearance (15th start) of the season, and second against the D-backs. He lost to Arizona in Miami, giving up four runs in five innings. But in 9 1/3 innings in July, his ERA is 0.96.

home_pitcher_note: Hellickson has completed seven innings in a start just once in 17 outings. He has no-decisions in three career starts against the Marlins but allowed just two runs in six innings against them on May 19.
away_pitcher_note: Scratched from his last start due to a sore right foot, Latos makes his first appearance since July 5. Latos has shown improvement over his last five starts, going 2-2 (3.31 ERA) with 31 strikeouts in 32 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Ray has given up two runs or fewer in seven of his nine starts, while pitching to a 2.29 ERA, the lowest among D-backs starters. The left-hander is pitching against the Marlins for the first time in his career.
away_pitcher_note: If his first three starts are any indication, Fernandez is back to his old form. The right-hander has struck out 21 and walked just one in 19 innings. He comes off a no-decision at Philly, throwing 70 pitches in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Ross has turned into a reliable pitcher in the rotation, as he has allowed more than three earned runs in a start just once, yielding four runs on April 28. He also hasn't allowed a home run in 15 starts, which has tied the franchise record.
away_pitcher_note: Koehler's road troubles continued at Philadelphia, where he battled through six innings, but mistakes proved costly. In 10 road starts, he is 3-5 with a 4.85 ERA. Koehler's last road win was on July 3 against the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Cashner had his last start cut short -- not by poor performance but by Mother Nature, as the Padres and Rockies had a game postponed on July 19. Cashner has a 4.75 ERA in 12 career games (six starts) vs. the Giants and lost to them on May 5.
away_pitcher_note: Haren continues to impress with his ability to keep his team in games. He's gone at least six innings in seven of his last eight starts. On the road, he's 3-3 with a 4.13 ERA, compared to 4-2 (2.83) at Marlins Park.

home_pitcher_note: Kennedy earned a win Monday against the Giants, pitching six innings while allowing two runs and striking out six. He has a 2.98 ERA over his last 51 1/3 innings (nine starts) and hasn't allowed more than three earned runs in a start since May 28.
away_pitcher_note: Phelps gave up three runs on seven hits and four walks in 5 2/3 innings and took the loss in his last start at Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: Despaigne was solid in the month of July until his first outing after the All-Star break. The right-hander struggled against the Giants on Tuesday, pitching five innings, allowing seven hits, six runs (all earned) and two home runs.
away_pitcher_note: Latos struck out seven in seven shutout innings in a win vs. the D-backs in his last start. He gave up just four hits and walked one.

home_pitcher_note: For Fernandez, there is no place like home. The 23-year-old sports a 14-0 (1.17) record in 22 career starts at Marlins Park. Fernandez's dominance is reflected by the fact he has struck out 168 in 145 2/3 innings at home.
away_pitcher_note: Zimmermann has had trouble on the road this year, as a 5.14 ERA shouldn't sit well heading down to Miami. While his ERA over the last three starts is 5.06, he hasn't walked more than one batter in a game since June 7.

home_pitcher_note: Koehler snapped a two-game losing streak, collecting a win at San Diego, where he matched his season high with seven strikeouts. Koehler's last four starts have been on the road. At home, he is 4-1 (1.68).
away_pitcher_note: The 30-year-old right-hander has allowed four or more earned runs in six of his last 10 outings (5.24 ERA). He has succeeded historically when facing the Marlins, boasting a 1.09 ERA in four appearances (three starts).

home_pitcher_note: Haren has just one win in his last nine outings, despite turning in six quality starts in that span. He also has a solid 2.83 ERA in 10 home starts, compared to a 4.16 ERA in 10 road outings.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer surrendered five runs against Pittsburgh on Friday. But, in the starts directly following two other five-run outings this year, the veteran owns a 2-0 record and 1.72 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Phelps will open the Marlins' set against the Padres, who defeated the right-hander in his last outing, a quality start. Phelps will be looking for his first win since June 16.
away_pitcher_note: Ian Kennedy was supposed to leave  the team for the birth of his child, but will make the start after all.

home_pitcher_note: Replacing the recently traded Mat Latos, Urena gets his eighth start of the year as he’s recalled for the first time since being optioned July 2. In his last big league start on June 28, the rookie allowed one earned run in five IPs vs. the Dodgers.
away_pitcher_note: Despaigne was good his last time out, allowing one earned run in six innings in a victory over the Marlins, his first victory since May 31. He has a 5.31 ERA in 13 road games in his short career, including 11 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Fernandez is looking to work his way into the record books as he's one win shy of tying Johnny Allen (1932-33) and LaMarr Hoyt (1980-82) for most consecutive decisions won at home to start a career. The ace is 15-0 with a 1.19 ERA in 23 home starts.
away_pitcher_note: The Major League leader in games started lowered his ERA half a run over six July starts, yet won just once. He was the only Padres starter to miss Miami during the Marlins' four-game series at Petco Park last weekend.

home_pitcher_note: Koehler has faced the Mets twice this season -- both times at Citi Field -- and went just 3 1/3 innings in each outing while giving up a combined 12 runs. However, he gets them at home this time, where he owns a 2.32 ERA in 54 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Colon has alternated good starts with rough ones in recent weeks. He allowed six runs in just 2 1/3 innings in his last start against the Padres on Wednesday. In August, Colon has a 3.92 career ERA in 68 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Making his first start since June 8, Hand is getting the first chance to fill the open rotation spot left by Dan Haren, who was traded on Friday. In three starts this season, the lefty is 1-1, having allowed eight earned runs in 11 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: After a rough patch early in the season, Niese has recovered well, pitching to a 2.94 ERA in June and July. He's made 17 career starts against the Marlins, holding a 5-5 record and a 4.38 ERA against them.

home_pitcher_note: Phelps has three no-decisions in three starts vs. the Mets this season, allowing five earned runs in 16 2/3 innings. The righty went 0-3 in five July games.
away_pitcher_note: Harvey dominated in his last start, holding the Nationals to one run over 7 2/3 innings Friday. Mets manager Terry Collins said it was the best performance, command-wise, Harvey's put on all season.

home_pitcher_note: Wisler had another learning experience in his most recent start against the Phillies, where he allowed seven runs on eight hits through 4 2/3 innings. Specifically, Wisler's slider didn't look as sharp as it had in previous outings.
away_pitcher_note: Urena is trying to make his case to be a member of the '16 rotation, and he'll get his second start since being recalled on Friday. He allowed four earned runs and took a loss Saturday, and also pitched a scoreless inning of relief on April 14.

home_pitcher_note: Teheran is coming off one of his best starts this year. He held a lefty-heavy Phillies lineup to two runs over seven innings, while striking out seven. Teheran credited fastball command for the success, and he didn't walk a batter.
away_pitcher_note: Fernandez won in Atlanta on April 22, 2014, when he tossed eight scoreless innings and allowed just three hits. The righty is 3-0 at home this season, while he's 1-0 in two road starts. He won his last road outing on July 22 in Arizona.

home_pitcher_note: Foltynewicz gave up four home runs in four innings his last time out, after hanging sliders over the plate and missing up throughout the start. Keeping his mid-to-upper 90s fastball down and under control has been a lingering issue.
away_pitcher_note: Koehler is coming off two straight rough starts, as he has allowed nine earned runs in his past 10 innings. In three outings vs. the Braves this season, he is 1-1 with four earned runs allowed over 14 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: After allowing just two runs to the Giants in his most recent outing, Miller has now given up two runs or fewer in 17 of his 22 starts this season. Still, his winless streak is up to 14 straight games, despite a 3.14 ERA over that period.
away_pitcher_note: Hand has bounced back and forth from bullpen to rotation, but now he is getting his second straight start. The lefty threw 84 pitches in a no-decision against the Mets. Making his fifth start, Hand is 0-2  (9.18) on the road.

home_pitcher_note: Initially David Phelps was lined up for this start, but he's been pushed back and Nicolino is getting the call from Triple-A, where he is 7-7 (3.52) in 20 starts. The lefty has made two starts for Miami, logging 11 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Wright has given the Red Sox back-to-back strong starts. In his last outing, The knuckleballer tossed eight innings of one-run ball and earned his fifth win Wednesday against the Yankees in New York.

home_pitcher_note: Conley is filling the rotation spot of Jose Urena, who is on the disabled list with a bruised left knee. This is the rookie's second start. He has made four relief appearances. At home, he is 1-0 with a 2.89 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Rodriguez has settled down in his past three starts. The rookie left-hander took the loss Thursday, but gave Boston seven innings of two-run ball against the Yankees.

home_pitcher_note: In three starts since coming off the disabled list, Garcia has allowed four runs on eight hits and 10 walks over 18 innings. He limited the Marlins to one run over seven innings in a June start that ended with him suffering a groin strain.
away_pitcher_note: Koehler tops the team with 127 1/3 innings. He will be making his 22nd start in the opener in St. Louis. He's lost three straight decisions since beating the Padres on July 23. On the road, Koehler is 4-6 with a 4.22 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Lackey has a 1.89 ERA in 12 starts at Busch Stadium this season. The Marlins are one of just two teams (the Cardinals being the other) against whom Lackey has never registered a win. He has faced the Marlins just once in his career.
away_pitcher_note: After bouncing back and forth from the bullpen to the rotation, Hand is getting his chance to start. If his last outing is any indication, he might stick. Hand gave up one run on one hit in seven innings at Atlanta in his last start.

home_pitcher_note: Martinez tied career game highs in innings (eight) and pitches (108) his last time out. The Cardinals are 18-3 in his starts, and he has 16 quality starts. He has gone at least seven innings deep eight times this season.
away_pitcher_note: Approaching a career high in innings, Phelps was pushed back in the rotation. He will be back on the mound after a 10-day rest. Phelps is at 109 2/3 innings, and his career high is 113 with Yankees last year.

home_pitcher_note: Garza is coming off back-to-back starts of seven innings -- the first time the right-hander has accomplished the feat this season. His ERA sits below 5.00 after allowing just two runs last time out, and he has seemingly turned his season around.
away_pitcher_note: Nicolino relies heavily on command, and continues to go through the learning curve. He gave up four runs in 5 2/3 innings in a no-decision against Boston. He's at 131 2/3 innings, counting 115 at Triple-A New Orleans.

home_pitcher_note: The Brewers will continue to let their rookie right-hander audition for a role in the starting rotation despite his struggles. The 26-year-old Cravy is 0-4 this season and carries a 5.92 ERA after 24 1/3 Major League innings.
away_pitcher_note: Is the rookie a starter or reliever? The Marlins are still trying to find that out about Conley, who has a 5.00 ERA in his last 18 innings, with nine strikeouts. In two starts, he's posted a 5.59 ERA in 9 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Peralta put together his best start since returning from the disabled list on July 28 last time out against the Phillies. The right-hander blanked Philadelphia over seven innings, scattering six hits.
away_pitcher_note: Koehler has emerged as the most reliable starter on the staff, and his 134 1/3 innings are the most on the team. The right-hander, however, is seeking his first win since July 23. He's dropped four straight decisions.

home_pitcher_note: Hand started off August throwing the ball well, allowing just one earned run in 11 innings (two starts). However, his last outing was a different story. The lefty surrendered 11 hits and six runs over six innings against the Cardinals.
away_pitcher_note: Williams has had a rough season, but his first three starts this month have been much improved. He is 1-0 with a 1.50 ERA, allowing three earned runs over 18 innings against the Dodgers, Padres and Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: Flores will make his first career start, taking the rotation spot of the injured David Phelps. The rookie picked up his first win in a relief appearance against the Brewers on Tuesday, albeit facing just one batter.
away_pitcher_note: The Phillies get a look at one of the pitching prospects they acquired in the Cole Hamels trade. Eickhoff pitched well in three starts with Triple-A Lehigh Valley, making him the obvious choice to replace David Buchanan.

home_pitcher_note: Nicolino is one of three rookie starters relatively new to the Marlins’ rotation. The lefty picked up a win in his fourth career start his last time out, allowing two runs and scattering six hits over 6 2/3 innings against the Brewers.
away_pitcher_note: August has not been kind to Harang. He is 0-3 with a 10.80 ERA in three starts this month, allowing 26 hits and 18 earned runs over just 15 innings against the Dodgers, D-backs and Brewers.

home_pitcher_note: Conley’s last outing was an odd one. The rookie left-hander struck out the six batters through the first three innings against the Brewers before falling apart in the fourth. Ultimately, Conley surrendered four runs on nine hits in 3 2/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Nola has excellent control, but he struggled Tuesday against Toronto. He walked four batters in five innings. It was the first time in his professional career (29 starts in Minors, six in Majors) he walked four in a start.

home_pitcher_note: Since his last win on July 23, Koehler has dropped five straight starts, and he has a 7.48 ERA in that stretch. At Marlins Park, he is 4-3 (3.07). In two of his last four starts, he's lasted just 4 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Concerns after Happ’s debut start in Pittsburgh were allayed by two ensuing efforts, one run allowed in 11 1/3 innings. He picked up his first win in eight starts since July 3 by two-hitting Arizona for six innings in his last outing.

home_pitcher_note: Hand is settling into the rotation, after bouncing back and forth from starter to reliever. He's worked at least six innings in each of his last three starts, allowing one run in six innings in a win over the Phillies.
away_pitcher_note: Morton has breezed through the first six innings of each of his last two starts, which have featured a devastating curve. He continues to give the Bucs their best chance to win, with the team victorious in 12 of his 16 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Narveson, replacing the injured Kendry Flores, is making his first Major League start since 2012 with Milwaukee. While the lefty has made six relief appearances with Miami this season, he was a starter in Japan last season after missing all of 2013.
away_pitcher_note: Locke tries to rebound on the tough road (6.02 ERA in 10 starts this season) after being battered for 11 hits and six runs in five innings in his last start at PNC Park, where he is usually sharp (prior 3.16 ERA in 13 starts).

home_pitcher_note: The rookie left-hander is coming off his finest MLB start. Nicolino worked a personal high for innings (7 2/3) and pitches (101) in a no-decision against the Phillies. Counting Minor League innings, he's at 146 this year.
away_pitcher_note: Cole returned to form Saturday against the Giants, permitting only an unearned run while striking out eight in his first seven-inning start of the month. Cole is 1-1 with a 4.26 ERA in three career starts against the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer will face the Marlins after the rotation was shuffled for matchups down the road. Scherzer is 2-0 with a 3.60 ERA in three career starts against the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: Conley made strides in his last start, the fourth of his career. The rookie worked six innings and threw 106 pitches, both career highs. He did suffer a loss to the Phillies, but showed progress going deeper into the game.

home_pitcher_note: After allowing 13 home runs all of last season, Zimmermann has allowed 17 in 2015, including eight in August. He is 7-4 with a 3.28 ERA in 20 career starts vs. the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: Koehler is trying to snap a six-game losing streak, as his last win came on July 23 in San Diego. In his last five starts, the righty has allowed three-or-less runs three times, while also logging six and seven-run outings.

home_pitcher_note: Strasburg is 3-1 with a 1.73 ERA in four starts since the All-Star break. The right-hander has started 21 times against Miami in his career, three more than any other team. He is 9-7 with a 3.65 ERA against the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: While Hand has been excellent since rejoining the rotation on Aug. 4 (10 earned runs in 31 innings), he's coming off his best outing of the season, Tuesday vs. Pittsburgh. Earning the win, he tossed a career-high eight-plus innings of two-run ball.

home_pitcher_note: Miller replaces Mike Foltynewicz, scratched due to flu symptoms. Miller has not won since coming one out away from no-hitting the Marlins on May 17. He has allowed two or fewer earned runs 11 times during his 18-start winless streak.
away_pitcher_note: The veteran had a rough go on Wednesday in his first Major League start since 2012. The Pirates tagged Narveson for seven earned runs in 3 2/3 innings, as he admitted afterwards that he was over-hyped for his long awaited return start.

home_pitcher_note: Banuelos will be limited to 50-55 pitches as he makes his first start since being sidelined on July 28 with a bone spur in his left elbow. His effective changeup has helped him allow one run or less in three of four career starts.
away_pitcher_note: Nicolino has logged three straight impressive outings, allowing a combined six earned runs in 20 1/3 against the Brewers, Phillies and Pirates. In his last outing vs. Pittsburgh, the rookie allowed two runs in six innings.

home_pitcher_note: Perez was recalled from Triple-A Gwinnett when Mike Foltynewicz was placed on the disabled list late Thursday night. Perez has posted a 9.87 ERA and allowed opponents to produce a .427 on-base percentage in his past six starts.
away_pitcher_note: Conley is coming off two straight games in which he worked into the sixth inning. He went five-plus at Washington in his last start, giving up three runs. He's allowed four runs in 11 innings (3.27 ERA) in his last two outings.

home_pitcher_note: Koehler has dropped seven straight decisions since July 23. He's been hurt by home runs, having allowed three in a loss at Washington. Three times he's allowed three homers in a game. He's lost to the Mets twice this year.
away_pitcher_note: The lanky righty was uncharacteristically wild his last time out, firing two wild pitches and another to the backstop with a runner aboard. deGrom did manage his fifth double-digit strikeout game of the year. He owns 171 strikeouts in 163 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Hand had been on a roll over a four-start span, which began on Aug. 9 at Atlanta. He was 3-1 with a 3.33 ERA in 27 innings. However, in his last outing, Hand was knocked out after 4 2/3 innings and five runs at Washington.
away_pitcher_note: Colon is starting on normal rest but on what was Noah Syndergaard’s originally scheduled day, as the Mets continue to monitor the rookie’s innings. Colon is riding a streak of 16 consecutive scoreless innings.

home_pitcher_note: Cosart will make his first big league start since July 4, when he was tagged for seven runs in 1 2/3 innings by the Cubs. Cosart was sent to Triple-A after that game, and he also has dealt with vertigo and an inner ear disorder.
away_pitcher_note: The prized lefty returns after missing two months with a lat tear in his left arm. Matz impressed on the mound (2-0, 1.32 ERA) and at the plate (5 RBIs) in two starts following his promotion in late June.

home_pitcher_note: The maturation process for Nicolino is going as scheduled. Over his last four starts, the rookie has a 1.98 ERA over 27 1/3 innings. Nicolino also has thrown at least six innings in each of those games.
away_pitcher_note: Davies dazzled with a fastball/changeup combo in his first turn through a Major League lineup on Wednesday, but the Pirates gave him trouble the second time through, after Davies tried working in a curveball.

home_pitcher_note: Conley is starting to work deeper into games. The rookie left-hander has worked at least five innings in three straight starts, with an ERA of 3.94 over that span. He struggled to go five two previous starts before that.
away_pitcher_note: Jungmann's ERA after 16 Major League starts is 2.42, a mark which would be significant were the season to end now. In the past 40 seasons, only three rookies have made at least 16 starts and finished with an ERA that low.

home_pitcher_note: Koehler paces the Marlins with 156 2/3 innings after his third straight six-inning start. He was in line for his first win since July 23, but had to settle for a no-decision against the Mets. Since the All-Star break, Koehler is 1-8 (5.26 ERA).
away_pitcher_note: After picking up his first Major League victory with three relief innings following a rain delay on Saturday in Cincinnati, the hard-throwing Pena will make his first Major League start.

home_pitcher_note: Cosart's first MLB start since July 4 could be called a success. He gave up one run in 4 2/3 innings in a no-decision against the Mets. He was on a pitch limit and was lifted after 88. He should be pushed to get close to 100.
away_pitcher_note: Fresh off six innings of two-hit ball against the Braves, Gonzalez will start the opener against the Marlins. He is 0-1 against Miami this season, with six earned runs and 10 hits allowed in his one five-inning start.

home_pitcher_note: Making his return from a right biceps strain, Fernandez gets his first start since Aug. 7. With a win, the righty would tie the Major League record for most home victories without a loss to begin a career (16).
away_pitcher_note: Roark is back in the starting rotation for the final month after Joe Ross was moved to the bullpen in an innings-limiting effort. Roark has pitched 28 times out of the bullpen this season with seven starts. In those starts, he is 3-1 with a 5.21 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Finding consistency has been an issue for Hand. In his last two starts, both losses, he's given up 12 runs in 6 1/3 innings. In his two starts before that (both wins), he gave up three runs in 14 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer has been disappointing in the second half of his first season with the Nationals. In 10 starts since the break, Scherzer is 1-4 with a 5.12 ERA and 14 home runs allowed.

home_pitcher_note: Verrett will sub for Matt Harvey as the Mets look to limit the latter pitcher’s innings down the stretch. He’s done so quite capably once already this season, limiting the Rockies to one run in eight innings of an Aug. 23 start at Coors Field.
away_pitcher_note: Nicolino is looking to bounce back from a rough start. The rookie allowed five runs on nine hits in 4 1/3 innings against the Brewers on Monday. Previously, he had allowed two or fewer runs in four straight starts.

home_pitcher_note: Striking out nine batters in seven innings last time out, deGrom squelched talk that he might be growing tired. The Mets still hope to skip him at some point in September, but only if they build a big enough division lead to afford that luxury.
away_pitcher_note: Koehler got his first win in eight starts in his last outing, beating the Brewers on Wednesday while tying a career-high in innings (8) and strikeouts (10). In two September starts, the righty has allowed just four runs in 14 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Not long ago considered a long shot for the playoff rotation, Colon is pitching like an ace. He’s allowed two runs over his past 31 2/3 innings and recently posted the longest consecutive scoreless-innings streak by a 42-year-old in MLB history.
away_pitcher_note: Getting through the order three times is a challenge for Conley, who has not lasted as much as six innings in five of his past six starts. The lefty has won his past two decisions. He's 2-0 (6.62) on the road.

home_pitcher_note: Roark allowed two runs on eight hits over 4 2/3 innings in his last start, a 2-0 loss to the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: Two starts, two impressive showings for Cosart, who has returned from a right inner ear disorder. Eased back slowly, Cosart has allowed one run in 9 2/3 innings with eight strikeouts in two no-decisions.

home_pitcher_note: In his last start, Scherzer tossed eight scoreless innings in a 5-0 victory over the Marlins. The 31-year-old righty allowed five hits with six strikeouts and no walks. Scherzer hasn't issued a walk in four straight starts.
away_pitcher_note: In three big league seasons, Fernandez has not lost at home. He is 16-0 in his career and 4-0 at Marlins Park this year. Only the road, he is more vulnerable, although still strong. He's 1-0 (3.50) in three away starts.

home_pitcher_note: Zimmermann lasted six innings, allowing six runs on seven hits and two home runs. Zimmermann was given a 6-2 lead after five innings, but gave it right back when he allowed a three-run homer to Cody Asche to tie the score at 6.
away_pitcher_note: The Nats have not been an easy matchup for Hand. Lifetime, the lefty is 0-7 (7.97) against them, including 0-2 (9.00) this year. In general, Hand has had a rough time on the road, 1-4 with a 7.60 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: Strasburg had arguably his best start of the season in a 4-0 victory over the Phillies. He pitched eight scoreless innings, didn't allow a baserunner to reach scoring position and struck out a career-high-tying 14 batters.
away_pitcher_note: The rookie had a solid bounce-back start at the Mets (three runs in six innings) after he gave up five runs in 4 1/3 innings in a loss to the Brewers. His innings are getting up there -- 169 1/3, counting the Minor Leagues.

home_pitcher_note: For the second straight year, Koehler is a 10-game winner. He reached double-digits in his last outing at New York. He also leads the team with 170 2/3 innings, and this will be his 29th start. He is 5-4 (2.97) at home.
away_pitcher_note: Harang will be in search of his first win since July (a span of eight starts) when he gets the ball Tuesday against the Marlins. The veteran is 5-7 with a 6.00 ERA in 20 career starts against Miami.

home_pitcher_note: If his last start is any indication, Conley may have a bright future. At the Mets, he threw a career-high seven innings, not allowing a run while giving up three hits with six whiffs and no walks. Conley had gone as much as six innings once before.
away_pitcher_note: Buchanan has had a tough season, but he put together one of his better starts of the season Tuesday against the Nationals. He allowed five hits, two runs, two walks and struck out five in six innings in Philadelphia.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Cosart's fourth start since returning from vertigo in early September. He's been solid in the first three -- allowing three earned runs in 15 2/3 innings -- and is coming off a win in Washington on Thursday (six innings, two runs).
away_pitcher_note: Asher has not found the big leagues to be easy in his first four starts since being promoted Aug. 30. He has not pitched more than 5 2/3 innings or allowed fewer than four runs in any start.

home_pitcher_note: With a victory, Fernandez would set a Major League record for most home wins without a loss to begin a career. He's currently 16-0 with a 1.11 ERA in 25 starts at Marlins Park. This will be his third outing since returning from right biceps strain.
away_pitcher_note: Weber has certainly exceeded expectations as he has completed at least six innings in each of his first three career starts. Though he's just filling a spot in an injury-depleted rotation, he has at least enhanced his future stock.

home_pitcher_note: The lefty has sandwiched a solid start between two tough ones in his past three outings. Nicolino allowed five runs vs. the Brewers on Sept. 7 and three runs in six innings in New York on Sept. 14, before allowing seven runs in 5 2/3 IP vs. the Nats.
away_pitcher_note: Teheran has allowed two runs or less in each of his past four starts and he took a perfect game into the seventh inning of Sunday's start against the Phillies. He has a 2.69 ERA in 11 career starts against the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander allowed three earned runs on seven hits over five innings in a loss to Philadelphia on Tuesday. Koehler has allowed eight earned runs over 25 innings in September (2.88 ERA).
away_pitcher_note: This will be Miller's first Marlins Park appearance since he finished an out away from completing a no-hitter on May 17. He's gone winless in the 23 starts that have followed. But he's posted a 1.16 ERA in five starts against Miami this year.

home_pitcher_note: Moore delivered his second straight quality start on Tuesday night, when he held the Red Sox to two runs on seven hits and two walks, while striking out seven, over 6 2/3 innings to earn his second win of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Conley has been phenomenal in September, allowing just five earned runs in 22 1/3 innings over four starts. The rookie has also logged 25 strikeouts over that time, including a career-high eight K's in his last outing vs. the Phillies on Wednesday.

home_pitcher_note: Smyly held the Red Sox scoreless on five hits and three walks, while striking out seven, on Wednesday en route to his fourth win of the season. He is 1-0 with a 4.35 ERA in four starts at home this season.
away_pitcher_note: Cosart left his last start on Thursday after just four innings when he was struck by a liner in the left forearm. However, he avoided serious injury, suffering a left forearm contusion.

home_pitcher_note: Odorizzi has struggled in his last two starts, allowing eight earned runs on 15 hits -- including three homers -- in 10 2/3 innings. The right-hander is 0-1 with a 10.00 ERA in two career starts vs. the Marlins, with both coming at Tropicana Field.
away_pitcher_note: Fernandez  will make his final start of the year against the Rays. While he's 1-0 with a 3.42 ERA in four road starts this season, he also started vs. the Rays on May 27, 2013, allowing seven runs (four earned) in just 3 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: The Phillies plan to use their bullpen. Aaron Nola had been scheduled to pitch this weekend, but the Phillies shut him down because he reached his innings limit. He threw 187 innings this season.
away_pitcher_note: Koehler has been Miami's most durable pitcher. He paces the staff with 182 1/3 innings, and the right-hander is 3-3 with a 3.92 ERA in his last seven starts. On the road, he's 5-9 with a 4.70 ERA in 16 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Asher, 23, will face the Marlins for the second time in about a week. On Sept. 24 at Miami, he gave up one run on three hits in seven innings, but suffered the loss.
away_pitcher_note: Nicolino has been a bright spot. The rookie comes off a win over the Braves, giving up one earned run in seven innings. After opening the season at Triple-A, he's logged 182 total innings, counting 67 with the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: Buchanan gets the nod in the 2015 finale, his 15th start of the campaign. The righty hasn't had a great year, but he has not allowed more than two earned runs in each of his last three starts.
away_pitcher_note: Conley has saved his best for last. In September, the rookie was 2-0 with a 2.54 ERA in five starts. In his last seven outings, he has a 2.75 ERA with 41 strikeouts in 39 1/3 innings. He's at 168 innings, counting the Minors.

summary: 2016-03-04 - Miami Marlins @ New York Mets (Final: Tied)

home_pitcher_note: The Marlins acquired the left-hander to provide a strong one-two punch at the top of the rotation with Jose Fernandez. But few saw him starting Opening Day. Chen has at made least 30 starts in three of his first four seasons.
away_pitcher_note: Verlander makes his eighth career Opening Day start after a one-year hiatus, a reward for a dominant stretch run last year. Verlander posted a 2.27 ERA and allowed a .207 BA over his final 14 starts, surrendering 74 hits over 99 1/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Working within an innings range of 180, Fernandez has been slotted in Game 2 instead of Opening Day. The 23-year-old made 11 starts and threw 64 2/3 innings last year. At Marlins Park his record is perfect, 17-0 with a 1.40 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: What looked like a potential season-opening DL stint for Sanchez with triceps inflammation instead became a front-line spot between Justin Verlander and Jordan Zimmermann, thanks to effective pitching upon his return.

home_pitcher_note: One year after shuffling in between the rotation and bullpen, Roark is a full-time starter again and starting the team's home opener. The Nationals are hoping he can return to his form from 2014, when he made 31 starts and posted a 2.85 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Manager Don Mattingly said Conley entered Spring Training like he was on a mission. The lefty was one of the most impressive players in camp, winning a rotation spot after throwing 67 innings in his 2015 rookie season.

home_pitcher_note: Ross will begin his first full season in Washington trying to build off an impressive rookie season. After being called up from Double-A for a spot start, Ross eventually forced his way into the rotation.
away_pitcher_note: Miami's most durable starter the past two seasons, Koehler has been a workhorse, posting a team-high 187 1/3 innings in 2015. He was struck by a comebacker on the elbow late in Spring Training, but he is fine.

home_pitcher_note: One of the National League’s leading Rookie of the Year candidates will debut Monday, after going unused last week out of the bullpen in Kansas City. Matz gave up two runs in 5 2/3 innings last year in his lone start against the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: It was a trying 2015 for Cosart, who dealt with vertigo, an inner ear disorder and a demotion to Triple-A. He made just 13 MLB starts and logged 69 2/3 innings. Now healthy, he's refined his delivery and touched 98 mph in spring.

home_pitcher_note: All eyes will be on Syndergaard as he looks to duplicate his six-inning, nine-strikeout performance last week in Kansas City. During that game, Syndergaard leaned heavily on his newest weapon: a slider that he throws upward of 93 mph.
away_pitcher_note: Now that his MLB-record home win streak of 17 to open his career has been snapped, Fernandez looks to improve on his road mark. Away from Miami, he is 5-9 (3.78). At Citi Field, Fernandez has a 1.64 ERA but no decisions.

home_pitcher_note: When the Mets decided to skip Jacob deGrom with a sore right lat, Verrett was the obvious choice to take his place. The right-hander has ample experience spot starting, most notably delivering eight solid innings in place of Matt Harvey last August.
away_pitcher_note: Thus far, Conley's season has mostly been a series of waiting and seeing. The lefty threw one inning on Thursday before a long rain delay came in Washington. Since then, he's been tentative until landing the series finale in New York.

home_pitcher_note: Ten days after pitching on Opening Day, Chen will open the homestand. In the opener, Chen was struck on the left elbow by a line drive, and he's been eased back slowly. He was tentatively set for Wednesday at New York.
away_pitcher_note: Perez struggled with his command as he needed 83 pitches to complete 4 2/3 innings against the Cardinals on Sunday. The right-hander relies heavily on a sinker that can keep opponents off base.

home_pitcher_note: The rotation has struggled to log innings, but Koehler worked 6 1/3 frames at Washington. This is his first home start. At Marlins Park, he is 15-16 with a 3.63 ERA. Against the Braves, the right-hander is 2-4 with a 3.36 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Norris impressed during his season debut against the Nationals, but he struggled while facing them again five days later. The right-hander has regained the strength he lost while battling illness during last year’s disappointing season.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Cosart's second start, and he's matched against a club he has enjoyed success against. The right-hander is 3-0 with a 1.66 ERA versus the Braves. Cosart labored with his command in his first start at the Mets.
away_pitcher_note: Chacin impressed during his season debut Tuesday, notching eight strikeouts while throwing 69 pitches over six scoreless innings against the Nationals. The veteran pitcher battled a sore shoulder the past two years.

home_pitcher_note: Fernandez has yet to throw at least six innings in his first two starts. He has logged 10 2/3 frames with 18 strikeouts. At home, he had his MLB-record streak of 17 straight starts without a loss snapped in Game 2 of the season.
away_pitcher_note: Roark is 2-2 with a 2.39 ERA  in six appearances at Marlins Park. Roark stepped in for Stephen Strasburg (flu) and tossed seven shutout innings vs. Atlanta on Wednesday.

home_pitcher_note: Conley established a career high with nine strikeouts in six innings at the Mets. In two starts, the lefty has fanned 11 in seven innings. Conley worked one inning at Washington on April 7 before leaving because of rain.
away_pitcher_note: Dusty Baker said he didn't know if Strasburg would be ready to pitch until several hours before game time. But Strasburg not only started, he lasted 7 2/3 innings, allowing two runs on four hits with seven strikeouts vs. Atlanta on Thursday.

home_pitcher_note: A bruised left elbow prevented Chen from facing the Nationals on April 10. But any signs of that injury bothering him were erased in Chen's splendid 6 1/3-inning, two-run outing against Atlanta on Friday.
away_pitcher_note: Ross never started at Marlins Park and has pitched there once, which was last September in relief. At Nationals Park, however,  Ross held Miami to one run in seven innings on April 10.

home_pitcher_note: Koehler was knocked out of his last start after 3 2/3 innings, giving up six runs to Atlanta. It was his shortest start since going 3 1/3 innings in May 2015 against the Mets. Koehler went 6 1/3 in his season debut on April 10 in D.C.
away_pitcher_note: Only three current Marlins are hitting over .250 in their careers -- Martin Prado, Christian Yelich and Dee Gordon -- against Scherzer, who struck out seven over seven innings vs. Philadelphia on Saturday.

home_pitcher_note: The eight-year veteran has fared well vs. Miami in his career, striking out 52 in 44 1/3 innings while posting a 3-1 record in 15 games (six starts). This will be Samardzija's first start as a Giant at AT&T Park after three road assignments.
away_pitcher_note: Control has been an issue for Cosart, who has walked nine batters in 10 1/3 innings. He walked six in his last start, a no-decision against Atlanta. He has faced San Francisco once, giving up four runs in four innings last year.

home_pitcher_note: The right-hander can’t seem to shake out of his early-season slump. Peavy was roughed up for four runs over five innings of his most recent start yet still managed to lower his ERA to 9.00. Opponents are batting .431 against Peavy.
away_pitcher_note: Fernandez has been a strikeout machine, fanning 27 batters in 16 2/3 IP. His swing-and-miss percentage is 34.1. His WHIP is 1.14. But getting all these K's is coming at the expense of high pitch counts. He has thrown six innings once.

home_pitcher_note: Cain has been unable to pitch past the fifth inning in his three starts. Most recently, Cain developed control issues when he walked four batters over the first four innings against Arizona. His 6.46 ERA is second-highest among Giants starters.
away_pitcher_note: The Marlins feel Conley is pitching like an ace with the way he's throwing. He has struck out 19 batters in 13 2/3 innings. The question the club has is finding his tiring point. They're not sure if it is around 90, 95 or 100 pitches.

home_pitcher_note: Stripling had the shortest outing of his career in his start in Atlanta, going just 3 2/3 innings and giving up three runs. Coming off Tommy John surgery, Stripling has struck out at least four hitters in all three of his starts.
away_pitcher_note: Chen has faced the Dodgers once, while he was with the Orioles. On April 20, 2013, he gave up one run in six innings in a win. In his career, Chen is 22-17 with a 3.68 ERA on the road. He has a 3.38 ERA in his last two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw got a no-decision his last time out, despite going eight innings, allowing one run and striking out 10 in Atlanta. He also allowed a season-high 10 hits. He’s 5-2 with a 1.91 ERA in his career against Miami, whiffing 60 in 56 2/3 frames.
away_pitcher_note: Signs show Koehler's command is improving. He walked six in his first 10 innings, but issued one in five innings (5 K's) in his last start. His fastball velocity also has picked up to 92.46 mph, right around league average.

home_pitcher_note: Kazmir has been dealing with soreness where the base of the left thumb and wrist meet, which he said he will continue to pitch through. ERA in last three starts is 9.69.
away_pitcher_note: Nicolino is being called up Wednesday to join the rotation, replacing Jarred Cosart (optioned). In four Triple-A starts, the lefty is 2-2 (3.60). Nicolino threw 74 MLB innings in 12 starts in 2015. He finished 5-4 (4.01).

home_pitcher_note: Maeda has been nothing short of spectacular in his first four MLB starts, allowing just run in 25 1/3 innings. That translates to a 0.36 ERA, which leads the NL. His record stands at 3-0.
away_pitcher_note: The road remains rough for Fernandez, now 5-10 with a 3.81 ERA away from Marlins Park. At Dodger Stadium, he is 1-0, with a win as a rookie in 2013. Lifetime, he is 2-0 (2.84) vs. L.A. He has fanned 32 in 22 2/3 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Davies had a 3.71 ERA in six Brewers starts last season, but he has struggled through his first two outings in place of the injured Matt Garza. He pitched six scoreless innings at Wrigley Field in his only start against the Cubs last season.
away_pitcher_note: Minimizing damage in late innings has plagued Conley in each of his last two starts. The team is still finding out his "tiring point." Still, he's gone at least 5 2/3 innings in three straight outings, but has yet to win.

home_pitcher_note: Anderson (1-2, 4.50 ERA) allowed six runs over four innings against the Phillies in his last start. Anderson has only made it past the fifth inning once in four outings this season.
away_pitcher_note: Since Opening Day, when he was struck on the left elbow by a comeback liner, Chen has gotten into a groove. In his last three starts, he has a 3.15 ERA, 17 strikeouts, four walks in 20 innings. On the road, he's 23-17 (3.66).

home_pitcher_note: Peralta (1-3, 7.40 ERA) got his first win of the season in his latest outing, giving up four runs (three earned) in six innings against the Phillies. He is 3-1 with a 3.35 ERA in six career starts against the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: Koehler has gone five innings in each of his last two starts, and has a 3.18 ERA in that span. Manager Don Mattingly has been primed to lift him in the 90-pitch range. Lifetime at Miller Park, his ERA is 8.68 in two starts.

home_pitcher_note: The 24-year-old lefty impressed in his first start, tossing 7 1/3 shutout innings at the Dodgers. Nicolino's tempo has picked up from a year ago, and he's throwing fewer cutters and more changeups and curveballs.
away_pitcher_note: The D-backs left-hander allowed seven runs on seven hits and five walks with two strikeouts in 5 2/3 innings in his last start against the Cardinals, a loss. Seven of the 17 earned runs he allowed in April came via a home run.

home_pitcher_note: Fernandez is racking up big strikeout numbers, fanning 40 in 22 2/3 innings. But he's is getting into trouble in first innings, allowing five runs (9.00 ERA) in that frame on eight hits. Fernandez has fanned nine in first innings.
away_pitcher_note: The right-hander lived up to his potential in his last outing, allowing two hits and two walks with 10 strikeouts over seven scoreless innings vs. the Cardinals. He’s allowed just one run on five hits with 16 strikeouts in his last two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Conley will be making his first start since taking a no-hitter through 7 2/3 innings against the Brewers on April 29. The 25-year-old lefty was pulled 4 outs shy of history at 116 pitches. Conley will face Arizona for the first time in his career.
away_pitcher_note: Ray has struggled his last two outings. He allowed five runs on seven hits and lasted four innings Friday against the Cardinals. Prior to that against the Pirates, he went just three innings and allowed five runs.

home_pitcher_note: Since giving up five runs in five innings on Opening Day, Chen is 2-1 with a 3.38 ERA. He's been a strike-throwing machine, and his ground-ball percentage is 47.3 percent. He has allowed four homers.
away_pitcher_note: Velasquez pitched six scoreless innings Sunday against Cleveland, becoming the only pitcher to have three starts with six or more innings, no runs and three or fewer hits allowed. Opponents have hit just .164 against him.

home_pitcher_note: Working deep into games has been an issue for Koehler. Since throwing 6 1/3 innings in his first outing, he hasn't gone more than five in his last four starts. His last start was just 2 1/3 innings. At home, he's 1-1.
away_pitcher_note: Hellickson struggled to keep the ball in the park Monday at St. Louis, giving up three home runs in 5 1/3 innings. He’s given up seven home runs in 26 1/3 innings and 19.4 percent of the fly balls.

home_pitcher_note: In each of his two starts, Nicolino has gone deep into games, logging 13 1/3 innings. The lefty, however, isn't missing bats, as he has just two strikeouts. But he minimizes damage, pitching off his fastball and changeup.
away_pitcher_note: Nola was dominant, allowing two-hits over seven shutout innings at St. Louis on Tuesday. He has a 20-inning shutout streak and opponents are hitting just .176 off of him. Nola has been tough on the road, posting an ERA of 0.64.

home_pitcher_note: Rising pitch counts have been an issue all season for Fernandez, who has yet to work past six innings in six starts. He's notched 47 strikeouts in 33 2/3 innings, but it is taking deep counts to get results.
away_pitcher_note: Peralta was pushed back three days after going on the paternity list for the birth of a daughter in Milwaukee. He's won back-to-back starts, despite allowing a career-high 13 Marlins hits at Miller Park in his most recent outing.

home_pitcher_note: Conley threw 7 2/3 hitless innings at Milwaukee on April 29. Including Thursday's start vs. the D-backs, he has 13 scoreless innings, 2 hits, 13 strikeouts and 204 combined pitches in his last 2 outings. The club is monitoring his pitch counts.
away_pitcher_note: Davies had an 8.78 ERA after three starts but was much better against the Angels his last time out, allowing two runs in six innings. Davies said he made a point of being more aggressive against hitters.

home_pitcher_note: Chen had a stretch of four straight starts lasting at least 6 1/3 innings snapped in his last outing. He didn't strike out a batter for just the second time in 123 career starts, while allowing 11 hits and four runs in five innings.
away_pitcher_note: After allowing no earned runs in his first two starts, Anderson has lost four in a row while allowing 21 earned runs on 34 hits, including eight home runs.

home_pitcher_note: Gonzalez had his worst outing last Saturday, allowing five runs in 5 2/3 innings. The big blow was a home run to Kris Bryant in the fourth inning.
away_pitcher_note: Koehler gets his third shot of the season against the Nationals. He's 1-1 with a 2.38 ERA, but he has had a rough time at Nationals Park in his career, going 1-5 with a 5.60 ERA in six starts. Bryce Harper has six career homers off Koehler.

home_pitcher_note: Strasburg pitches Game 1 of the doubleheader against the Marlins. It comes a few days after he signed a 7-year extension worth $175 million. Since he entered the league in 2010, Strasburg has averaged 10.45 strikeouts per 9 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Nicolino has success working at a quick tempo, working both sides of the plate and pitching off his fastball and changeup. He's thrown 61.7 percent fastballs, 19.5 percent changeups. He's struck out just three in 19 1/3 IP.

home_pitcher_note: Roark will pitch game 2 of the doubleheader against Miami. He has pitched six or more innings in six of his seven starts this season.
away_pitcher_note: Flores, Miami's 5th-rated prospect per MLBPipeline.com,  is being promoted from Triple-A New Orleans to make the Game 2 start. He made one start in seven MLB outings in 2015. At New Orleans, he had a 2.59 ERA in 31 innings.

home_pitcher_note: Ross' last start was his worst of the year. He allowed five runs on eight hits in six innings against the Tigers. Ross was cruising until the fourth, when he allowed a homer to Nick Castellanos.
away_pitcher_note: Fernandez might have turned the corner in his last start, striking out 11 in seven shutout innings vs. the Brewers. He's gone full counts to 34 of the 146 batters he's faced this year. Fernandez beat the Nationals on 4/18 in Miami.

home_pitcher_note: Eickhoff didn’t expand his repertoire beyond his fastball and curve vs. the Braves, and it hurt him as he lasted 4 1/3 innings and allowing 4 runs in a 5-1 loss. He’ll rediscover his early-season success when rediscovers his changeup and slider.
away_pitcher_note: Perhaps the 116 pitches Conley threw on April 29 in his 7 2/3 hitless innings vs. Milwaukee are catching up to him. The lefty has gone 9 1/3 in his last two starts, and his four innings in a rematch with the Brewers was a rough outing.

home_pitcher_note: This will be Velasquez’s second start against the Marlins in three turns. The sensational 23-year-old has appeared mortal of late, going six innings and allowing four runs in each of his last two starts.
away_pitcher_note: Chen matched his career high with 12 strikeouts in his last start, at home against Milwaukee. Just twice in his career has he reached double digits in K's. On May 6, Chen gave up four runs in five innings at home to the Phillies.

home_pitcher_note: Hellickson said he had his best changeup of the season in his last outing, going seven innings and allowing no earned runs to the Reds, striking out nine in a 3-2 victory.
away_pitcher_note: Koehler is coming off back-to-back strong starts, in which he allowed a total of two runs in 12 2/3 innings vs. the Phillies and Nationals. The righty allowed 11 baserunners vs. Washington on Friday but pitched around trouble in a no-decision.

home_pitcher_note: Nicolino threw at least six innings in his first three starts of the season, but he lasted just 4 2/3 innings in his last outing, a loss in Washington. Nicolino has increased the amount of changeups he has thrown this year to 19.3 percent.
away_pitcher_note: Roark gets another crack at the Marlins after they touched him for seven runs on eight hits in five innings in his last outing. He has a 4.63 career ERA against Miami.

home_pitcher_note: Fernandez, the reigning National League Player of the Week, is 2-0 with a 0.64 ERA and 22 strikeouts in his last two starts. He fanned 11 in seven innings in a win vs. the Nationals his last time out.
away_pitcher_note: Ross took the loss in his last outing against the Marlins, allowing five runs (three earned) in 5 2/3 innings. He’s 1-1 with a 2.20 ERA in five career games (three starts) against Miami.

home_pitcher_note: This is Conley's third meeting with the Nationals, and his 8.22 ERA against them is a little misleading. All seven runs allowed came in two of his 7 2/3 innings. They lefty is 1-2 with a 4.50 ERA in three home starts.
away_pitcher_note: Scherzer has lost two of his past three outings and has given up eight homers in that span. He took the loss against Miami on April 21, giving up five runs in five innings.

home_pitcher_note: The Rays are no strangers to Chen. He's made 19 starts and thrown 111 2/3 innings against them, both personal highs vs. any club. Chen is 5-6 with a 3.55 ERA lifetime in the matchup. Chen is 1-1 (4.85) at home this year.
