home_pitcher_note: Aaron Sanchez gets the start as the Giants open their series against the Marlins. The right-hander is looking for his first win of the season despite allowing two runs or fewer in each of his first three outings.
away_pitcher_note: Castano made his season debut on Friday against the Giants, limiting them to one run on three hits with two walks and no strikeouts.

home_pitcher_note: After pitching five scoreless innings in his debut against the Marlins on Sunday, Wood will again take the mound against Miami -- this time in San Francisco. He allowed just three hits and zero runs in the last meeting.
away_pitcher_note: Last Saturday, Alcantara held the Giants scoreless through six innings before things unraveled in a four-run seventh. His stretch of 44 2/3 regular-season frames without allowing a homer ended when Brandon Belt took him deep.

home_pitcher_note: Gausman has been an ace for the Giants so far this season. He looks to keep his dominant run going after tossing six scoreless innings against the Phillies on Monday.
away_pitcher_note: López was the tough-luck loser his last time out on Sunday against the Giants. Though he set a career high with nine strikeouts -- all on the changeup -- across six innings, an unearned run proved to be the difference in the 1-0 defeat.

home_pitcher_note: Webb will be looking to bounce back when he wraps up the Giants' four-game series against the Marlins. He allowed four runs in four innings against the Phillies on Tuesday, and he has a 5.87 ERA through 15 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: With inclement weather in the forecast, Detwiler will open a bullpen game for the Marlins in the series finale. One of two lefties among Miami's relief corps, Detwiler last started in 2019 with the White Sox.

home_pitcher_note: This season, Burnes is at 40 strikeouts and counting without issuing his first walk, an all-time record for a starting pitcher. Now he's chasing Dodgers closer Kenley Jansen, who struck out 51 batters before walking one in 2017.
away_pitcher_note: Rogers put together arguably the best start of his young career last time out, pitching seven scoreless innings with eight strikeouts against the Orioles on Wednesday. He enters the second leg of Miami's 10-game trip with a 12.7 K/9 rate.

home_pitcher_note: Perhaps overshadowed by strikeout machines Corbin Burnes, Freddy Peralta and Brandon Woodruff, Houser's solid start should not go unnoticed. After recording a 5.30 ERA last year, Houser has not allowed more than three runs in any of his first four starts.
away_pitcher_note: Castano will get to face a new opponent after back-to-back starts against the Giants to begin his 2021 season. Last Thursday, he allowed three two-out runs in the first before holding San Francisco scoreless over the next four frames. The rookie has struck out two of the 40 batters he has faced.

home_pitcher_note: One week after his 31st birthday, Godley was activated by the Brewers to start in place of injured left-hander Brett Anderson. Godley, who pitched for Boston last year, signed with Milwaukee late in Spring Training.
away_pitcher_note: His last time out, Alcantara walked four batters in a start for the first time since Sept. 3, 2019. Despite the lack of command, his lone blemish was a two-run homer across five innings. On June 5, 2019, Alcantara held the host Brewers to one run over seven frames.

home_pitcher_note: Lester will make his 2021 season debut -- and first regular-season start as a member of the Nationals – after being reinstated from the injured list on Friday afternoon. Last season, Lester went 3-3 with a 5.16 ERA over 12 starts with the Cubs.
away_pitcher_note: López has allowed two or fewer runs in all but one of his five starts this season. In four career starts at Nationals Park, he has an 8.10 ERA with eight strikeouts, five walks and six homers allowed in 16 2/3 innings. Last season, he permitted three unearned runs across five frames.

home_pitcher_note: Corbin looks to find a rhythm after allowing four runs in as many innings Sunday against the Mets. He is 4-3 with a 3.91 ERA over 12 career starts vs. the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: Campbell, who has been pitching in long relief, will get his first Major League start in his fifth outing. The Rule 5 Draft pick had been on a starter's schedule leading up to his most recent appearance last Sunday, when he allowed three runs during a rainy second inning before pitching two scoreless frames.

home_pitcher_note: Scherzer is looking to return to form after allowing two home runs (including a grand slam) to Vladimir Guerrero Jr. in his last start on Tuesday against the Blue Jays. Over his career, he is 13-5 with a 3.11 ERA in 24 starts vs. the Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: Rogers outdueled Brewers ace Corbin Burnes in his last start, pitching six scoreless innings with seven strikeouts. In his past two outings -- both caught by veteran Sandy León -- the rookie lefty hasn't given up a run in 13 frames with 15 strikeouts and one walk.

home_pitcher_note: Alcantara pitched a season-high seven innings his last time out, allowing just a two-run homer in a win over the Brewers. After striking out 17 batters in his first 12 frames of the season, he has just 19 in his past 24 2/3.
away_pitcher_note: Making his third career start, Smith is facing the Marlins for the first time. In his previous start, he took the loss against the Padres, allowing three runs on six hits over four-plus innings.
Weaver was not sharp in his last start against the Rockies, as he allowed three runs over four innings in a no-decision. Over his past three starts, the right-hander is 0-2 with a 7.62 ERA.

home_pitcher_note: López received an extra day of rest as part of the club's plan to monitor its young arms' workload. López has given up two or fewer runs in all but one of his six starts. Last time out, he pitched a career-high-tying seven scoreless innings on 79 pitches.
away_pitcher_note: Bumgarner has been outstanding in his past three starts, going 3-0 with a 1.06 ERA over that stretch. That also included a seven-inning no-hitter against the Braves in Atlanta on April 25.

home_pitcher_note: Rogers, the reigning NL Rookie of the Month, shut out the Brewers across six innings on April 26, outdueling Milwaukee ace Corbin Burnes. Then, on Sunday against the Nationals, his lone mistake in five frames was a three-run homer to Ryan Zimmerman.
away_pitcher_note: Suter will start a bullpen day. He made four such starts during the 2020 regular season, covering at least three innings each time and holding the opponent scoreless three times. It didn't go as well in the playoffs against the Dodgers.

Houser is quietly having a comeback season after a posting 5.30 ERA in 56 innings last year. He allowed three earned runs in 5 2/3 innings and set a season high with seven strikeouts against Miami during Milwaukee's last homestand.

home_pitcher_note: Alcantara faces the Brewers for the second time in his past three starts. He pitched a season-high seven frames against them on April 28, surrendering just a two-run homer in the win. Alcantara has allowed two earned runs or fewer in five of seven starts in 2021.
away_pitcher_note: Anderson returns for his first start since April 23, when he suffered a right hamstring injury and had to be pulled after 11 pitches. In the two starts preceding the injury, he allowed just one earned run in 12 innings of work.

home_pitcher_note: Weaver has struggled over his last four starts after throwing a no-hitter for six innings against the Reds in early April. Over his last four outings, he has allowed 17 runs in 17 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Miami's No. 22 prospect will make his first Major League start, with a pitch count in the 60-75 range. Holloway has been impressive out of the bullpen this season, pitching 10 scoreless innings with 10 strikeouts and a 0.70 WHIP.

home_pitcher_note: Bumgarner has been on a roll of late. Over his last four starts, he has a 1.17 ERA and has struck out 25 while walking just two in 23 innings. He threw a seven-inning no-hitter against the Braves on April 25.
away_pitcher_note: López faces the D-backs for a second straight start. Last Thursday, he held Arizona to an unearned run on three hits with two walks and six strikeouts over five innings. Despite a 2.04 ERA, López has yet to win in seven outings.

Poteet, whose contract was selected from Triple-A Jacksonville, will make his Major League debut. The 26-year-old right-hander was Miami's fourth-round Draft pick in 2015. He struck out 10 batters over 5 2/3 innings last Thursday in a Minor League start.

home_pitcher_note: Kelly was  on the injured list for three days due to a COVID protocol issue but he didn't miss a start. Last time out against the Mets he allowed three runs (two earned) on three hits over 5 2/3 innings and took the loss.
away_pitcher_note: Rogers has a 1.09 WHIP and 12.3 strikeouts per nine innings in four road starts this season. He has not pitched more than five innings in each of his past two starts.

home_pitcher_note: Kershaw tossed five scoreless innings in his last start against the Angels, the 84th time in his career that he has completed a scoreless start. That's the sixth most by a starter since 1920.
away_pitcher_note: Alcantara has recorded three straight quality starts, with a 1.80 ERA and an opponent's .634 OPS during that span. The righty has pitched at Dodger Stadium just once, giving up six runs on seven hits in five innings in a no-decision on July 20, 2019.

home_pitcher_note: In two starts at Dodger Stadium this season, Bauer is 2-0 with a 1.38 ERA. He has recorded 18 strikeouts over 13 innings and opposing hitters have a .437 OPS.

Nelson will serve as the Dodgers' opener in what will be a bullpen day. Nelson, who was a former starter with the Brewers, hasn't allowed a run in his last five appearances. He could provide the Dodgers with two or three innings on Sunday.
away_pitcher_note: López will face the reigning World Series champions in his first career start at Dodger Stadium. In his last outing, López allowed a season-high-tying six earned runs in 4 1/3 innings. In his other six starts, he has a combined ERA of 0.76.

home_pitcher_note: Wheeler deserved a better fate Wednesday in DC. A defensive gaffe allowed the Nats to score their second run against him in six innings. Still, he has a 2.10 ERA in his last four starts, striking out 30 and walking five in 30 innings.
away_pitcher_note:
Poteet earned the win in his big league debut on Wednesday in Arizona, becoming the third pitcher in
franchise history to earn the win in a start in which he tossed at least five innings without allowing a walk.

home_pitcher_note: Eflin had an uncharacteristic start Thursday against the Nats, allowing one walk and two homers in a span of three batters in the first inning. Prior to that outing, he had walked only three batters in his first seven starts and had allowed only one homer since April 16.
away_pitcher_note: Trevor Rogers will be looking for his third straight win when he takes the mound against the Phillies. In Rogers' last outing, against the D-backs, he went six innings and allowed one run on four hits. He also struck out seven and walked two.

home_pitcher_note: Velasquez has been a nice surprise since he replaced left-hander Matt Moore in the rotation during April. In five starts, Velasquez has a 2.84 ERA. He has allowed one run in each of his last three starts, pitching at least 5 1/3 innings in each of those three starts.
away_pitcher_note: The last time through the order, Sandy Alcantara gave up eight runs in 1 1/3 innings against the Dodgers making it the shortest outing the Marlins starter had delivered through his nine starts. The righty held a 2.72 ERA before his quick exit.

home_pitcher_note: Curtiss will be the opener in a bullpen game for the Marlins. This will be his first career start for Miami, but the 28-year-old served as the Rays' opener three times last season, allowing one earned run on six hits over 3 1/3 innings.
away_pitcher_note: Stroman allowed five earned runs in his last start Sunday, the most he's allowed since joining the Mets. The club has scored a total of nine runs in Stroman's past six outings.

home_pitcher_note: López picked up his first win of the season on Sunday, when he allowed two runs over five innings against the reigning World Series-champion Dodgers in L.A. López has not completed six innings in any of his three May starts.

Poteet has been solid in his first two Major League starts, allowing two runs over 10 innings with nine strikeouts and two walks. He has given the Marlins five frames in each outing, something the club has needed with two members of the rotation sidelined.

Rogers went a career-high 7 2/3 innings in his last start, holding the Phillies to one run on five hits. He picked up his 100th career strikeout in the outing, and became the third-fastest Marlin to achieve the milestone.
away_pitcher_note: Eflin has struck out 57 and walked five in 57 1/3 innings this season as he continues to pound the strike zone with success. He has pitched six or more innings in each of his nine starts this season.

home_pitcher_note: After a career-worst outing (1 1/3 IP, 8 ER) against the Dodgers, Alcantara bounced back with six scoreless innings vs. the Phillies. He struck out nine, walked three and allowed just two hits.
away_pitcher_note: Velasquez was scratched about 20 minutes before his scheduled start Thursday because of numbness in his right index finger. It has happened before, but the Phillies said Friday that Velasquez was fine, so he is expected to make his start against the Marlins.

home_pitcher_note: Neidert was recalled to make a spot start with Jordan Holloway on the injured list. In three starts this season, Neidert was unable to complete five innings.
away_pitcher_note: Since Nola threw the first nine-inning shutout of his career on April 18 against the Cardinals, he is 2-3 with a 5.19 ERA in six starts. The Phillies are 2-4 in that stretch, and they need better from Nola if they want to get on a roll.

home_pitcher_note: López has a 0.61 ERA in five starts at loanDepot park this season, and he takes the mound for the homestand finale. López went a season-high-tying seven scoreless innings in his most recent outing against the Mets.
away_pitcher_note: Howard's fastball averaged 95.3 mph and touched 97.3 mph in his first two innings Saturday against Boston. It averaged 92.9 mph after that, which is a continuing and troubling trend for Howard, who suffered from those drop-offs last season, too.

home_pitcher_note: Pérez has been Boston's hottest pitcher of late, notching a 2.22 ERA in his last five starts. This will be Pérez's first start against the Marlins since 2017, when he held them to three runs over seven innings.
away_pitcher_note: Last time out, Poteet pitched a career-high seven innings in his third big league start. He has not allowed a run in 12 consecutive frames.
summary: 2021-05-28 - Miami Marlins @ Boston Red Sox (Completed Early: Rain)

home_pitcher_note: The flame-throwing righty will face the team he pitched for from 2012-14. In his last three starts against Miami, Eovaldi is 1-0 with a 1.59 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: Rogers didn't have his best command (three walks) and still managed to allow only one earned run over five innings in his last start. He struck out a season-low five. Rogers has gone just five frames in three of his five May outings.

home_pitcher_note: Ray wasn't as sharp last time out, and the home run ball continues to be a problem, with 10 allowed over 29 1/3 innings in May. He's still pounding the zone, though, as he reinvents his pitching style in 2021.
away_pitcher_note: Alcantara is coming off his longest outing of the year -- an eight-inning effort against the Phillies in which he allowed just two runs on two hits but took the loss. He's allowed two earned runs or fewer in eight of 11 starts.

home_pitcher_note: What can Manoah do for an encore? The club's No. 5 prospect dominated the Yankees with six shutout innings in his debut, and when his fastball-slider mix is combined with his aggression on the mound, Manoah puts on a show.
away_pitcher_note: It’s not reflected in his 1-3 record this season, but López has allowed just four runs on 15 hits with three walks and 16 strikeouts in 19 innings over his past three starts. This will be his first career start against the Blue Jays.

home_pitcher_note: After allowing nine runs in five innings vs. the Braves on May 21, Anderson bounced back Thursday vs. the Cubs, allowing two earned runs (four total) in five innings. Against Miami, he’s 1-3 with a 3.96 ERA in five career starts.
away_pitcher_note: Hernandez, who rejoined the club in Buffalo, N.Y., is eligible to be activated off the 60-day injured list. He exited in the third inning of his season debut on April 3 with right biceps inflammation.

home_pitcher_note: Keller has been up and down in his results this season -- a trend he said he's noticed -- but he's coming off a strong one: five scoreless innings against the Rockies in a doubleheader sweep on Saturday.
away_pitcher_note: Poteet was terrific in the first three starts of his career but struggled with his execution last Friday in Boston, allowing five runs in 4 1/3 innings. His 0.84 WHIP is among the top rookie starters in MLB.

home_pitcher_note: De Jong said he feels like an entirely different pitcher than he was in 2019, when he was released by the Twins. He showed it on Sunday, allowing just one run in five innings against the Rockies.
away_pitcher_note: Though he took the loss last Saturday in Boston, Rogers’ breakout season continued. He held the potent Red Sox lineup to a pair of runs with no walks in six innings and has now gone five straight starts without allowing more than two earned runs. He is the two-time reigning NL Rookie of the Month.

home_pitcher_note: Kuhl returned from the injured list (right shoulder discomfort) on Tuesday to pitch four innings with three runs allowed in Kansas City. He has reached five innings only once this season.
away_pitcher_note: Alcantara allowed four runs, three on Vladimir Guerrero Jr.'s homer, over six innings in a loss on Tuesday. That marked just the third time in 12 starts this season he has given up four earned runs or more.

home_pitcher_note: Pivetta took a tough-luck loss in his last start, giving up two runs over six innings while striking out nine against the Astros. In 11 career appearances (eight starts) vs. the Marlins, he's 2-4 with a 5.36 ERA.
away_pitcher_note: With the Marlins losing an off-day due to the makeup game in Boston, they elected to give Pablo López an extra day of rest. It's part of the organization's plan to monitor its starting pitchers' innings over a long season. Thompson will make his MLB debut.

home_pitcher_note: López, who was originally slated to start Monday's makeup game in Boston, received an extra day of rest. He struck out a career-high-tying nine batters last Wednesday against the Blue Jays, but he lasted just four innings.
away_pitcher_note: After a rocky start to the season, Senzatela has put together a consistent run of strong outings, posting a 2.28 ERA over his last four starts. The right-hander has never started against the Marlins, but in four career relief appearances against them, he's given up two runs on three hits over nine innings.

home_pitcher_note: With Cody Poteet on the injured list, Garrett will fill in. Miami's seventh-ranked prospect made two starts in 2020, and a three-inning-relief outing last month in Los Angeles.
away_pitcher_note: Gomber looks to continue a tremendous run over which he owns a 1.53 ERA in five starts since May 12. He's only made one appearance against Miami in his career, giving up two runs over an inning of relief while with the Cardinals in 2018.

home_pitcher_note: The reigning two-time NL Rookie of the Month retired 13 of the last 14 batters he faced following a two-out, two-run single by Bryan Reynolds in the second on Saturday. That was Rogers' only mistake across six innings.
away_pitcher_note: Gonzalez will make a spot start for the injured Jon Gray, who is on the 10-day injured list with a right forearm flexor strain. Gonzalez was hit hard in his last relief appearance, which came when Gray was injured last Friday -- he gave up three runs on seven hits over 4 1/3 innings against the A's.

home_pitcher_note: Alcantara played the role of stopper to perfection on Sunday, pitching a season-high-tying eight innings against the Pirates. He allowed just one unearned run to help the Marlins snap an eight-game skid.
away_pitcher_note: Morton will be looking to win a fourth straight start. As the veteran has posted a 2.74 ERA over his past four starts, he has been able to avoid the big innings that sunk him during the early weeks of this season. He still has allowed at least three runs in an inning in six of his 12 starts.

home_pitcher_note: Thompson wasn't used out of the bullpen Friday night against the Braves, so the Marlins are hoping to get at least three or four innings from him on Saturday. Thompson last appeared in a game on Monday against the Red Sox. He pitched three innings and allowed two runs.
away_pitcher_note: Fried has posted a 2.41 ERA in six starts since returning from the injured list. The lefty stumbled against the Nationals on June 1, but returned with six strong innings against the Dodgers on Sunday.

home_pitcher_note: López went a career-high eight innings his last time out vs. the Rockies. But the Braves always give him trouble, including six runs over four frames on April 13 in Atlanta.
away_pitcher_note: Smyly's turn remains the trouble spot for Atlanta's rotation. He has allowed three runs or fewer in six of his past seven starts, but he has completed just 4 1/3 innings in each of his past two outings.

home_pitcher_note: Wainwright will look to be the steadying force for a struggling rotation, with at least seven innings in each of his last two starts. Also comforting is that Wainwright is pitching at home, where he owns a 2.62 ERA this season vs. 8.20 on the road.
away_pitcher_note: Garrett allowed two runs on five hits across four innings in his first MLB start of 2021. Miami's No. 7 prospect didn't have his best command or stuff, walking three batters and striking out three.

home_pitcher_note: Kim (right lower back tightness) will be  activated off the IL for his first start since June 4. In the end, it will be just one missed start for the lefty, who endured his second bout with the back ailment after missing two weeks in Spring Training with a similar issue.
away_pitcher_note: Rogers has gone at least six innings in each of his last three starts. In his 2021 debut, he walked a season-high four batters in a loss to the Cardinals.

home_pitcher_note: Recently graduated from prospect status and still in search of his first win, Oviedo was two outs away from qualifying for it his last outing, but a ruinous fifth inning dashed such hopes. The Havana native will make his first career start against the nearby Marlins.
away_pitcher_note: Alcantara struck out a season-high 10 batters in a start vs. his former club in April. He has a 2.38 ERA in five starts since the worst outing of his career (8 ER, 1 1/3 IP) in L.A.

home_pitcher_note: Davies looks to extend his winning streak to three, having thrown 12 2/3 scoreless innings in his past two starts. He is 3-2 with a 5.74 ERA in six career starts against the Marlins, whom he last faced in 2019.
away_pitcher_note: Poteet will be activated from the IL to start the series opener. Prior to sustaining a sprained right MCL, Poteet had provided stability at the back of the rotation.

home_pitcher_note: Arrieta is seeking his first win in five starts, having gone 0-3 with a 7.47 ERA in his past four outings. The Marlins might be the perfect opponent; Arrieta is 8-1 in 12 career starts against Miami.
away_pitcher_note: López has been a consistent arm in the Miami rotation this season, but in his last start against the Braves on June 13 he allowed six hits and four runs through three innings for his shortest start of the season. He looks to regroup in his first matchup of the season against the Cubs.

home_pitcher_note: Mills will make his 15th appearance of the season -- but just his third start -- when he takes the mound for his first career outing against the Marlins. He allowed three runs over 4 1/3 innings on Tuesday against the Mets.
away_pitcher_note: The Marlins will give rookie Trevor Rogers extra rest, so Thompson will start the series finale. He last pitched on June 12, shutting out the Braves over five innings.

home_pitcher_note: Alcantara threw his third career complete game last Wednesday, but it resulted in a Cardinals walk-off win with one out in the ninth. He allowed four runs on nine hits over six innings vs. the Blue Jays on June 1.
away_pitcher_note: Stripling looked sharp again his last time out, striking out nine over 6 2/3 innings. That's one of his deepest outings with the Blue Jays and the first time he's hit the 100-pitch plateau in 2021, so he's in a nice groove.

home_pitcher_note: Rogers will be working on seven days' rest thanks to a pair of off-days. This is part of the organization's long-term plan to monitor the workload of its young starting pitchers. Rogers has recorded four straight quality starts.
